95/// A conversion from SOCK_* flags to O_* flags which makes unsafe (but checked during testing) assumptions.
96fn oflag_from_sock_bits(s_bits: i32) -> OFlag {
97    // An otherwise unsafe "cast" which leans on the `linux_flags_assumptions` below.
98    OFlag::from_bits_truncate(s_bits & (libc::SOCK_CLOEXEC | libc::SOCK_NONBLOCK))
99}

103// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-2150): Review timer-slack procfs parsing,

105const TIMER_SLACK_PARSE_BYTES: usize = 66;
106#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
107struct TimerSlackIovec {
108    base: usize,
109    len: usize,
110}

112#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
113struct TimerSlackBinding {
114    target: i32,
115    device: u64,
116    inode: u64,
117}
118
119fn classify_timer_slack_binding(
120    binding: TimerSlackBinding,
121    observed_identity: Option<(u64, u64)>,
122    current_tid: i32,
123) -> Result<(), Errno> {
124    if observed_identity != Some((binding.device, binding.inode)) {
125        // The bound task exited. A missing path and a new task that recycled
126        // the same numeric TID are both ESRCH for the old open inode.
127        return Err(Errno::ESRCH);
128    }
129    if current_tid != binding.target {
130        // Cross-task CAP_SYS_NICE access is intentionally not exposed.
131        return Err(Errno::EPERM);
132    }
133    Ok(())
134}

136fn parse_timer_slack_write(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<u64, Errno> {
137    // `kstrtoull_from_user` copies at most sign + 64 binary digits + newline,
138    // then accepts decimal digits with one optional leading '+' and one
139    // optional trailing newline. An embedded NUL terminates the C string.
140    let bytes = &bytes[..bytes.len().min(TIMER_SLACK_PARSE_BYTES)];
141    let end = bytes
142        .iter()
143        .position(|byte| *byte == 0)
144        .unwrap_or(bytes.len());
145    let mut value = &bytes[..end];
146    if value.first() == Some(&b'+') {
147        value = &value[1..];
148    }
149    if value.last() == Some(&b'\n') {
150        value = &value[..value.len() - 1];
151    }
152    if value.is_empty() || !value.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_digit) {
153        return Err(Errno::EINVAL);
154    }
155    value.iter().try_fold(0_u64, |parsed, digit| {
156        parsed
157            .checked_mul(10)
158            .and_then(|parsed| parsed.checked_add(u64::from(digit - b'0')))
159            .ok_or(Errno::ERANGE)
160    })
161}

163fn vectored_offset(low: u64, high: u64) -> i64 {
164    if std::mem::size_of::<usize>() == 8 {
165        low as i64
166    } else {
167        ((high << 32) | (low & u32::MAX as u64)) as i64
168    }
169}

172struct RandomVectoredRead {

174    count: usize,

176    flags: i32,
177}

179/// Apply Linux's checks after complete iovec import, before touching output.
180fn validate_random_vector_read(offset: Option<u64>, total: usize, flags: i32) -> Result<(), Errno> {
181    if total == 0 {
182        return Ok(());
183    }
184    if let Some(offset) = offset
185        && offset
186            .checked_add(total as u64)
187            .is_none_or(|end| end > i64::MAX as u64)
188    {
189        return Err(Errno::EINVAL);
190    }
191    // Linux 7.1's RWF_NOSIGNAL is newer than the pinned libc crate. Native
192    // random-device controls accept it, including with RWF_NOWAIT.
193    const RWF_NOSIGNAL: i32 = 0x100;
194    const KNOWN: i32 = libc::RWF_HIPRI
195        | libc::RWF_DSYNC
196        | libc::RWF_SYNC
197        | libc::RWF_NOWAIT
198        | libc::RWF_APPEND
199        | libc::RWF_NOAPPEND
200        | libc::RWF_ATOMIC
201        | libc::RWF_DONTCACHE
202        | RWF_NOSIGNAL;
203    // Unknown flags win over conflicting recognized flags, while recognized
204    // but unsupported ATOMIC/DONTCACHE are rejected after APPEND/NOAPPEND.
205    if flags & !KNOWN != 0 {
206        return Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP);
207    }
208    if flags & libc::RWF_APPEND != 0 && flags & libc::RWF_NOAPPEND != 0 {
209        return Err(Errno::EINVAL);
210    }
211    if flags & (libc::RWF_ATOMIC | libc::RWF_DONTCACHE) != 0 {
212        return Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP);
213    }
214    Ok(())
215}

217fn read_iovecs<M: MemoryAccess>(
218    memory: &M,
219    address: Option<Addr<libc::iovec>>,
220    count: usize,
221) -> Result<Vec<TimerSlackIovec>, Errno> {
222    if count > libc::UIO_MAXIOV as usize {
223        return Err(Errno::EINVAL);
224    }
225    if count == 0 {
226        return Ok(Vec::new());
227    }
228    let address = address.ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
229    let mut iovecs = vec![
230        libc::iovec {
231            iov_base: std::ptr::null_mut(),
232            iov_len: 0,
233        };
234        count
235    ];
236    memory.read_values(address, &mut iovecs)?;
237    let total = iovecs.iter().try_fold(0_usize, |total, iovec| {
238        total.checked_add(iovec.iov_len).ok_or(Errno::EINVAL)
239    })?;
240    if total > isize::MAX as usize {
241        return Err(Errno::EINVAL);
242    }
243    Ok(iovecs
244        .into_iter()
245        .map(|iovec| TimerSlackIovec {
246            base: iovec.iov_base as usize,
247            len: iovec.iov_len,
248        })
249        .collect())
250}

252fn copy_timer_slack_output<M: MemoryAccess>(
253    memory: &mut M,
254    destination: Option<AddrMut<'_, u8>>,
255    bytes: &[u8],
256) -> Result<usize, Errno> {
257    if bytes.is_empty() {
258        return Ok(0);
259    }
260    let copied = memory.write(destination.ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?, bytes)?;
261    if copied == 0 {
262        Err(Errno::EFAULT)
263    } else {
264        Ok(copied)
265    }
266}

268/// Copy sanitized procfs bytes to the caller's buffer as the kernel's
269/// `copy_to_user` does: through the guest's page protections, stopping at the
270/// first byte that cannot be written. Returns the bytes copied, or `EFAULT`
271/// when none could be. A debugger write is not equivalent: the ptrace
272/// backend writes exactly eight bytes with `PTRACE_POKEDATA`, which ignores
273/// `PROT_READ` and `PROT_NONE`.
274fn copy_procfs_output<M: MemoryAccess>(
275    memory: &mut M,
276    destination: Option<AddrMut<'_, u8>>,
277    bytes: &[u8],
278) -> Result<usize, Error> {
279    if bytes.is_empty() {
280        return Ok(0);
281    }
282    let destination = destination.ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
283    let mut copied = 0;
284    while copied < bytes.len() {
285        let Some(address) = destination
286            .as_raw()
287            .checked_add(copied)
288            .and_then(AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw)
289        else {
290            break;
291        };
292        match memory.write_with_user_access(address, &bytes[copied..]) {
293            Ok(0) | Err(Errno::EFAULT) => break,
294            Ok(n) => copied += n,
295            // Any other failure is the backend's, not a guest fault: report it
296            // as a tool error and commit nothing.
297            Err(errno) => {
298                return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
299                    "procfs read publication failed after {copied} bytes: {errno}"
300                )));
301            }
302        }
303    }
304    if copied == 0 {
305        Err(Errno::EFAULT.into())
306    } else {
307        Ok(copied)
308    }
309}

311/// Whether a descriptor with status flags `status` can read: not `O_PATH`,
312/// and opened for reading (`O_RDONLY` or `O_RDWR`; not `O_WRONLY`, nor access
313/// mode 3, which grants neither).
314fn can_read(status: i32) -> bool {
315    status & libc::O_PATH == 0 && matches!(status & libc::O_ACCMODE, libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_RDWR)
316}
317
318/// Copy the bytes of a read of a procfs file as its read handler does: a
319/// `seq_file` copies up to the first byte it cannot write, and a sysctl
320/// (`faults_on_a_short_copy`) copies all of them or fails with `EFAULT`, so
321/// that the caller commits nothing.
322fn copy_procfs_read<M: MemoryAccess>(
323    memory: &mut M,
324    destination: Option<AddrMut<'_, u8>>,
325    bytes: &[u8],
326    faults_on_a_short_copy: bool,
327) -> Result<usize, Error> {
328    let copied = copy_procfs_output(memory, destination, bytes)?;
329    if faults_on_a_short_copy && copied < bytes.len() {
330        return Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
331    }
332    Ok(copied)
333}

335/// The `RWF_*` flags of a vectored read of a procfs file Detcore renders, as
336/// `kiocb_set_rw_flags` checks them for a file with `read_iter` and without
337/// `FMODE_NOWAIT` or `FOP_DONTCACHE`: an unknown flag, then `RWF_APPEND` with
338/// `RWF_NOAPPEND` (`EINVAL`), then `RWF_NOWAIT`, `RWF_ATOMIC` (a read) and
339/// `RWF_DONTCACHE` (`EOPNOTSUPP`). Measured on Linux 7.1 for `/proc/version`
340/// and the sysctls, which also accept `RWF_NOSIGNAL`. A file without
341/// `read_iter` (`/proc/modules`, `/proc/swaps`) is read by
342/// `do_loop_readv_writev`, which refuses every flag but `RWF_HIPRI`.
343fn validate_procfs_vector_flags(flags: i32, read_iter: bool) -> Result<(), Errno> {
344    if !read_iter {
345        return if flags & !libc::RWF_HIPRI != 0 {
346            Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP)
347        } else {
348            Ok(())
349        };
350    }
351    // Linux 7.1's RWF_NOSIGNAL is newer than the pinned libc crate.
352    const RWF_NOSIGNAL: i32 = 0x100;
353    const KNOWN: i32 = libc::RWF_HIPRI
354        | libc::RWF_DSYNC
355        | libc::RWF_SYNC
356        | libc::RWF_NOWAIT
357        | libc::RWF_APPEND
358        | libc::RWF_NOAPPEND
359        | libc::RWF_ATOMIC
360        | libc::RWF_DONTCACHE
361        | RWF_NOSIGNAL;
362    if flags & !KNOWN != 0 {
363        return Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP);
364    }
365    if flags & libc::RWF_APPEND != 0 && flags & libc::RWF_NOAPPEND != 0 {
366        return Err(Errno::EINVAL);
367    }
368    if flags & (libc::RWF_NOWAIT | libc::RWF_ATOMIC | libc::RWF_DONTCACHE) != 0 {
369        return Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP);
370    }
371    Ok(())
372}

374/// Check the caller's whole requested range as `vfs_read`'s `access_ok` does
375/// before the file is read, so an address range beyond the user address limit
376/// is `EFAULT` even at EOF, when nothing would be copied. A procfs snapshot read
377/// never hands that range to the kernel.
378///
379/// `limit` is asked for the guest's user address limit only when the answer
380/// can matter, so a count that no limit admits is `EFAULT` before any query
381/// can fail.
382fn validate_procfs_destination(
383    limit: impl FnOnce() -> Result<crate::iovecs::UserAddressLimit, Error>,
384    destination: Option<AddrMut<'_, u8>>,
385    len: usize,
386) -> Result<(), Error> {
387    // No count past isize::MAX fits below a user address limit, so `read`'s
388    // `access_ok` refuses it, whatever the limit.
389    if isize::try_from(len).is_err() {
390        return Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
391    }
392    // Two descriptors keep the range uncapped, as `access_ok` sees it; a
393    // single one may be capped at MAX_RW_COUNT first (`import_ubuf`).
394    limit()?.validate(&[
395        crate::iovecs::ImportedIovec {
396            base: destination.map_or(0, |address| address.as_raw()),
397            len,
398        },
399        crate::iovecs::ImportedIovec { base: 0, len: 0 },
400    ])
401}

403/// Save the bytes at `scratch` into `original` if the guest's own protections
404/// let the capture read land there: the range is readable, and writing the
405/// same bytes back through the guest's protections copies all of them.
406fn save_procfs_scratch<M: MemoryAccess>(
407    memory: &mut M,
408    scratch: AddrMut<'_, u8>,
409    original: &mut [u8],
410) -> bool {
411    read_guest_exact(memory, scratch, original).is_ok()
412        && memory
413            .write_with_user_access(scratch, original)
414            .is_ok_and(|written| written == original.len())
415}
416
417/// Read exactly `buf.len()` bytes at `addr`, in one `read_vectored` of that
418/// length, or fail `EFAULT` if not all of them can be read. `read` and
419/// `read_exact` may widen a short read (ptrace turns up to eight bytes into one
420/// eight-byte `PTRACE_PEEKDATA`), which fails when a valid extent ends less
421/// than eight bytes before an unmapped page.
422pub(crate) fn read_guest_exact<M: MemoryAccess>(
423    memory: &M,
424    addr: AddrMut<'_, u8>,
425    buf: &mut [u8],
426) -> Result<(), Errno> {
427    let len = buf.len();
428    let remote = unsafe { AddrSlice::from_raw_parts(addr.into(), len) };
429    let remote = [unsafe { remote.as_ioslice() }];
430    let mut local = [std::io::IoSliceMut::new(buf)];
431    match memory.read_vectored(&remote, &mut local) {
432        Ok(copied) if copied == len => Ok(()),
433        Ok(_) => Err(Errno::EFAULT),
434        Err(errno) => Err(errno),
435    }
436}

438/// Capacity used for pipes that Detcore makes physically nonblocking: two of
439/// the host's pages.
440///
441/// Linux normally creates 16-page pipes (64 KiB on 4 KiB pages), but silently falls back to two
442/// pages once the creating UID crosses `pipe-user-pages-soft`. That host-global accounting can
443/// change between the two executions of `hermit run --verify`, changing whether the same write
444/// succeeds immediately or enters the scheduler's `InternalIOPolling` retry path. Two pages is the
445/// pressure-mode capacity (`PIPE_MIN_DEF_BUFFERS`, fs/pipe.c) and, unlike 16, never requires an
446/// unprivileged capacity increase while the soft limit is active.
447///
448/// It is counted in pages because Linux sizes every pipe in whole pages: `F_SETPIPE_SZ` rounds a
449/// request up to a power-of-two number of them (`round_pipe_size`). Two pages is 8 KiB on 4 KiB
450/// pages (every x86-64 host) and 128 KiB on a 64 KiB-page aarch64 kernel. A fixed 8 KiB pin could
451/// not be applied there: Linux gives the pipe one 64 KiB page, and the creation pin, which accepts
452/// only exactly the capacity it asked for, ends the run (`pipe_capacity_failure`).
453///
454/// Two pages is attainable and independent of host load on Linux 5.14 and later (whose quota
455/// fallback is two pages, not one) when `pipe-max-size` is at least two pages (the default is
456/// 1 MiB). A host that hardens it to one 64 KiB page gives a new pipe one page, or two under the
457/// quota, so there every pipe creation and capacity read is refused (`host_pipe_floor`).
458///
459/// This is also the ceiling the guest is allowed to raise a pipe to, and the
460/// value `/proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size` reports. Those three must be ONE value:
461/// a pinned capacity, an advertised maximum and an enforced maximum that can
462/// drift apart are three copies of one rule, and a duplicated rule drifts in
463/// N-1 places while each copy looks right on its own.
464pub(crate) fn deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes() -> i32 {
465    static CAPACITY: std::sync::OnceLock<i32> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
466    *CAPACITY.get_or_init(|| {
467        // SAFETY: sysconf has no preconditions.
468        let page = unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) };
469        i32::try_from(page)
470            .ok()
471            .filter(|page| *page > 0)
472            .and_then(|page| page.checked_mul(2))
473            .expect("the host's page size is a small positive number")
474    })
475}
476
477/// Whether a guest's `F_SETPIPE_SZ` request must be refused as a growth past
478/// the deterministic ceiling.
479///
480/// Separated from the handler so the BOUNDARY is testable without a guest. The
481/// boundary is the whole content of this rule: a request for exactly the pinned
482/// capacity must be allowed, or hermit's own pin value becomes unreachable to a
483/// guest that reads `/proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size` and asks for precisely what it
484/// was told.
485pub(crate) fn pipe_capacity_request_exceeds_ceiling(requested: i32) -> bool {
486    requested > deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()
487}
488
489/// The capacity a guest's `F_GETPIPE_SZ` reports for a pipe or FIFO whose
490/// host capacity is `host`: never more than the deterministic ceiling.
491///
492/// A pipe Hermit did not create (an inherited stdout, a FIFO whose other end
493/// is on the host) keeps the capacity the host gave it: 16 pages (64 KiB)
494/// normally, but two pages (8192 on 4 KiB pages) once the user crosses
495/// `pipe-user-pages-soft`, which host load decides. Passed through, that made the same guest read 65536 in one
496/// run of `--verify` and 8192 in the other (`/bin/cat` on DBT, the validate of
497/// hermit 2cd56771). A pipe can never hold more than the ceiling a guest can
498/// raise it to, so above it the ceiling is reported, as `pipe-max-size` is. A
499/// capacity at or below it is the one a pipe Hermit created was pinned to, or
500/// one the guest set itself, and is reported as it is. Host load cannot make
501/// a pipe smaller than the ceiling on Linux 5.14 and later: the quota fallback
502/// is exactly two pages, and past the hard limit Linux refuses the pipe
503/// instead. So an inherited pipe below it is one its creator sized on purpose,
504/// the same in every run. Before 5.14 the fallback was one page; the creation
505/// pin already needs 5.14 there, since under the same quota its growth of a
506/// one-page pipe to the ceiling is refused and the run stops
507/// (`pipe_capacity_failure`).
508///
509/// Only the reported value is made deterministic. A write to a pipe drained on
510/// the host still completes as far as its real capacity and that reader allow.
511pub(crate) fn reported_pipe_capacity(host: i64) -> i64 {
512    host.min(i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()))
513}
514
515/// Whether two pages is the capacity no host load can change on this host:
516/// whether its `pipe-max-size` is at least two pages, decided once per process.
517/// Linux caps a new unprivileged pipe at `pipe-max-size` and, under
518/// `pipe-user-pages-soft`, gives it two pages instead (fs/pipe.c
519/// `alloc_pipe_info`). With a `pipe-max-size` below two pages, host load
520/// therefore decides between one page and two, whatever capacity a given pipe
521/// shows, so the answer rests on the setting alone, never on a guest pipe's
522/// observed capacity. Where Detcore cannot read the setting, a pipe of its own
523/// can still prove it (`probe_two_page_pipe_max_size`).
524fn host_pipe_floor() -> bool {
525    static FLOOR: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
526    *FLOOR.get_or_init(|| {
527        host_pipe_floor_is_two_pages(host_pipe_max_size(), probe_two_page_pipe_max_size)
528    })
529}
530
531/// [`host_pipe_floor`] given the host's `pipe-max-size` (`None` when
532/// unreadable), with `probe` deciding only when it is unreadable.
533pub(crate) fn host_pipe_floor_is_two_pages(
534    host_pipe_max_size: Option<i64>,
535    probe: impl FnOnce() -> bool,
536) -> bool {
537    match host_pipe_max_size {
538        Some(max) => max >= i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()),
539        None => probe(),
540    }
541}
542
543/// Whether a pipe of this process's own proves `pipe-max-size` at least two
544/// pages. For a caller without `CAP_SYS_RESOURCE`, Linux creates a pipe no
545/// larger than `pipe-max-size` (`alloc_pipe_info`) and refuses growth past it
546/// with `EPERM` (`pipe_set_size`, fs/pipe.c v6.9 :1356-1358): a new pipe of
547/// more than two pages, or a one-page pipe grown to two, proves it. A caller
548/// with `CAP_SYS_RESOURCE` passes that limit, so its probe proves nothing.
549/// Under `pipe-user-pages-soft` growth is refused too, so a probe can fail
550/// where the setting allows two pages; it then refuses, the safe side.
551fn probe_two_page_pipe_max_size() -> bool {
552    if holds_cap_sys_resource() {
553        return false;
554    }
555    let mut fds = [-1; 2];
556    // SAFETY: `fds` has room for both descriptors.
557    if unsafe { libc::pipe2(fds.as_mut_ptr(), libc::O_CLOEXEC) } != 0 {
558        return false;
559    }
560    let ceiling = deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes();
561    let page = ceiling / 2;
562    // SAFETY: F_GETPIPE_SZ and F_SETPIPE_SZ only read and resize the pipe.
563    let proved = unsafe {
564        libc::fcntl(fds[0], libc::F_GETPIPE_SZ) > ceiling
565            || (libc::fcntl(fds[0], libc::F_SETPIPE_SZ, page) == page
566                && libc::fcntl(fds[0], libc::F_SETPIPE_SZ, ceiling) == ceiling)
567    };
568    // SAFETY: both descriptors were opened above and nothing else owns them.
569    unsafe {
570        libc::close(fds[0]);
571        libc::close(fds[1]);
572    }
573    proved
574}
575
576/// Whether this process may have `CAP_SYS_RESOURCE` in its effective set,
577/// read with `capget`, which needs no `/proc`. A set that cannot be read may
578/// hold it.
579fn holds_cap_sys_resource() -> bool {
580    #[repr(C)]
581    struct Header {
582        version: u32,
583        pid: i32,
584    }
585    #[repr(C)]
586    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
587    struct Data {
588        effective: u32,
589        permitted: u32,
590        inheritable: u32,
591    }
592    const LINUX_CAPABILITY_VERSION_3: u32 = 0x2008_0522;
593    const CAP_SYS_RESOURCE: u32 = 24;
594    let mut header = Header {
595        version: LINUX_CAPABILITY_VERSION_3,
596        pid: 0,
597    };
598    let mut data = [Data::default(); 2];
599    // SAFETY: capget writes only the header and the two data structs given.
600    let result = unsafe {
601        libc::syscall(
602            libc::SYS_capget,
603            &mut header as *mut Header,
604            data.as_mut_ptr(),
605        )
606    };
607    result != 0 || data[0].effective & (1 << CAP_SYS_RESOURCE) != 0
608}

610/// Ends the run because this host's `pipe-max-size` is below two pages, or
611/// cannot be shown to be at least two ([`host_pipe_floor`]), for `what`.
612fn below_two_page_pipe_floor(what: &str) -> String {
613    format!(
614        "[detcore] {what}: this host's pipe-max-size ({:?}; None when unreadable and not proved \
615         by a probe) is below two pages ({} bytes), so host load decides whether a pipe has one \
616         page or two. Determinism is unavailable for this run.",
617        host_pipe_max_size(),
618        deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes(),
619    )
620}

622/// The host's `/proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size`, read once.
623fn host_pipe_max_size() -> Option<i64> {
624    static MAX: std::sync::OnceLock<Option<i64>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
625    *MAX.get_or_init(|| {
626        std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size")
627            .ok()?
628            .trim()
629            .parse()

634/// SIGIO and SIGURG, the signals Linux sends to a descriptor's owner when
635/// data, out-of-band data, a lease break, or a directory change arrives.
636fn async_io_signals() -> u64 {
637    kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGIO) | kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGURG)
638}
639
640/// The signals an `fcntl` command lets Linux send at a moment set by host
641/// timing, as a kernel sigset; 0 for every other command. `F_SETOWN` and
642/// `F_SETOWN_EX` name the owner, `F_SETLEASE` and `F_NOTIFY` make the caller
643/// the owner, `O_ASYNC` enables SIGIO, and `F_SETSIG` replaces SIGIO with
644/// another signal.
645fn fcntl_host_timed_signals(cmd: syscalls::FcntlCmd<'_>) -> u64 {
646    match cmd {
647        F_SETFL(flags) if flags & libc::O_ASYNC != 0 => async_io_signals(),
648        F_SETOWN | F_SETOWN_EX(_) | F_SETLEASE(_) | F_NOTIFY(_) => async_io_signals(),
649        F_SETSIG(signal) => async_io_signals() | kernel_sigset_bit(signal),
650        _ => 0,
651    }
652}
653
654/// The signals an `ioctl` request lets Linux send at a moment set by host
655/// timing, as a kernel sigset; 0 for every other request. `FIOASYNC` enables
656/// SIGIO, and `FIOSETOWN` and `SIOCSPGRP` name the owner. `TIOCSCTTY` makes
657/// the terminal the caller's controlling terminal, `TIOCGPTPEER` without
658/// `O_NOCTTY` opens a pseudoterminal's other end as `open` does and so can
659/// make it one (`open_can_acquire_controlling_terminal`), and `TIOCSPGRP`
660/// names the terminal's foreground process group, so the terminal can then
661/// signal the session and that group (`terminal_signals`). `TIOCNOTTY` and
662/// `TIOCSWINSZ` are not among them: the signals they send, they send inside
663/// the caller's call, in the caller's turn.
664fn ioctl_host_timed_signals(request: syscalls::ioctl::Request<'_>) -> u64 {
665    match request {
666        syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIOASYNC(_)
667        | syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIOSETOWN(_)
668        | syscalls::ioctl::Request::SIOCSPGRP(_) => async_io_signals(),
669        syscalls::ioctl::Request::TIOCSCTTY(_) | syscalls::ioctl::Request::TIOCSPGRP(_) => {
670            terminal_signals()
671        }
672        syscalls::ioctl::Request::TIOCGPTPEER(flags)
673            if open_can_acquire_controlling_terminal(OFlag::from_bits_truncate(flags)) =>
674        {
675            terminal_signals()
676        }
677        _ => 0,
678    }
679}
680
681/// Whether an `open` with these flags can make the terminal it opens the
682/// caller's controlling terminal. Linux's `tty_open` does that for a session
683/// leader that has none, unless `O_NOCTTY` is given; an `O_PATH` open never
684/// reaches `tty_open`.
685fn open_can_acquire_controlling_terminal(flags: OFlag) -> bool {
686    !flags.intersects(OFlag::O_NOCTTY | OFlag::O_PATH)
687}
688
689/// Whether the character device `rdev` is a terminal that an `open` can make
690/// its caller's controlling terminal. `tty_drivers` is the text of
691/// `/proc/tty/drivers`, one line per range of device numbers a terminal
692/// driver serves, ending in the major number, the minor number or range, and
693/// the driver's type. A device no line names is not a terminal. Linux's
694/// `tty_open` never makes `/dev/console` (5:1), `/dev/vc/0` (4:0) or a
695/// pseudoterminal master controlling, and `/dev/ptmx` (5:2) opens a master
696/// without reaching `tty_open`. `/dev/tty` (5:0) stays in: it reopens the
697/// caller's controlling terminal, and if a hangup clears that terminal during
698/// the `open`, the `open` can make it controlling again. A table that could
699/// not be read (`None`), or a line that does not parse when no other line
700/// names the device, answers true.
701fn terminal_can_become_controlling(rdev: libc::dev_t, tty_drivers: Option<&str>) -> bool {
702    let (major, minor) = (libc::major(rdev), libc::minor(rdev));
703    if matches!((major, minor), (5, 1) | (5, 2) | (4, 0)) {
704        return false;
705    }
706    let Some(table) = tty_drivers else {
707        return true;
708    };
709    let mut unparsed = false;
710    for line in table.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty()) {
711        let fields: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
712        let range = match fields[..] {
713            [.., line_major, minors, kind] => {
714                line_major.parse::<u32>().ok().and_then(|line_major| {
715                    let (first, last) = minors.split_once('-').unwrap_or((minors, minors));
716                    Some((
717                        line_major,
718                        first.parse::<u32>().ok()?,
719                        last.parse::<u32>().ok()?,
720                        kind,
721                    ))
722                })
723            }
724            _ => None,
725        };
726        match range {
727            Some((line_major, first, last, kind))
728                if line_major == major && (first..=last).contains(&minor) =>
729            {
730                return kind != "pty:master";
731            }
732            Some(_) => {}
733            None => unparsed = true,
734        }
735    }
736    unparsed
737}
738
739/// Whether an `open` in process `pid`, whose `/proc/<pid>/stat` lists
740/// `session`, of the character device `rdev` may have made that device
741/// `pid`'s controlling terminal: `pid` leads its session and the device is a
742/// terminal that can become controlling (`terminal_can_become_controlling`).
743/// Neither fact is the controlling terminal procfs lists, which a hangup of
744/// the terminal clears at any moment, so the answer does not depend on
745/// whether a hangup came before or after the read. A session leader that
746/// reopens the terminal it already controls, or opens a terminal while it
747/// controls another, also answers true.
748fn may_have_acquired_controlling_terminal(
749    pid: i32,
750    session: i32,
751    rdev: libc::dev_t,
752    tty_drivers: Option<&str>,
753) -> bool {
754    session == pid && terminal_can_become_controlling(rdev, tty_drivers)
755}
756
757/// Whether the `open` in process `pid` that returned `fd` may have made the
758/// opened terminal `pid`'s controlling terminal
759/// (`may_have_acquired_controlling_terminal`). `host_stat` is the
760/// descriptor's stat when the caller already read it. Every host read that
761/// fails answers true: a needless record only holds the terminal's signals
762/// (`terminal_signals`) to the end of the gated waits that follow, while a
763/// missed one lets the terminal interrupt one at a turn the host chose.
764fn opened_controlling_terminal(pid: i32, fd: RawFd, host_stat: Option<&libc::stat>) -> bool {
765    let rdev = match host_stat {
766        Some(stat) if stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFCHR => stat.st_rdev,
767        Some(_) => return false,
768        None => match std::fs::metadata(format!("/proc/{pid}/fd/{fd}")) {
769            Ok(metadata) if metadata.file_type().is_char_device() => metadata.rdev(),
770            Ok(_) => return false,
771            Err(_) => return true,
772        },
773    };
774    let session = match procfs::process::Process::new(pid).and_then(|process| process.stat()) {
775        Ok(stat) => stat.session,
776        Err(_) => return true,
777    };
778    let tty_drivers = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/tty/drivers").ok();
779    may_have_acquired_controlling_terminal(pid, session, rdev, tty_drivers.as_deref())
780}

782/// Why the pin failed, and which descriptors Linux had already created when it did.
783///
784/// `pipe2` has already SUCCEEDED by the time the capacity is pinned, so the two descriptors
785/// exist in the guest whatever happens next. Carrying them alongside the errno is what makes
786/// releasing them possible; classifying separately from acting on it is what makes the
787/// classification unit-testable without a guest.
788#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
789struct PipeCapacityFailure {
790    created_fds: [i32; 2],
791    error: Errno,
792}
793
794impl PipeCapacityFailure {
795    fn close_syscalls(&self) -> [syscalls::Close; 2] {
796        self.created_fds
797            .map(|fd| syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd))
798    }
799}
800
801/// Classify the result of pinning a pipe's capacity.
802///
803/// The ONLY success shape is Linux returning exactly the requested capacity. `F_SETPIPE_SZ`
804/// returns the capacity it actually applied, and it may round; a rounded value is a pipe whose
805/// size we did not choose, which is the host-dependent capacity this path exists to remove. It
806/// is not a kernel errno, so it is reported as `EIO` rather than dressed up as one.
807fn pipe_capacity_failure(
808    created_fds: [i32; 2],
809    capacity_result: Result<i64, Errno>,
810) -> Option<PipeCapacityFailure> {
811    let error = match capacity_result {
812        Ok(applied) if applied == i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()) => return None,
813        Ok(_) => Errno::EIO,
814        Err(error) => error,
815    };
816    Some(PipeCapacityFailure { created_fds, error })
817}

819fn random_device_lseek_result(status_flags: i32, whence: Whence) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
820    if status_flags & OFlag::O_PATH.bits() != 0 {
821        return Err(Errno::EBADF);
822    }
823    match whence {
824        Whence::SEEK_SET
825        | Whence::SEEK_CUR
826        | Whence::SEEK_END
827        | Whence::SEEK_DATA
828        | Whence::SEEK_HOLE => Ok(0),
829        _ => Err(Errno::EINVAL),
830    }
831}
832
833/// How a procfs file Detcore renders seeks (`Detcore::handle_lseek`), by its
834/// file operations' `llseek`.
835#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
836enum RenderedSeek {
837    /// `seq_lseek`: only from the start or the position.
838    SeqFile,
839    /// `generic_file_llseek` (a process's `auxv` and `cmdline`).
840    Generic,
841    /// `default_llseek` (a sysctl file).
842    Default,
843}
844
845/// The position a seek of a rendered procfs file, every one of which has
846/// size 0, moves to from `current`: Linux's answer for its `llseek` (`seek`).
847///
848/// `generic_file_llseek` (fs/read_write.c, v6.17) compares a `SEEK_DATA` or
849/// `SEEK_HOLE` offset with the size as an unsigned number (`must_set_pos`,
850/// read_write.c:120 and 129), so every offset, a negative one included, is
851/// at or past the end: ENXIO. Its `vfs_setpos` refuses a negative position or
852/// one past the superblock's `s_maxbytes` (EINVAL): procfs keeps
853/// `alloc_super`'s MAX_NON_LFS, 2^31 - 1. `default_llseek` (read_write.c:
854/// 349-370) compares signed and has no `s_maxbytes` bound: an offset at or
855/// past the size 0 is ENXIO; a negative `SEEK_DATA` offset stays and reaches
856/// its EINVAL for a negative position; a negative `SEEK_HOLE` offset is
857/// replaced by the size, so the seek moves to 0. `seq_lseek` refuses every
858/// whence but `SEEK_SET` and `SEEK_CUR` with EINVAL.
859/// `rw_verify_area`'s range check for a read of a procfs file that has no
860/// unsigned offsets (fs/read_write.c:456-470 in 6.17): a count above
861/// `SSIZE_MAX`, or a position plus count past `LLONG_MAX`, is EINVAL.
862fn verify_procfs_read_range(position: usize, count: usize) -> Result<(), Errno> {
863    let count = i64::try_from(count).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
864    i64::try_from(position)
865        .ok()
866        .and_then(|position| position.checked_add(count))
867        .map(drop)
868        .ok_or(Errno::EINVAL)
869}
870
871fn rendered_procfs_seek(
872    seek: RenderedSeek,
873    whence: Whence,
874    offset: i64,
875    current: usize,
876) -> Result<usize, Errno> {
877    const MAX_NON_LFS: usize = (1 << 31) - 1;
878    let requested = i128::from(offset);
879    let new_offset = match whence {
880        Whence::SEEK_SET => requested,
881        Whence::SEEK_CUR => current as i128 + requested,
882        _ if seek == RenderedSeek::SeqFile => return Err(Errno::EINVAL),
883        Whence::SEEK_END => requested,
884        // At or past the end, which is 0.
885        Whence::SEEK_DATA | Whence::SEEK_HOLE
886            if requested >= 0 || seek == RenderedSeek::Generic =>
887        {
888            return Err(Errno::ENXIO);
889        }
890        // default_llseek: the hole at the end, the size.
891        Whence::SEEK_HOLE => 0,
892        Whence::SEEK_DATA => requested,
893        _ => return Err(Errno::EINVAL),
894    };
895    let new_offset = usize::try_from(new_offset).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
896    if seek == RenderedSeek::Generic && new_offset > MAX_NON_LFS {
897        return Err(Errno::EINVAL);
898    }
899    Ok(new_offset)
900}

902/// Why a stat Detcore takes for its own bookkeeping failed.
903#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
904enum StatFailure {
905    /// The stat call failed: the kernel's answer, or under record and replay
906    /// the recorded one.
907    Call(Errno),
908    /// Its buffer could not be prepared (the stack scratch faulted, or the
909    /// transient page could not be mapped), and then nothing was recorded; or,
910    /// after a successful stat, the guest's borrowed stack bytes could not be
911    /// written back.
912    Scratch(Errno),
913}
914
915impl StatFailure {
916    fn errno(self) -> Errno {
917        match self {
918            Self::Call(errno) | Self::Scratch(errno) => errno,
919        }
920    }
921}

923fn require_random_device_read_access(status_flags: i32) -> Result<(), Errno> {
924    if status_flags & libc::O_PATH != 0
925        || !matches!(
926            status_flags & libc::O_ACCMODE,
927            libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_RDWR
928        )
929    {
930        Err(Errno::EBADF)
931    } else {
932        Ok(())
933    }
934}

936/// Inherited container output is a stream even when an outer runner stores it
937/// in a seekable file.  The backing file also carries Hermit's own diagnostics,
938/// so exposing its live offset makes tool logging guest-visible.  Preserve real
939/// file semantics after a guest replaces stdout/stderr: `dup2(file, 1)` copies
940/// the file's resource rather than this container-output resource.
941fn is_inherited_container_output(resource: Option<ResourceID>) -> bool {
942    matches!(
943        resource,
944        Some(ResourceID::Device(
945            Device::ContainerStdout | Device::ContainerStderr
946        ))
947    )

950/// The one-time notice for a guest's bind of the abstract `AF_UNIX` name
951/// `name` (without its leading NUL) in a `--network=host` run
952/// ([`Config::notice_host_network_abstract_binds`]): `in_use` when the bind
953/// failed with `EADDRINUSE`.
954fn host_network_abstract_bind_notice(name: &[u8], in_use: bool) -> String {
955    let what = if in_use {
956        "the guest's bind of the abstract unix socket"
957    } else {
958        "the guest bound the abstract unix socket"
959    };
960    let outcome = if in_use {
961        " failed with EADDRINUSE: another program on the host, possibly a concurrent Hermit run, \
962         holds that name"
963    } else {
964        ""
965    };
966    format!(
967        "hermit: NOTICE: {what} \"@{name}\" under --network=host{outcome}. Abstract names \
968         belong to the network namespace, here the host's, and every Hermit run reuses the same \
969         pids and autobind names, so concurrent runs that bind the same name collide with \
970         EADDRINUSE. --network=local (the default) gives each run its own names. (Shown once \
971         per run.)",
972        name = name.escape_ascii()
973    )
974}
975
976/// Print [`host_network_abstract_bind_notice`] for a bind of `name` that
977/// returned `result`, on Hermit's own standard error, the first time this
978/// process sees one that succeeded or failed with `EADDRINUSE`. Any other
979/// failure is the guest's own mistake and prints nothing. Only set where
980/// Detcore runs in Hermit's process, so the guest never sees the line;
981/// Hermit's diagnostics share the container's output, whose offset the guest
982/// is never shown ([`is_inherited_container_output`]).
983fn notice_host_network_abstract_bind(name: &[u8], result: &Result<i64, Errno>) {
984    static NOTICED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
985    let in_use = match result {
986        Ok(_) => false,
987        Err(Errno::EADDRINUSE) => true,
988        Err(_) => return,
989    };
990    if !NOTICED.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
991        use std::io::Write as _;
992        let _ = writeln!(
993            crate::util::RetryingStderr,
994            "{}",
995            host_network_abstract_bind_notice(name, in_use)
996        );
997    }
998}

1000/// The name, without its leading NUL, of the abstract `AF_UNIX` address
1001/// `bytes` holds: the first `addrlen` bytes of a `sockaddr_un`. `None` for a
1002/// path name, a bare family (an autobind), or an address too short to hold a
1003/// name.
1004fn abstract_unix_name(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<&[u8]> {
1005    let path = std::mem::offset_of!(libc::sockaddr_un, sun_path);
1006    match bytes.get(path..)? {
1007        [0, name @ ..] => Some(name),
1008        _ => None,
1009    }
1010}
1011
1012fn unix_autobind_addrlen() -> i32 {
1013    (std::mem::offset_of!(libc::sockaddr_un, sun_path) + UNIX_AUTOBIND_NAME_LEN) as i32
1014}
1015
1016fn unix_autobind_address(port: u16) -> libc::sockaddr_un {
1017    // Linux autobind names are a leading NUL followed by five lowercase hex digits.
1018    let mut address: libc::sockaddr_un = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
1019    address.sun_family = libc::AF_UNIX as libc::sa_family_t;
1020    for (destination, source) in address.sun_path[1..UNIX_AUTOBIND_NAME_LEN]
1021        .iter_mut()
1022        .zip(format!("{port:05x}").bytes())
1023    {
1024        *destination = source as libc::c_char;
1025    }
1026    address
1027}

1029// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-904): Review the TCP_INFO compatibility boundary.
1030/// Retain the logical TCP state and negotiated option header while hiding all
1031/// host timing, rate, packet, and byte counters.
1032fn canonicalize_tcp_info(info: &mut [u8]) {
1033    for (offset, byte) in info.iter_mut().enumerate() {
1034        if !matches!(offset, 0 | 1 | 5 | 6) {
1035            *byte = 0;
1036        }
1037    }
1038}

1040// Hermit exposes exactly one isolated guest network namespace.
1041const DETERMINISTIC_NETNS_COOKIE: u64 = 1;
1042
1043// Above Linux's PID range and below the high-bit IDs used by kernel autobind.
1044const DETERMINISTIC_NETLINK_PORT_ID_BASE: u32 = 0x4000_0000;
1045
1046/// Does the new guest descriptor `fd` reopen an anonymous pipe that the same
1047/// process already holds as a scheduler-managed pipe (`managed_pipe_fds`)?
1048///
1049/// Both `/proc/<pid>/fd/<fd>` links read `pipe:[<inode>]` for the same pipe.
1050/// A named FIFO links to its path, and on ptrace a host pipe is never in
1051/// `managed_pipe_fds` (see `scheduler_managed_pipe_fds` for SaBRe), so neither
1052/// matches: a host writer is outside the scheduler and must not be polled as if
1053/// it were a guest
1054/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3534#issuecomment-5962369261>).
1055fn reopens_scheduler_managed_pipe(
1056    backend: &reverie::BackendCapabilities,
1057    pid: i32,
1058    fd: RawFd,
1059    managed_pipe_fds: &[RawFd],
1060) -> bool {
1061    // Under KVM `/proc/<pid>` is an unrelated host task, if any, and its
1062    // links say nothing about this guest's pipes.
1063    if !crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors(backend) {
1064        return false;
1065    }
1066    let link = |fd: RawFd| std::fs::read_link(format!("/proc/{pid}/fd/{fd}")).ok();
1067    let Some(opened) = link(fd) else {
1068        return false;
1069    };
1070    if !opened
1071        .to_str()
1072        .is_some_and(|name| name.starts_with("pipe:["))
1073    {
1074        return false;
1075    }
1076    managed_pipe_fds
1077        .iter()
1078        .any(|&held| held != fd && link(held).as_ref() == Some(&opened))
1079}
1080
1081/// The path the kernel resolved an open descriptor to, read from the guest's
1082/// own `/proc/<pid>/fd/<fd>` link. This is the evidence authority for "which
1083/// object was opened": it is produced by the kernel from the descriptor itself,
1084/// so it is independent of the pathname spelling the guest used.
1085///
1086/// Used ONLY as a fallback for a pathname that does not classify on its own
1087/// (see the call site): a spelling that already classifies must keep its own
1088/// classification, because `/proc/self/...` and `/proc/thread-self/...` are
1089/// defined by the spelling and resolve to a different numeric path.
1090///
1091/// `None` when the link cannot be read (the descriptor is gone, or procfs is
1092/// unavailable), in which case the lexical result stands unchanged. Also
1093/// `None` under KVM, where `/proc/<pid>` does not name the guest (see
1094/// [`crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors`]).
1095fn resolved_open_path(
1096    backend: &reverie::BackendCapabilities,
1097    pid: i32,
1098    fd: RawFd,
1099) -> Option<PathBuf> {
1100    if !crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors(backend) {
1101        return None;
1102    }
1103    let link = std::fs::read_link(format!("/proc/{pid}/fd/{fd}")).ok()?;
1104    // A deleted or anonymous target is not a stable object name.
1105    link.is_absolute().then_some(link)
1106}

1111pub(crate) enum SocketRole {
1112    /// `connect` connected it or `accept` returned it, so it has a peer.

1128/// The scope `pidfd_send_signal`'s flags select (Linux's `pidfd_send_signal`
1129/// since 6.9; <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4108>).
1130#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1131pub(crate) enum PidfdSignalScope {
1132    /// No flag, or `PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD_GROUP`: the process (Detcore's
1133    /// `pidfd_open` makes no thread pidfds).
1134    Process,
1135    /// `PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD`: the thread whose id is the pid.
1136    Thread,
1137    /// `PIDFD_SIGNAL_PROCESS_GROUP`: the process's process group.
1138    ProcessGroup,
1139}
1140
1141const PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD: u32 = 1 << 0;
1142const PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD_GROUP: u32 = 1 << 1;
1143const PIDFD_SIGNAL_PROCESS_GROUP: u32 = 1 << 2;
1144
1145/// `flags`' scope, or EINVAL as Linux answers: for a bit outside the three
1146/// scope flags, or for more than one of them.
1147pub(crate) fn pidfd_signal_scope(flags: u32) -> Result<PidfdSignalScope, Errno> {
1148    match flags {
1149        0 | PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD_GROUP => Ok(PidfdSignalScope::Process),
1150        PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD => Ok(PidfdSignalScope::Thread),
1151        PIDFD_SIGNAL_PROCESS_GROUP => Ok(PidfdSignalScope::ProcessGroup),
1152        _ => Err(Errno::EINVAL),
1153    }
1154}
1155
1156/// `pidfd_send_signal`'s sentinel for the calling thread (Linux 6.15 and later).
1157const PIDFD_SELF_THREAD: RawFd = -10000;
1158/// `pidfd_send_signal`'s sentinel for the calling thread's thread group.
1159const PIDFD_SELF_THREAD_GROUP: RawFd = -10001;
1160
1161/// The task a `PIDFD_SELF_*` sentinel names, and the scope Linux gives it when
1162/// no flag is set: the calling thread (thread-directed) or its thread group
1163/// (process-directed); `None` for any other descriptor
1164/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4147).
1165fn pidfd_self_target<T, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
1166    guest: &mut G,
1167    pidfd: RawFd,
1168) -> Option<(DetPid, PidfdSignalScope)>
1169where
1170    T: RecordOrReplay,
1171{
1172    let state = guest.thread_state();
1173    match pidfd {
1174        PIDFD_SELF_THREAD => Some((
1175            DetPid::from_raw(state.dettid.as_raw()),
1176            PidfdSignalScope::Thread,
1177        )),
1178        PIDFD_SELF_THREAD_GROUP => Some((state.detpid?, PidfdSignalScope::Process)),
1179        _ => None,
1180    }
1181}

1183/// What a descriptor that is not a modeled pidfd names for `pidfd_send_signal`.
1184#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1185pub(crate) enum ProcessDirectoryDescriptor {
1186    /// A `/proc/<pid>` directory of the guest's procfs: Linux takes it as the
1187    /// process `<pid>`.
1188    Process(DetPid),
1189    /// Any other file, which Linux answers EBADF.
1190    NotAProcess,
1191    /// Detcore cannot tell; the reason names why.
1192    Unknown(&'static str),
1193}
1194
1195/// Facts the tracer reads about a guest descriptor (`process_directory_descriptor`).
1196#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
1197pub(crate) struct DescriptorFacts {
1198    /// The descriptor's `/proc/<tid>/fd/<fd>` link, as the kernel spells it.
1199    pub(crate) link: PathBuf,
1200    /// Whether the file is on procfs.
1201    pub(crate) on_procfs: bool,
1202    /// Whether the file is a directory.
1203    pub(crate) is_dir: bool,
1204    /// The file's device, and its parent directory's device and inode.
1205    pub(crate) dev: u64,
1206    pub(crate) parent: Option<(u64, u64)>,
1207    /// The device of the procfs mounted at the guest's `/proc`.
1208    pub(crate) guest_proc_dev: Option<u64>,
1209}
1210
1211/// The inode of a procfs root directory (Linux's `PROC_ROOT_INO`).
1212const PROC_ROOT_INO: u64 = 1;
1213
1214/// Classify a descriptor from `facts` (`None`: unreadable). Linux's
1215/// `tgid_pidfd_to_pid` accepts exactly a procfs process directory, whose name
1216/// is its pid in the procfs instance's pid namespace and whose parent is the
1217/// procfs root. That instance must be the guest's own, at its `/proc`, so the
1218/// pid is a guest pid. A pidfd Detcore did not open cannot be classified.
1219pub(crate) fn classify_process_directory(
1220    facts: Option<&DescriptorFacts>,
1221) -> ProcessDirectoryDescriptor {
1222    use ProcessDirectoryDescriptor as D;
1223    let Some(facts) = facts else {
1224        return D::Unknown("Hermit cannot read what the descriptor names");
1225    };
1226    let link = facts.link.to_string_lossy();
1227    if link == "anon_inode:[pidfd]" || link.starts_with("pidfd:") {
1228        return D::Unknown("it is a pidfd that Detcore did not open with pidfd_open");
1229    }
1230    if !facts.on_procfs {
1231        return D::NotAProcess;
1232    }
1233    if !facts.is_dir {
1234        return D::NotAProcess;
1235    }
1236    let name = facts
1237        .link
1238        .file_name()
1239        .map(|name| name.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
1240        .unwrap_or_default();
1241    // A reaped task's directory is spelled with " (deleted)", and its ".."
1242    // cannot be read (ESRCH); Linux still takes it as the task, and answers
1243    // ESRCH for it. The spelling is then the only evidence, so it must be a
1244    // top-level entry of the guest's /proc.
1245    let name = match name.strip_suffix(" (deleted)") {
1246        Some(name) if facts.parent.is_none() => {
1247            if facts.link.parent() != Some(Path::new("/proc")) {
1248                return if facts.link.starts_with("/proc/") {
1249                    D::NotAProcess
1250                } else {
1251                    D::Unknown("it names a reaped task outside the guest's /proc")
1252                };
1253            }
1254            name.to_owned()
1255        }
1256        _ if facts.parent != Some((facts.dev, PROC_ROOT_INO)) => return D::NotAProcess,
1257        _ => name,
1258    };
1259    let Ok(pid) = name.parse::<i32>() else {
1260        return D::NotAProcess;
1261    };
1262    if pid <= 0 || name.starts_with(['+', '0']) {
1263        return D::NotAProcess;
1264    }
1265    if facts.guest_proc_dev != Some(facts.dev) {
1266        return D::Unknown("it is a procfs that is not the guest's /proc");
1267    }
1268    D::Process(DetPid::from_raw(pid))
1269}
1270
1271/// Read the facts for the guest descriptor `fd` of thread `tid` through
1272/// `/proc/<tid>/fd/<fd>` and classify it (`classify_process_directory`).
1273fn process_directory_descriptor(tid: i32, fd: RawFd) -> ProcessDirectoryDescriptor {
1274    let facts = (|| {
1275        let (link, on_procfs) = descriptor_identity(tid, fd)?;
1276        let target = std::fs::metadata(format!("/proc/{tid}/fd/{fd}")).ok()?;
1277        let parent = std::fs::metadata(format!("/proc/{tid}/fd/{fd}/.."))
1278            .ok()
1279            .map(|parent| (parent.dev(), parent.ino()));
1280        let guest_proc_dev = std::fs::metadata(format!("/proc/{tid}/root/proc"))
1281            .ok()
1282            .filter(|proc| proc.ino() == PROC_ROOT_INO)
1283            .map(|proc| proc.dev());
1284        Some(DescriptorFacts {
1285            link,
1286            on_procfs,
1287            is_dir: target.is_dir(),
1288            dev: target.dev(),
1289            parent: if target.is_dir() { parent } else { None },
1290            guest_proc_dev,
1291        })
1292    })();
1293    classify_process_directory(facts.as_ref())
1294}
1295
1296/// The host's default huge page size (`Hugepagesize` in /proc/meminfo), the
1297/// size of a MAP_HUGETLB mapping that names none, or 2 MiB, the x86_64
1298/// default, when it cannot be read (see [`may_change_untraced_code`]).
1299fn default_huge_page_size() -> u64 {
1300    static SIZE: std::sync::OnceLock<u64> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
1301    *SIZE.get_or_init(|| {
1302        std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/meminfo")
1303            .ok()
1304            .and_then(|meminfo| {
1305                let line = meminfo
1306                    .lines()
1307                    .find(|line| line.starts_with("Hugepagesize:"))?;
1308                let kib: u64 = line.split_whitespace().nth(1)?.parse().ok()?;
1309                kib.checked_mul(1024)
1310            })
1311            .unwrap_or(2 << 20)
1312    })
1313}
1314
1315/// What a guest descriptor is, read through the opening thread's
1316/// `/proc/<tid>/fd/<fd>`: its link as the kernel spells it, and whether the
1317/// file is on procfs (see [`may_write_process_memory`]). Read through the
1318/// thread because its descriptor table may not be its leader's (a thread
1319/// cloned without CLONE_FILES). `None` when either cannot be read.
1320fn descriptor_identity(tid: i32, fd: RawFd) -> Option<(PathBuf, bool)> {
1321    let path = format!("/proc/{tid}/fd/{fd}");
1322    let link = std::fs::read_link(&path).ok()?;
1323    let path = std::ffi::CString::new(path).ok()?;
1324    let mut buf = std::mem::MaybeUninit::<libc::statfs>::uninit();
1325    // SAFETY: `path` is NUL-terminated and `buf` is large enough for statfs.
1326    if unsafe { libc::statfs(path.as_ptr(), buf.as_mut_ptr()) } != 0 {
1327        return None;
1328    }
1329    // SAFETY: statfs succeeded, so it filled `buf`.
1330    let on_procfs = unsafe { buf.assume_init() }.f_type as u64
1331        == reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::PROC_SUPER_MAGIC as u64;
1332    Some((link, on_procfs))
1333}
1334
1335/// Resolve an `AT_FDCWD`-relative spelling in the guest's filesystem view.
1336///
1337/// Replayer chroots the guest, so the tracer-visible cwd includes the replay
1338/// root. Stripping `/proc/<pid>/root` produces the same guest-absolute path in
1339/// record and replay without depending on the opened descriptor (which is an
1340/// eventfd placeholder during replay).
1341///
1342/// A working directory whose path is longer than the kernel renders into its
1343/// link has none here (`ENAMETOOLONG`); for that case see
1344/// [`climbed_out_of_unrendered_cwd`].
1345pub(crate) fn resolved_at_fdcwd_path(pid: i32, path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
1346    debug_assert!(!path.is_absolute());
1347    let root = std::fs::read_link(format!("/proc/{pid}/root")).ok()?;
1348    let cwd = match std::fs::read_link(format!("/proc/{pid}/cwd")) {
1349        Ok(cwd) => cwd,
1350        Err(error) if error.raw_os_error() == Some(libc::ENAMETOOLONG) => {
1351            return climbed_out_of_unrendered_cwd(pid, &root, path);
1352        }
1353        Err(_) => return None,
1354    };
1355    let guest_cwd = cwd.strip_prefix(root).ok()?;
1356    Some(Path::new("/").join(guest_cwd).join(path))
1357}
1358
1359/// [`resolved_at_fdcwd_path`] where the kernel cannot render the working
1360/// directory of process `pid` into its link because its path is longer than
1361/// `PATH_MAX`, which Linux still walks `..` out of. A spelling whose leading
1362/// `..` climb out of it is made absolute from the directory they reach, which
1363/// the kernel's own walk names: an `O_PATH` open of `/proc/<pid>/cwd/..` (as
1364/// many `..` as the spelling leads with), whose descriptor's link is that
1365/// directory's path; the rest of the spelling follows byte for byte
1366/// ([`split_leading_climb`]). `None`, resolving nothing, for any other
1367/// spelling, and where the open or the link fails: the call's own walk then
1368/// decides the spelling, with its own error
1369/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4541>). Both reads are raw
1370/// syscalls ([`crate::util::RawFd`], [`crate::util::raw_read_link`]), as
1371/// Detcore may run inside the guest.
1372fn climbed_out_of_unrendered_cwd(pid: i32, root: &Path, path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
1373    let (climbs, rest) = split_leading_climb(path);
1374    if climbs == 0 {
1375        return None;
1376    }
1377    let climbed = crate::util::RawFd::open(
1378        Path::new(&format!("/proc/{pid}/cwd/{}", climb_spelling(climbs))),
1379        libc::O_PATH | libc::O_DIRECTORY,
1380    )
1381    .ok()?;
1382    let directory =
1383        crate::util::raw_read_link(Path::new(&format!("/proc/self/fd/{}", climbed.raw()))).ok()?;
1384    let guest_directory = directory.strip_prefix(root).ok()?;
1385    Some(joined_verbatim(&Path::new("/").join(guest_directory), rest))
1386}
1387
1388/// How many `..` the relative `path` climbs before its first other name,
1389/// past any `.`, and the rest of the spelling after them, byte for byte, so
1390/// that a trailing `/` or `/.` keeps its meaning for the walk of the rest:
1391/// `../../proc/fs` climbs 2, to `proc/fs`; `./..//proc/uptime/` climbs 1, to
1392/// `proc/uptime/`; `x/..` climbs none.
1393pub(crate) fn split_leading_climb(path: &Path) -> (usize, &std::ffi::OsStr) {
1394    use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
1395    let mut rest = path.as_os_str().as_bytes();
1396    let mut climbs = 0;
1397    while !rest.is_empty() {
1398        let end = rest
1399            .iter()
1400            .position(|&byte| byte == b'/')
1401            .unwrap_or(rest.len());
1402        match &rest[..end] {
1403            b".." => climbs += 1,
1404            b"." => {}
1405            _ => break,
1406        }
1407        let slashes = rest[end..].iter().take_while(|&&byte| byte == b'/').count();
1408        rest = &rest[end + slashes..];
1409    }
1410    (climbs, std::ffi::OsStr::from_bytes(rest))
1411}
1412
1413/// Whether `path` is `PATH_MAX` bytes long or more, which no name may be:
1414/// Linux copies at most `PATH_MAX` bytes of a pathname, its NUL included,
1415/// and refuses one whose NUL is not among them with `ENAMETOOLONG`, before
1416/// any walk (`getname_flags`, fs/namei.c:206-210 at v6.17). Such a spelling
1417/// is never resolved, so that the call's own lookup refuses it.
1418pub(crate) fn names_past_path_max(path: &Path) -> bool {
1419    path.as_os_str().len() >= libc::PATH_MAX as usize
1420}
1421
1422/// `rest`, a relative spelling, below `directory`, byte for byte;
1423/// `directory` itself where `rest` is empty.
1424fn joined_verbatim(directory: &Path, rest: &std::ffi::OsStr) -> PathBuf {
1425    if rest.is_empty() {
1426        directory.to_path_buf()
1427    } else {
1428        directory.join(rest)
1429    }
1430}
1431
1432/// `..` `climbs` times: `..`, `../..`, and so on.
1433fn climb_spelling(climbs: usize) -> String {
1434    vec![".."; climbs].join("/")
1435}
1436
1437/// The calling thread's working directory, read for the syscall it is
1438/// running where the tool cannot read it from host procfs
1439/// (`procfs_inode::tool_can_read_guest_cwd`: KVM), at most once per syscall
1440/// (`ThreadState::syscall_cwd`, `Detcore::prepare_guest_cwd`).
1441#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1442pub(crate) enum SyscallCwd {
1443    /// Its path, as the thread's `getcwd` answered it.
1444    Path(PathBuf),
1445    /// No path: `getcwd` failed with `ENOENT`, for a removed directory, or
1446    /// for one whose path is longer than `PATH_MAX` (`ENAMETOOLONG`,
1447    /// `ERANGE`), which Linux still walks `..` from. By how many `..` a
1448    /// spelling of the syscall climbs out of it, the path of the directory
1449    /// it climbs to, read through a descriptor for it
1450    /// (`Detcore::read_climbed_directory`), `None` where that failed.
1451    Unrendered(BTreeMap<usize, Option<PathBuf>>),
1452    /// No path otherwise (`getcwd` answered no path from the root, or failed
1453    /// another way): its spellings are decided as given.
1454    Unknown,
1455}
1456
1457/// The directory a listing of a descriptor reads, for
1458/// `Detcore::drop_absent_entries`. Where the tool's `/proc` entry for the
1459/// caller is the caller's (`tool_sees_caller`,
1460/// `procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors`): the kernel's path for
1461/// the descriptor (`linked`, its link in that entry), or, where that link
1462/// cannot be read (after a `chroot` into a root without `/proc`, where the
1463/// tool runs inside the guest), the path the guest opened it by (`recorded`).
1464/// Where the guest's threads are no host tasks (KVM), that entry names one of
1465/// the supervisor's own tasks, whose descriptor of that number is no guest's,
1466/// so its link is never read
1467/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4541>): the directory is the
1468/// recorded path, with its `.` and `..` folded in by name, as the kernel's
1469/// path has neither (`/sys/devices/system/cpu/.` is the directory the
1470/// listing filters). `None` where the path is not absolute.
1471fn listed_directory(
1472    tool_sees_caller: bool,
1473    linked: impl FnOnce() -> Option<PathBuf>,
1474    recorded: impl FnOnce() -> Option<PathBuf>,
1475) -> Option<PathBuf> {
1476    let directory = if tool_sees_caller {
1477        linked().or_else(recorded)
1478    } else {
1479        recorded().map(|path| {
1480            let mut folded = PathBuf::new();
1481            for component in path.components() {
1482                match component {
1483                    std::path::Component::ParentDir => {
1484                        folded.pop();
1485                    }
1486                    std::path::Component::CurDir => {}
1487                    other => folded.push(other),
1488                }
1489            }
1490            folded
1491        })
1492    };
1493    directory.filter(|path| path.is_absolute())
1494}
1495
1496#[cfg(test)]
1497mod leading_climb_tests {
1498    use super::*;
1499
1500    /// A spelling climbs out of the working directory by the `..` before its
1501    /// first other name, past any `.`; the rest is kept byte for byte, a
1502    /// trailing `/` or `/.` included, for the walk below where they lead
1503    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4541>).
1504    #[test]
1505    fn a_spelling_climbs_by_its_leading_dotdots() {
1506        let climb = |path: &'static str| {
1507            let (climbs, rest) = split_leading_climb(Path::new(path));
1508            (climbs, rest.to_str().unwrap().to_owned())
1509        };
1510        let split = |climbs: usize, rest: &str| (climbs, rest.to_owned());
1511        assert_eq!(climb("../../proc/fs"), split(2, "proc/fs"));
1512        assert_eq!(climb("./../x"), split(1, "x"));
1513        assert_eq!(climb("..//./..//proc/uptime/"), split(2, "proc/uptime/"));
1514        assert_eq!(climb("../proc/."), split(1, "proc/."));
1515        assert_eq!(climb(".."), split(1, ""));
1516        assert_eq!(climb("../"), split(1, ""));
1517        assert_eq!(climb("x/.."), split(0, "x/.."));
1518        assert_eq!(climb("...x/../y"), split(0, "...x/../y"));
1519        assert_eq!(climb("proc/fs"), split(0, "proc/fs"));
1520        assert_eq!(climb(""), split(0, ""));
1521        assert_eq!(
1522            joined_verbatim(Path::new("/"), std::ffi::OsStr::new("proc/uptime/")),
1523            PathBuf::from("/proc/uptime/")
1524        );
1525        assert_eq!(
1526            joined_verbatim(Path::new("/tmp"), std::ffi::OsStr::new("")),
1527            PathBuf::from("/tmp")
1528        );
1529        assert_eq!(climb_spelling(1), "..");
1530        assert_eq!(climb_spelling(3), "../../..");
1531    }
1532}
1533
1534#[cfg(test)]
1535mod listed_directory_tests {
1536    use super::*;
1537
1538    /// Where the tool's `/proc` entry for the caller is not the caller's
1539    /// (KVM), a listing's directory is the path the guest opened it by, its
1540    /// `.` and `..` folded in, and the descriptor link of the entry is never
1541    /// read; elsewhere the link is the directory, and the recorded path, as
1542    /// it is, the fallback (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4541>).
1543    #[test]
1544    fn a_listing_is_named_by_the_link_only_where_the_entry_is_the_callers() {
1545        // Compared byte for byte: `Path`'s own comparison ignores a `.`.
1546        let bytes = |path: Option<PathBuf>| path.map(PathBuf::into_os_string);
1547        let cpu = || Some(PathBuf::from("/sys/devices/system/cpu"));
1548        let unread = || -> Option<PathBuf> { panic!("the link of a host task was read") };
1549        for recorded in [
1550            "/sys/devices/system/cpu/.",
1551            "/sys/devices/system/cpu/",
1552            "/sys/devices/system/./cpu",
1553            "/sys/devices/system/cpu/../cpu",
1554        ] {
1555            assert_eq!(
1556                bytes(listed_directory(false, unread, || Some(PathBuf::from(
1557                    recorded
1558                )))),
1559                bytes(cpu()),
1560                "{recorded}"
1561            );
1562        }
1563        assert_eq!(
1564            listed_directory(false, unread, || Some(PathBuf::from("cpu"))),
1565            None
1566        );
1567        assert_eq!(
1568            bytes(listed_directory(true, cpu, || Some(PathBuf::from(
1569                "/tmp/x"
1570            )))),
1571            bytes(cpu())
1572        );
1573        // Where the link cannot be read, the recorded path as it is.
1574        assert_eq!(
1575            bytes(listed_directory(
1576                true,
1577                || None,
1578                || Some(PathBuf::from("/tmp/x/../y"))
1579            )),
1580            Some("/tmp/x/../y".into())
1581        );
1582    }
1583}
