1585/// A name `call` removes, as `(dirfd, path)`.
1586type RemovedName<'a> = (RawFd, Option<PathPtr<'a>>);
1587
1588/// The name `call` removes and, for a rename, its source, which replaces
1589/// nothing when it is the target's own file: the name an `unlink`,
1590/// `unlinkat` or (with `with_rmdir`) `rmdir` removes, or the target a
1591/// `rename`, `renameat` or `renameat2` replaces (not with
1592/// `RENAME_EXCHANGE`). `None` for every other call. What
1593/// [`Detcore::last_names_removed_by`] (with `rmdir`) and
1594/// [`Detcore::guest_made_fifos_removed_by`] (without) look up.
1595fn removed_names<'a>(
1596    call: &'a Syscall,
1597    #[cfg_attr(
1598        target_arch = "aarch64",
1599        allow(unused_variables, reason = "only x86_64 has rmdir")
1600    )]
1601    with_rmdir: bool,
1602) -> Option<(RemovedName<'a>, Option<RemovedName<'a>>)> {
1603    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
1604    let at = libc::AT_FDCWD;
1605    Some(match call {
1606        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
1607        Syscall::Unlink(c) => ((at, c.path()), None),
1608        Syscall::Unlinkat(c) => ((c.dirfd(), c.path()), None),
1609        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
1610        Syscall::Rmdir(c) if with_rmdir => ((at, c.path()), None),
1611        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
1612        Syscall::Rename(c) => ((at, c.newpath()), Some((at, c.oldpath()))),
1613        Syscall::Renameat(c) => (
1614            (c.newdirfd(), c.newpath()),
1615            Some((c.olddirfd(), c.oldpath())),
1616        ),
1617        Syscall::Renameat2(c) if c.flags() & libc::RENAME_EXCHANGE == 0 => (
1618            (c.newdirfd(), c.newpath()),
1619            Some((c.olddirfd(), c.oldpath())),
1620        ),
1621        _ => return None,
1622    })
1623}
1624
1625/// Whether a call numbered `sysno` may remove a name ([`removed_names`],
1626/// whatever its arguments): the syscalls [`Detcore::last_names_removed_by`]
1627/// and [`Detcore::guest_made_fifos_removed_by`] can act on. Part of
1628/// [`may_name_file_or_descriptor`]; `syscall_hot_path_tests` checks it
1629/// against [`removed_names`] for every syscall number.
1630pub(crate) fn removes_a_name(sysno: Sysno) -> bool {
1631    match sysno {
1632        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
1633        Sysno::unlink | Sysno::rmdir | Sysno::rename => true,
1634        Sysno::unlinkat | Sysno::renameat | Sysno::renameat2 => true,
1635        _ => false,
1636    }
1637}
1638
1639/// Whether a call numbered `sysno` can be acted on by any of the file and
1640/// descriptor checks `Detcore::handle_syscall_event` makes before it
1641/// dispatches the call: the names it removes ([`removes_a_name`]), the
1642/// rendered procfs descriptors it names
1643/// ([`rendered_procfs::names_a_descriptor`]), the `/proc` names it looks up
1644/// ([`procfs_levels::looks_up_names`]), and the rendered procfs calls
1645/// Detcore answers ([`rendered_procfs::may_answer_operation`],
1646/// [`rendered_procfs::may_answer_mapping`],
1647/// [`rendered_procfs::may_answer_path_call`]). Each check answers its
1648/// trivial value, with no effect, for any other call, so skipping them
1649/// for those calls changes nothing but the work. It reads the number only,
1650/// never the backend or the arguments.
1651pub(crate) fn may_name_file_or_descriptor(sysno: Sysno) -> bool {
1652    removes_a_name(sysno)
1653        || rendered_procfs::names_a_descriptor(sysno)
1654        || procfs_levels::looks_up_names(sysno)
1655        || rendered_procfs::may_answer_operation(sysno)
1656        || rendered_procfs::may_answer_mapping(sysno)
1657        || rendered_procfs::may_answer_path_call(sysno)
1658}
1659
1660/// Whether removing a name of the file `stat` describes leaves it with no
1661/// name: a directory has only one, and a non-directory with one link loses
1662/// its last. A host may then give its inode to another file
1663/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3840>).
1664fn retires_on_removal(stat: &libc::stat) -> bool {
1665    stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFDIR || stat.st_nlink == 1
1666}
1667
1668/// The path to report for one operand of a successful namespace change (see
1669/// `Detcore::record_host_namespace_change`): the operand made absolute, or
1670/// `/` when it could not be read or made absolute. A tracer that may not read
1671/// a non-dumpable guest's memory, for one, cannot read it while the change
1672/// itself succeeds. `/` is an ancestor of every path, so no host input change
1673/// is named in that run, rather than one the guest may have made.
1674fn rebound_path(observed: Option<PathBuf>) -> String {
1675    match observed {
1676        Some(path) if path.is_absolute() => path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
1677        _ => String::from("/"),
1678    }
1679}
1680
1681/// Whether the raw call `number(args)` may change the guest memory in
1682/// `range`, `[start, end)` (see `Config::untraced_code_range`):
1683/// - a fixed mapping over any part of it: `mmap` with MAP_FIXED, `mremap`
1684///   with MREMAP_FIXED, `shmat` with SHM_REMAP;
1685/// - a protection, advice or unmapping over any part of it: `mprotect`,
1686///   `pkey_mprotect`, `madvise`, `munmap`, the old range of `mremap`.
1687///
1688/// Linux takes page-aligned addresses for these calls and rounds a length up
1689/// to whole pages, and `range` is whole pages, so the unrounded interval
1690/// overlaps it exactly when the rounded one does. A MAP_HUGETLB `mmap` rounds
1691/// to its own page size on both ends, so it is widened to the size its
1692/// MAP_HUGE_* bits name, or else to `default_huge_page` (the host's
1693/// `Hugepagesize`). A zero length counts as its first byte, and a `shmat` as
1694/// reaching the end of the address space, since its size is the segment's.
1695/// A mapping without a fixed address never lands on an existing one, and the
1696/// guest's `process_vm_writev`, `ptrace` and `remap_file_pages` are refused.
1697/// Scalar arguments are never read as addresses, so an ordinary call is
1698/// never counted.
1699pub(crate) fn may_change_untraced_code(
1700    number: Sysno,
1701    args: &syscalls::SyscallArgs,
1702    (start, end): (u64, u64),
1703    default_huge_page: u64,
1704) -> bool {
1705    let [arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4] =
1706        [args.arg0, args.arg1, args.arg2, args.arg3, args.arg4].map(|arg| arg as u64);
1707    let overlaps = |addr: u64, len: u64| addr < end && addr.saturating_add(len.max(1)) > start;
1708    let overlaps_huge = |addr: u64, len: u64, page: u64| {
1709        let page = page.max(1);
1710        let first = addr - addr % page;
1711        let last = addr
1712            .saturating_add(len.max(1))
1713            .div_ceil(page)
1714            .saturating_mul(page);
1715        overlaps(first, last.saturating_sub(first).max(1))
1716    };
1717    let huge_page = |flags: u64| match (flags >> libc::MAP_HUGE_SHIFT) & libc::MAP_HUGE_MASK as u64
1718    {
1719        0 => default_huge_page,
1720        shift => 1u64.checked_shl(shift as u32).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
1721    };
1722    match number {
1723        Sysno::mmap if arg3 & libc::MAP_FIXED as u64 == 0 => false,
1724        Sysno::mmap if arg3 & libc::MAP_HUGETLB as u64 != 0 => {
1725            overlaps_huge(arg0, arg1, huge_page(arg3))
1726        }
1727        Sysno::mmap => overlaps(arg0, arg1),
1728        Sysno::mprotect | Sysno::pkey_mprotect | Sysno::madvise | Sysno::munmap => {
1729            overlaps(arg0, arg1)
1730        }
1731        Sysno::mremap => {
1732            overlaps(arg0, arg1) || (arg3 & libc::MREMAP_FIXED as u64 != 0 && overlaps(arg4, arg2))
1733        }
1734        Sysno::shmat => arg1 != 0 && arg2 & libc::SHM_REMAP as u64 != 0 && overlaps(arg1, u64::MAX),
1735        _ => false,
1736    }
1737}
1738
1739/// Whether an open with `flags` that returned a descriptor may write a
1740/// process's memory: `/proc/<pid>/mem` and `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/mem`
1741/// write through page protections. `descriptor` is what the descriptor is,
1742/// read through the opening thread's `/proc/<tid>/fd/<fd>` (see
1743/// [`descriptor_identity`]): its link, which names the file however the guest
1744/// reached it (a symlink, a `/proc/self/fd` reopen), and whether it is on
1745/// procfs. It counts only when it is a procfs file named `mem`, so an
1746/// ordinary file of that name, or a name that leads to a pipe, does not. A
1747/// descriptor that cannot be read at all counts, since Detcore cannot
1748/// establish what it is.
1749pub(crate) fn may_write_process_memory(flags: OFlag, descriptor: Option<(&Path, bool)>) -> bool {
1750    let writes = !flags.contains(OFlag::O_PATH) && flags & OFlag::O_ACCMODE != OFlag::O_RDONLY;
1751    writes
1752        && descriptor.is_none_or(|(link, on_procfs)| {
1753            on_procfs && link.file_name() == Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new("mem"))
1754        })
1755}
1756
1757/// The guest call after which [`Detcore::refresh_description_locks`] reads a
1758/// descriptor's locks.
1759#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1760pub(crate) enum LockCall {
1761    /// `F_OFD_SETLK` or `F_OFD_SETLKW`.
1762    Fcntl,
1763    /// `flock`.
1764    Flock,
1765    /// `pidfd_getfd`, which adds a slot.
1766    PidfdGetfd,
1767    /// `recvmsg` with `SCM_RIGHTS`, which adds a slot.
1768    Recvmsg,
1769    /// `recvmmsg` with `SCM_RIGHTS`, which adds slots.
1770    Recvmmsg,
1771    /// `ioctl(BINDER_WRITE_READ)` delivering a transaction that carries
1772    /// descriptors, which adds slots.
1773    BinderWriteRead,
1774}
1775
1776impl LockCall {
1777    /// The call's name, as a refusal names it.
1778    fn name(self) -> &'static str {
1779        match self {
1780            Self::Fcntl => "fcntl",
1781            Self::Flock => "flock",
1782            Self::PidfdGetfd => "pidfd_getfd",
1783            Self::Recvmsg => "recvmsg",
1784            Self::Recvmmsg => "recvmmsg",
1785            Self::BinderWriteRead => "ioctl(BINDER_WRITE_READ)",
1786        }
1787    }
1788
1789    /// Whether the call can take or release a lock.
1790    fn changes_locks(self) -> bool {
1791        matches!(self, Self::Fcntl | Self::Flock)
1792    }
1793}
1794
1795/// The inode number an fdinfo names (its `ino:` line), as `/proc/locks`
1796/// prints the last field of a lock's object.
1797fn fdinfo_inode(fdinfo: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
1798    String::from_utf8_lossy(fdinfo)
1799        .lines()
1800        .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("ino:"))
1801        .map(|inode| inode.trim().to_string())
1802        .filter(|inode| !inode.is_empty() && inode.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()))
1803}
1804
1805/// The fdinfo page [`Detcore::read_own_fdinfo`] stages its calls in, and its
1806/// layout: the path, `openat2`'s `struct open_how`, the `fstatfs`/`fstat`
1807/// buffer, then the read buffer.
1808const FDINFO_PAGE: usize = 4096;
1809const FDINFO_PATH: usize = 0;
1810const FDINFO_HOW: usize = 64;
1811const FDINFO_HOW_SIZE: usize = 24;
1812const FDINFO_STAT: usize = 128;
1813const FDINFO_READ: usize = 512;
1814const _: () = assert!(FDINFO_HOW + FDINFO_HOW_SIZE <= FDINFO_STAT);
1815const _: () = assert!(FDINFO_STAT + std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>() <= FDINFO_READ);
1816const _: () = assert!(FDINFO_STAT + std::mem::size_of::<libc::statfs>() <= FDINFO_READ);
1817/// `openat2`'s resolution for the fdinfo entry: no step out of the anchor
1818/// and no mount crossed.
1819const FDINFO_RESOLVE: u64 = libc::RESOLVE_NO_XDEV | libc::RESOLVE_BENEATH;
1820
1821/// What [`Detcore::read_own_fdinfo`] found.
1822pub(crate) enum FdinfoRead {
1823    /// The fdinfo's text, from an entry proved to be on the guest's procfs.
1824    Contents(Vec<u8>),
1825    /// A step failed for a reason that says nothing about the description's
1826    /// locks: they are unknown (`procfs::locks::LockLedger::note_unknown`).
1827    Unknown(String),
1828    /// The guest's `/proc` could not be proved to be procfs, or a step failed
1829    /// for a cause the guest's own view or the backend decides
1830    /// ([`fdinfo_failure_hides`]): the description contributes no lock, which
1831    /// can hide the guest's row but never admits a host's.
1832    Untrackable(String),
1833}
1834
1835impl FdinfoRead {
1836    /// The inode number the fdinfo names, if it was read.
1837    fn inode(&self) -> Option<String> {
1838        match self {
1839            Self::Contents(contents) => fdinfo_inode(contents),
1840            Self::Unknown(_) | Self::Untrackable(_) => None,
1841        }
1842    }
1843}
1844
1845/// Why [`Detcore::read_staged_fdinfo`] did not read an fdinfo.
1846enum FdinfoFailure {
1847    /// A step (`open`, `fstatfs`, `fstat`, `read`) failed with an errno.
1848    Failed(&'static str, Errno),
1849    /// The guest's `/proc` was shown not to be procfs, for this reason.
1850    NotProcfs(&'static str),
1851}
1852
1853/// Whether an fdinfo step that failed with `errno` shows the description
1854/// is untrackable: a cause the guest's own filesystem view or the backend
1855/// decides, the same in every run of the same program (no `/proc` or an
1856/// entry missing, ENOENT or ENOTDIR; a symlink loop, ELOOP; an entry outside
1857/// the anchor or across a mount, EXDEV; a backend that refuses the call,
1858/// EINVAL, as KVM refuses an `O_PATH` open of its `/proc`). Every other
1859/// errno, ambient or resource state that can differ between runs, leaves the
1860/// locks unknown, so a later `/proc/locks` read refuses rather than shows a
1861/// row that depends on host state: a full descriptor table, EMFILE; a full
1862/// host file table, ENFILE; no memory, ENOMEM; an interruption, EINTR; an I/O
1863/// error, EIO; EAGAIN; a kernel without `openat2`, ENOSYS; a permission
1864/// refusal, EACCES or EPERM, which a host security module keyed by the host
1865/// process can give as well as the guest's own seccomp filter; anything
1866/// unlisted.
1867fn fdinfo_failure_hides(errno: Errno) -> bool {
1868    matches!(
1869        errno,
1870        Errno::ENOENT | Errno::ENOTDIR | Errno::ELOOP | Errno::EXDEV | Errno::EINVAL
1871    )
1872}
1873
1874/// Why Detcore does not know which locks the description descriptor `fd`
1875/// names holds after the guest's `call` through it: `step` (the open or a
1876/// read of its fdinfo) failed with `errno`. A failure says nothing about
1877/// which locks it holds (`Detcore::read_own_fdinfo`); a later `/proc/locks`
1878/// read refuses with this reason (`procfs::locks::LockLedger::unknown`).
1879fn fdinfo_refusal(call: &str, fd: RawFd, step: &str, errno: Errno) -> String {
1880    format!(
1881        "after {call} on fd {fd}, Detcore could not {step} that descriptor's fdinfo \
1882         ({errno}), so it does not know which locks the description holds"
1883    )
1884}
1885
1886/// What a status snapshot reports for the signal mask and D37's held masks
1887/// of the thread it describes (`status_published_sigblk`).
1888#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
1889pub(crate) struct StatusMaskFacts {
1890    /// The `SigBlk` reported in place of the kernel's, or `None` to keep the
1891    /// kernel's.
1892    pub(crate) sigblk: Option<u64>,
1893    /// Under the in-guest delivery gate, while the thread holds a
1894    /// temporary-mask publication (A5 step 3c.1e A, IR-23(a)), the ignored
1895    /// signals it keeps pending from its masked call's entry in its private
1896    /// and shared queues (D37's held masks), which the status shows although
1897    /// the published temporary mask does not block them; zero otherwise.
1898    pub(crate) held_private: u64,
1899    pub(crate) held_shared: u64,
1900}
1901
1902/// The `SigBlk` a status snapshot reports for the thread it describes
1903/// (`mask_thread`, from `ProcfsFile::status_mask_thread`) in place of the
1904/// kernel's, or `None` to keep the kernel's: the guest mask that thread
1905/// published to the scheduler (`Scheduler::published_guest_sigmask`), where
1906/// guest masks are published at all (`publishes_guest_masks`): under
1907/// signal-target modelling, where the kernel's mask is Detcore's private one
1908/// while it holds the thread under it (Codex review of R2b-2 stage 2, P2;
1909/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273>), and under the in-guest
1910/// delivery gate, where each request publishes the guest's mask and the
1911/// kernel's may be the in-guest runtime's (A5 step 3c.1b). With nothing
1912/// published for the thread the scheduler answers `None`, and the kernel's
1913/// `SigBlk` is reported, as before.
1914///
1915/// Under the gate (A5 step 3c.1e A) the answer is tri-state (IR-18) and
1916/// carries D37's held masks of a temporary-mask publication in force
1917/// (`Scheduler::status_guest_mask`). A mask the scheduler holds as unknown is
1918/// shown neither as the call's earlier mask nor as the kernel's `SigBlk`
1919/// (the in-guest runtime's mask once it has one): the read is refused by name
1920/// through the run-wide stopping refusal HERMIT_GUEST_MASK_UNKNOWN (D49),
1921/// never an errno to the reader; were the run to go on, Hermit's own failure
1922/// (`Error::Tool`) ends the read. `reader` is the reading thread.
1923pub(crate) async fn status_published_sigblk<G, T>(
1924    guest: &mut G,
1925    mask_thread: Option<i32>,
1926) -> Result<StatusMaskFacts, Error>
1927where
1928    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
1929    T: RecordOrReplay,
1930{
1931    use crate::scheduler::guest_mask_publication::PublishedGuestMask;
1932    let Some(thread) = mask_thread else {
1933        return Ok(StatusMaskFacts::default());
1934    };
1935    if !crate::syscalls::helpers::publishes_guest_masks(guest.config()) {
1936        return Ok(StatusMaskFacts::default());
1937    }
1938    if !guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery {
1939        return Ok(StatusMaskFacts {
1940            sigblk: crate::tool_global::published_guest_sigmask(guest, DetTid::from_raw(thread))
1941                .await,
1942            ..Default::default()
1943        });
1944    }
1945    let status = crate::tool_global::status_guest_mask(guest, DetTid::from_raw(thread)).await;
1946    let sigblk = match status.mask {
1947        Some(PublishedGuestMask::Known(mask)) => Some(mask),
1948        None => None,
1949        Some(PublishedGuestMask::Unknown) => {
1950            let reason = crate::refused_signal_controls::guest_mask_unknown_refusal(
1951                guest.thread_state().dettid.as_raw(),
1952                thread,
1953            );
1954            tracing::error!("{}", reason);
1955            crate::tool_global::stopping_refusal(guest, reason.clone()).await;
1956            return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(reason)));
1957        }
1958    };
1959    Ok(StatusMaskFacts {
1960        sigblk,
1961        held_private: status.held_private,
1962        held_shared: status.held_shared,
1963    })
1964}

1966#[cfg(test)]
1967mod fdinfo_refusal_tests {
1968    use super::*;
1969
1970    /// A guest at its descriptor limit gets EMFILE from Detcore's fdinfo
1971    /// open after a lock call that needed no new descriptor; a later
1972    /// `/proc/locks` read stops the run with that named, naming the call,
1973    /// rather than taking the description to hold nothing. hermit-cli's
1974    /// `a_full_descriptor_table_refuses_the_next_proc_locks_read` runs that
1975    /// end to end; this pins the reason's wording.
1976    #[test]
1977    fn a_failed_fdinfo_read_is_a_named_refusal_not_an_empty_one() {
1978        let reason = fdinfo_refusal("recvmsg", 7, "open", Errno::EMFILE);
1979        assert!(reason.contains("after recvmsg on fd 7"), "{reason}");
1980        assert!(
1981            reason.contains("could not open that descriptor's fdinfo"),
1982            "{reason}"
1983        );
1984        assert!(reason.contains("EMFILE"), "{reason}");
1985        assert!(fdinfo_refusal("flock", 7, "read", Errno::EIO).contains("could not read that"));
1986    }
1987
1988    /// A failure the guest's filesystem view or the backend decides hides
1989    /// the description; ambient or resource state, and anything unlisted,
1990    /// leaves its locks unknown (and a later `/proc/locks` read refused).
1991    #[test]
1992    fn only_a_guest_or_backend_decided_failure_hides_the_description() {
1993        for errno in [
1994            Errno::ENOENT,
1995            Errno::ENOTDIR,
1996            Errno::ELOOP,
1997            Errno::EXDEV,
1998            Errno::EINVAL,
1999        ] {
2000            assert!(fdinfo_failure_hides(errno), "{errno}");
2001        }
2002        for errno in [
2003            Errno::EACCES,
2004            Errno::EPERM,
2005            Errno::EMFILE,
2006            Errno::ENFILE,
2007            Errno::ENOMEM,
2008            Errno::EINTR,
2009            Errno::EIO,
2010            Errno::EAGAIN,
2011            Errno::ENOSYS,
2012            Errno::EBADF,
2013        ] {
2014            assert!(!fdinfo_failure_hides(errno), "{errno}");
2015        }
2016    }
2017
2018    #[test]
2019    fn an_fdinfo_names_its_inode_as_proc_locks_prints_it() {
2020        let fdinfo = b"pos:\t0\nflags:\t0100002\nmnt_id:\t31\nino:\t1234\n\
2021            lock:\t1: OFDLCK ADVISORY READ -1 00:18:1234 0 0\n";
2022        assert_eq!(fdinfo_inode(fdinfo).as_deref(), Some("1234"));
2023        assert_eq!(fdinfo_inode(b"pos:\t0\n"), None);
2024        assert_eq!(fdinfo_inode(b"ino:\tx\n"), None);
2025    }
2026}

2028/// Puts back the guest bytes under a `Detcore::probe_socket_option` buffer.
2029fn restore_socket_option_probe<M: MemoryAccess>(memory: &mut M, buffer: AddrMut<u8>, saved: &[u8]) {
2030    if memory.write_exact(buffer, saved).is_err() {
2031        info!("Could not restore the guest bytes under a socket option probe.");
2032    }
2033}
2034
2035/// Writes back the guest bytes that a pre-call lookup buffer (utimensat's, or
2036/// the removal lookup's) covered.
2037fn restore_lookup_buffer<M: MemoryAccess>(memory: &mut M, buffer: StatPtr, saved: &[u8]) {
2038    if memory.write_exact(buffer.0.cast(), saved).is_err() {
2039        info!("Could not restore the guest bytes under a pre-call lookup buffer.");
2040    }
2041}
2042
2043/// Whether a lookup `buffer` overlaps `path` through its NUL, which a guest
2044/// call still has to read. A path that cannot be read counts as overlapping,
2045/// so that the kernel, not a lookup, reports the fault.
2046fn path_overlaps_buffer<M: MemoryAccess>(
2047    memory: &M,
2048    path: Option<syscalls::PathPtr<'_>>,
2049    buffer: StatPtr,
2050) -> bool {
2051    path_overlaps_bytes(
2052        memory,
2053        path,
2054        buffer.0.as_raw(),
2055        std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>(),
2056    )
2057}
2058
2059/// Whether the `len` bytes at `start` overlap `path` through its NUL. A path
2060/// that cannot be read counts as overlapping.
2061fn path_overlaps_bytes<M: MemoryAccess>(
2062    memory: &M,
2063    path: Option<syscalls::PathPtr<'_>>,
2064    start: usize,
2065    len: usize,
2066) -> bool {
2067    use reverie::syscalls::FromToRaw;
2068
2069    let end = start.saturating_add(len);
2070    path.is_some_and(|ptr| match ptr.read(memory) {
2071        Ok(read) => {
2072            let addr = Some(ptr).into_raw();
2073            let read: PathBuf = read;
2074            addr < end && start < addr.saturating_add(read.as_os_str().len() + 1)
2075        }
2076        Err(_) => true,
2077    })
2078}
2079
2080/// Whether the utimensat lookup buffer overlaps the guest memory Linux reads
2081/// for `call`: the path through its NUL and, with `guest_times`, the two
2082/// timespecs. A path that cannot be read counts as overlapping, so that the
2083/// kernel, not a lookup, reports the fault.
2084fn utimensat_input_overlaps<M: MemoryAccess>(
2085    memory: &M,
2086    call: &syscalls::Utimensat,
2087    guest_times: bool,
2088    buffer: StatPtr,
2089) -> bool {
2090    let start = buffer.0.as_raw();
2091    let end = start + std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>();
2092    let overlaps = |addr: usize, len: usize| addr < end && start < addr.saturating_add(len);
2093    let path = path_overlaps_buffer(memory, call.path(), buffer);
2094    let times = guest_times
2095        && call
2096            .times()
2097            .is_some_and(|times| overlaps(times.as_raw(), std::mem::size_of::<[Timespec; 2]>()));
2098    path || times
2099}
2100
2101/// Whether a `*at` stat call names no path: it passes `AT_EMPTY_PATH` with an
2102/// empty or NULL path (Linux 6.11 accepts NULL), and so describes `dirfd`
2103/// itself, or the working directory for `AT_FDCWD`. A path that cannot be
2104/// read counts as nonempty, so the call keeps the path-based numbering and
2105/// the kernel reports the fault. The path is read only after the flag check,
2106/// so an ordinary `stat()` reads no guest memory here.
2107fn names_no_path<M: MemoryAccess>(memory: &M, path: Option<PathPtr>, flags: AtFlags) -> bool {
2108    flags.contains(AtFlags::AT_EMPTY_PATH)
2109        && match path {
2110            None => true,
2111            Some(path) => path
2112                .read(memory)
2113                .is_ok_and(|path| path.as_os_str().is_empty()),
2114        }
2115}
2116
2117/// The fixed inode that `fd` reports when it is still the container's
2118/// inherited stdin, stdout or stderr, as fdinfo and `/proc/self/fd/N` report
2119/// it. Every stat call that describes the descriptor itself must use it, or
2120/// the guest's libc decides which number `fstat()` sees.
2121fn stdio_inode_override<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2122    guest: &G,
2123    fd: i32,
2124) -> Option<DetInode> {
2125    guest
2126        .thread_state()
2127        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2128            deterministic_stdio_inode_for_resource(fd, detfd.resource())
2129        })
2130        .ok()
2131        .flatten()
2132}
2133
2134/// The file a stat call describes, as Detcore finds it again to learn the
2135/// canonical path of a procfs file (see [`procfs_inode`]).
2136#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
2137enum StatTarget<'a> {
2138    /// The file open as this descriptor.
2139    Descriptor(RawFd),
2140    /// The calling thread's working directory.
2141    Cwd,
2142    /// The file `path` names relative to `dirfd`, or the symbolic link itself
2143    /// when `follow` is false.
2144    Path {
2145        dirfd: i32,
2146        path: Option<PathPtr<'a>>,
2147        follow: bool,
2148    },
2149    /// A file named by a path that the call's result overwrote, which Detcore
2150    /// cannot look up again.
2151    Overwritten,
2152}
2153
2154impl<'a> StatTarget<'a> {
2155    /// The target of an `fstatat` or `statx` call with these operands.
2156    fn at<M: MemoryAccess>(
2157        memory: &M,
2158        dirfd: i32,
2159        path: Option<PathPtr<'a>>,
2160        flags: AtFlags,
2161    ) -> Self {
2162        if names_no_path(memory, path, flags) {
2163            if dirfd == libc::AT_FDCWD {
2164                return StatTarget::Cwd;
2165            }
2166            if dirfd >= 0 {
2167                return StatTarget::Descriptor(dirfd);
2168            }
2169        }
2170        StatTarget::Path {
2171            dirfd,
2172            path,
2173            follow: !flags.contains(AtFlags::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW),
2174        }
2175    }
2176
2177    /// This target, or [`StatTarget::Overwritten`] if it is a path that the
2178    /// `len` bytes of the call's result at `result` overlap. Linux reads the
2179    /// path before it writes the result, so the call succeeds, but the path
2180    /// the guest named is gone once it returns. Found before the call.
2181    fn unless_overwritten<M: MemoryAccess>(self, memory: &M, result: usize, len: usize) -> Self {
2182        match self {
2183            StatTarget::Path { path, .. } if path_overlaps_bytes(memory, path, result, len) => {
2184                StatTarget::Overwritten
2185            }
2186            target => target,
2187        }
2188    }
2189
2190    /// The descriptor the call describes itself, if it names no path.
2191    fn descriptor(&self) -> Option<RawFd> {
2192        match self {
2193            StatTarget::Descriptor(fd) => Some(*fd),
2194            StatTarget::Cwd | StatTarget::Path { .. } | StatTarget::Overwritten => None,
2195        }
2196    }
2197}
2198
2199/// The rendered procfs file that a stat result describes, if it is one: by
2200/// the name Detcore gave it, or by its kernel identity where Detcore names no
2201/// procfs files. Never a per-process file, whose kernel-reached instances
2202/// keep the kernel's identity. `files` are the files the session renders
2203/// (`Detcore::rendered_files`); `recordreplay_modes` is the run's
2204/// `Config::recordreplay_modes`, under which Detcore renders none.
2205fn rendered_entry(
2206    procfs: &ProcfsEntry,
2207    stat: &DetStat,
2208    recordreplay_modes: bool,
2209    files: crate::procfs::RenderedFiles,
2210) -> Option<&'static Path> {
2211    if recordreplay_modes {
2212        return None;
2213    }
2214    let found = match procfs {
2215        ProcfsEntry::At(within) => rendered_procfs::rendered_path_within(within, files),
2216        ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs | ProcfsEntry::Unknown => {
2217            rendered_procfs::rendered_path_of_raw(stat, files)
2218        }
2219        ProcfsEntry::Unnamed => None,
2220    };
2221    // A per-process file the kernel reached (through `..`, after `chroot`,
2222    // in a nested PID namespace) is served from the kernel's bytes
2223    // (`ProcfsFile::served_rendered_path`), so it keeps the kernel's metadata
2224    // too: its identity is the kernel's file's, not the rendered file's.
2225    found.filter(|path| !crate::procfs::rendered_path_is_per_process(path))
2226}
2227
2228/// `STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE` (include/uapi/linux/stat.h, since Linux 6.8). Reverie's
2229/// `StatxMask` does not name it and drops it from a mask read through it, so
2230/// Detcore reads a call's raw mask ([`statx_requested_mask`]).
2231const STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE: u32 = 0x4000;
2232
2233/// What Linux adds to every unique mount ID so that none equals a classic
2234/// 32-bit one: `MNT_UNIQUE_ID_OFFSET` (v6.12 fs/namespace.c:73). Linux counts
2235/// up from it and never reuses an ID, so the first mount's is the offset plus
2236/// one (fs/namespace.c:74 and 244).
2237const MNT_UNIQUE_ID_OFFSET: u64 = 1 << 31;
2238
2239/// The mask a `statx` call asks for, every bit kept.
2240fn statx_requested_mask(call: syscalls::Statx) -> u32 {
2241    syscalls::SyscallArgs::from(call).arg3 as u32
2242}
2243
2244/// `call` asking the kernel for the classic mount ID (`STATX_MNT_ID`) where
2245/// it asked for the unique one, and otherwise the same call.
2246fn statx_asking_classic_mount_id(call: syscalls::Statx) -> syscalls::Statx {
2247    let mut args = syscalls::SyscallArgs::from(call);
2248    let mask = args.arg3 as u32;
2249    if mask & STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE != 0 {
2250        args.arg3 =
2251            ((mask & !STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE) | reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::STATX_MNT_ID) as usize;
2252    }
2253    syscalls::Statx::from(args)
2254}
2255
2256/// The `stx_mask` bits of the fields a recording keeps: every field up to
2257/// `stx_mnt_id` (`STATX_BASIC_STATS`, `STATX_BTIME`, `STATX_MNT_ID`) and the
2258/// unique mount ID, which is also `stx_mnt_id`.
2259const STATX_MODELED_MASK: u32 = 0x1fff | STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE;
2260
2261/// Where a `struct statx` stops holding fields Detcore models: the direct-I/O
2262/// alignments (0x98), `stx_subvol` (0xa0), the atomic-write limits and the
2263/// spare words up to its end (0x100) follow `stx_mnt_id`.
2264const STATX_UNMODELED_TAIL: usize = 0x98;
2265
2266/// Make the `statx` result at `addr` report only the fields Detcore models:
2267/// clear the other `stx_mask` bits and zero the rest of the structure, as a
2268/// kernel without those fields would. A recording keeps only the modeled
2269/// fields (Reverie's `StatxBuf` skips the rest), so without this a recorded
2270/// run saw the host's `stx_subvol` (a btrfs subvolume ID) and its replay saw
2271/// zero; and outside recording Detcore already writes back only the modeled
2272/// fields (`determinize_stat`). Applied after the call in recording and in
2273/// replay alike, so both show the same bytes.
2274fn canonicalize_statx_tail<M: MemoryAccess>(memory: &mut M, addr: usize) -> Result<(), Errno> {
2275    const SIZE: usize = std::mem::size_of::<reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx>();
2276    let start = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(addr).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
2277    let mut bytes = [0u8; SIZE];
2278    memory.read_exact(start, &mut bytes)?;
2279    let mut canonical = bytes;
2280    let mask = u32::from_ne_bytes(canonical[..4].try_into().unwrap()) & STATX_MODELED_MASK;
2281    canonical[..4].copy_from_slice(&mask.to_ne_bytes());
2282    canonical[STATX_UNMODELED_TAIL..].fill(0);
2283    if canonical != bytes {
2284        memory.write_exact(start, &canonical)?;
2285    }
2286    Ok(())
2287}
2288
2289#[cfg(test)]
2290mod statx_tail_tests {
2291    use reverie::syscalls::LocalMemory;
2292
2293    use super::*;
2294
2295    /// What a recording keeps of a `statx` result is what the guest sees: the
2296    /// modeled fields and mask bits stay, `stx_subvol` and the rest of the
2297    /// tail become zero and their mask bits are cleared.
2298    #[test]
2299    fn a_statx_result_keeps_only_the_fields_a_recording_keeps() {
2300        let mut buf = [0xa5u8; 256];
2301        // STATX_BASIC_STATS | STATX_BTIME | STATX_MNT_ID | STATX_DIOALIGN |
2302        // STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE | STATX_SUBVOL | STATX_WRITE_ATOMIC.
2303        let mask: u32 = 0x7ff | 0x800 | 0x1000 | 0x2000 | 0x4000 | 0x8000 | 0x10000;
2304        buf[..4].copy_from_slice(&mask.to_ne_bytes());
2305        let modeled = buf[4..STATX_UNMODELED_TAIL].to_vec();
2306        let mut memory = LocalMemory::new();
2307        canonicalize_statx_tail(&mut memory, buf.as_mut_ptr() as usize).unwrap();
2308        assert_eq!(
2309            u32::from_ne_bytes(buf[..4].try_into().unwrap()),
2310            0x7ff | 0x800 | 0x1000 | 0x4000
2311        );
2312        assert_eq!(buf[4..STATX_UNMODELED_TAIL], modeled[..]);
2313        assert!(buf[STATX_UNMODELED_TAIL..].iter().all(|byte| *byte == 0));
2314        // Idempotent: replay applies it to what recording already produced.
2315        let once = buf;
2316        canonicalize_statx_tail(&mut memory, buf.as_mut_ptr() as usize).unwrap();
2317        assert_eq!(buf, once);
2318    }
2319}
2320
2321/// Whether `statx` accepts these `flags` and `mask` (`vfs_statx`'s and the
2322/// syscall's own checks): no reserved mask bit, known flags only (unless the
2323/// call names no path), and not both synchronization types at once.
2324fn statx_arguments_valid(flags: i32, mask: u32, names_no_path: bool) -> bool {
2325    let known = libc::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW
2326        | libc::AT_EMPTY_PATH
2327        | libc::AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT
2328        | reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::AT_STATX_SYNC_TYPE;
2329    // A call on the descriptor itself (`AT_EMPTY_PATH` with an empty or
2330    // NULL path) does not look at the other flags (measured on Linux 7.1).
2331    mask & 0x8000_0000 == 0
2332        && (names_no_path || flags & !known == 0)
2333        && flags & reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::AT_STATX_SYNC_TYPE
2334            != reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::AT_STATX_SYNC_TYPE
2335}
2336
2337/// Whether `path` spells a descriptor link: `/dev/fd/N`, `/proc/*/fd/N` or
2338/// `/proc/*/task/*/fd/N`.
2339fn names_descriptor_link(path: &Path) -> bool {
2340    let parts = path
2341        .components()
2342        .filter_map(|component| match component {
2343            std::path::Component::Normal(part) => {
2344                Some(std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt::as_bytes(part))
2345            }
2346            _ => None,
2347        })
2348        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
2349    let number = |part: &[u8]| !part.is_empty() && part.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_digit);
2350    match parts.as_slice() {
2351        [b"dev", b"fd", fd] | [b"proc", _, b"fd", fd] | [b"proc", _, b"task", _, b"fd", fd] => {
2352            number(fd)
2353        }
2354        _ => false,
2355    }
2356}
2357
2358/// Who opens a path that may be one of its descriptor links, for
2359/// [`path_to_record_for_open`].
2360#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
2361struct DescriptorLinkOpener {
2362    /// The caller's pid and tid as the guest's `/proc/<pid>` and
2363    /// `.../task/<tid>` spellings name them on every backend, or `None`
2364    /// where Detcore does not know those names (a nested PID namespace).
2365    /// See [`Detcore::procfs_caller_ids`].
2366    own: Option<(i32, i32)>,
2367    /// Whether the descriptor table procfs reads for a process-level link
2368    /// (`/proc/self/fd/N`, `/dev/fd/N`), the thread-group leader's, is
2369    /// provably the caller's own: the caller leads its group, or holds the
2370    /// table the leader holds now (`ThreadState::process_files`). A thread
2371    /// cloned without `CLONE_FILES` holds a table of its own.
2372    holds_process_table: bool,
2373}
2374
2375/// The descriptor `N` that a descriptor link in an open's spelling names,
2376/// as it stood when the open looked the link up: in the open's own turn,
2377/// before the call, which may block and leave the turn (a FIFO waiting for
2378/// its other end) while a thread sharing the table replaces `N`. The kernel
2379/// follows the link at that lookup, so the file it opens is the one `N` was
2380/// then, whatever `N` is when the open completes.
2381#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
2382struct LinkSource {
2383    fd: RawFd,
2384    /// The path Detcore had recorded for `N`.
2385    path: Option<PathBuf>,
2386    /// `N`'s open file description.
2387    open_file: OpenFileId,
2388    /// Where `N`'s `/proc/self` or `/proc/thread-self` spelling led, and the
2389    /// identity of the task it led to (`DetFd::procfs_reached`).
2390    reached: Option<(PathBuf, Option<crate::procfs::TaskIncarnation>)>,
2391}
2392
2393impl LinkSource {
2394    /// The path to record, for [`path_to_record_for_open`], for descriptor
2395    /// `fd` of the caller's table, whose open file description is `current`
2396    /// when the open completes: `N`'s path as the lookup saw it, only if
2397    /// `fd` is `N` and `N` still holds that description. Where `N` was
2398    /// replaced meanwhile, nothing, and the open keeps its spelling, as
2399    /// before this change.
2400    fn path_if_unchanged(&self, fd: RawFd, current: Option<OpenFileId>) -> Option<PathBuf> {
2401        (fd == self.fd && current == Some(self.open_file))
2402            .then(|| self.path.clone())
2403            .flatten()
2404    }
2405
2406    /// Where `N`'s selector spelling led, for a new descriptor opened through
2407    /// the link to `N` (`fd`), only if `fd` is `N` and `N` still holds its
2408    /// description: the new open file is that task's directory too.
2409    fn reached_if_unchanged(
2410        &self,
2411        fd: RawFd,
2412        current: Option<OpenFileId>,
2413    ) -> Option<(PathBuf, Option<crate::procfs::TaskIncarnation>)> {
2414        (fd == self.fd && current == Some(self.open_file))
2415            .then(|| self.reached.clone())
2416            .flatten()
2417    }
2418}
2419
2420/// Where the spelling `recorded` led, if it names a task's directory: through
2421/// a `/proc` selector, `/proc/self`, `/proc/self/task`,
2422/// `/proc/self/task/<tid>` or `/proc/thread-self`, with the selector replaced
2423/// by the opener's numbers (`own`, its pid and tid as `/proc` spells them), as
2424/// Linux resolved it at the open; or by number, `/proc/<pid>`,
2425/// `/proc/<pid>/task` or `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>`, itself
2426/// (`DetFd::procfs_reached`). Linux binds the directory to the task it named
2427/// at the open, not to the number, so either is that task while it lives.
2428/// Nothing for any other path, such as a descriptor link (`fd/N`), which
2429/// leads to another file, and nothing where Detcore does not know the
2430/// caller's numbers (`own` is `None` in a nested PID namespace).
2431fn procfs_selector_reached(recorded: &Path, own: Option<(i32, i32)>) -> Option<PathBuf> {
2432    let (pid, tid) = own?;
2433    let below = recorded.strip_prefix("/proc").ok()?;
2434    let names = below
2435        .components()
2436        .map(|component| match component {
2437            std::path::Component::Normal(name) => name.to_str(),
2438            _ => None,
2439        })
2440        .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
2441    let number = |name: &str| {
2442        (!name.starts_with('0') && !name.is_empty() && name.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()))
2443            .then(|| name.parse::<i32>().ok())
2444            .flatten()
2445    };
2446    Some(PathBuf::from(match names.as_slice() {
2447        ["self"] => format!("/proc/{pid}"),
2448        ["self", "task"] => format!("/proc/{pid}/task"),
2449        ["self", "task", thread] => format!("/proc/{pid}/task/{}", number(thread)?),
2450        ["thread-self"] => format!("/proc/{pid}/task/{tid}"),
2451        [process] => format!("/proc/{}", number(process)?),
2452        [process, "task"] => format!("/proc/{}/task", number(process)?),
2453        [process, "task", thread] => {
2454            format!("/proc/{}/task/{}", number(process)?, number(thread)?)
2455        }
2456        _ => return None,
2457    }))
2458}
2459
2460/// The task whose directory `reached` (where a `/proc` selector led,
2461/// `procfs_selector_reached`) is or is below: `/proc/<pid>`, and the thread of
2462/// `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>`.
2463fn procfs_reached_task(reached: &Path) -> Option<crate::procfs::BoundTask> {
2464    let names = reached
2465        .strip_prefix("/proc")
2466        .ok()?
2467        .components()
2468        .map(|component| component.as_os_str().to_str())
2469        .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
2470    let number = |name: &str| name.parse::<i32>().ok().filter(|number| *number > 0);
2471    let process = number(names.first()?)?;
2472    let thread = match names.as_slice() {
2473        [_, "task", thread, ..] => Some(number(thread)?),
2474        _ => None,
2475    };
2476    Some(crate::procfs::BoundTask { process, thread })
2477}
2478
2479/// Whether `spelling` names a `/proc` selector link itself: `/proc/self` or
2480/// `/proc/thread-self`, which are symbolic links to a task's directory.
2481fn names_a_selector_link(spelling: &Path) -> bool {
2482    spelling.parent() == Some(Path::new("/proc"))
2483        && spelling
2484            .file_name()
2485            .is_some_and(|name| name == "self" || name == "thread-self")
2486}
2487
2488/// Whether an open of the absolute spelling `observed` with `flags` opens a
2489/// descriptor link itself rather than the file it reaches: `O_NOFOLLOW`
2490/// does not follow the last component (with `O_PATH` the link is opened,
2491/// without it the open fails with `ELOOP`), unless the spelling follows it
2492/// anyway with a trailing slash or `/.`.
2493fn opens_the_link_itself(observed: &Path, flags: OFlag) -> bool {
2494    let bytes = std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt::as_bytes(observed.as_os_str());
2495    flags.contains(OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW) && !(bytes.ends_with(b"/") || bytes.ends_with(b"/."))
2496}
2497
2498/// The path Detcore records for a descriptor the guest opened at the absolute
2499/// spelling `observed` with `flags`. Opened through one of the caller's own
2500/// descriptor links (`/proc/self/fd/N`, `/dev/fd/N`, ... see
2501/// [`crate::syscalls::namespace::own_descriptor_link`]), the new descriptor
2502/// is the file that descriptor `N` is, so it takes the path recorded for `N`
2503/// (by `recorded`): a name relative to the new descriptor is then looked up
2504/// below that file, as Linux looks it up, and not below the link's spelling,
2505/// which names no procfs file of its own.
2506///
2507/// It keeps the spelling, as every other open does, wherever the recorded
2508/// path could name another file than the one the kernel opened:
2509/// - the open does not follow the link (`O_NOFOLLOW` without a trailing
2510///   slash or `/.`), so it opened the link itself;
2511/// - the link names the process's table, which is the thread-group
2512///   leader's, and the caller is not proven to hold that table
2513///   (`opener.holds_process_table`); `recorded` reads the caller's;
2514/// - descriptor `N` has no recorded path, or a relative one;
2515/// - `N`'s recorded path is resolved per caller (`/proc/self`,
2516///   `/proc/thread-self`, `/dev/fd`, ... see
2517///   [`crate::syscalls::namespace::names_through_caller_selector`]): `N` is
2518///   the file its opener reached, which another process or thread that
2519///   inherited or shares it would not reach by that path.
2520///
2521/// Where the link names the caller's own table and `N` has no recorded path
2522/// at all, as for a descriptor received through `SCM_RIGHTS`, `identity` is
2523/// recorded instead if given: the procfs directory that the kernel names for
2524/// the opened descriptor (see `Detcore::procfs_directory_named_for`). Not
2525/// where `N`'s recorded path is refused above, nor where the link names a
2526/// table the caller is not proven to hold, whose `N` is not the one
2527/// `recorded` describes.
2528fn path_to_record_for_open(
2529    observed: &Path,
2530    flags: OFlag,
2531    opener: DescriptorLinkOpener,
2532    recorded: impl FnOnce(RawFd) -> Option<PathBuf>,
2533    identity: Option<PathBuf>,
2534) -> PathBuf {
2535    use crate::syscalls::namespace::DescriptorTable;
2536    if opens_the_link_itself(observed, flags) {
2537        return observed.to_path_buf();
2538    }
2539    let Some(link) = crate::syscalls::namespace::own_descriptor_link(observed, opener.own) else {
2540        return observed.to_path_buf();
2541    };
2542    if !(link.table == DescriptorTable::Thread || opener.holds_process_table) {
2543        return observed.to_path_buf();
2544    }
2545    match recorded(link.fd) {
2546        Some(path) => {
2547            (!crate::syscalls::namespace::names_through_caller_selector(&path)).then_some(path)
2548        }
2549        None => identity,
2550    }
2551    .unwrap_or_else(|| observed.to_path_buf())
2552}
2553
2554/// The components below `/proc` of the kernel's name for a procfs directory
2555/// (a descriptor link), and the positions among them of the task numbers it
2556/// names: `/proc/<pid>` and its `task/<tid>`. `None` for a name outside
2557/// `/proc`, a deleted or anonymous object, a relative name, or a task number
2558/// procfs would not have (a leading zero).
2559fn procfs_directory_task_positions(link: &str) -> Option<(Vec<String>, Vec<usize>)> {
2560    if link.ends_with(" (deleted)") {
2561        return None;
2562    }
2563    let below = link.strip_prefix("/proc")?;
2564    if !(below.is_empty() || below.starts_with('/')) {
2565        return None;
2566    }
2567    let names = below
2568        .split('/')
2569        .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
2570        .map(str::to_owned)
2571        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
2572    if names.iter().any(|name| name == "." || name == "..") {
2573        return None;
2574    }
2575    let number = |name: &str| {
2576        !name.is_empty() && !name.starts_with('0') && name.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit())
2577    };
2578    let mut positions = Vec::new();
2579    if let Some(first) = names.first()
2580        && first.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit())
2581    {
2582        if !number(first) {
2583            return None;
2584        }
2585        positions.push(0);
2586        if names.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("task")
2587            && let Some(thread) = names.get(2)
2588        {
2589            if !number(thread) {
2590                return None;
2591            }
2592            positions.push(2);
2593        }
2594    }
2595    Some((names, positions))
2596}
2597
2598/// Whether `link`, the kernel's name for a descriptor (its
2599/// `/proc/thread-self/fd/N` link), names a procfs directory path Detcore
2600/// may record for it: `/proc`, or a path below it that names no process or
2601/// thread (`procfs::ids::named_ids`, and no numeric component at all),
2602/// whose numbers are the kernel's and need not be the guest's, nor a
2603/// selector procfs resolves per caller. Not a deleted directory
2604/// (`" (deleted)"`), an anonymous object or a relative target, nor any other
2605/// directory.
2606fn procfs_directory_link(link: &Path) -> bool {
2607    use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
2608    let bytes = link.as_os_str().as_bytes();
2609    link.starts_with("/proc")
2610        && !bytes.ends_with(b" (deleted)")
2611        && link.components().all(|component| match component {
2612            std::path::Component::RootDir => true,
2613            std::path::Component::Normal(name) => !name.as_bytes().iter().all(u8::is_ascii_digit),
2614            _ => false,
2615        })
2616        && crate::procfs::ids::named_ids(link).is_empty()
2617        && !crate::syscalls::namespace::names_through_caller_selector(link)
2618}
2619
2620/// Whether a stat call's own arguments are ones Linux accepts before it looks
2621/// up any file: `newfstatat` refuses unknown flags (`vfs_fstatat`), except on
2622/// the descriptor itself (`AT_EMPTY_PATH` with an empty path), which it
2623/// stats without looking at them (measured on Linux 7.1).
2624fn stat_family_arguments_valid<M: MemoryAccess>(memory: &M, call: &StatFamily) -> bool {
2625    match call {
2626        StatFamily::Fstatat(call) => {
2627            let known = libc::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW
2628                | libc::AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT
2629                | libc::AT_EMPTY_PATH
2630                | reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::AT_STATX_SYNC_TYPE;
2631            names_no_path(memory, call.path(), call.flags()) || call.flags().bits() & !known == 0
2632        }
2633        _ => true,
2634    }
2635}
2636
2637/// The file a call of the stat family describes.
2638fn stat_family_target<'a, M: MemoryAccess>(memory: &M, call: &'a StatFamily) -> StatTarget<'a> {
2639    match call {
2640        StatFamily::Fstat(call) => StatTarget::Descriptor(call.fd()),
2641        StatFamily::Fstatat(call) => {
2642            StatTarget::at(memory, call.dirfd(), call.path(), call.flags())
2643        }
2644        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
2645        StatFamily::Stat(call) => StatTarget::Path {
2646            dirfd: libc::AT_FDCWD,
2647            path: call.path(),
2648            follow: true,
2649        },
2650        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
2651        StatFamily::Lstat(call) => StatTarget::Path {
2652            dirfd: libc::AT_FDCWD,
2653            path: call.path(),
2654            follow: false,
2655        },
2656    }
2657}
2658
2659/// How many times Detcore injects the `openat` or the `close` of the
2660/// `O_PATH` descriptor it opens in the guest to name a procfs entry when the
2661/// call had no effect, before it records a determinism loss instead.
2662const OBJECT_DESCRIPTOR_ATTEMPTS: usize = 8;
2663
2664/// What Detcore learned of a stat result that may describe a procfs file
2665/// (see [`procfs_inode`]).
2666#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
2667enum ProcfsEntry {
2668    /// Not a file on a procfs mount, or a mode in which Detcore does not name
2669    /// procfs files.
2670    NotProcfs,
2671    /// A procfs file at this path within procfs.
2672    At(PathBuf),
2673    /// A procfs file that Detcore could not name. It recorded a determinism
2674    /// loss.
2675    Unnamed,
2676    /// A file Detcore could not tell from a procfs file, as it could not read
2677    /// the guest's mount table or the file's filesystem type, or did not look,
2678    /// as the guest's threads are not sequentialized. It recorded a
2679    /// determinism loss.
2680    Unknown,
2681}
2682
2683impl ProcfsEntry {
2684    /// Whether the file is known to be on a procfs mount.
2685    fn is_procfs(&self) -> bool {
2686        matches!(self, ProcfsEntry::At(_) | ProcfsEntry::Unnamed)
2687    }
2688
2689    /// The name of the file, which is on `device`.
2690    fn name(&self, device: u64) -> Option<ProcfsName> {
2691        match self {
2692            ProcfsEntry::At(within) => Some(ProcfsName::new(device, within)),
2693            ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs | ProcfsEntry::Unnamed | ProcfsEntry::Unknown => None,
2694        }
2695    }
2696}
2697
2698impl<T: RecordOrReplay> Detcore<T> {
2699    async fn observe_timer_slack_identity<G: Guest<Self>>(
2700        &self,
2701        guest: &mut G,
2702        target: i32,
2703    ) -> Result<Option<(u64, u64)>, Error> {
2704        // Re-resolve the numeric proc path on every operation. Linux gives a
2705        // recycled TID a different proc inode, while the original open file
2706        // description remains bound to the exited task's inode.
2707        // The kernel's number for the guest's (DBT; `procfs_numbers`): one
2708        // `/proc` does not list has no file to bind.
2709        let Some(target) = Self::kernel_procfs_number(guest, target).await else {
2710            return Ok(None);
2711        };
2712        let path = format!("/proc/{target}/timerslack_ns");
2713        let path_bytes = path.as_bytes();
2714        let mut path_buffer = [0_u8; 64];
2715        assert!(path_bytes.len() < path_buffer.len());
2716        path_buffer[..path_bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(path_bytes);
2717
2718        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
2719        let path_address = stack.push(path_buffer).cast::<libc::c_char>();
2720        let statptr = StatPtr(stack.reserve());
2721        let stack_guard = stack.commit()?;
2722        let call = syscalls::Fstatat::new()
2723            .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
2724            .with_path(PathPtr::from_ptr(
2725                path_address.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char
2726            ))
2727            .with_stat(Some(statptr))
2728            .with_flags(AtFlags::empty());
2729        let mut identity = match guest.inject_with_retry(call).await {
2730            Ok(_) => {
2731                let stat = statptr.read(&guest.memory())?;
2732                Some((stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino))
2733            }
2734            Err(Errno::ENOENT) | Err(Errno::ESRCH) => None,
2735            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
2736        };
2737        drop(stack_guard);
2738        // Replayer runs the guest in a filesystem chroot whose `/proc` path is
2739        // intentionally absent, while the tracing process remains in the same
2740        // PID namespace and can resolve the task through its own proc mount.
2741        // Use that equivalent view only for record/replay; other backends keep
2742        // the guest-path result above as their sole authority.
2743        if identity.is_none()
2744            && guest.config().recordreplay_modes
2745            && let Ok(metadata) = std::fs::metadata(path)
2746        {
2747            identity = Some((metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()));
2748        }
2749        Ok(identity)
2750    }
2751
2752    async fn require_current_timer_slack_target<G: Guest<Self>>(
2753        &self,
2754        guest: &mut G,
2755        binding: TimerSlackBinding,
2756    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
2757        let observed_identity = self
2758            .observe_timer_slack_identity(guest, binding.target)
2759            .await?;
2760        let current = guest.inject(syscalls::Gettid::new()).await? as i32;
2761        classify_timer_slack_binding(binding, observed_identity, current).map_err(Into::into)
2762    }
2763
2764    fn timer_slack_binding<G: Guest<Self>>(
2765        &self,
2766        guest: &G,
2767        fd: RawFd,
2768    ) -> Result<Option<TimerSlackBinding>, Errno> {
2769        guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2770            detfd
2771                .procfs_timer_slack_binding()
2772                .map(|(target, device, inode)| TimerSlackBinding {
2773                    target,
2774                    device,
2775                    inode,
2776                })
2777        })
2778    }
2779
2780    fn require_timer_slack_access<G: Guest<Self>>(
2781        &self,
2782        guest: &G,
2783        fd: RawFd,
2784        write: bool,
2785    ) -> Result<(), Errno> {
2786        guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2787            let flags = detfd.status_flags();
2788            let mode = flags & libc::O_ACCMODE;
2789            let denied = flags & libc::O_PATH != 0
2790                || if write {
2791                    mode == libc::O_RDONLY
2792                } else {
2793                    mode == libc::O_WRONLY
2794                };
2795            (!denied).then_some(()).ok_or(Errno::EBADF)
2796        })?
2797    }
2798
2799    fn read_timer_slack_input<G: Guest<Self>>(
2800        &self,
2801        guest: &G,
2802        buffer: Option<Addr<u8>>,
2803        count: usize,
2804    ) -> Result<u64, Errno> {
2805        let mut bytes = vec![0_u8; count.min(TIMER_SLACK_PARSE_BYTES)];
2806        if !bytes.is_empty() {
2807            guest
2808                .memory()
2809                .read_exact(buffer.ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?, &mut bytes)?;
2810        }
2811        parse_timer_slack_write(&bytes)
2812    }
2813
2814    async fn read_timer_slack<G: Guest<Self>>(
2815        &self,
2816        guest: &mut G,
2817        fd: RawFd,
2818        buffer: Option<AddrMut<'_, u8>>,
2819        maximum: usize,
2820    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
2821        self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, fd, false)?;
2822        if maximum == 0 {
2823            return Ok(0);
2824        }
2825        let binding = self
2826            .timer_slack_binding(guest, fd)?
2827            .expect("timer-slack read lost its procfs classification");
2828        self.require_current_timer_slack_target(guest, binding)
2829            .await?;
2830        let value = guest.thread_state().timer_slack_ns;
2831        let preview = guest
2832            .thread_state()
2833            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.preview_procfs_timer_slack(value, maximum))?
2834            .expect("timer-slack procfs state disappeared");
2835        let copied = copy_timer_slack_output(&mut guest.memory(), buffer, &preview.bytes)?;
2836        if copied != 0 {
2837            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2838                detfd.commit_procfs_timer_slack_read(&preview, copied);
2839            })?;
2840        }
2841        Ok(copied as i64)
2842    }
2843
2844    async fn pread_timer_slack<G: Guest<Self>>(
2845        &self,
2846        guest: &mut G,
2847        fd: RawFd,
2848        buffer: Option<AddrMut<'_, u8>>,
2849        maximum: usize,
2850        offset: i64,
2851    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
2852        if offset < 0 {
2853            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
2854        }
2855        self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, fd, false)?;
2856        if maximum == 0 {
2857            return Ok(0);
2858        }
2859        let binding = self
2860            .timer_slack_binding(guest, fd)?
2861            .expect("timer-slack pread lost its procfs classification");
2862        self.require_current_timer_slack_target(guest, binding)
2863            .await?;
2864        let value = guest.thread_state().timer_slack_ns;
2865        let bytes = guest
2866            .thread_state()
2867            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2868                detfd.take_procfs_timer_slack_at(value, offset as usize, maximum)
2869            })?
2870            .expect("timer-slack procfs state disappeared");
2871        Ok(copy_timer_slack_output(&mut guest.memory(), buffer, &bytes)? as i64)
2872    }
2873
2874    /// A vectored read of a procfs file Detcore renders: one read of its
2875    /// snapshot, as Linux's `read_iter` serves the whole vector at once,
2876    /// scattered over the `count` vectors at `address`, at `offset` or at
2877    /// (and advancing) the shared cursor. The order is `vfs_readv`'s: the
2878    /// descriptor's access mode, then the vectors' import (`EFAULT` for any
2879    /// destination outside the user address range, even at end of file), an
2880    /// empty vector (0), the range (`rw_verify_area`), and the flags.
2881    async fn readv_rendered_procfs<G: Guest<Self>>(
2882        &self,
2883        guest: &mut G,
2884        fd: RawFd,
2885        address: usize,
2886        count: usize,
2887        offset: Option<i64>,
2888        flags: i32,
2889    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
2890        let status = guest
2891            .thread_state()
2892            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.status_flags())?;
2893        if !can_read(status) {
2894            return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
2895        }
2896        let iovecs = crate::iovecs::import_read_iovecs(&guest.memory(), address, count, || {
2897            crate::iovecs::UserAddressLimit::from_query(guest.user_address_limit())
2898        })?;
2899        let maximum = iovecs.iter().map(|iovec| iovec.len).sum::<usize>();
2900        if maximum == 0 {
2901            return Ok(0);
2902        }
2903        // `rw_verify_area` checks the position the read starts at, explicit
2904        // or the shared cursor (`readv`, `preadv2` at -1), plus the whole
2905        // count, before the flags are looked at (fs/read_write.c
2906        // `vfs_readv`): an end past LLONG_MAX is EINVAL.
2907        let position = match offset {
2908            Some(offset) => offset,
2909            None => {
2910                self.adopt_rendered_procfs_position(guest, fd).await?;
2911                let cursor = guest
2912                    .thread_state()
2913                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_position())?
2914                    .map_or(0, |(position, _)| position);
2915                i64::try_from(cursor).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?
2916            }
2917        };
2918        if i64::try_from(maximum)
2919            .ok()
2920            .and_then(|maximum| position.checked_add(maximum))
2921            .is_none()
2922        {
2923            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
2924        }
2925        let read_iter = guest
2926            .thread_state()
2927            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_has_read_iter())?;
2928        validate_procfs_vector_flags(flags, read_iter)?;
2929        // A rendered `cmdline` has a plain `read`, which Linux calls once per
2930        // vector, in order, at the advancing position, stopping at the first
2931        // short or failed one (`do_loop_readv_writev`, fs/read_write.c), each
2932        // call reading memory again.
2933        if guest
2934            .thread_state()
2935            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_reads_memory_at_every_read())?
2936        {
2937            let start = position as u64;
2938            let mut total = 0_usize;
2939            for iovec in iovecs {
2940                match self
2941                    .read_rendered_cmdline(guest, fd, iovec.base, iovec.len, start + total as u64)
2942                    .await
2943                {
2944                    Ok(copied) => {
2945                        total += copied;
2946                        if copied != iovec.len {
2947                            break;
2948                        }
2949                    }
2950                    Err(error) if total == 0 => return Err(error),
2951                    Err(_) => break,
2952                }
2953            }
2954            if offset.is_none() {
2955                guest
2956                    .thread_state()
2957                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.commit_procfs_read(start as usize, total))?;
2958                self.sync_rendered_procfs_position(guest, fd).await?;
2959            }
2960            return Ok(total as i64);
2961        }
2962        // A rendered `stat` renders anew where the read does not continue
2963        // the sequence (`ProcfsFile::drop_stale_task_snapshot`).
2964        let renders_task_record = guest
2965            .thread_state()
2966            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_renders_task_record())?;
2967        let task_record_start = if renders_task_record {
2968            let start = usize::try_from(position).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
2969            guest
2970                .thread_state()
2971                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_drop_stale_task_snapshot(start))?;
2972            Some(start)
2973        } else {
2974            None
2975        };
2976        // A task's `schedstat` shows the runtime anew at a positioned read at
2977        // 0 (`ProcfsFile::drop_schedstat_snapshot_for_read_at`).
2978        if offset.is_some() {
2979            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2980                detfd.procfs_drop_schedstat_snapshot_for_read_at(position as u64)
2981            })?;
2982        }
2983        // A file the kernel opened takes its snapshot at its first read.
2984        if guest
2985            .thread_state()
2986            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_needs_snapshot())?
2987        {
2988            let rendered = self
2989                .initialize_procfs_snapshot(guest, syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(fd))
2990                .await;
2991            if let Some(start) = task_record_start {
2992                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2993                    detfd.procfs_note_task_record_rendered(start, rendered.is_ok())
2994                })?;
2995            }
2996            rendered?;
2997        } else if let Some(offset) = offset
2998            && !renders_task_record
2999            && guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3000                detfd
3001                    .procfs_position()
3002                    .is_some_and(|(position, _)| position as i64 != offset)
3003            })?
3004        {
3005            // A read at a position the buffered snapshot does not start at
3006            // runs a per-process file's `show` again (`traverse`).
3007            self.require_rendered_task(guest, fd).await?;
3008        }
3009        let start = match offset {
3010            Some(offset) => offset as usize,
3011            None => {
3012                self.adopt_rendered_procfs_position(guest, fd).await?;
3013                guest
3014                    .thread_state()
3015                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_position())?
3016                    .map_or(0, |(offset, _)| offset)
3017            }
3018        };
3019        let (bytes, faults_on_a_short_copy) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3020            (
3021                detfd.take_procfs_at(start, maximum).unwrap_or_default(),
3022                detfd.procfs_faults_on_a_short_copy(),
3023            )
3024        })?;
3025        // Like `copy_to_iter`, stop at the first byte that cannot be written,
3026        // leaving later vectors untouched.
3027        let mut copied = 0;
3028        for iovec in iovecs {
3029            if copied == bytes.len() {
3030                break;
3031            }
3032            if iovec.len == 0 {
3033                continue;
3034            }
3035            let end = (copied + iovec.len).min(bytes.len());
3036            let written = match copy_procfs_output(
3037                &mut guest.memory(),
3038                AddrMut::from_raw(iovec.base),
3039                &bytes[copied..end],
3040            ) {
3041                Ok(written) => written,
3042                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EFAULT)) => 0,
3043                Err(error) => return Err(error),
3044            };
3045            copied += written;
3046            if copied < end {
3047                break;
3048            }
3049        }
3050        if copied < bytes.len() && (faults_on_a_short_copy || copied == 0) {
3051            return Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
3052        }
3053        if offset.is_none() {
3054            guest
3055                .thread_state()
3056                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.commit_procfs_read(start, copied))?;
3057            self.sync_rendered_procfs_position(guest, fd).await?;
3058        } else {
3059            guest
3060                .thread_state()
3061                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_note_read_end(start + copied))?;
3062        }
3063        Ok(copied as i64)
3064    }
3065
3066    async fn readv_timer_slack<G: Guest<Self>>(
3067        &self,
3068        guest: &mut G,
3069        fd: RawFd,
3070        iovecs: Vec<TimerSlackIovec>,
3071        offset: Option<i64>,
3072        flags: i32,
3073    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
3074        self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, fd, false)?;
3075        let maximum = iovecs.iter().map(|iovec| iovec.len).sum::<usize>();
3076        if maximum == 0 {
3077            return Ok(0);
3078        }
3079        if flags & !libc::RWF_HIPRI != 0 {
3080            return Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP.into());
3081        }
3082        let binding = self
3083            .timer_slack_binding(guest, fd)?
3084            .expect("timer-slack readv lost its procfs classification");
3085        self.require_current_timer_slack_target(guest, binding)
3086            .await?;
3087        let value = guest.thread_state().timer_slack_ns;
3088        let mut positioned_offset = offset.map(|offset| offset as usize);
3089        let mut total = 0_usize;
3090        for iovec in iovecs {
3091            if iovec.len == 0 {
3092                continue;
3093            }
3094            let sequential_preview = if positioned_offset.is_none() {
3095                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3096                    detfd.preview_procfs_timer_slack(value, iovec.len)
3097                })?
3098            } else {
3099                None
3100            };
3101            let bytes = match (&sequential_preview, positioned_offset) {
3102                (Some(preview), None) => preview.bytes.clone(),
3103                (None, Some(offset)) => guest
3104                    .thread_state()
3105                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3106                        detfd.take_procfs_timer_slack_at(value, offset, iovec.len)
3107                    })?
3108                    .expect("timer-slack procfs state disappeared"),
3109                _ => unreachable!("timer-slack read mode changed while reading"),
3110            };
3111            if bytes.is_empty() {
3112                break;
3113            }
3114            let copied = match copy_timer_slack_output(
3115                &mut guest.memory(),
3116                AddrMut::from_raw(iovec.base),
3117                &bytes,
3118            ) {
3119                Ok(copied) => copied,
3120                Err(_) if total > 0 => return Ok(total as i64),
3121                Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
3122            };
3123            if let Some(preview) = &sequential_preview {
3124                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3125                    detfd.commit_procfs_timer_slack_read(preview, copied);
3126                })?;
3127            }
3128            total += copied;
3129            if let Some(offset) = positioned_offset.as_mut() {
3130                *offset += copied;
3131            }
3132            if copied != bytes.len() {
3133                return Ok(total as i64);
3134            }
3135            if bytes.len() != iovec.len {
3136                break;
3137            }
3138        }
3139        Ok(total as i64)
3140    }
