3142    async fn write_timer_slack<G: Guest<Self>>(
3143        &self,
3144        guest: &mut G,
3145        fd: RawFd,
3146        buffer: Option<Addr<'_, u8>>,
3147        count: usize,
3148    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
3149        self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, fd, true)?;
3150        let requested = self.read_timer_slack_input(guest, buffer, count)?;
3151        let binding = self
3152            .timer_slack_binding(guest, fd)?
3153            .expect("timer-slack write lost its procfs classification");
3154        self.require_current_timer_slack_target(guest, binding)
3155            .await?;
3156        let state = guest.thread_state_mut();
3157        state.timer_slack_ns = if requested == 0 {
3158            state.default_timer_slack_ns
3159        } else {
3160            requested
3161        };
3162        i64::try_from(count).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL.into())
3163    }
3164
3165    async fn writev_timer_slack<G: Guest<Self>>(
3166        &self,
3167        guest: &mut G,
3168        fd: RawFd,
3169        iovecs: Vec<TimerSlackIovec>,
3170        flags: i32,
3171    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
3172        self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, fd, true)?;
3173        if iovecs.iter().all(|iovec| iovec.len == 0) {
3174            return Ok(0);
3175        }
3176        if flags & !libc::RWF_HIPRI != 0 {
3177            return Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP.into());
3178        }
3179        // Procfs supplies only `.write`, so Linux's writev fallback invokes it
3180        // once per nonempty iovec. Preserve its partial-success behavior and
3181        // let the last successful segment determine the current slack.
3182        let mut total = 0_i64;
3183        for iovec in iovecs {
3184            if iovec.len == 0 {
3185                continue;
3186            }
3187            let buffer = Addr::from_raw(iovec.base).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT);
3188            let requested = match buffer
3189                .and_then(|buffer| self.read_timer_slack_input(guest, Some(buffer), iovec.len))
3190            {
3191                Ok(requested) => requested,
3192                Err(_error) if total > 0 => return Ok(total),
3193                Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
3194            };
3195            let binding = self
3196                .timer_slack_binding(guest, fd)?
3197                .expect("timer-slack writev lost its procfs classification");
3198            if let Err(error) = self
3199                .require_current_timer_slack_target(guest, binding)
3200                .await
3201            {
3202                return if total > 0 { Ok(total) } else { Err(error) };
3203            }
3204            let state = guest.thread_state_mut();
3205            state.timer_slack_ns = if requested == 0 {
3206                state.default_timer_slack_ns
3207            } else {
3208                requested
3209            };
3210            total = total
3211                .checked_add(i64::try_from(iovec.len).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?)
3212                .ok_or(Errno::EINVAL)?;
3213        }
3214        Ok(total)
3215    }
3216    /// Set the kernel's O_NONBLOCK on `fd`'s open file description, keeping its
3217    /// other status flags. The caller records the change with
3218    /// `maybe_set_nonblocking_fd`; the guest-visible flags are unchanged.
3219    async fn inject_physical_nonblocking<G: Guest<Self>>(
3220        &self,
3221        guest: &mut G,
3222        fd: RawFd,
3223    ) -> Result<(), Errno> {
3224        let flags = guest
3225            .inject(syscalls::Fcntl::new().with_fd(fd).with_cmd(F_GETFL))
3226            .await?;
3227        guest
3228            .inject(
3229                syscalls::Fcntl::new()
3230                    .with_fd(fd)
3231                    .with_cmd(F_SETFL(flags as i32 | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK.bits())),
3232            )
3233            .await?;
3234        Ok(())
3235    }
3236
3237    /// A blocking `openat` of the FIFO `fifo` (found by the tracer at `path`),
3238    /// which a guest made in this run (`crate::fifo_peer::is_guest_made`), for
3239    /// reading or for writing. On Linux it waits in the kernel until the other
3240    /// end is open; injected as is, it would wait while it holds the scheduler
3241    /// turn, and a guest that opens the other end could never run
3242    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/2203>).
3243    ///
3244    /// First the open is tried nonblocking. Any error other than "no reader
3245    /// yet" (`ENXIO`, for a writer) is the open's own, returned at once, as
3246    /// Linux returns it before waiting (`EEXIST`, `ENOENT`, `EACCES`, ...), and
3247    /// nothing else is opened. A writer that finds a reader completes then, as
3248    /// does a reader whose writer a guest holds or waits to open. Otherwise the
3249    /// open waits in polling turns ([`crate::fifo_peer::PendingOpen`]), and the
3250    /// guest's try is closed in the same turn, so no sibling sees a descriptor
3251    /// for it. It waits until a guest holds the other end, is waiting to open
3252    /// it, or has opened it since, then opens nonblocking and is made
3253    /// blocking, as the guest asked.
3254    ///
3255    /// A signal ends the wait as Linux's: `ERESTARTSYS`, which the kernel turns
3256    /// into `EINTR` or a restart by the guest's disposition.
3257    ///
3258    /// When the scheduler answers that nothing else can run
3259    /// (`ResumeStatus::NothingElseCanRun`), no guest can open the other end,
3260    /// so the open is made as the guest asked, waiting in the kernel while it
3261    /// holds the turn, as without the poll: only a host could complete it.
3262    ///
3263    /// Either way the open completes on the FIFO it waited on
3264    /// ([`Self::open_fifo_waited_on`]).
3265    async fn open_fifo_once_a_guest_holds_its_peer<G: Guest<Self>>(
3266        &self,
3267        guest: &mut G,
3268        call: syscalls::Openat,
3269        fifo: (u64, u64),
3270        path: &std::ffi::OsStr,
3271    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
3272        let reading = call.flags().bits() & libc::O_ACCMODE == libc::O_RDONLY;
3273        let peer = if reading {
3274            FifoPeer::Writer
3275        } else {
3276            FifoPeer::Reader
3277        };
3278        let nonblocking = call.with_flags(call.flags() | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK);
3279        let opens_before = crate::fifo_peer::guest_opens(fifo);
3280        // Guest state only, which changes in guest turns: the answer at each
3281        // polling turn is deterministic.
3282        let guest_peer_ready = || {
3283            crate::fifo_peer::guest_holds_peer_of(fifo, peer)
3284                || crate::fifo_peer::pending_opens(fifo).of(peer) > 0
3285                || crate::fifo_peer::guest_opens(fifo).of(peer) > opens_before.of(peer)
3286        };
3287        // A nonblocking FIFO open never waits, so an injection a signal
3288        // interrupts did not run, and is made again; the signal is delivered
3289        // as the guest resumes.
3290        // Each try is one injection, its path respelled for that injection
3291        // alone where it leads below a descriptor directory
3292        // (`Self::inject_translated`): nothing staged outlives a try, or the
3293        // polling turns between them.
3294        let pending =
3295            match Self::inject_translated_retrying(guest, Syscall::from(nonblocking), true).await {
3296                // A writer found a reader: Linux's open completes at once.
3297                Ok(fd) if !reading => return Ok(self.make_blocking(guest, fd as RawFd).await?),
3298                Ok(fd) if guest_peer_ready() => {
3299                    crate::fifo_peer::stand_in_for_waiting_writers(fifo, path);
3300                    return Ok(self.make_blocking(guest, fd as RawFd).await?);
3301                }
3302                Ok(fd) => {
3303                    // The tracer's reader opens before the guest's try closes, so
3304                    // the FIFO keeps a reader throughout.
3305                    let pending =
3306                        crate::fifo_peer::PendingOpen::begin(fifo, path, call.flags().bits());
3307                    guest
3308                        .inject_with_retry(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd as RawFd))
3309                        .await?;
3310                    pending
3311                }
3312                Err(Errno::ENXIO) if !reading => {
3313                    crate::fifo_peer::PendingOpen::begin(fifo, path, call.flags().bits())
3314                }
3315                Err(errno) => return Err(errno.into()),
3316            };
3317        info!("[detcore] the FIFO open polls for a guest peer");
3318        // A waiting open is an end on Linux: it readies the opens waiting for
3319        // this end (`--pipe-wake-latency`).
3320        let in_effect = self.cfg.pipe_wake_latency_in_effect().is_some();
3321        let channel = crate::pipe_wake::ChannelId::Fifo(if in_effect {
3322            crate::fifo_peer::fifo_channel(fifo)
3323        } else {
3324            0
3325        });
3326        let (readies, waits_for) = if reading {
3327            (
3328                crate::pipe_wake::Wants::PeerReader,
3329                crate::pipe_wake::Wants::PeerWriter,
3330            )
3331        } else {
3332            (
3333                crate::pipe_wake::Wants::PeerWriter,
3334                crate::pipe_wake::Wants::PeerReader,
3335            )
3336        };
3337        self.note_pipe_readied(guest, channel, readies).await;
3338
3339        let mut resources = Resources::new(guest.thread_state().dettid);
3340        resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
3341        resources.fyi(call.name());
3342        resources.polls_guest_state_only = true;
3343        resources.waits_until_nothing_else_can_run = true;
3344        if in_effect {
3345            resources.polls_channel = Some(Box::new((channel, waits_for)));
3346        }
3347        // As a polled pipe read: a signal another task sends ends the wait.
3348        resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
3349        resources.signal_state_task = crate::syscalls::helpers::guest_signal_state_task(guest);
3350        // The peer is checked again after every answer, the last one included:
3351        // a guest may have opened (and closed) the other end in the turns
3352        // before it.
3353        loop {
3354            let status = resource_request(guest, resources.clone()).await;
3355            resources.poll_attempt += 1;
3356            if guest_peer_ready() {
3357                break;
3358            }
3359            match status {
3360                ResumeStatus::Signaled(_) => return Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into()),
3361                ResumeStatus::NothingElseCanRun => {
3362                    info!(
3363                        "[detcore] nothing else can run; the FIFO open waits in the kernel, as without the poll"
3364                    );
3365                    let waited_on = pending.guest_path();
3366                    return self
3367                        .open_fifo_waited_on(
3368                            guest,
3369                            call,
3370                            fifo,
3371                            waited_on.as_deref(),
3372                            call.flags(),
3373                            false,
3374                        )
3375                        .await;
3376                }
3377                _ => {}
3378            }
3379        }
3380        let waited_on = pending.guest_path();
3381        let open = async |guest: &mut G| {
3382            self.open_fifo_waited_on(
3383                guest,
3384                call,
3385                fifo,
3386                waited_on.as_deref(),
3387                nonblocking.flags(),
3388                true,
3389            )
3390            .await
3391        };
3392        let mut opened = open(guest).await;
3393        if matches!(opened, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ENXIO))) {
3394            // A writer whose only reader has come and gone opens as Linux's did
3395            // when the reader opened; the tracer stands in for that reader while
3396            // the guest opens, so the guest's writes then fail with `EPIPE`, as
3397            // on Linux.
3398            let _stand_in = pending.open_in_tracer(libc::O_RDONLY);
3399            opened = open(guest).await;
3400        }
3401        if reading && opened.is_ok() {
3402            pending.stand_in_for_waiting_writers();
3403        }
3404        drop(pending);
3405        Ok(self.make_blocking(guest, opened? as RawFd).await?)
3406    }
3407
3408    /// Open, in the guest, the FIFO `fifo` a blocking open waited on, with
3409    /// the guest's `flags`, whatever its name is now: through the tracer's
3410    /// descriptor for it, `waited_on` ([`Self::open_waited_on_fifo`]).
3411    ///
3412    /// The kernel lets a guest into the tracer's descriptors only if it holds
3413    /// `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` or every capability the tracer has
3414    /// (`proc_fd_access_allowed`), and only if the tracer's `/proc` is under
3415    /// its root; and a root whose `/proc` is not the tracer's may name another
3416    /// file at that path, so what it opened is checked to be the FIFO, and
3417    /// closed if not. A guest that cannot reach the descriptor (`EACCES`,
3418    /// `ENOENT`, another file), or whose open waited without one (`waited_on`
3419    /// is `None`),
3420    /// opens the FIFO by the name it gave, as its first try did, provided the
3421    /// name still reaches that FIFO: looked up first, so that no other file
3422    /// is opened, and checked again once open. If the name reaches another
3423    /// file or none, the open cannot complete on its FIFO, as Linux's does,
3424    /// and is refused (Claude re-check of
3425    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4329> at revision 4,
3426    /// MEDIUM-A).
3427    ///
3428    /// Either way this is a new open, so the FIFO's mode is checked again
3429    /// against the guest's credentials when it completes: a FIFO whose mode
3430    /// the guest may no longer open (a `chmod` during the wait) gives
3431    /// `EACCES`, where Linux checked only at the start.
3432    ///
3433    /// `retry`: an open that cannot wait (nonblocking), which a signal stops
3434    /// only before it runs. `ENXIO` (a writer whose reader is gone) and
3435    /// `ERESTARTSYS` (a signal ended a blocking open) are the caller's.
3436    async fn open_fifo_waited_on<G: Guest<Self>>(
3437        &self,
3438        guest: &mut G,
3439        call: syscalls::Openat,
3440        fifo: (u64, u64),
3441        waited_on: Option<&str>,
3442        flags: OFlag,
3443        retry: bool,
3444    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
3445        let is_the_fifo = |stat: &libc::stat| (stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino) == fifo;
3446        let unreachable = match waited_on {
3447            Some(waited_on) => {
3448                match Self::open_waited_on_fifo(guest, fifo, waited_on, flags, retry).await {
3449                    Err(errno) if !matches!(errno, Errno::ENXIO | Errno::ERESTARTSYS) => {
3450                        Some(errno)
3451                    }
3452                    // A root whose `/proc` is not the tracer's can name
3453                    // another file at that path (Claude re-check at
3454                    // revision 5, LOW-C).
3455                    Ok(fd)
3456                        if !self
3457                            .inject_fstat(guest, fd as RawFd)
3458                            .await
3459                            .is_ok_and(|stat| is_the_fifo(&stat)) =>
3460                    {
3461                        info!(
3462                            "[detcore] the tracer's descriptor path reached another file in the guest's root"
3463                        );
3464                        guest
3465                            .inject_with_retry(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd as RawFd))
3466                            .await?;
3467                        Some(Errno::ENOENT)
3468                    }
3469                    opened => return Ok(opened?),
3470                }
3471            }
3472            None => None,
3473        };
3474        if let Some(errno) = unreachable {
3475            info!(
3476                "[detcore] the guest cannot reach the tracer's descriptor for the FIFO ({}); it opens the FIFO by its name",
3477                errno
3478            );
3479        }
3480        let path = call.path().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
3481        let lookup = if flags.contains(OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW) {
3482            AtFlags::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW
3483        } else {
3484            AtFlags::empty()
3485        };
3486        if Self::inject_statat(guest, call.dirfd(), path, [Some(path), None], lookup)
3487            .await
3488            .is_ok_and(|stat| is_the_fifo(&stat))
3489        {
3490            // The name was checked by the first try, and reaches the FIFO:
3491            // nothing is created.
3492            let open = call.with_flags(flags - (OFlag::O_CREAT | OFlag::O_EXCL));
3493            let fd = Self::inject_translated_retrying(guest, Syscall::from(open), retry).await?;
3494            if self
3495                .inject_fstat(guest, fd as RawFd)
3496                .await
3497                .is_ok_and(|stat| is_the_fifo(&stat))
3498            {
3499                return Ok(fd);
3500            }
3501            guest
3502                .inject_with_retry(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd as RawFd))
3503                .await?;
3504        }
3505        error!(
3506            "[detcore] a blocking open of a FIFO a guest made waited for its peer, and cannot complete \
3507             on that FIFO: the guest cannot reach the tracer's descriptor for it, and its name no \
3508             longer reaches it (a guest without CAP_SYS_PTRACE, or without the tracer's /proc, whose \
3509             FIFO was renamed or unlinked during the wait); refused \
3510             (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4329)"
3511        );
3512        self.refuse_unserviceable_operation(
3513            guest,
3514            Sysno::openat,
3515            unreachable.unwrap_or(Errno::ENOENT),
3516        )
3517        .await
3518    }
3519
3520    /// Open, in the guest, the FIFO a waiting open waited on, at `waited_on`
3521    /// (`fifo_peer::PendingOpen::guest_path`), with the guest's `flags`: the
3522    /// checks of its name were made by the first try, so `O_CREAT`, `O_EXCL`
3523    /// and `O_NOFOLLOW` go (the path is the tracer's descriptor link).
3524    /// `retry`: an open that cannot wait (nonblocking), which a signal stops
3525    /// only before it runs.
3526    ///
3527    /// The path is staged in a private page mapped for this open only, not
3528    /// in the guest stack scratch, so that an open needs no spare stack
3529    /// below the guest's stack pointer, which Linux's does not (Codex
3530    /// re-check of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4329> at revision
3531    /// 4, P2). The page is unmapped before the guest resumes, so the guest's
3532    /// memory keeps no tracer descriptor number (Claude's LOW-B there). An
3533    /// error mapping or writing the page is returned, and the caller opens
3534    /// the FIFO by its name instead.
3535    ///
3536    /// A task killed while the open waits in the kernel drops this call
3537    /// before its unmap; the page is then unmapped by the next task of the
3538    /// same address space to reach Detcore
3539    /// ([`crate::fifo_peer::StagedPage`], [`Self::unmap_orphaned_staging_pages`]).
3540    ///
3541    /// What the path names is looked up first, and must be the FIFO `fifo`:
3542    /// a root whose `/proc` is not the tracer's can name another file there,
3543    /// which is not opened (`ESTALE`; Claude re-check at revision 6, LOW-H).
3544    async fn open_waited_on_fifo<G: Guest<Self>>(
3545        guest: &mut G,
3546        fifo: (u64, u64),
3547        waited_on: &str,
3548        flags: OFlag,
3549        retry: bool,
3550    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
3551        let mut path_buffer = [0_u8; crate::fifo_peer::STAGED_PAGE_LENGTH];
3552        let bytes = waited_on.as_bytes();
3553        if bytes.len() >= path_buffer.len() {
3554            return Err(Errno::ENAMETOOLONG);
3555        }
3556        path_buffer[..bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
3557        // The page's owner exists before its `mmap` runs, at an address
3558        // chosen first: a task killed during the `mmap` leaves its address
3559        // space's next task an address to check.
3560        let address =
3561            crate::fifo_peer::free_staging_address(guest.tid().as_raw()).ok_or(Errno::ENOMEM)?;
3562        let page = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(address).ok_or(Errno::ENOMEM)?;
3563        let staged =
3564            crate::fifo_peer::StagedPage::new(guest.thread_state().mm_id, address, path_buffer);
3565        match guest
3566            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
3567                syscalls::Mmap::new()
3568                    .with_addr(Some(page.cast::<libc::c_void>().into()))
3569                    .with_len(path_buffer.len())
3570                    .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
3571                    .with_flags(
3572                        MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE
3573                            | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS
3574                            | MapFlags::MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE,
3575                    )
3576                    .with_fd(-1)
3577                    .with_offset(0),
3578            ))
3579            .await
3580        {
3581            Ok(mapped) if mapped as usize == address => {
3582                crate::race_probe::delay(crate::race_probe::FIFO_STAGING_MAPPED).await;
3583            }
3584            // Nothing was mapped at the address (`EEXIST`: something is
3585            // there): this route is not taken.
3586            Err(errno) => {
3587                staged.unmapped();
3588                return Err(errno);
3589            }
3590            // A kernel without MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE takes the address as a
3591            // hint and maps elsewhere.
3592            Ok(mapped) => {
3593                staged.unmapped();
3594                if let Some(elsewhere) = Addr::<libc::c_void>::from_raw(mapped as usize) {
3595                    let _ = guest
3596                        .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
3597                            syscalls::Munmap::new()
3598                                .with_addr(Some(elsewhere))
3599                                .with_len(path_buffer.len()),
3600                        ))
3601                        .await;
3602                }
3603                return Err(Errno::ENOMEM);
3604            }
3605        }
3606        let path = PathPtr::from_ptr(page.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char)
3607            .expect("a mapped page is not null");
3608        let opened = match guest.memory().write_exact(page, &path_buffer) {
3609            Ok(()) => match Self::inject_statat(
3610                guest,
3611                libc::AT_FDCWD,
3612                path,
3613                [Some(path), None],
3614                AtFlags::empty(),
3615            )
3616            .await
3617            {
3618                Ok(stat) if (stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino) == fifo => {
3619                    let open = syscalls::Openat::new()
3620                        .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
3621                        .with_path(Some(path))
3622                        .with_flags(flags - (OFlag::O_CREAT | OFlag::O_EXCL | OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW))
3623                        .with_mode(None);
3624                    if retry {
3625                        guest.inject_with_retry(open).await
3626                    } else {
3627                        guest.inject(open).await
3628                    }
3629                }
3630                Ok(_) => {
3631                    info!(
3632                        "[detcore] the tracer's descriptor path names another file in the guest's root"
3633                    );
3634                    Err(Errno::ESTALE)
3635                }
3636                Err(errno) => Err(errno),
3637            },
3638            Err(error) => Err(error),
3639        };
3640        match guest
3641            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
3642                syscalls::Munmap::new()
3643                    .with_addr(Some(page.cast::<libc::c_void>().into()))
3644                    .with_len(path_buffer.len()),
3645            ))
3646            .await
3647        {
3648            Ok(_) => staged.unmapped(),
3649            // An unmap that did not run (stopped before it ran) is left, with
3650            // the guard, to this address space's next task.
3651            Err(errno) => info!(
3652                "[detcore] the transient FIFO path page is left to the next task: {}",
3653                errno
3654            ),
3655        }
3656        opened
3657    }
3658
3659    /// Unmap the pages a completing FIFO open staged in this task's address
3660    /// space and could not unmap, because its task went away while the open
3661    /// waited ([`crate::fifo_peer::StagedPage`]). Called as a task reaches
3662    /// Detcore, before it runs guest code again; costs one load while no page
3663    /// is left.
3664    pub(crate) async fn unmap_orphaned_staging_pages<G: Guest<Self>>(guest: &mut G) {
3665        // Each taken page is owned by its guard until it is unmapped: one this
3666        // task does not get to (its unmap does not run, or the task exits
3667        // while it waits) is left again.
3668        for page in crate::fifo_peer::take_orphaned_pages(guest.thread_state().mm_id) {
3669            // Only a page that still holds what was staged: the guest may have
3670            // unmapped it and mapped something else there.
3671            let mut contents = [0_u8; crate::fifo_peer::STAGED_PAGE_LENGTH];
3672            let Some(address) = Addr::<u8>::from_raw(page.address()) else {
3673                page.unmapped();
3674                continue;
3675            };
3676            let readable = guest.memory().read_exact(address, &mut contents).is_ok();
3677            // A task killed during the `mmap` may have left the page before
3678            // anything was written to it: a page of zeros is the staging page
3679            // only where it is a lone one-page anonymous mapping.
3680            if !readable
3681                || (contents != *page.contents()
3682                    && !(contents == [0; crate::fifo_peer::STAGED_PAGE_LENGTH]
3683                        && crate::fifo_peer::is_lone_staging_mapping(
3684                            guest.tid().as_raw(),
3685                            page.address(),
3686                        )))
3687            {
3688                info!("[detcore] a FIFO open's path page that a killed task left is gone");
3689                page.unmapped();
3690                continue;
3691            }
3692            info!("[detcore] unmapping a FIFO open's path page that a killed task left");
3693            crate::race_probe::delay(crate::race_probe::FIFO_STAGING_RECLAIM).await;
3694            let unmapped = guest
3695                .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
3696                    syscalls::Munmap::new()
3697                        .with_addr(Addr::<libc::c_void>::from_raw(page.address()))
3698                        .with_len(contents.len()),
3699                ))
3700                .await;
3701            match unmapped {
3702                Ok(_) => page.unmapped(),
3703                Err(Errno::EINVAL) => {
3704                    warn!(
3705                        "[detcore] could not unmap the transient FIFO path page: {}",
3706                        Errno::EINVAL
3707                    );
3708                    page.unmapped();
3709                }
3710                // Stopped before it ran: the guard leaves it to the next task
3711                // (Claude re-check at revision 6, MEDIUM-G).
3712                Err(errno) => info!(
3713                    "[detcore] the transient FIFO path page is left to the next task: {}",
3714                    errno
3715                ),
3716            }
3717        }
3718    }
3719
3720    /// Clear `O_NONBLOCK` on the guest's FIFO descriptor `fd`, which was opened
3721    /// nonblocking in place of a blocking open, and return it.
3722    async fn make_blocking<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &mut G, fd: RawFd) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
3723        let flags = guest
3724            .inject_with_retry(syscalls::Fcntl::new().with_fd(fd).with_cmd(F_GETFL))
3725            .await?;
3726        guest
3727            .inject_with_retry(
3728                syscalls::Fcntl::new()
3729                    .with_fd(fd)
3730                    .with_cmd(F_SETFL(flags as i32 & !OFlag::O_NONBLOCK.bits())),
3731            )
3732            .await?;
3733        Ok(fd as i64)
3734    }
3735
3736    /// Before a logically blocking read (`peer` is `Writer`) or write
3737    /// (`Reader`) on a FIFO that `handle_openat` marked: if a guest holds the
3738    /// other end (`crate::fifo_peer`), shrink the FIFO's capacity to the one
3739    /// `handle_pipe2` pins a pipe to (never growing one the guest shrank), make
3740    /// it physically nonblocking, and treat it from then on as a
3741    /// scheduler-managed pipe. The call then polls in
3742    /// turns instead of blocking in the kernel while it holds the turn, where
3743    /// the guest at the other end could never run
3744    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4200>). A FIFO whose other
3745    /// ends are all on the host is left blocking, as before.
3746    ///
3747    /// The open file description may be shared with another process that
3748    /// already made this change: the kernel then reports it nonblocking while
3749    /// this process still sees it blocking, and this process follows. On
3750    /// ptrace a forked child shares the parent's model (`fork_for` clones the
3751    /// `Arc`), so it sees the change at once; this branch is for a backend
3752    /// whose fork copies the model into the child's address space (DBT), and
3753    /// the ptrace tests do not reach it.
3754    /// Shrink a FIFO that is about to be polled as a pipe to the capacity
3755    /// `handle_pipe2` pins a pipe to, if it is larger, so that its partial
3756    /// writes do not depend on the host's pipe defaults. A capacity the guest
3757    /// set smaller is kept, as Linux keeps it. The kernel refuses (`EBUSY`)
3758    /// while more is buffered than the new capacity holds; the FIFO is then
3759    /// polled at its current capacity, which only that buffered amount
3760    /// decides.
3761    async fn shrink_fifo_capacity<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &mut G, fd: RawFd) {
3762        let Ok(capacity) = guest
3763            .inject(syscalls::Fcntl::new().with_fd(fd).with_cmd(F_GETPIPE_SZ))
3764            .await
3765        else {
3766            return;
3767        };
3768        if capacity > i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes())
3769            && let Err(errno) = guest
3770                .inject(
3771                    syscalls::Fcntl::new()
3772                        .with_fd(fd)
3773                        .with_cmd(F_SETPIPE_SZ(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes())),
3774                )
3775                .await
3776        {
3777            info!(
3778                "[detcore] FIFO fd {} keeps its {}-byte capacity: shrinking it failed with {}",
3779                fd, capacity, errno
3780            );
3781        }
3782    }
3783
3784    async fn fifo_polls_if_a_guest_holds_its_peer<G: Guest<Self>>(
3785        &self,
3786        guest: &mut G,
3787        fd: RawFd,
3788        peer: FifoPeer,
3789    ) {
3790        let Ok((awaiting, logically_nonblocking)) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3791            (detfd.fifo_awaiting_guest_peer(), detfd.is_nonblocking())
3792        }) else {
3793            return;
3794        };
3795        if !awaiting || logically_nonblocking {
3796            return;
3797        }
3798        // The calling thread's own table: it may not be its leader's (a thread
3799        // cloned without CLONE_FILES), and `fd` is changed in this one.
3800        let tid = guest.tid().as_raw();
3801        let kernel_nonblocking = crate::fifo_peer::kernel_nonblocking(tid, fd);
3802        let joins = match kernel_nonblocking {
3803            Some(true) => true,
3804            Some(false) => crate::fifo_peer::guest_holds_peer(tid, fd, peer),
3805            None => false,
3806        };
3807        if !joins {
3808            return;
3809        }
3810        // A FIFO the scheduler polls is polled at its capacity, which host
3811        // load chooses where `pipe-max-size` is below two pages.
3812        if !host_pipe_floor() {
3813            self.refuse_below_two_page_pipe_floor(
3814                guest,
3815                &format!("FIFO fd {fd} has a guest at its other end and would be polled as a pipe"),
3816            )
3817            .await;
3818        }
3819        if kernel_nonblocking == Some(false) {
3820            self.shrink_fifo_capacity(guest, fd).await;
3821            if self.inject_physical_nonblocking(guest, fd).await.is_err() {
3822                return;
3823            }
3824        }
3825        info!(
3826            "[detcore] fd {} is a FIFO with a guest at its other end; polling it as a pipe",
3827            fd
3828        );
3829        let _ = guest
3830            .thread_state()
3831            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.fifo_joins_internal_polling());
3832    }
3833
3834    /// Ends the run where a pipe's capacity is one host load chose
3835    /// ([`host_pipe_floor`]), for `what`.
3836    async fn refuse_below_two_page_pipe_floor<G: Guest<Self>>(
3837        &self,
3838        guest: &mut G,
3839        what: &str,
3840    ) -> ! {
3841        error!("{}", below_two_page_pipe_floor(what));
3842        unrecoverable_shutdown(guest, detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT).await
3843    }

3845    /// Inject an extra fstat to retrieve file metadata.
3846    ///
3847    /// The kernel needs a writable `struct stat` in the guest. It is staged
3848    /// first in the guest stack scratch, which on the ptrace backend lies just
3849    /// below the red zone under the guest's stack pointer and costs nothing
3850    /// when the stack has room. That memory is not guaranteed to be writable:
3851    /// the guest may run with its stack pointer just above a guard page (a
3852    /// thread, fiber or alternate signal stack), or within a few hundred bytes
3853    /// of the lowest page of the main-thread stack, which a tracer's write does
3854    /// not grow. The fault then belongs to Detcore's bookkeeping, not to the
3855    /// guest, so the same fstat is repeated with its buffer in a transient
3856    /// private page that is unmapped before the guest resumes
3857    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3328>).
3858    pub(crate) async fn inject_fstat<G: Guest<Self>>(
3859        &self,
3860        guest: &mut G,
3861        raw_fd: RawFd,
3862    ) -> Result<libc::stat, Errno> {
3863        crate::ordered_info!(
3864            "Injecting additional fstat to retrieve file metadata on fd {}.",
3865            raw_fd
3866        );
3867        let fstat = move |statptr: StatPtr<'_>| {
3868            Syscall::Fstat(
3869                syscalls::Fstat::new()
3870                    .with_fd(raw_fd)
3871                    .with_stat(Some(statptr)),
3872            )
3873        };
3874        let copied = Self::stat_with_fallback(guest, raw_fd, fstat, None)
3875            .await
3876            .map_err(StatFailure::errno)?;
3877        trace!("extra fstat returned inode {}", copied.st_ino);
3878        Ok(copied)
3879    }
3880
3881    /// `stat_call` for descriptor `raw_fd` with its buffer in the guest stack
3882    /// scratch or, where the scratch cannot hold it (the commit or the call
3883    /// faults), in a transient private page; see [`Self::inject_fstat`].
3884    /// `recorded` routes the call through that Detcore's recording
3885    /// ([`Self::recorded_fstat`]); `None` injects it.
3886    async fn stat_with_fallback<G: Guest<Self>>(
3887        guest: &mut G,
3888        raw_fd: RawFd,
3889        stat_call: impl Fn(StatPtr<'_>) -> Syscall + Copy,
3890        recorded: Option<&Self>,
3891    ) -> Result<libc::stat, StatFailure> {
3892        match Self::inject_stat_on_stack(guest, stat_call, recorded).await {
3893            Err(StatFailure::Scratch(Errno::EFAULT) | StatFailure::Call(Errno::EFAULT)) => {
3894                info!(
3895                    "Guest stack scratch cannot hold the fstat buffer for fd {}; \
3896                     using a transient page instead.",
3897                    raw_fd
3898                );
3899                Self::inject_stat_in_transient_page(guest, stat_call, recorded).await
3900            }
3901            result => result,
3902        }
3903    }
3904
3905    /// `fstatat(dirfd, path, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` for a path the guest named
3906    /// in a call that has not run yet and must still read `inputs`, its paths
3907    /// ([`Detcore::inject_statat`]).
3908    async fn inject_lstatat<G: Guest<Self>>(
3909        guest: &mut G,
3910        dirfd: RawFd,
3911        path: syscalls::PathPtr<'_>,
3912        inputs: [Option<syscalls::PathPtr<'_>>; 2],
3913    ) -> Result<libc::stat, Errno> {
3914        Self::inject_statat(guest, dirfd, path, inputs, AtFlags::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW).await
3915    }
3916
3917    /// `fstatat(dirfd, path, flags)` for a path the guest named in a call that
3918    /// has not run yet and must still read `inputs`, its paths.
3919    ///
3920    /// The buffer is staged as the utimensat target lookup stages its own: in
3921    /// the guest stack scratch, below the red zone, where a raw syscall may
3922    /// keep its own path, so only when it overlaps none of `inputs`, and with
3923    /// the bytes under it saved and put back after the commit and after the
3924    /// lookup, so that the call reads its inputs unchanged (claude review of
3925    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3849>, P3-2). Otherwise it is
3926    /// a transient private page, unmapped before the guest resumes.
3927    pub(crate) async fn inject_statat<G: Guest<Self>>(
3928        guest: &mut G,
3929        dirfd: RawFd,
3930        path: syscalls::PathPtr<'_>,
3931        inputs: [Option<syscalls::PathPtr<'_>>; 2],
3932        flags: AtFlags,
3933    ) -> Result<libc::stat, Errno> {
3934        // A `/proc` path naming a process or thread by the guest's number
3935        // is looked up by the kernel's (DBT), as the guest's own call is
3936        // (`procfs_numbers`).
3937        let probe = crate::arch::fstatat_syscall(
3938            syscalls::Fstatat::new()
3939                .with_dirfd(dirfd)
3940                .with_path(Some(path))
3941                .with_flags(flags),
3942        );
3943        let Some(translated) = Self::procfs_translated_call(guest, &probe).await? else {
3944            return Self::inject_statat_as_spelled(guest, dirfd, path, inputs, flags).await;
3945        };
3946        // The one path, where the translation staged it, looked up from the
3947        // directory it gives (`AT_FDCWD` for a path respelled below a
3948        // descriptor directory).
3949        let (_, staged) = translated.call.into_parts();
3950        let respelled = PathPtr::from_ptr(staged.arg1 as *const libc::c_char);
3951        let dirfd = staged.arg0 as RawFd;
3952        let looked_up = match respelled {
3953            Some(respelled) => {
3954                Self::inject_statat_as_spelled(
3955                    guest,
3956                    dirfd,
3957                    respelled,
3958                    [Some(respelled), None],
3959                    flags,
3960                )
3961                .await
3962            }
3963            None => Err(Errno::ENOMEM),
3964        };
3965        Self::finish_translated_call(guest, translated).await;
3966        looked_up
3967    }
3968
3969    /// [`Self::inject_statat`] of `path` as it is spelled.
3970    async fn inject_statat_as_spelled<G: Guest<Self>>(
3971        guest: &mut G,
3972        dirfd: RawFd,
3973        path: syscalls::PathPtr<'_>,
3974        inputs: [Option<syscalls::PathPtr<'_>>; 2],
3975        flags: AtFlags,
3976    ) -> Result<libc::stat, Errno> {
3977        let lstatat = move |statptr: StatPtr<'_>| {
3978            crate::arch::fstatat_syscall(
3979                syscalls::Fstatat::new()
3980                    .with_dirfd(dirfd)
3981                    .with_path(Some(path))
3982                    .with_stat(Some(statptr))
3983                    .with_flags(flags),
3984            )
3985        };
3986        // The scratch starts 128 bytes below the stack pointer, at addresses
3987        // computed by subtraction.
3988        let scratch = 128 + std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>();
3989        if usize::try_from(crate::arch::stack_pointer(&guest.regs().await))
3990            .map_or(true, |rsp| rsp <= scratch)
3991        {
3992            return Self::inject_stat_in_transient_page(guest, lstatat, None)
3993                .await
3994                .map_err(StatFailure::errno);
3995        }
3996        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
3997        let statptr: StatPtr = StatPtr(stack.reserve());
3998        let mut saved = [0u8; std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>()];
3999        let staged_on_stack = !inputs
4000            .iter()
4001            .any(|input| path_overlaps_buffer(&guest.memory(), *input, statptr))
4002            && guest
4003                .memory()
4004                .read_exact(statptr.0.cast(), &mut saved)
4005                .is_ok();
4006        if !staged_on_stack {
4007            drop(stack);
4008            return Self::inject_stat_in_transient_page(guest, lstatat, None)
4009                .await
4010                .map_err(StatFailure::errno);
4011        }
4012        let guard = match stack.commit() {
4013            Ok(guard) => guard,
4014            Err(_) => {
4015                restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
4016                return Self::inject_stat_in_transient_page(guest, lstatat, None)
4017                    .await
4018                    .map_err(StatFailure::errno);
4019            }
4020        };
4021        restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
4022        let looked_up = Self::inject_stat_into(guest, lstatat(statptr), statptr, None)
4023            .await
4024            .map_err(StatFailure::errno);
4025        restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
4026        drop(guard);
4027        looked_up
4028    }
4029
4030    /// The fast path of [`Self::inject_fstat`]: the buffer lives in the guest
4031    /// stack scratch. Returns `Scratch(EFAULT)` when that scratch is not
4032    /// writable.
4033    async fn inject_stat_on_stack<G: Guest<Self>>(
4034        guest: &mut G,
4035        stat_call: impl Fn(StatPtr<'_>) -> Syscall,
4036        recorded: Option<&Self>,
4037    ) -> Result<libc::stat, StatFailure> {
4038        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
4039        let statptr: StatPtr = StatPtr(stack.reserve());
4040        // Ptrace lends bytes below the guest red zone. Save them before
4041        // commit can zero or partially write the reserved buffer, as the
4042        // adjacent pre-call lookup path does. Tool-owned scratch is likewise
4043        // held by stack/guard throughout every access.
4044        let mut saved = [0u8; std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>()];
4045        guest
4046            .memory()
4047            .read_exact(statptr.0.cast(), &mut saved)
4048            .map_err(StatFailure::Scratch)?;
4049        let guard = match stack.commit() {
4050            Ok(guard) => guard,
4051            Err(errno) => {
4052                restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
4053                return Err(StatFailure::Scratch(errno));
4054            }
4055        };
4056        restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
4057        // No early `?`: even kernel/readback errors must put back the borrowed
4058        // bytes before the guard releases a backend's Tool-owned arena.
4059        let copied = Self::inject_stat_into(guest, stat_call(statptr), statptr, recorded).await;
4060        let restored = guest.memory().write_exact(statptr.0.cast(), &saved);
4061        drop(guard);
4062        // Preserve the actual injection/readback errno. On success, preserve
4063        // the old contract that a failed final scratch write is an error.
4064        match copied {
4065            Ok(copied) => restored.map(|()| copied).map_err(StatFailure::Scratch),
4066            Err(failure) => {
4067                if restored.is_err() {
4068                    info!("Could not restore the guest bytes under a pre-call lookup buffer.");
4069                }
4070                Err(failure)
4071            }
4072        }
4073    }
4074
4075    /// The fallback of [`Self::inject_fstat`] and [`Self::inject_lstatat`]:
4076    /// the buffer lives in a private
4077    /// anonymous page mapped for this call only. The guest never learns its
4078    /// address, and it is unmapped before the guest resumes, so the guest's
4079    /// address space is the same as before the call.
4080    async fn inject_stat_in_transient_page<G: Guest<Self>>(
4081        guest: &mut G,
4082        stat_call: impl Fn(StatPtr<'_>) -> Syscall,
4083        recorded: Option<&Self>,
4084    ) -> Result<libc::stat, StatFailure> {
4085        let len = std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>();
4086        let mapped = guest
4087            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
4088                syscalls::Mmap::new()
4089                    .with_addr(None)
4090                    .with_len(len)
4091                    .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
4092                    .with_flags(MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS)
4093                    .with_fd(-1)
4094                    .with_offset(0),
4095            ))
4096            .await
4097            .map_err(StatFailure::Scratch)?;
4098        let page = usize::try_from(mapped)
4099            .ok()
4100            .and_then(AddrMut::<libc::stat>::from_raw)
4101            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("transient fstat page mmap returned {mapped}"));
4102        let copied =
4103            Self::inject_stat_into(guest, stat_call(StatPtr(page)), StatPtr(page), recorded).await;
4104        if let Err(errno) = guest
4105            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
4106                syscalls::Munmap::new()
4107                    .with_addr(Some(page.cast::<libc::c_void>().into()))
4108                    .with_len(len),
4109            ))
4110            .await
4111        {
4112            // Not expected: the page was mapped by this call and its address
4113            // never reached the guest. The metadata is still valid, so a
4114            // leftover page is no reason to fail the guest's syscall.
4115            warn!(
4116                "[detcore] could not unmap the transient stat page: {}",
4117                errno
4118            );
4119        }
4120        copied
4121    }
4122
4123    /// Inject `stat_call`, which writes a `struct stat` at `statptr`, and read
4124    /// back what the kernel wrote. With `recorded`, the call goes through that
4125    /// Detcore's recording ([`Detcore::record_or_replay`]): recorded under
4126    /// record, served from the recording under replay, injected otherwise.
4127    async fn inject_stat_into<G: Guest<Self>>(
4128        guest: &mut G,
4129        stat_call: Syscall,
4130        statptr: StatPtr<'_>,
4131        recorded: Option<&Self>,
4132    ) -> Result<libc::stat, StatFailure> {
4133        // NOTE: Must retry the injection here. This could get interrupted and
4134        // we don't want to rerun the entire syscall handler twice. Through the
4135        // recording, every attempt is a recorded event, so replay consumes the
4136        // same attempts, in order, and retries exactly as the record did.
4137        match recorded {
4138            None => {
4139                guest
4140                    .inject_with_retry(stat_call)
4141                    .await
4142                    .map_err(StatFailure::Call)?;
4143            }
4144            Some(detcore) => loop {
4145                match detcore.record_or_replay(guest, stat_call).await {
4146                    Ok(_) => break,
4147                    Err(Errno::EINTR | Errno::ERESTARTSYS) => continue,
4148                    Err(errno) => return Err(StatFailure::Call(errno)),
4149                }
4150            },
4151        }
4152        statptr.read(&guest.memory()).map_err(StatFailure::Call)
4153    }
4154
4155    // helper function to track a new file descriptor.
4156    pub(crate) async fn add_fd<G: Guest<Self>>(
4157        &self,
4158        guest: &mut G,
4159        fd: RawFd,
4160        flags: OFlag,
4161        ty: FdType,
4162    ) -> Result<(), Errno> {
4163        self.add_fd_with_stat(guest, fd, flags, ty).await.map(drop)
4164    }
4165
4166    /// Track `fd`, which the guest already holds from a call that has
4167    /// succeeded whatever happens here (a clone's pidfd), as [`Self::add_fd`]
4168    /// does, except that a failure leaves the descriptor open and untracked
4169    /// rather than closing it: the guest keeps what Linux gave it.
4170    pub(crate) async fn track_held_fd<G: Guest<Self>>(
4171        &self,
4172        guest: &mut G,
4173        fd: RawFd,
4174        flags: OFlag,
4175        ty: FdType,
4176    ) -> Result<(), Errno> {
4177        let host_stat = if guest.config().virtualize_metadata {
4178            Some(self.inject_fstat(guest, fd).await?)
4179        } else {
4180            None
4181        };
4182        guest
4183            .thread_state()
4184            .add_fd(fd, flags, ty, host_stat.map(Into::into))
4185    }
4186
4187    /// [`Self::add_fd`], also returning the host `fstat` it took of `fd`, which
4188    /// it takes only when metadata is virtualized.
4189    async fn add_fd_with_stat<G: Guest<Self>>(
4190        &self,
4191        guest: &mut G,
4192        fd: RawFd,
4193        flags: OFlag,
4194        ty: FdType,
4195    ) -> Result<Option<libc::stat>, Errno> {
4196        let host_stat = if guest.config().virtualize_metadata {
4197            match self.inject_fstat(guest, fd).await {
4198                Ok(stat) => Some(stat),
4199                Err(errno) => {
4200                    // `fd` is already open in the guest, but Detcore cannot
4201                    // model it: with metadata virtualization on, a descriptor
4202                    // without its stat is an invariant violation. The caller
4203                    // reports this error as the syscall's result, so close
4204                    // the descriptor rather than leave an untracked one open
4205                    // behind that error. Not retried on EINTR: Linux releases
4206                    // the descriptor even then, and a retry could close a
4207                    // reused number.
4208                    if let Err(close_errno) = guest.inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd)).await
4209                    {
4210                        warn!(
4211                            "[detcore] could not close fd {} after failing to record its \
4212                             metadata ({}): {}",
4213                            fd, errno, close_errno
4214                        );
4215                    }
4216                    return Err(errno);
4217                }
4218            }
4219        } else {
4220            None
4221        };
4222        guest
4223            .thread_state()
4224            .add_fd(fd, flags, ty, host_stat.map(Into::into))?;
4225        Ok(host_stat)
4226    }
4227
4228    /// Under replay, makes descriptor `fd`, which an `SCM_RIGHTS` receive
4229    /// installed and which the recording found to name the open file of `other`
4230    /// in this table, name that file in the kernel too.
4231    ///
4232    /// Replay serves the receive from the log and holds a placeholder eventfd
4233    /// in `fd`, but the guest keeps using both descriptors: a write to a
4234    /// received eventfd must reach the reader of the original, as it does in
4235    /// the recording, and replay applies eventfd reads and writes in the kernel
4236    /// (`ReplayFdKind::Eventfd`). `dup3` replaces the placeholder with `other`'s
4237    /// file, which is the live object the recording's file corresponds to: the
4238    /// open file the descriptor table names at `other` in both runs.
4239    pub(crate) async fn install_live_alias<G: Guest<Self>>(
4240        &self,
4241        guest: &mut G,
4242        other: RawFd,
4243        fd: RawFd,
4244        flags: OFlag,
4245    ) -> Result<(), Errno> {
4246        let installed = guest
4247            .inject_with_retry(
4248                syscalls::Dup3::new()
4249                    .with_oldfd(other)
4250                    .with_newfd(fd)
4251                    .with_flags(flags & OFlag::O_CLOEXEC),
4252            )
4253            .await?;
4254        if installed != i64::from(fd) {
4255            warn!("[detcore] replay's alias of {other} landed in {installed}, not {fd}");
4256            return Err(Errno::EBADF);
4257        }
4258        Ok(())
4259    }
4260
4261    /// Marks a socket whose peer is a guest of this container as internal
4262    /// (`DetFd::set_guest_peer`), so record and replay poll a blocking call on
4263    /// it in the caller's turn, as they do on a pipe or a socketpair endpoint,
4264    /// instead of running it outside the turn as external I/O.
4265    ///
4266    /// Outside the turn, the kernel completed such a call at a host-timed
4267    /// moment relative to the other threads' calls. A `recvmsg` that receives
4268    /// descriptors over `SCM_RIGHTS` then took descriptor slots at that moment,
4269    /// while replay, which serves the call from the log, reserves them when the
4270    /// call rejoins the schedule; another thread's open in between took a
4271    /// different slot in each, and replay refused with "replay FD namespace
4272    /// diverged". In the turn, no other guest thread runs between the attempt
4273    /// that receives and the reservation that replays it.
4274    ///
4275    /// The peer's credentials decide. Only `AF_UNIX` stream and seqpacket
4276    /// sockets carry a peer's; Linux reports any other socket's, and a peer
4277    /// outside the recording's PID namespace, as pid 0, which leaves the socket
4278    /// external. So a pid above 0 names a guest only because `hermit record`
4279    /// runs its guests in a PID namespace of their own (`cred_to_ucred` maps
4280    /// the peer's pid into the caller's namespace, `pid_nr_ns`); a recording
4281    /// that shared the host's PID namespace would count a host process's
4282    /// socket as internal, and poll a wait on it in the caller's turn. Every
4283    /// probe goes through the recording, so replay, which holds
4284    /// placeholders, classifies the socket exactly as the recording did. A run
4285    /// without sequentialized threads, or with `--debug-externalize-sockets`,
4286    /// keeps every socket external; a plain run polls every socket already.
4287    pub(crate) async fn classify_socket_peer<G: Guest<Self>>(
4288        &self,
4289        guest: &mut G,
4290        fd: RawFd,
4291        role: SocketRole,
4292    ) {
4293        if !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes || !self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets() {
4294            return;
4295        }
4296        match self.mark_guest_peer(guest, fd, role).await {
4297            Ok(true) => trace!("[detcore] socket {fd} has a guest peer: polled as internal"),
4298            Ok(false) => trace!("[detcore] socket {fd} has no guest peer: stays external"),
4299            Err(errno) => {
4300                trace!("[detcore] socket {fd} stays external: peer probe failed with {errno}")
4301            }
4302        }
4303    }
4304
4305    /// [`Self::classify_socket_peer`]'s probes. Returns whether it marked the
4306    /// socket.
4307    async fn mark_guest_peer<G: Guest<Self>>(
4308        &self,
4309        guest: &mut G,
4310        fd: RawFd,
4311        role: SocketRole,
4312    ) -> Result<bool, Errno> {
4313        // A listener reports its own credentials as SO_PEERCRED, not a peer's
4314        // (sock_getsockopt in net/core/sock.c).
4315        if role == SocketRole::Received
4316            && self
4317                .probe_socket_option::<_, libc::c_int>(guest, fd, libc::SO_ACCEPTCONN)
4318                .await?
4319                != 0
4320        {
4321            return Ok(false);
4322        }
4323        let peer: libc::ucred = self
4324            .probe_socket_option(guest, fd, libc::SO_PEERCRED)
4325            .await?;
4326        if peer.pid <= 0 {
4327            return Ok(false);
4328        }
4329        let (physically_nonblocking, status_flags) =
4330            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
4331                (detfd.physically_nonblocking(), detfd.status_flags())
4332            })?;
4333        if !physically_nonblocking {
4334            // The guest's flags are unchanged: F_GETFL reports the logical ones.
4335            self.record_or_replay(
4336                guest,
4337                syscalls::Fcntl::new()
4338                    .with_fd(fd)
4339                    .with_cmd(F_SETFL(status_flags | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK.bits())),
4340            )
4341            .await?;
4342            guest
4343                .thread_state()
4344                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_physically_nonblocking())?;
4345        }
4346        guest
4347            .thread_state()
4348            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_guest_peer())?;
4349        Ok(true)
4350    }
4351
4352    /// Reads the `SOL_SOCKET` option `optname` of `fd` through the recording
4353    /// into a buffer borrowed from the guest stack scratch, whose bytes are put
4354    /// back afterwards, as `inject_stat_on_stack` borrows its buffer.
4355    async fn probe_socket_option<G: Guest<Self>, V: Copy>(
4356        &self,
4357        guest: &mut G,
4358        fd: RawFd,
4359        optname: libc::c_int,
4360    ) -> Result<V, Errno> {
4361        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
4362        let probe: AddrMut<SocketOptionProbe<V>> = stack.reserve();
4363        let value: AddrMut<V> = probe.cast();
4364        let length = AddrMut::<libc::socklen_t>::from_raw(
4365            probe.as_raw() + std::mem::offset_of!(SocketOptionProbe<V>, length),
4366        )
4367        .ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
4368        // Ptrace lends bytes below the guest's red zone; save them before
4369        // commit can write the reservation.
4370        let mut saved = vec![0u8; std::mem::size_of::<SocketOptionProbe<V>>()];
4371        guest.memory().read_exact(probe.cast(), &mut saved)?;
4372        let guard = match stack.commit() {
4373            Ok(guard) => guard,
4374            Err(errno) => {
4375                restore_socket_option_probe(&mut guest.memory(), probe.cast(), &saved);
4376                return Err(errno);
4377            }
4378        };
4379        let probed = match guest
4380            .memory()
4381            .write_value(length, &(std::mem::size_of::<V>() as libc::socklen_t))
4382        {
4383            Ok(()) => self
4384                .record_or_replay(
4385                    guest,
4386                    syscalls::Getsockopt::new()
4387                        .with_fd(fd)
4388                        .with_level(libc::SOL_SOCKET)
4389                        .with_optname(optname)
4390                        .with_optval(Some(value.cast()))
4391                        .with_optlen(Some(length)),
4392                )
4393                .await
4394                .and_then(|_| guest.memory().read_value(value)),
4395            Err(errno) => Err(errno),
4396        };
4397        restore_socket_option_probe(&mut guest.memory(), probe.cast(), &saved);
4398        drop(guard);
4399        probed
4400    }

4428    /// [`Self::observed_path`], with a `/proc` directory that `dirfd` names
4429    /// taken as the directory it is open on, as Linux looks a relative name up
4430    /// below that directory whoever holds the descriptor: a `/proc/self` or
4431    /// `/proc/thread-self` directory is the task the selector reached when it
4432    /// was opened (`DetFd::procfs_reached`), and a descriptor Detcore has no
4433    /// record of (one received over `SCM_RIGHTS`, which its record or a fresh
4434    /// discovery leaves without one) is named as the kernel names the directory it is
4435    /// open on, where that is on procfs ([`Self::unrecorded_procfs_directory`]).
4436    /// Detcore's own decisions about procfs names (the files it renders, the
4437    /// `--proc` level, the links it canonicalizes) use this spelling. A name
4438    /// below the recorded directory of a task that is gone is ESRCH, and one
4439    /// below a selector link opened as the link itself ENOTDIR, as Linux
4440    /// answers them.
4441    pub(crate) async fn procfs_spelling_at<G: Guest<Self>>(
4442        &self,
4443        guest: &mut G,
4444        dirfd: i32,
4445        path: &Path,
4446    ) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
4447        if !path.is_absolute() && !path.as_os_str().is_empty() && dirfd != libc::AT_FDCWD {
4448            let (reached, link_itself) = guest
4449                .thread_state()
4450                .with_detfd(dirfd, |detfd| {
4451                    (detfd.procfs_reached(), detfd.procfs_link_itself())
4452                })
4453                .unwrap_or((None, false));
4454            // A selector link itself is no directory.
4455            if link_itself {
4456                return Err(Errno::ENOTDIR.into());
4457            }
4458            if let Some((reached, incarnation)) = reached {
4459                // The directory's task, while it lives: Linux checks the
4460                // task a pid directory was opened on at every lookup below it
4461                // (`proc_pid_permission`), and a task that is gone, whose
4462                // number another task may hold by now, fails every name with
4463                // ESRCH (measured on Linux 7.1: `cgroup`, `status`, `exe` and
4464                // a name no task has alike).
4465                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#4213): Review the stale task-directory
4466                // decision: a directory bound to a task identity at its open
4467                // answers ESRCH for every name once that identity no longer
4468                // holds its numbers (`ProcfsTaskAnswer::still_names`).
4469                if let Some(incarnation) = incarnation
4470                    && let Some(task) = procfs_reached_task(&reached)
4471                {
4472                    let answer = crate::tool_global::procfs_task(guest, task).await;
4473                    if !answer.still_names(incarnation) {
4474                        return Err(Errno::ESRCH.into());
4475                    }
4476                }
4477                return Ok(reached.join(path));
4478            }
4479            if let Some(directory) = self.unrecorded_procfs_directory(guest, dirfd).await {
4480                return Ok(directory.join(path));
4481            }
4482        }
4483        Self::prepare_guest_cwd(guest, dirfd, path).await;
4484        Self::observed_path(guest, dirfd, path)
4485    }
4486
4487    /// The procfs directory descriptor `dirfd` is open on, where Detcore has
4488    /// no record of the descriptor, as the guest names it: the kernel's name
4489    /// for it (its `/proc/thread-self/fd/N` link, one injected `readlinkat`),
4490    /// if that is `/proc` or a path below it, with the kernel's numbers of
4491    /// the task it names taken back to the guest's where the two differ (DBT,
4492    /// `Self::translates_procfs_numbers`). Every backend's kernel beneath
4493    /// answers that link for the calling thread's own table: the host kernel
4494    /// on ptrace and DBT, KVM's provider (`guest_fd_path`), which has one
4495    /// table per process. `None` for a descriptor Detcore has a record of, any
4496    /// other object, a task number no task of the guest's holds, and where
4497    /// Detcore does not render procfs files (record and replay, after
4498    /// `chroot`).
4499    ///
4500    /// In every threading mode, `--no-sequentialize-threads` included. For a
4501    /// file Detcore renders, the link is the only observation of the
4502    /// descriptor, read once inside the guest's own call, and the answer comes
4503    /// from that name alone: another thread that replaces the descriptor
4504    /// concurrently is ordered before that read (the call looks below the new
4505    /// directory) or after it (below the old one), and Linux takes the
4506    /// descriptor at one point inside the call too (`path_init`), so each
4507    /// answer is one Linux can give. Without this a relaxed run's received
4508    /// `/proc` would leave its mount tables to the backend, which keeps no copy
4509    /// (KVM).
4510    ///
4511    /// Where the name only guides a call the kernel then resolves through the
4512    /// same descriptor, there are two observations, and without
4513    /// sequentialized threads another thread can replace the descriptor
4514    /// between them. A directory opened below it gets procfs provenance only
4515    /// if the descriptor the kernel returned holds a directory below `/proc`
4516    /// (`handle_openat`). The `--proc` level's refusal of an omitted name below
4517    /// it is best-effort there for `stat`, `access` and `readlink`, which have
4518    /// no check after the kernel's lookup: a residual of the relaxed mode,
4519    /// narrower than before, when no level applied below a received descriptor
4520    /// in that mode at all.
4521    pub(crate) async fn unrecorded_procfs_directory<G: Guest<Self>>(
4522        &self,
4523        guest: &mut G,
4524        dirfd: i32,
4525    ) -> Option<PathBuf> {
4526        if dirfd < 0 || !self.renders_procfs(guest) {
4527            return None;
4528        }
4529        let recorded = guest
4530            .thread_state()
4531            .with_detfd(dirfd, |detfd| detfd.path())
4532            .unwrap_or(None);
4533        if recorded.is_some() {
4534            return None;
4535        }
4536        const LINK_CAPACITY: usize = 40;
4537        const TARGET_CAPACITY: usize = 256;
4538        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
4539        let link = stack.push(rendered_procfs::c_string::<LINK_CAPACITY>(
4540            format!("/proc/thread-self/fd/{dirfd}").as_bytes(),
4541        ));
4542        let target = stack.reserve::<[u8; TARGET_CAPACITY]>();
4543        let stack_guard = stack.commit().ok()?;
4544        let length = guest
4545            .inject(
4546                syscalls::Readlinkat::new()
4547                    .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
4548                    .with_path(PathPtr::from_ptr(link.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char))
4549                    .with_buf(Some(target.cast::<libc::c_char>()))
4550                    .with_buf_len(TARGET_CAPACITY),
4551            )
4552            .await;
4553        let bytes = match length.map(|length| length as usize) {
4554            Ok(length) if length < TARGET_CAPACITY => {
4555                let mut bytes = vec![0; length];
4556                guest
4557                    .memory()
4558                    .read_exact(target.cast::<u8>(), &mut bytes)
4559                    .ok()
4560                    .map(|()| bytes)
4561            }
4562            _ => None,
4563        };
4564        drop(stack_guard);
4565        let text = String::from_utf8(bytes?).ok()?;
4566        // The placeholder directory Detcore serves `/proc` and descriptor
4567        // directories on, which no guest path reaches: the directory the
4568        // descriptor stands for (`descriptor_directory`).
4569        if guest
4570            .config()
4571            .directory_placeholder
4572            .as_deref()
4573            .is_some_and(|placeholder| placeholder.as_os_str() == std::ffi::OsStr::new(&text))
4574        {
4575            return Self::unrecorded_placeholder_base(guest, dirfd).await;
4576        }
4577        let (mut names, positions) = procfs_directory_task_positions(&text)?;
4578        if Self::translates_procfs_numbers(guest) && !positions.is_empty() {
4579            let kernel = positions
4580                .iter()
4581                .map(|position| names[*position].parse::<i32>().ok())
4582                .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
4583            let translated = crate::tool_global::procfs_ids(guest, false, kernel).await;
4584            for (position, number) in positions.iter().zip(translated) {
4585                names[*position] = number?.to_string();
4586            }
4587        }
4588        let mut directory = PathBuf::from("/proc");
4589        directory.extend(names);
4590        Some(directory)
4591    }
4592
4593    /// Whether a decision about `path`, looked up relative to `dirfd`, reads
4594    /// the guest's working directory from the guest
4595    /// ([`Self::prepare_guest_cwd`]): a nonempty spelling relative to the
4596    /// working directory (`AT_FDCWD`), where the tool cannot read the working
4597    /// directory from host procfs
4598    /// ([`crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_read_guest_cwd`]: KVM). An absolute
4599    /// spelling is bound already, and a directory descriptor supplies its own
4600    /// recorded path. The empty spelling (`AT_EMPTY_PATH`) is the working
4601    /// directory itself, which no decision classifies (`Detcore::decide`
4602    /// takes it for no name), so it is kept as given
4603    /// ([`Self::observed_path`]); so is a spelling `PATH_MAX` bytes long or
4604    /// more, which Linux refuses before any walk ([`names_past_path_max`]).
4605    fn reads_guest_cwd<G: Guest<Self>>(guest: &G, dirfd: i32, path: &Path) -> bool {
4606        dirfd == libc::AT_FDCWD
4607            && !path.is_absolute()
4608            && !path.as_os_str().is_empty()
4609            && !names_past_path_max(path)
4610            && !crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_read_guest_cwd(&guest.config().backend)
4611    }
4612
4613    /// Read what a decision about `path` needs of the calling thread's
4614    /// working directory for the syscall it is running, where
4615    /// [`Self::reads_guest_cwd`] says it reads it from the guest, before the
4616    /// decision, which does not await ([`Self::observed_path`]): the
4617    /// directory's path, once per syscall
4618    /// ([`Self::read_guest_cwd_for_syscall`]); and where that has none (a
4619    /// removed directory, or one whose path is longer than `PATH_MAX`), the
4620    /// directory the spelling climbs to out of it with `..`, once per number
4621    /// of `..` ([`Self::read_climbed_directory`]). Nothing happens elsewhere,
4622    /// so no other spelling, and no backend whose tool reads the working
4623    /// directory from host procfs, makes a call for it.
4624    ///
4625    /// The calls it injects stage their buffers in the guest stack scratch,
4626    /// which KVM gives out once at a time and refuses with a panic while
4627    /// taken (Reverie's `KvmStack`); so it must run before its caller takes
4628    /// that scratch, never while the caller holds it. A caller that holds the
4629    /// scratch across a call whose translation may reach it prepares the
4630    /// spelling first (`Detcore::whole_link`), which leaves nothing for it to
4631    /// read again.
4632    pub(crate) async fn prepare_guest_cwd<G: Guest<Self>>(guest: &mut G, dirfd: i32, path: &Path) {
4633        if !Self::reads_guest_cwd(guest, dirfd, path) {
4634            return;
4635        }
4636        if guest.thread_state().syscall_cwd.is_none() {
4637            Box::pin(Self::read_guest_cwd_for_syscall(guest)).await;
4638        }
4639        let (climbs, _) = split_leading_climb(path);
4640        let unread = climbs > 0
4641            && matches!(
4642                &guest.thread_state().syscall_cwd,
4643                Some(SyscallCwd::Unrendered(climbed)) if !climbed.contains_key(&climbs)
4644            );
4645        if unread {
4646            let climbed = Box::pin(Self::read_climbed_directory(guest, climbs)).await;
4647            if let Some(SyscallCwd::Unrendered(paths)) = &mut guest.thread_state_mut().syscall_cwd {
4648                paths.insert(climbs, climbed);
4649            }
4650        }
4651    }
4652
4653    /// The calling thread's working directory as its own `getcwd` answers
4654    /// it, read once for the syscall it is running
4655    /// ([`ThreadState::syscall_cwd`]): one `getcwd` injected in the thread,
4656    /// its buffer staged by [`crate::syscalls::scratch::inject_with_scratch`]
4657    /// (the guest stack scratch, whose bytes are put back after the call, or
4658    /// a transient private page where that scratch cannot hold the buffer).
4659    /// On KVM that scratch is not the guest's stack but the Tool's own page in
4660    /// the boot-reserved layout, open to user access only while a Tool
4661    /// callback runs (Reverie's `KvmStack`), and `PATH_MAX` bytes fill it
4662    /// exactly, so no guest memory holds the buffer and no page is mapped
4663    /// for it.
4664    ///
4665    /// A `getcwd` that fails with `ENOENT` (the directory was removed) or
4666    /// with `ENAMETOOLONG` or `ERANGE` (its path is longer than `PATH_MAX`)
4667    /// leaves the directory unrendered, as Linux leaves it walkable: a
4668    /// spelling that climbs out of it with `..` is then decided from the
4669    /// directory it climbs to ([`Self::prepare_guest_cwd`]). One that fails
4670    /// otherwise, or that answers no path from the root (its "(unreachable)"
4671    /// prefix), leaves every spelling to be decided as given, as a spelling
4672    /// Detcore could not resolve always was. Called through
4673    /// [`Self::prepare_guest_cwd`], boxed, so that its buffers do not grow
4674    /// every system call's future.
4675    async fn read_guest_cwd_for_syscall<G: Guest<Self>>(guest: &mut G) {
4676        const PATH_MAX: usize = libc::PATH_MAX as usize;
4677        let answered =
4678            crate::syscalls::scratch::inject_with_scratch(guest, [0_u8; PATH_MAX], |buffer| {
4679                Syscall::from(
4680                    syscalls::Getcwd::new()
4681                        .with_buf(Some(buffer.cast::<libc::c_char>()))
4682                        .with_size(PATH_MAX),
4683                )
4684            })
4685            .await;
4686        let cwd = match answered {
4687            // The length counts the NUL.
4688            Ok((length, bytes)) => usize::try_from(length)
4689                .ok()
4690                .filter(|length| (1..=PATH_MAX).contains(length))
4691                .map(|length| &bytes[..length - 1])
4692                .filter(|path| path.starts_with(b"/"))
4693                .map_or(SyscallCwd::Unknown, |path| {
4694                    SyscallCwd::Path(PathBuf::from(
4695                        <std::ffi::OsStr as std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt>::from_bytes(path),
4696                    ))
4697                }),
4698            Err(Errno::ENOENT | Errno::ENAMETOOLONG | Errno::ERANGE) => {
4699                SyscallCwd::Unrendered(BTreeMap::new())
4700            }
4701            Err(_) => SyscallCwd::Unknown,
4702        };
4703        guest.thread_state_mut().syscall_cwd = Some(cwd);
4704    }
4705
4706    /// The path of the directory `climbs` `..` lead to from the calling
4707    /// thread's working directory, where `getcwd` renders none for it (a
4708    /// removed directory, or one whose path is longer than `PATH_MAX`), read
4709    /// through a descriptor for that directory, three calls injected in the
4710    /// thread: an `O_PATH` open of `..` (`climbs` of them), which the
4711    /// executor walks from the working directory itself, as Linux's walk
4712    /// leaves a removed directory for its parent; a `readlinkat` of that
4713    /// descriptor's link (`/proc/thread-self/fd/<it>`, which the executor
4714    /// answers from its own descriptor, as for
4715    /// `Detcore::received_descriptor_link`); and the descriptor's `close`,
4716    /// before the guest runs again, so the guest's next descriptor number
4717    /// does not move. Each call's path and buffer are staged as
4718    /// [`Self::read_guest_cwd_for_syscall`] stages `getcwd`'s. `None` where a
4719    /// call fails, or where the link fills its buffer and may be cut.
4720    async fn read_climbed_directory<G: Guest<Self>>(
4721        guest: &mut G,
4722        climbs: usize,
4723    ) -> Option<PathBuf> {
4724        const PATH_MAX: usize = libc::PATH_MAX as usize;
4725        const LINK_PATH: usize = 64;
4726        const LINK_TARGET: usize = PATH_MAX - LINK_PATH;
4727        let climbed = climb_spelling(climbs);
4728        if climbed.len() >= PATH_MAX {
4729            return None;
4730        }
4731        let mut spelled = [0_u8; PATH_MAX];
4732        spelled[..climbed.len()].copy_from_slice(climbed.as_bytes());
4733        let flags = OFlag::O_PATH | OFlag::O_DIRECTORY | OFlag::O_CLOEXEC;
4734        let (opened, _) = crate::syscalls::scratch::inject_with_scratch(guest, spelled, |base| {
4735            syscalls::Openat::new()
4736                .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
4737                .with_path(PathPtr::from_ptr(base.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char))
4738                .with_flags(flags)
4739                .with_mode(None)
4740                .into()
4741        })
4742        .await
4743        .ok()?;
4744        let fd = RawFd::try_from(opened).ok()?;
4745        let mut buffer = [0_u8; LINK_PATH + LINK_TARGET];
4746        let link = format!("/proc/thread-self/fd/{fd}");
4747        buffer[..link.len()].copy_from_slice(link.as_bytes());
4748        let linked = crate::syscalls::scratch::inject_with_scratch(guest, buffer, |base| {
4749            // SAFETY: the buffer holds LINK_PATH + LINK_TARGET bytes.
4750            let target = unsafe { base.add(LINK_PATH) };
4751            syscalls::Readlinkat::new()
4752                .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
4753                .with_path(PathPtr::from_ptr(base.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char))
4754                .with_buf(Some(target.cast::<libc::c_char>()))
4755                .with_buf_len(LINK_TARGET)
4756                .into()
4757        })
4758        .await;
4759        let _ = guest.inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd)).await;
4760        let (length, bytes) = linked.ok()?;
4761        let length = usize::try_from(length)
4762            .ok()
4763            .filter(|length| *length < LINK_TARGET)?;
4764        let path = &bytes[LINK_PATH..LINK_PATH + length];
4765        path.starts_with(b"/").then(|| {
4766            PathBuf::from(<std::ffi::OsStr as std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt>::from_bytes(path))
4767        })
4768    }
4769
4770    /// `path`, as a guest syscall named it relative to `dirfd`, made
4771    /// absolute in the guest's view. A relative spelling is not the object:
4772    /// absolute paths are already bound, a dirfd supplies its own prefix, and
4773    /// AT_FDCWD-relative spellings are resolved through the guest's root and
