4774    /// cwd, so the result does not depend on Replayer's placeholder
4775    /// descriptor. A spelling that cannot be resolved is kept as given.
4776    ///
4777    /// Where the tool cannot read the guest's working directory from host
4778    /// procfs ([`crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_read_guest_cwd`]: KVM, whose
4779    /// guest process IDs name the supervisor's own threads), the working
4780    /// directory is the one the guest's `getcwd` answered for this syscall,
4781    /// which an async caller reads first ([`Self::prepare_guest_cwd`]). Where
4782    /// `getcwd` answered none (a removed directory, or one whose path is
4783    /// longer than `PATH_MAX`), a spelling whose leading `..` climb out of it
4784    /// is made absolute from the directory they reach, as the executor's own
4785    /// walk named it ([`Self::read_climbed_directory`]), the rest of the
4786    /// spelling following byte for byte ([`split_leading_climb`]). Any other
4787    /// spelling, and one whose climb failed, is kept as given, so that the
4788    /// call's own walk decides it, with its own error.
4789    ///
4790    /// A spelling relative to the working directory that is `PATH_MAX` bytes
4791    /// long or more is kept as given before anything is read or reused for
4792    /// it, on every backend: Linux refuses it with `ENAMETOOLONG` before any
4793    /// walk ([`names_past_path_max`]), and a climb would shorten it into a
4794    /// name Detcore serves.
4795    pub(crate) fn observed_path<G: Guest<Self>>(
4796        guest: &G,
4797        dirfd: i32,
4798        path: &Path,
4799    ) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
4800        // An absolute spelling is bound already; a relative one of PATH_MAX
4801        // bytes or more names nothing, and the call refuses it.
4802        let as_given = path.is_absolute() || (dirfd == libc::AT_FDCWD && names_past_path_max(path));
4803        Ok(if as_given {
4804            path.to_path_buf()
4805        } else if dirfd == libc::AT_FDCWD {
4806            if crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_read_guest_cwd(&guest.config().backend) {
4807                resolved_at_fdcwd_path(guest.pid().as_raw(), path)
4808                    .unwrap_or_else(|| path.to_path_buf())
4809            } else {
4810                match &guest.thread_state().syscall_cwd {
4811                    _ if path.as_os_str().is_empty() => path.to_path_buf(),
4812                    Some(SyscallCwd::Path(cwd)) => cwd.join(path),
4813                    Some(SyscallCwd::Unrendered(climbed)) => {
4814                        let (climbs, rest) = split_leading_climb(path);
4815                        match climbed.get(&climbs) {
4816                            Some(Some(directory)) if climbs > 0 => joined_verbatim(directory, rest),
4817                            _ => path.to_path_buf(),
4818                        }
4819                    }
4820                    _ => path.to_path_buf(),
4821                }
4822            }
4823        } else {
4824            // A descriptor Detcore has no state for (one received over
4825            // `SCM_RIGHTS` and not recorded,
4826            // `Detcore::record_received_descriptors`) keeps the relative spelling, which
4827            // the kernel looks up from it; the kernel, not this lookup,
4828            // decides whether the descriptor is open. Before, such an `openat`
4829            // failed with EBADF though the descriptor was open.
4830            guest
4831                .thread_state()
4832                .with_detfd(dirfd, |detfd| detfd.path())
4833                .unwrap_or(None)
4834                .map_or_else(|| path.to_path_buf(), |directory| directory.join(path))
4835        })
4836    }
4837
4838    /// For `hermit run --verify`, report each path `call` may rebind in the
4839    /// guest's file namespace: both names of a rename, the new name of a link
4840    /// or symlink, an unlinked name, and a node, directory or file it makes
4841    /// or removes (see `detcore_model::host_input::HostMutationRecord`). A
4842    /// host file whose path the guest rebinds may have been replaced by the
4843    /// guest itself. Called before the call runs, whatever its outcome.
4844    pub(crate) async fn record_host_namespace_change<G: Guest<Self>>(
4845        &self,
4846        guest: &mut G,
4847        call: &Syscall,
4848    ) {
4849        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4850        let at = libc::AT_FDCWD;
4851        let changed: Vec<(i32, Option<syscalls::PathPtr>)> = match call {
4852            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4853            Syscall::Rename(c) => vec![(at, c.oldpath()), (at, c.newpath())],
4854            Syscall::Renameat(c) => vec![(c.olddirfd(), c.oldpath()), (c.newdirfd(), c.newpath())],
4855            Syscall::Renameat2(c) => {
4856                vec![(c.olddirfd(), c.oldpath()), (c.newdirfd(), c.newpath())]
4857            }
4858            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4859            Syscall::Link(c) => vec![(at, c.newpath())],
4860            Syscall::Linkat(c) => vec![(c.newdirfd(), c.newpath())],
4861            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4862            Syscall::Unlink(c) => vec![(at, c.path())],
4863            Syscall::Unlinkat(c) => vec![(c.dirfd(), c.path())],
4864            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4865            Syscall::Symlink(c) => vec![(at, c.linkpath())],
4866            Syscall::Symlinkat(c) => vec![(c.newdirfd(), c.linkpath())],
4867            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4868            Syscall::Mknod(c) => vec![(at, c.path())],
4869            Syscall::Mknodat(c) => vec![(c.dirfd(), c.path())],
4870            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4871            Syscall::Mkdir(c) => vec![(at, c.path())],
4872            Syscall::Mkdirat(c) => vec![(c.dirfd(), c.path())],
4873            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4874            Syscall::Rmdir(c) => vec![(at, c.path())],
4875            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
4876            Syscall::Creat(c) => vec![(at, c.path())],
4877            _ => return,
4878        };
4879        for (dirfd, path) in changed {
4880            let observed = match path.map(|path| path.read(&guest.memory())) {
4881                Some(Ok(path)) => {
4882                    let path: PathBuf = path;
4883                    Self::prepare_guest_cwd(guest, dirfd, &path).await;
4884                    Self::observed_path(guest, dirfd, &path).ok()
4885                }
4886                _ => None,
4887            };
4888            crate::tool_global::record_host_mutation(guest, rebound_path(observed)).await;
4889        }
4890    }
4891
4892    /// The host inodes whose last name `call` would remove: the name an
4893    /// `unlink`, `unlinkat` or `rmdir` removes, or the target a `rename`,
4894    /// `renameat` or `renameat2` replaces (not with `RENAME_EXCHANGE`), when
4895    /// it is a directory or a file with one link (see [`retires_on_removal`]).
4896    /// Each name is stat'ed with an injected `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`
4897    /// before the call runs; a name that does not resolve removes nothing.
4898    /// Pass the result to [`Self::retire_removed_inodes`] if the call
4899    /// succeeds. Only with virtualized metadata, the only mode that numbers
4900    /// inodes.
4901    ///
4902    /// Nothing is retired without sequentialized threads. Only then do the
4903    /// lookups, the call and the retirement run in one turn; otherwise another
4904    /// thread can link, unlink or rename the file in between, and a file that
4905    /// keeps a name could be retired and renumbered (codex review of
4906    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3849>, P2). Without them inode
4907    /// numbers behave as before retirement existed.
4908    pub(crate) async fn last_names_removed_by<G: Guest<Self>>(
4909        &self,
4910        guest: &mut G,
4911        call: &Syscall,
4912    ) -> Vec<RawInode> {
4913        if !guest.config().virtualize_metadata || !guest.config().sequentialize_threads {
4914            return Vec::new();
4915        }
4916        // The name removed, and for a rename the source, which replaces
4917        // nothing when it is the target's own file (`rename(a, a)`, or two
4918        // links of one file).
4919        let Some((removed, source)) = removed_names(call, true) else {
4920            return Vec::new();
4921        };
4922        // Every path the call reads, which the lookups must leave unchanged.
4923        let inputs = [removed.1, source.and_then(|source| source.1)];
4924        let Some(path) = removed.1 else {
4925            return Vec::new();
4926        };
4927        let Ok(stat) = Self::inject_lstatat(guest, removed.0, path, inputs).await else {
4928            return Vec::new();
4929        };
4930        let inode = RawInode::new(stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino);
4931        if let Some((dirfd, Some(path))) = source
4932            && Self::inject_lstatat(guest, dirfd, path, inputs)
4933                .await
4934                .is_ok_and(|source| RawInode::new(source.st_dev, source.st_ino) == inode)
4935        {
4936            return Vec::new();
4937        }
4938        if retires_on_removal(&stat) {
4939            vec![inode]
4940        } else {
4941            Vec::new()
4942        }
4943    }
4944
4945    /// The guest-made FIFO (`crate::fifo_peer::is_guest_made`) whose last
4946    /// name `call` removes: the name an `unlink` or `unlinkat` removes, or the
4947    /// target a `rename`, `renameat` or `renameat2` replaces (not with
4948    /// `RENAME_EXCHANGE`), when it is that FIFO's only link
4949    /// ([`retires_on_removal`]) and not the rename's own source (another link
4950    /// of the same FIFO, or `rename(a, a)`). Stat'ed before the call runs; pass
4951    /// the result to `crate::fifo_peer::forget_guest_made` if the call
4952    /// succeeds, so that a FIFO that later reuses the number is not taken for
4953    /// a guest's, while a FIFO that keeps a name stays a guest's. Only where
4954    /// the set is shared by every guest (`fifo_peer::guest_descriptors_are_visible`).
4955    pub(crate) fn guest_made_fifos_removed_by<'a, G: Guest<Self>>(
4956        &'a self,
4957        guest: &'a mut G,
4958        call: &'a Syscall,
4959    ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Vec<(u64, u64)>> + 'a {
4960        // The run's set, through no wrapper future of its own.
4961        self.guest_made_fifos_removed_from(guest, call, &crate::fifo_peer::GuestMadeRegistry)
4962    }
4963
4964    /// [`Self::guest_made_fifos_removed_by`] against the guest-made FIFOs
4965    /// `made`: the run's registry in production, a test's own set in tests,
4966    /// which so leave the process-wide registry untouched.
4967    pub(crate) async fn guest_made_fifos_removed_from<G, M>(
4968        &self,
4969        guest: &mut G,
4970        call: &Syscall,
4971        made: &M,
4972    ) -> Vec<(u64, u64)>
4973    where
4974        G: Guest<Self>,
4975        M: crate::fifo_peer::GuestMadeFifos + Sync,
4976    {
4977        // The call's number, then the backend capability, both lock-free,
4978        // before the registry's lock: most calls remove no name, and where
4979        // the capability is false (KVM, DBT) the set is never consulted. The
4980        // three conjuncts are pure, so their order changes no answer.
4981        if !removes_a_name(call.number())
4982            || !crate::fifo_peer::guest_descriptors_are_visible(
4983                &self.cfg.backend,
4984                guest.thread_state().physical_tid,
4985            )
4986            || !made.any()
4987        {
4988            return Vec::new();
4989        }
4990        let Some((removed, source)) = removed_names(call, false) else {
4991            return Vec::new();
4992        };
4993        let inputs = [removed.1, source.and_then(|source| source.1)];
4994        let Some(path) = removed.1 else {
4995            return Vec::new();
4996        };
4997        let Ok(stat) = Self::inject_lstatat(guest, removed.0, path, inputs).await else {
4998            return Vec::new();
4999        };
5000        let fifo = (stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino);
5001        if stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT != libc::S_IFIFO
5002            || !made.contains(fifo)
5003            || !retires_on_removal(&stat)
5004        {
5005            return Vec::new();
5006        }
5007        if let Some((dirfd, Some(path))) = source
5008            && Self::inject_lstatat(guest, dirfd, path, inputs)
5009                .await
5010                .is_ok_and(|source| (source.st_dev, source.st_ino) == fifo)
5011        {
5012            return Vec::new();
5013        }
5014        vec![fifo]
5015    }
5016
5017    /// After a successful `mknod` or `mknodat` that made a FIFO, record it as
5018    /// a guest's (`crate::fifo_peer::note_guest_made`), stat'ed at the name the
5019    /// call made, in the same turn. Only where a blocking open of it can wait
5020    /// in polling turns (sequentialized `hermit run` under a separate tracer
5021    /// whose guest thread IDs are host tasks).
5022    pub(crate) async fn note_guest_made_fifo<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &mut G, call: &Syscall) {
5023        // Only where one set serves every guest, as `fifo_at` requires.
5024        if !self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets()
5025            || self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
5026            || !crate::fifo_peer::guest_descriptors_are_visible(
5027                &self.cfg.backend,
5028                guest.thread_state().physical_tid,
5029            )
5030        {
5031            return;
5032        }
5033        let (dirfd, path, mode) = match call {
5034            #[cfg(not(target_arch = "aarch64"))]
5035            Syscall::Mknod(c) => (libc::AT_FDCWD, c.path(), c.mode().bits()),
5036            Syscall::Mknodat(c) => (c.dirfd(), c.path(), c.mode().bits()),
5037            _ => return,
5038        };
5039        if mode & libc::S_IFMT != libc::S_IFIFO {
5040            return;
5041        }
5042        let Some(path) = path else {
5043            return;
5044        };
5045        if let Ok(stat) = Self::inject_lstatat(guest, dirfd, path, [Some(path), None]).await
5046            && stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFIFO
5047        {
5048            crate::fifo_peer::note_guest_made((stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino));
5049        }
5050    }
5051
5052    /// Retire the mappings of `inodes`, whose last names a successful call
5053    /// removed (see [`Self::last_names_removed_by`] and `InodePool::retire`).
5054    pub(crate) async fn retire_removed_inodes<G: Guest<Self>>(
5055        &self,
5056        guest: &mut G,
5057        inodes: Vec<RawInode>,
5058    ) {
5059        for inode in inodes {
5060            retire_inode(guest, inode).await;
5061        }
5062    }
5063
5064    /// For `hermit run --verify` on a backend whose guest holds code that
5065    /// makes untraced syscalls (`Config::untraced_code_range`): report `/`
5066    /// when `call` may change the memory holding it (see
5067    /// [`may_change_untraced_code`]). Intact, that code faults right after
5068    /// its syscall, and the fault is reported (`handle_signal_event`); a
5069    /// guest that rewrote or replaced it could use it without faulting, so
5070    /// Detcore could not establish what the guest changed, and `/`, the
5071    /// ancestor of every path, keeps a host input change from being named
5072    /// in that run. Called before the call runs, whatever its outcome.
5073    pub(crate) async fn record_untraced_code_change<G: Guest<Self>>(
5074        &self,
5075        guest: &mut G,
5076        call: &Syscall,
5077    ) {
5078        let Some(range) = guest.config().untraced_code_range else {
5079            return;
5080        };
5081        let (number, args) = call.into_parts();
5082        if may_change_untraced_code(number, &args, range, default_huge_page_size()) {
5083            crate::tool_global::record_host_mutation(guest, String::from("/")).await;
5084        }
5085    }
5086
5087    /// Open an `exe` link, by `call`, as the image Detcore recorded for the
5088    /// process it reaches, `exe` (`Detcore::launched_exe`): Linux opens the
5089    /// image the link names, which the kernel's link here does not (it names
5090    /// the launcher). The kernel first opens the guest's spelling itself as
5091    /// a path (`O_PATH`), so whether the link is there and every error stay
5092    /// its own (an exited thread-group leader's `ENOENT`). Without a record,
5093    /// or for an image no longer at its path, which only the kernel's link to
5094    /// the image could still open, the run is refused by name.
5095    async fn open_launched_exe<G: Guest<Self>>(
5096        &self,
5097        guest: &mut G,
5098        call: syscalls::Openat,
5099        exe: Option<&crate::exec_record::ExecRecord>,
5100    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
5101        // The longest path Linux opens, NUL included.
5102        const CAPACITY: usize = libc::PATH_MAX as usize;
5103        let probe = syscalls::Openat::new()
5104            .with_dirfd(call.dirfd())
5105            .with_path(call.path())
5106            .with_flags(OFlag::O_PATH | OFlag::O_CLOEXEC);
5107        let probed = Self::inject_translated(guest, Syscall::from(probe)).await?;
5108        let _ = guest
5109            .inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(probed as RawFd))
5110            .await;
5111        let present = exe.filter(|exe| {
5112            self.guest_root(guest)
5113                .is_some_and(|root| exe.is_present(&root))
5114        });
5115        let Some(exe) = present else {
5116            return self.refuse_launched_exe(guest, Sysno::openat, exe).await;
5117        };
5118        let bytes = std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt::as_bytes(exe.exe.as_os_str());
5119        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
5120        if bytes.len() >= CAPACITY || stack.capacity() < CAPACITY {
5121            drop(stack);
5122            let reason = format!(
5123                "unsupported: opening the /proc/<pid>/exe link of {:?}, whose path does not \
5124                 fit the guest stack, where the kernel's link names the launcher",
5125                exe.exe
5126            );
5127            return self
5128                .refuse_launched_exe_because(guest, Sysno::openat, reason)
5129                .await;
5130        }
5131        let mut buffer = [0_u8; CAPACITY];
5132        buffer[..bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
5133        let address = stack.push(buffer).cast::<libc::c_char>();
5134        let stack_guard = stack.commit()?;
5135        let call = call.with_path(PathPtr::from_ptr(address.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char));
5136        let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, Syscall::Openat(call)).await;
5137        drop(stack_guard);
5138        Ok(result?)
5139    }
5140
5141    /// Whether guest descriptor `fd` is open on the launcher a launched run
5142    /// declared (`Detcore::launched_exe`), read where the tool shares the
5143    /// guest's descriptor table, as a launcher's tool does. Asked only for an
5144    /// open of a possible `exe` link
5145    /// (`crate::syscalls::namespace::exe_link_candidate`).
5146    fn opened_the_launcher(&self, fd: RawFd) -> bool {
5147        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
5148        let Some(launcher) = self.declared_launcher() else {
5149            return false;
5150        };
5151        if !self.cfg.backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table {
5152            return false;
5153        }
5154        let mut opened: libc::stat = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
5155        // Runtime-owned read-only inspection of the shared descriptor table.
5156        let result = unsafe {
5157            crate::util::raw_syscall(
5158                libc::SYS_fstat,
5159                [fd as u64, (&raw mut opened) as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0],
5160            )
5161        };
5162        result == 0
5163            && std::fs::metadata(launcher)
5164                .is_ok_and(|meta| (meta.dev(), meta.ino()) == (opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino))
5165    }
5166
5167    /// Openat system call.
5168    pub async fn handle_openat<G: Guest<Self>>(
5169        &self,
5170        guest: &mut G,
5171        call: syscalls::Openat,
5172    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
5173        let path = call.path().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
5174        let path: PathBuf = path.read(&guest.memory())?;
5175        // A relative spelling is not the object. `chdir("/sys/module/kvm");
5176        // open("refcnt")` and an absolute open name the SAME kernel object, so
5177        // classifying the unresolved lexical pathname lets one spelling bypass
5178        // normalization and expose the host value. Absolute paths are already
5179        // bound; a dirfd supplies its own prefix; AT_FDCWD-relative spellings
5180        // are resolved through the guest's root and cwd before the open so the
5181        // result does not depend on Replayer's placeholder descriptor.
5182        Self::prepare_guest_cwd(guest, call.dirfd(), &path).await;
5183        let observed_path = Self::observed_path(guest, call.dirfd(), &path)?;
5184        // The spelling Detcore's own lookups of the files it renders see.
5185        let procfs_spelling = self.procfs_spelling_at(guest, call.dirfd(), &path).await?;
5186        // A path below a descriptor directory Detcore serves is decided about
5187        // as the path Linux resolves it to, which its injection respells it to
5188        // (`descriptor_directory`).
5189        let below_descriptor_directory =
5190            Self::path_below_descriptor_directory(guest, call.dirfd(), &path, &observed_path);
5191        // The guest's own spelling is kept for the open of a descriptor
5192        // directory, which counts the links the spelling leads through.
5193        let (observed_path, procfs_spelling, guest_spelled) = match &below_descriptor_directory {
5194            Some(below) => (
5195                below.clone(),
5196                below.clone(),
5197                Some((observed_path, procfs_spelling)),
5198            ),
5199            None => (observed_path, procfs_spelling, None),
5200        };
5201        crate::race_probe::delay(crate::race_probe::PROCFS_SPELLING_RESOLVED).await;
5202        if guest.config().record_host_inputs && call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_CREAT) {
5203            // It may create the file it opens. Reported before the open runs,
5204            // as `record_host_namespace_change` reports the other changes.
5205            crate::tool_global::record_host_mutation(
5206                guest,
5207                rebound_path(Some(observed_path.clone())),
5208            )
5209            .await;
5210        }
5211
5212        let resource = ResourceID::Path(path.clone());
5213        // Ask for permission to resolve this path into a file:
5214        let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::R);
5215        resource_request(guest, request).await;
5216        // An empty path names nothing to `openat`, which has no
5217        // `AT_EMPTY_PATH`: the kernel's ENOENT.
5218        // A writable open of a `..` spelling that may name a `comm` Detcore
5219        // renders, which it cannot resolve, is refused by name rather than
5220        // forwarded (`Detcore::refuse_undetermined_comm_write`).
5221        let rendered = match if path.as_os_str().is_empty() {
5222            Ok(None)
5223        } else {
5224            match self
5225                .refuse_undetermined_comm_write(guest, &procfs_spelling, call.flags())
5226                .await
5227            {
5228                Ok(()) => self.rendered_procfs_at(guest, &procfs_spelling).await,
5229                Err(error) => Err(error),
5230            }
5231        } {
5232            Ok(rendered) => rendered,
5233            Err(error) => {
5234                resource_release_all(guest).await;
5235                // Flags `build_open_flags` refuses fail before the lookup.
5236                return Err(
5237                    rendered_procfs::open_flags_refused(call.flags()).map_or(error, Into::into)
5238                );
5239            }
5240        };
5241        // `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW` opens a descriptor link itself, which the
5242        // kernel has. Every other open of a rendered file is Detcore's, an
5243        // open of a rendered `comm` for writing included, which it refuses
5244        // with no injected call (`open_rendered_procfs`,
5245        // `rendered_procfs::asks_to_write_comm`).
5246        if let Some(target) = rendered.filter(|target| {
5247            !(target.via_link && call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_PATH | OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW))
5248        }) {
5249            let result = self.open_rendered_procfs(guest, call.flags(), target).await;
5250            resource_release_all(guest).await;
5251            return result;
5252        }
5253        // `/proc` itself, or the caller's own descriptor directory, which
5254        // Detcore serves on a placeholder descriptor, listing them from its
5255        // model on ptrace and KVM (`descriptor_directory`).
5256        if !path.as_os_str().is_empty()
5257            && !Self::starts_at_a_recorded_link(guest, call.dirfd(), &path)
5258            && let Some(opened) = self
5259                .descriptor_directory_opened(
5260                    guest,
5261                    guest_spelled
5262                        .as_ref()
5263                        .map_or(&observed_path, |(observed, _)| observed),
5264                    guest_spelled
5265                        .as_ref()
5266                        .map_or(&procfs_spelling, |(_, spelling)| spelling),
5267                    call.flags(),
5268                )
5269                .await
5270        {
5271            let result = match opened {
5272                Ok(opened) => self.open_placeholder(guest, call.flags(), opened).await,
5273                Err(errno) => Err(errno.into()),
5274            };
5275            resource_release_all(guest).await;
5276            return result;
5277        }
5278        // `/proc` itself, or a descriptor directory, where the guest's procfs
5279        // is the backend's own and Detcore serves no placeholder: refused
5280        // before the open can reach the backend's `/proc`
5281        // (`descriptor_directory`).
5282        if !path.as_os_str().is_empty()
5283            && !Self::starts_at_a_recorded_link(guest, call.dirfd(), &path)
5284            && Self::refuses_backend_procfs_directory(
5285                guest,
5286                guest_spelled
5287                    .as_ref()
5288                    .map_or(&observed_path, |(observed, _)| observed),
5289                guest_spelled
5290                    .as_ref()
5291                    .map_or(&procfs_spelling, |(_, spelling)| spelling),
5292            )
5293            .await
5294        {
5295            resource_release_all(guest).await;
5296            return Err(Errno::EACCES.into());
5297        }
5298        // An `exe` link Detcore answers from its record (`Detcore::launched_exe`)
5299        // opens that image, for reading only: a write open of a running image
5300        // is the kernel's `ETXTBSY`, `O_NOFOLLOW` its `ELOOP`, and `O_PATH`
5301        // with it the link itself.
5302        let launched_exe = if call.flags().bits() & libc::O_ACCMODE == libc::O_RDONLY
5303            && !call
5304                .flags()
5305                .intersects(OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW | OFlag::O_TRUNC | OFlag::O_CREAT)
5306        {
5307            self.launched_exe(guest, (call.dirfd(), &path), true).await
5308        } else {
5309            None
5310        };
5311        // Signal phase 1 (`sigalrm_phase1`): in a process that handles SIGALRM,
5312        // an open that may wait (a FIFO, a character or block device) is
5313        // refused. Checked after the grant: no other guest runs before the open.
5314        if guest.thread_state().sigalrm_handled
5315            && !call.flags().intersects(OFlag::O_DIRECTORY | OFlag::O_PATH)
5316            && let Some(path) = call.path()
5317            && crate::sigalrm_phase1::open_refused(
5318                Self::inject_statat(
5319                    guest,
5320                    call.dirfd(),
5321                    path,
5322                    [Some(path), None],
5323                    AtFlags::empty(),
5324                )
5325                .await,
5326                call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_NONBLOCK),
5327            )
5328        {
5329            return Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP.into());
5330        }
5331        // The descriptor a descriptor link in the spelling names, as the open
5332        // finds it now, in its own turn, where the kernel looks the link up
5333        // (`LinkSource`). The open below may block and leave the turn.
5334        let link_source = crate::syscalls::namespace::own_descriptor_link(
5335            &observed_path,
5336            self.procfs_caller_ids(guest),
5337        )
5338        .and_then(|link| {
5339            guest
5340                .thread_state()
5341                .with_detfd(link.fd, |detfd| LinkSource {
5342                    fd: link.fd,
5343                    path: detfd.path(),
5344                    open_file: detfd.open_file_id(),
5345                    reached: detfd.procfs_reached(),
5346                })
5347                .ok()
5348        });
5349        // A blocking open, for reading or for writing, of a FIFO a guest made
5350        // waits in polling turns for a guest at the other end
5351        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/2203).
5352        let own_ids = self.procfs_caller_ids(guest);
5353        let fifo = (self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets()
5354            && !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
5355            && !call.flags().intersects(OFlag::O_NONBLOCK | OFlag::O_PATH)
5356            && call.flags().bits() & libc::O_ACCMODE != libc::O_RDWR)
5357            .then(|| {
5358                // The tracer looks a path below a descriptor directory up as
5359                // the guest's injection is respelled.
5360                let (dirfd, path) = match &below_descriptor_directory {
5361                    Some(below) => (libc::AT_FDCWD, below.as_path()),
5362                    None => (call.dirfd(), path.as_path()),
5363                };
5364                crate::fifo_peer::fifo_at(
5365                    &self.cfg.backend,
5366                    guest.thread_state().physical_tid,
5367                    guest.tid().as_raw(),
5368                    own_ids,
5369                    dirfd,
5370                    path,
5371                )
5372            })
5373            .flatten()
5374            // Only a FIFO a guest made; every other one is opened as before.
5375            .filter(|(fifo, _)| crate::fifo_peer::is_guest_made(*fifo));
5376        // A later descriptor lookup proves the object, while this observation
5377        // brackets its kernel open against target exec/PID replacement.
5378        let maps_before = if guest.runtime_private_memory_regions().is_some() {
5379            if let Some((pid, tid)) = self.procfs_caller_ids(guest)
5380                && let Some(task) = crate::procfs::maps_task_at(&procfs_spelling, pid, tid)
5381            {
5382                Some((task, crate::tool_global::procfs_task(guest, task).await))
5383            } else {
5384                None
5385            }
5386        } else {
5387            None
5388        };
5389        let res: Result<i64, Error> = match fifo {
5390            Some((fifo, fifo_path)) => {
5391                self.open_fifo_once_a_guest_holds_its_peer(guest, call, fifo, &fifo_path)
5392                    .await
5393            }
5394            None => match launched_exe {
5395                Some(exe) => self.open_launched_exe(guest, call, exe.as_deref()).await,
5396                None => self
5397                    .record_or_replay(guest, Syscall::Openat(call))
5398                    .await
5399                    .map_err(Error::from),
5400            },
5401        };
5402
5403        match res {
5404            Ok(fd) => {
5405                let fd = fd as RawFd;
5406                // A link Detcore could not resolve whose kernel open reached
5407                // the launcher, in the guest's image's place.
5408                if crate::syscalls::namespace::exe_link_candidate(&path)
5409                    && self.opened_the_launcher(fd)
5410                {
5411                    let _ = guest.inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd)).await;
5412                    resource_release_all(guest).await;
5413                    return self.refuse_launched_exe(guest, Sysno::openat, None).await;
5414                }
5415                // Another process's descriptor link, or another spelling of
5416                // this one's, to a placeholder: the guest opened the rendered
5417                // file again, as Linux opens the procfs file again.
5418                // (Where one tool process serves every guest, it knows every
5419                // placeholder, and a run that made none pays nothing.)
5420                if names_descriptor_link(&observed_path)
5421                    && !call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_PATH | OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW)
5422                    && (rendered_procfs::placeholders_exist()
5423                        || guest.config().backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table)
5424                {
5425                    let behind = self.rendered_procfs_behind(guest, fd).await;
5426                    if !matches!(behind, Ok(None)) {
5427                        let _ = guest.inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd)).await;
5428                    }
5429                    let result = match behind {
5430                        Ok(None) => None,
5431                        Ok(Some(path)) => {
5432                            let target = rendered_procfs::RenderedTarget {
5433                                procfs: ProcfsFile::from_rendered_path(path)
5434                                    .expect("a rendered path is a procfs file"),
5435                                via_link: true,
5436                            };
5437                            Some(self.open_rendered_procfs(guest, call.flags(), target).await)
5438                        }
5439                        Err(error) => Some(Err(error)),
5440                    };
5441                    if let Some(result) = result {
5442                        resource_release_all(guest).await;
5443                        return result;
5444                    }
5445                }
5446                // Under a network trace mode only; the run ends before the
5447                // guest sees the descriptor.
5448                let pid = guest.pid().as_raw();
5449                let backend = self.cfg.backend;
5450                self.network_check_open(guest, &observed_path, || {
5451                    resolved_open_path(&backend, pid, fd)
5452                })
5453                .await;
5454                // Linux's random devices are classified below by the device
5455                // the open reached. An `O_PATH` descriptor, which reads
5456                // nothing, keeps the type its literal name gave it before.
5457                let fd_type = path.to_str().map_or(FdType::Regular, |fname| {
5458                    if call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_PATH)
5459                        && (fname == "/dev/random" || fname == "/dev/urandom")
5460                    {
5461                        FdType::Rng
5462                    } else {
5463                        FdType::Regular
5464                    }
5465                });
5466                // A guest-created pipe reopened by path (`/dev/stdin`,
5467                // `/proc/self/fd/N`, bash's `< <(cmd)` as `/dev/fd/63`) is a NEW open
5468                // file description, so it carries neither the Pipe type nor the
5469                // physical O_NONBLOCK that `handle_pipe2` gave the original. Left as a
5470                // physically blocking Regular fd, a read that waits for a writer blocks
5471                // in the kernel while holding the scheduler turn, and the writer never
5472                // runs (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1850). Give it the
5473                // same treatment as `handle_pipe2`: Pipe type plus a Detcore-internal
5474                // physical O_NONBLOCK, which F_GETFL hides from the guest. Only a pipe
5475                // this process already holds as scheduler-managed qualifies; a host
5476                // pipe or a named FIFO keeps `deterministic_read`'s Regular handling.
5477                // Gated like the forced O_NONBLOCK in F_SETFL: Replayer's descriptor
5478                // is an eventfd placeholder, so record and replay would not classify
5479                // alike.
5480                let fd_type = if fd_type == FdType::Regular
5481                    && self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets()
5482                    && !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
5483                    && !call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_PATH)
5484                    && reopens_scheduler_managed_pipe(
5485                        &self.cfg.backend,
5486                        guest.pid().as_raw(),
5487                        fd,
5488                        &guest.thread_state().scheduler_managed_pipe_fds(),
5489                    )
5490                    && (call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_NONBLOCK)
5491                        || self.inject_physical_nonblocking(guest, fd).await.is_ok())
5492                {
5493                    FdType::Pipe
5494                } else {
5495                    fd_type
5496                };
5497                let host_stat = self
5498                    .add_fd_with_stat(guest, fd, call.flags(), fd_type)
5499                    .await?;
5500                // Linux names a random device by its device number, whatever
5501                // path reached it (a literal or relative name, `.` or `..`, a
5502                // symbolic link, `/proc/self/fd/N`, a bind mount, a copy of
5503                // the node), so every such open reads Detcore's stream, not
5504                // the host's entropy (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4544).
5505                // The device number comes from the `fstat` taken above when
5506                // metadata is virtualized, so the default run makes no extra
5507                // call; otherwise from one `fstat`, which under record and
5508                // replay goes through the recording, so replay classifies by
5509                // the recorded device, not by its placeholder's. If that
5510                // `fstat` fails, the open fails with its error: a descriptor
5511                // Detcore could not classify must not read the host.
5512                let fd_type = if fd_type == FdType::Regular && !call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_PATH)
5513                {
5514                    match self
5515                        .opened_random_device(guest, fd, host_stat.as_ref())
5516                        .await
5517                    {
5518                        Ok(true) => {
5519                            guest.thread_state().classify_random_device(fd)?;
5520                            FdType::Rng
5521                        }
5522                        Ok(false) => fd_type,
5523                        // Under record and replay, a buffer the guest's
5524                        // address space could not provide was never
5525                        // recorded; continuing would consume a different
5526                        // event than the other run did, so the run stops.
5527                        Err(StatFailure::Scratch(errno)) if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes => {
5528                            resource_release_all(guest).await;
5529                            return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
5530                                "cannot classify fd {fd} under record and replay: no buffer \
5531                                 for its fstat ({errno})"
5532                            )));
5533                        }
5534                        Err(failure) => {
5535                            let cleanup = self.close_unclassified(guest, fd).await;
5536                            resource_release_all(guest).await;
5537                            cleanup?;
5538                            return Err(failure.errno().into());
5539                        }
5540                    }
5541                } else {
5542                    fd_type
5543                };
5544                // A placeholder reached through any other spelling (a symbolic
5545                // link to a descriptor link, `/dev/stdin`): the kernel opened
5546                // the placeholder, which is the rendered file again, also for
5547                // `O_PATH`. The kernel already followed every link, so none
5548                // remains for `O_NOFOLLOW` to refuse (an `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW`
5549                // descriptor for a link is the link, no placeholder).
5550                // Without virtualized metadata no stat was taken; take one
5551                // while a placeholder may be about.
5552                let identity = match &host_stat {
5553                    Some(stat) => Some(*stat),
5554                    None if (self.renders_procfs(guest)
5555                        && (guest.thread_state().holds_a_rendered_procfs_file()
5556                            || rendered_procfs::placeholders_exist()))
5557                        || guest.config().directory_placeholder.is_some() =>
5558                    {
5559                        self.inject_fstat(guest, fd).await.ok()
5560                    }
5561                    None => None,
5562                };
5563                // The placeholder directory, reached through a spelling the
5564                // `--proc` level table could not resolve: hidden, as
5565                // `/proc/fs` is (`descriptor_directory`).
5566                if let Some(stat) = &identity
5567                    && Self::reaches_hidden_placeholder(
5568                        guest,
5569                        stat.st_mode,
5570                        stat.st_dev,
5571                        stat.st_ino,
5572                    )
5573                    .await
5574                {
5575                    guest.thread_state().remove_fd(fd);
5576                    let _ = guest.inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd)).await;
5577                    resource_release_all(guest).await;
5578                    return Err(Errno::ENOENT.into());
5579                }
5580                let reached = match &identity {
5581                    Some(stat) if self.renders_procfs(guest) => {
5582                        self.recognize_placeholder(
5583                            guest,
5584                            &DetStat::from(*stat),
5585                            StatTarget::Descriptor(fd),
5586                        )
5587                        .await
5588                    }
5589                    _ => None,
5590                };
5591                if let Some(path) = reached {
5592                    guest.thread_state().remove_fd(fd);
5593                    let _ = guest.inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd)).await;
5594                    let target = rendered_procfs::RenderedTarget {
5595                        procfs: ProcfsFile::from_rendered_path(path)
5596                            .expect("a rendered path is a procfs file"),
5597                        via_link: false,
5598                    };
5599                    let result = self.open_rendered_procfs(guest, call.flags(), target).await;
5600                    resource_release_all(guest).await;
5601                    return result;
5602                }
5603                // A `/proc` name outside the run's level that the kernel
5604                // reached through a spelling the lookup check does not
5605                // resolve (a symbolic link, `..`), named by the kernel's path
5606                // for the descriptor (see `refuse_procfs_name_outside_level`).
5607                if self
5608                    .opened_procfs_name_outside_level(
5609                        guest,
5610                        fd,
5611                        identity.as_ref().map(|stat| (stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino)),
5612                    )
5613                    .await
5614                {
5615                    guest.thread_state().remove_fd(fd);
5616                    let _ = guest.inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd)).await;
5617                    resource_release_all(guest).await;
5618                    return Err(Errno::ENOENT.into());
5619                }
5620                // A FIFO (a named one, or a pipe reached by path that the
5621                // check above left `Regular`) stays `Regular` and physically
5622                // blocking, so a FIFO whose other end is on the host blocks as
5623                // before. Its first blocking read or write that finds a guest
5624                // holding the other end makes it an internally polled pipe
5625                // (`fifo_polls_if_a_guest_holds_its_peer`). Run mode only, as
5626                // for a reopened pipe: Replayer's descriptor is a placeholder.
5627                // `fifo_of` finds a FIFO only where it can read the guest's
5628                // descriptors through `/proc/<tid>`: under a separate tracer
5629                // (not DBT, in its PID container) whose guest thread IDs are
5630                // host tasks (not KVM). Elsewhere a FIFO blocks as before.
5631                if fd_type == FdType::Regular
5632                    && self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets()
5633                    && !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
5634                    && !call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_PATH)
5635                    && let Some(fifo) = crate::fifo_peer::fifo_of(
5636                        &self.cfg.backend,
5637                        guest.thread_state().physical_tid,
5638                        guest.tid().as_raw(),
5639                        fd,
5640                    )
5641                {
5642                    guest
5643                        .thread_state()
5644                        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.mark_fifo_awaiting_guest_peer())?;
5645                    crate::fifo_peer::note_guest_open(fifo, call.flags().bits());
5646                    // Name the FIFO for `--pipe-wake-latency`, and ready the
5647                    // opens waiting for the end this one opened.
5648                    if self.cfg.pipe_wake_latency_in_effect().is_some() {
5649                        let accmode = call.flags().bits() & libc::O_ACCMODE;
5650                        let end = crate::pipe_wake::ChannelEnd {
5651                            channel: crate::pipe_wake::ChannelId::Fifo(
5652                                crate::fifo_peer::fifo_channel(fifo),
5653                            ),
5654                            reads: accmode != libc::O_WRONLY,
5655                            writes: accmode != libc::O_RDONLY,
5656                        };
5657                        guest
5658                            .thread_state()
5659                            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_channel(end))?;
5660                        for (applies, readies) in [
5661                            (end.reads, crate::pipe_wake::Wants::PeerReader),
5662                            (end.writes, crate::pipe_wake::Wants::PeerWriter),
5663                        ] {
5664                            if applies {
5665                                self.note_pipe_readied(guest, end.channel, readies).await;
5666                            }
5667                        }
5668                    }
5669                }
5670                if let (true, Some(stat)) = (guest.config().record_host_inputs, &host_stat) {
5671                    let identity = detcore_model::host_input::HostFileIdentity::from_stat(stat);
5672                    let file_type = stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT;
5673                    // Where the tool can name the guest's descriptor, the
5674                    // kernel's path for it (a readlink, which raises no
5675                    // inotify event the guest could see): whether it reached
5676                    // a kernel object whatever path the guest spelled, and
5677                    // otherwise, for a regular file or a directory, where the
5678                    // run's end reads its bytes or names, which the guest
5679                    // sees where it does not see the host's inode or times
5680                    // (`crate::host_inputs::content_at_end`). Nothing is read
5681                    // now, while the guest runs.
5682                    let target = crate::fifo_peer::guest_descriptors_are_visible(
5683                        &self.cfg.backend,
5684                        guest.thread_state().physical_tid,
5685                    )
5686                    .then(|| {
5687                        crate::util::raw_read_link(Path::new(&format!(
5688                            "/proc/{}/fd/{fd}",
5689                            guest.tid().as_raw()
5690                        )))
5691                        .ok()
5692                    })
5693                    .flatten();
5694                    // A FIFO, a socket or a device holds no bytes the run's
5695                    // end could read and no content a replay could compare:
5696                    // what the guest reads from it comes from whatever
5697                    // writes to it, and its times move with each write
5698                    // (the recorded run's own writes to a FIFO among them).
5699                    // It counts as a kernel object, as one under /dev does.
5700                    let kernel_object = matches!(
5701                        file_type,
5702                        libc::S_IFIFO | libc::S_IFSOCK | libc::S_IFCHR | libc::S_IFBLK
5703                    ) || target.as_deref().is_some_and(|target| {
5704                        detcore_model::host_input::is_kernel_object(&target.to_string_lossy())
5705                    });
5706                    let source = target
5707                        .filter(|_| {
5708                            !kernel_object && matches!(file_type, libc::S_IFREG | libc::S_IFDIR)
5709                        })
5710                        .and_then(|target| target.to_str().map(str::to_owned));
5711                    crate::tool_global::record_host_input(
5712                        guest,
5713                        observed_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
5714                        identity,
5715                        source,
5716                        file_type == libc::S_IFREG,
5717                        false,
5718                        kernel_object,
5719                    )
5720                    .await;
5721                }
5722                // An open that finds its file linked, or creates it
5723                // (`O_TMPFILE`), reaches a file that has a name or never had
5724                // one, so a retired mapping of its inode described a file the
5725                // host has freed (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3840).
5726                // Reopening an unlinked file through `/proc/self/fd/N` finds no
5727                // link and keeps it.
5728                if let Some(stat) = &host_stat
5729                    && (stat.st_nlink > 0 || call.flags().contains(OFlag::O_TMPFILE))
5730                {
5731                    // A procfs entry the host rebuilt keeps its number when it is
5732                    // next written or read through this descriptor.
5733                    let procfs =
5734                        Self::procfs_entry(guest, &DetStat::from(stat), StatTarget::Descriptor(fd))
5735                            .await;
5736                    forget_retired_inode(
5737                        guest,
5738                        RawInode::new(stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino),
5739                        procfs.name(stat.st_dev),
5740                    )
5741                    .await;
5742                }
5743                // A descriptor that writes process memory can rewrite the
5744                // untraced code (see `record_untraced_code_change`). Reported
5745                // once the open returns, before the guest has the descriptor;
5746                // the record has no position in the run, so it covers every
5747                // write through it.
5748                if guest.config().record_host_inputs
5749                    && guest.config().untraced_code_range.is_some()
5750                    && may_write_process_memory(
5751                        call.flags(),
5752                        descriptor_identity(guest.tid().as_raw(), fd)
5753                            .as_ref()
5754                            .map(|(link, on_procfs)| (link.as_path(), *on_procfs)),
5755                    )
5756                {
5757                    crate::tool_global::record_host_mutation(guest, String::from("/")).await;
5758                }
5759                // A session leader with no controlling terminal that opens a
5760                // terminal without O_NOCTTY gains it as one, and the terminal
5761                // can then signal the session and its foreground process group
5762                // at moments set by host timing (`terminal_signals`). Hold
5763                // those signals in every process, as `handle_ioctl` does for
5764                // TIOCSCTTY and TIOCGPTPEER. Only the kernel knows whether this
5765                // open made the terminal controlling, so the record is made
5766                // after the call; it is still this thread's turn, and no other
5767                // thread's gated wait reads the record before the turn ends.
5768                // Skipped under record and replay: Replayer's descriptor is a
5769                // placeholder that never becomes a terminal, so the two runs
5770                // would not record alike.
5771                if guest.config().backend.host_timed_signals_are_physical
5772                    && !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
5773                    && open_can_acquire_controlling_terminal(call.flags())
5774                    && opened_controlling_terminal(guest.pid().as_raw(), fd, host_stat.as_ref())
5775                {
5776                    record_host_timed_signals(
5777                        guest,
5778                        HostTimedSignalScope::Container,
5779                        terminal_signals(),
5780                    )
5781                    .await;
5782                }
5783                if fd_type == FdType::Pipe {
5784                    self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fd);
5785                }
5786                // Classify the spelling the guest used FIRST. Several kinds are
5787                // defined by that spelling and MUST keep it: `/proc/self/...`,
5788                // `/proc/thread-self/...` and the mountinfo aliases all resolve
5789                // through `/proc/<pid>/fd/<fd>` to a numeric `/proc/<pid>/...`
5790                // path, which is a DIFFERENT (or absent) classification. So
5791                // resolution must never overwrite a spelling that already
5792                // classifies.
5793                //
5794                // Only when the spelling yields nothing do we ask the kernel
5795                // what the descriptor actually names. That is exactly the
5796                // AT_FDCWD/alias gap -- `chdir("/sys/module/kvm"); open("refcnt")`
5797                // classifies as nothing lexically -- and scoping it this way
5798                // makes the fallback MONOTONE: it can only add a classification
5799                // where there was none, never change one that already existed.
5800                //
5801                // Under record and replay the descriptor's link is read through
5802                // the recording: replay holds the descriptor's number with an
5803                // eventfd, which resolves to no procfs file, so both runs must
5804                // classify the open by the link the recording read
5805                // (`recorded_open_path`).
5806                // A process's `auxv` the kernel opened keeps the kernel's
5807                // bytes, unclassified, as before Detcore rendered the file,
5808                // and so does a file of a CPU the machine does not have
5809                // (`ProcfsFile::of_kernel_open`): by its spelling here, and
5810                // by its link below.
5811                let cpus = self.cfg.virtual_cpu_count();
5812                let mut procfs = ProcfsFile::of_kernel_open(&observed_path, cpus);
5813                // Whether the guest's own spelling classified the open, not the
5814                // descriptor's link, whose numbers are the kernel's.
5815                let classified_by_spelling = procfs.is_some();
5816                // Under record and replay the link is read for every open,
5817                // also one whose spelling classifies: a spelling through `..`
5818                // (`/proc/self/../self/io`) classifies as the file it reaches,
5819                // which may be outside the level.
5820                if procfs.is_none() || self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
5821                    let resolved = if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
5822                        self.recorded_open_path(guest, fd).await?
5823                    } else if crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors(
5824                        &self.cfg.backend,
5825                    ) {
5826                        resolved_open_path(&self.cfg.backend, guest.pid().as_raw(), fd)
5827                    } else if call.dirfd() != libc::AT_FDCWD && !path.is_absolute() {
5828                        // Where the tool cannot read the guest's descriptor
5829                        // links itself, it asks the kernel beneath the backend
5830                        // for the same link (`descriptor_kernel_link`, one
5831                        // injected `readlinkat`), but only for a lookup
5832                        // relative to a directory descriptor: its prefix is
5833                        // that directory's recorded spelling, which need not
5834                        // name the directory (a symbolic link, a `..`, a `.`
5835                        // after `chdir`, a descriptor received over a
5836                        // socket), so `openat(dirfd, "cpu0/cpufreq/boost")`
5837                        // must classify by the object as it does where the
5838                        // tool reads the link. Absolute and AT_FDCWD-relative
5839                        // spellings stay lexical there, so that an
5840                        // unclassified open costs no injected call. Without
5841                        // sequentialized threads, a sibling's dup2 over the
5842                        // descriptor before the install below can misattach
5843                        // the class, as for a spelling-classified open on
5844                        // every backend
5845                        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4543).
5846                        Self::descriptor_kernel_link(guest, fd)
5847                            .await
5848                            .filter(|link| link.is_absolute())
5849                    } else {
5850                        None
5851                    };
5852                    // Under record and replay, a `/proc` name outside the
5853                    // run's level that a spelling the lookup check does not
5854                    // resolve reached, named by the link the recording read
5855                    // (in the guest's view, also after a `chroot`), so both
5856                    // runs refuse it alike (outside record and replay the
5857                    // check after the open above does it). Only where the
5858                    // recording saw that the descriptor is procfs: after a
5859                    // `chroot`, or under a user bind, `/proc` need not be.
5860                    if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
5861                        && resolved.as_deref().is_some_and(|resolved| {
5862                            levels::procfs_name(resolved)
5863                                .is_some_and(|name| name.absent_at(self.cfg.proc_level))
5864                        })
5865                        // And the descriptor is procfs, not a user bind over
5866                        // part of `/proc`, as the recording saw it.
5867                        && self.recorded_descriptor_is_on_procfs(guest, fd).await
5868                    {
5869                        guest.thread_state().remove_fd(fd);
5870                        let _ = self
5871                            .record_or_replay(guest, syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd))
5872                            .await;
5873                        resource_release_all(guest).await;
5874                        return Err(Errno::ENOENT.into());
5875                    }
5876                    if procfs.is_none() {
5877                        procfs = resolved
5878                            .filter(|resolved| resolved != &observed_path)
5879                            .and_then(|resolved| ProcfsFile::of_kernel_open(&resolved, cpus));
5880                    }
5881                }
5882                // A process's cgroup file bind-mounted at another path, or
5883                // reached through another procfs mount, classifies by neither
5884                // its spelling nor its link, which names the bind's mount
5885                // point, and would read as the host's bytes. Name the procfs
5886                // entry the descriptor reaches, as a stat does, and classify
5887                // that name, so the alias is the file it is (Codex review of
5888                // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4386). Only that
5889                // kind (`ProcfsFile::may_be_named_by_provenance`): a mountinfo
5890                // file of another procfs mount failed its identity check and
5891                // stopped the run (Claude re-check). Like the link above, this
5892                // only adds a classification. Record and replay name no
5893                // entries, and without sequentialized threads naming records a
5894                // determinism loss for any file that may be procfs, so neither
5895                // looks.
5896                if procfs.is_none()
5897                    && guest.config().sequentialize_threads
5898                    && let Some(stat) = host_stat
5899                    && let ProcfsEntry::At(within) =
5900                        Self::procfs_entry(guest, &DetStat::from(stat), StatTarget::Descriptor(fd))
5901                            .await
5902                {
5903                    procfs = ProcfsFile::from_path(
5904                        &Path::new("/proc").join(within.strip_prefix("/").unwrap_or(&within)),
5905                    )
5906                    .filter(ProcfsFile::may_be_named_by_provenance);
5907                }
5908                if guest.runtime_private_memory_regions().is_some()
5909                    && procfs
5910                        .as_ref()
5911                        .and_then(ProcfsFile::private_mapping_format)
5912                        .is_some()
5913                    && let Some(stat) = host_stat
5914                {
5915                    match self
5916                        .maps_descriptor_entry(guest, &DetStat::from(stat), fd)
5917                        .await
5918                    {
5919                        ProcfsEntry::At(within) => {
5920                            let actual = Path::new("/proc")
5921                                .join(within.strip_prefix("/").unwrap_or(&within));
5922                            if let Some(task) = self.maps_guest_target(guest, &actual).await
5923                                && let Some((before_task, before)) = maps_before.as_ref()
5924                                && *before_task == task
5925                            {
5926                                let after = crate::tool_global::procfs_task(guest, task).await;
5927                                if let Some(target) =
5928                                    crate::procfs::MapsTarget::from_open(task, before, &after)
5929                                    && guest.runtime_private_memory_is_current(&target.private)
5930                                {
5931                                    procfs.as_mut().unwrap().bind_maps_target(target);
5932                                }
5933                            }
5934                        }
5935                        // A shadowed proc spelling is an ordinary file. Its
5936                        // contents must not receive procfs projection at all.
5937                        ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs => procfs = None,
5938                        ProcfsEntry::Unnamed | ProcfsEntry::Unknown => {}
5939                    }
5940                }
5941                // A process's `mountinfo` or `mounts` the kernel opened reads
5942                // the view its task's root gives it, decided now, at the open,
5943                // as Linux takes the root at the open.
5944                if let Some(file) = procfs.as_ref()
5945                    && file.mount_table_rendering().is_some()
5946                {
5947                    let kernel = self.mount_view_is_kernel(guest, file).await;
5948                    procfs
5949                        .as_mut()
5950                        .expect("a classified procfs file disappeared")
5951                        .pin_mount_view(kernel);
5952                }
5953                if procfs
5954                    .as_ref()
5955                    .is_some_and(ProcfsFile::needs_bound_thread_identity)
5956                {
5957                    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-964): Bind thread-self at open time,
5958                    // matching procfs inode resolution even if another thread or
5959                    // a forked process later reads the shared descriptor.
5960                    let tgid = guest.inject(syscalls::Getpid::new()).await? as i32;
5961                    let tid = guest.inject(syscalls::Gettid::new()).await? as i32;
5962                    let ppid = guest.inject(syscalls::Getppid::new()).await? as i32;
5963                    procfs
5964                        .as_mut()
5965                        .expect("thread identity request lost its procfs file")
5966                        .bind_thread_identity(tgid, tid, ppid);
5967                }
5968                // A task's `schedstat` describes the task its path named at
5969                // the open, `self` and `thread-self` resolved then, as Linux
5970                // resolves them at lookup, and a directory descriptor's task as
5971                // its open found it (`procfs_spelling`). Only by a spelling,
5972                // whose numbers are Detcore's, and outside a nested PID
5973                // namespace (`Detcore::procfs_caller_ids`), where Linux reads
5974                // the numbers in the namespace of the procfs mount
5975                // (`proc_pid_lookup`), not the caller's: no task otherwise, and
5976                // the file shows no runtime.
5977                if procfs.as_ref().is_some_and(ProcfsFile::is_task_schedstat) {
5978                    let thread = self
5979                        .procfs_caller_ids(guest)
5980                        .filter(|_| classified_by_spelling)
5981                        .and_then(|(pid, tid)| {
5982                            crate::procfs::schedstat_task_at(&procfs_spelling, pid, tid)
5983                        })
5984                        .map(crate::types::DetTid::from_raw);
5985                    procfs
5986                        .as_mut()
5987                        .expect("a classified procfs file disappeared")
5988                        .bind_schedstat_thread(thread);
5989                }
5990                if procfs
5991                    .as_ref()
5992                    .and_then(ProcfsFile::timer_slack_target)
5993                    .is_some()
5994                {
5995                    let target = procfs
5996                        .as_ref()
5997                        .and_then(ProcfsFile::timer_slack_target)
5998                        .expect("timer-slack target disappeared");
5999                    let stat = match guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.stat())? {
6000                        Some(stat) => libc::stat::from(&stat),
6001                        None => self.inject_fstat(guest, fd).await?,
6002                    };
6003                    // Recorder opens a real proc inode, while Replayer reserves
6004                    // the recorded descriptor number with an anonymous eventfd.
6005                    // A real proc descriptor is the strongest open-time task
6006                    // incarnation witness. For a virtual replay descriptor,
6007                    // bind the live numeric proc path instead; every operation
6008                    // re-resolves that same path, so exit or TID reuse still
6009                    // changes the inode and returns ESRCH.
6010                    let identity = if stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFREG {
6011                        (stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino)
6012                    } else {
6013                        self.observe_timer_slack_identity(guest, target)
6014                            .await?
6015                            .unwrap_or((stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino))
6016                    };
6017                    procfs
6018                        .as_mut()
6019                        .expect("timer-slack classification disappeared")
6020                        .bind_timer_slack_identity(identity.0, identity.1);
6021                }
6022                // Signal phase 1: what the kernel says this file is, for the
6023                // table's descriptor rules (`sigalrm_phase1`).
6024                let provenance = guest
6025                    .thread_state()
6026                    .sigalrm_handled
6027                    .then(|| crate::sigalrm_phase1::kernel_provenance(guest.pid().as_raw(), fd));
6028                // An open through one of the caller's descriptor links
6029                // records the path of the descriptor it reopens, so that a
6030                // name relative to it (`openat(fd, "stat")` with `fd` from
6031                // `open("/proc/self/fd/<a /proc descriptor>")`) is the file
6032                // Linux finds there (see `path_to_record_for_open`, which
6033                // also keeps the spelling wherever the link may reach
6034                // another file). Not after a `chroot`, where `/proc` and
6035                // `/dev/fd` need not be what they are outside it.
6036                //
6037                // The leader holds the table procfs reads for
6038                // `/proc/self/fd`, and so does every thread that holds the
6039                // same table: the process's, which the group shares
6040                // (`process_files`). Not known only for a state restored
6041                // from before that was kept, where only the leader is shown
6042                // to hold it.
6043                let opener = {
6044                    let detpid = self.own_detpid(guest);
6045                    let state = guest.thread_state();
6046                    DescriptorLinkOpener {
6047                        own: self.procfs_caller_ids(guest),
6048                        holds_process_table: state.dettid == detpid || state.holds_process_files(),
6049                    }
6050                };
6051                // Where `N`, in the caller's own table, has no recorded path
6052                // at all (a descriptor received through SCM_RIGHTS, recorded
6053                // without one or not recorded, or one discovered without one), a
6054                // procfs directory is named as the kernel beneath the backend
6055                // names the opened descriptor (`procfs_directory_named_for`,
6056                // one injected `readlinkat`). Only where Detcore renders
6057                // procfs files (not under record and replay, which does not
6058                // record that call, nor after a `chroot`), and with
6059                // sequentialized threads, so that no other guest thread can
6060                // replace the descriptor before the link is read.
6061                let unrecorded_link_identity = if self.renders_procfs(guest)
6062                    && guest.config().sequentialize_threads
6063                    && !opens_the_link_itself(&observed_path, call.flags())
6064                    && host_stat.is_none_or(|stat| stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFDIR)
6065                    && link_source
6066                        .as_ref()
6067                        .is_none_or(|source| source.path.is_none())
6068                    && crate::syscalls::namespace::own_descriptor_link(&observed_path, opener.own)
6069                        .is_some_and(|link| {
6070                            link.table == crate::syscalls::namespace::DescriptorTable::Thread
6071                                || opener.holds_process_table
6072                        }) {
6073                    Self::procfs_directory_named_for(guest, fd).await
6074                } else {
6075                    None
6076                };
6077                let recorded_path = {
6078                    let state = guest.thread_state();
6079                    if state.changed_root.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
6080                        observed_path.clone()
6081                    } else {
6082                        // `N` as the lookup saw it, and only if `N` still holds
6083                        // the same open file description: a thread sharing
6084                        // the table may have replaced it while the open
6085                        // waited (`LinkSource`).
6086                        path_to_record_for_open(
6087                            &observed_path,
6088                            call.flags(),
6089                            opener,
6090                            |target| {
6091                                link_source.as_ref().and_then(|source| {
6092                                    source.path_if_unchanged(
6093                                        target,
6094                                        state.with_detfd(target, |detfd| detfd.open_file_id()).ok(),
6095                                    )
6096                                })
6097                            },
6098                            unrecorded_link_identity,
6099                        )
6100                    }
6101                };
6102                // A `/proc/self` or `/proc/thread-self` directory, opened by
6103                // that spelling or through a descriptor link to one, is the
6104                // task the selector reached at its first open; a name below it
6105                // is that task's file whoever looks it up (a fork's child, a
6106                // thread). Recorded only where Detcore renders per-process
6107                // files, which read it.
6108                let link_itself = self.renders_procfs(guest)
6109                    && opens_the_link_itself(&procfs_spelling, call.flags())
6110                    && names_a_selector_link(&procfs_spelling);
6111                let reached = if self.renders_procfs(guest) {
6112                    let linked = {
6113                        let state = guest.thread_state();
6114                        crate::syscalls::namespace::own_descriptor_link(&observed_path, opener.own)
6115                            .filter(|link| {
6116                                !opens_the_link_itself(&observed_path, call.flags())
6117                                    && (link.table
6118                                        == crate::syscalls::namespace::DescriptorTable::Thread
6119                                        || opener.holds_process_table)
6120                            })
6121                            .and_then(|link| {
6122                                link_source.as_ref().and_then(|source| {
6123                                    source.reached_if_unchanged(
6124                                        link.fd,
6125                                        state
6126                                            .with_detfd(link.fd, |detfd| detfd.open_file_id())
6127                                            .ok(),
6128                                    )
6129                                })
6130                            })
6131                    };
6132                    match linked {
6133                        Some(reached) => Some(reached),
6134                        // An `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW` open of `/proc/self` or
6135                        // `/proc/thread-self` is the link itself, no
6136                        // directory: nothing is below it (ENOTDIR,
6137                        // `procfs_link_itself` below).
6138                        None if link_itself => None,
6139                        None => match procfs_selector_reached(&procfs_spelling, opener.own) {
6140                            // The caller's own task, as the process table
6141                            // identifies it now.
6142                            Some(selected) => {
6143                                let incarnation = match procfs_reached_task(&selected) {
6144                                    Some(task) => {
6145                                        let answer =
6146                                            crate::tool_global::procfs_task(guest, task).await;
6147                                        answer.exists.then(|| answer.incarnation())
6148                                    }
6149                                    None => None,
6150                                };
6151                                Some((selected, incarnation))
6152                            }
6153                            // Below a directory Detcore named: a selector's
6154                            // keeps its task's identity, and one the kernel
6155                            // named (received over SCM_RIGHTS) is named again
6156                            // at each use.
6157                            None if procfs_spelling != observed_path => {
6158                                let inherited = (!path.is_absolute()
6159                                    && call.dirfd() != libc::AT_FDCWD)
6160                                    .then(|| {
6161                                        guest
6162                                            .thread_state()
6163                                            .with_detfd(call.dirfd(), |detfd| {
6164                                                detfd.procfs_reached()
6165                                            })
6166                                            .ok()
6167                                            .flatten()
6168                                    })
6169                                    .flatten()
6170                                    .and_then(|(_, incarnation)| incarnation);
6171                                Some((procfs_spelling.clone(), inherited))
6172                            }
6173                            None => None,
6174                        },
6175                    }
6176                } else {
6177                    None
