6178                };
6179                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4213):
6180                // Review binding procfs directory provenance to the object the
6181                // kernel opened, without sequentialized threads.
6182                // Without sequentialized threads another guest thread can
6183                // replace the descriptor (or move the working directory) that
6184                // a relative lookup starts from, between Detcore naming it and
6185                // the kernel's open. Provenance taken from the spelling then
6186                // describes an object the new descriptor may not hold: a
6187                // `/proc/self` mark on an ordinary directory would make a
6188                // later relative `mountinfo` render a file Linux has no way to
6189                // open there. So it is installed only if the descriptor the
6190                // kernel returned holds a directory below `/proc`, as its own
6191                // link names it (`descriptor_kernel_link`, one more injected
6192                // `readlinkat`); for `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW` of a selector, only
6193                // if it holds that selector link. With sequentialized threads
6194                // no other thread runs in between, and nothing is checked.
6195                let (reached, link_itself) = if (reached.is_some() || link_itself)
6196                    && !path.is_absolute()
6197                    && !guest.config().sequentialize_threads
6198                {
6199                    let held = Self::descriptor_kernel_link(guest, fd).await;
6200                    let below_proc = |name: &Path| {
6201                        use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
6202                        name.starts_with("/proc")
6203                            && !name.as_os_str().as_bytes().ends_with(b" (deleted)")
6204                    };
6205                    let reached = reached.filter(|_| held.as_deref().is_some_and(below_proc));
6206                    let link_itself = link_itself
6207                        && held.as_deref().is_some_and(|name| {
6208                            name == Path::new("/proc/self")
6209                                || name == Path::new("/proc/thread-self")
6210                        });
6211                    (reached, link_itself)
6212                } else {
6213                    (reached, link_itself)
6214                };
6215                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
6216                    detfd.set_path(&recorded_path);
6217                    if let Some((reached, incarnation)) = reached.clone() {
6218                        detfd.set_procfs_reached(reached, incarnation);
6219                    }
6220                    if link_itself {
6221                        detfd.set_procfs_link_itself();
6222                    }
6223                    if let Some(procfs) = procfs.clone() {
6224                        detfd.set_procfs(procfs);
6225                    }
6226                    if let Some(provenance) = provenance {
6227                        detfd.set_sigalrm_phase1_provenance(provenance);
6228                    }
6229                })?;
6230                resource_release_all(guest).await;
6231                Ok(fd as i64)
6232            }
6233            // TODO: audit for error-nondeterminism:
6234            Err(e) => {
6235                // A root-only `/proc` name outside the run's level, reached
6236                // through a spelling the lookup check does not resolve,
6237                // refuses the open before its descriptor can be named; and
6238                // the KVM executor refuses whatever reaches procfs.
6239                let e = if matches!(e, Error::Errno(Errno::EACCES | Errno::EPERM))
6240                    && self
6241                        .refused_open_reaches_procfs_name_outside_level(guest, &call)
6242                        .await
6243                {
6244                    Errno::ENOENT.into()
6245                } else {
6246                    e
6247                };
6248                resource_release_all(guest).await;
6249                Err(e)
6250            }
6251        }
6252    }

6254    /// SYS_close system call.
6255    pub async fn handle_close<G: Guest<Self>>(
6256        &self,
6257        guest: &mut G,
6258        call: syscalls::Close,
6259    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
6260        let fd = call.fd();
6261        if let Ok(waited) = u32::try_from(fd)
6262            && let Some(refusal) = self
6263                .refuse_close_of_waited_listener(guest, Sysno::close, waited..=waited)
6264                .await
6265        {
6266            return refusal;
6267        }
6268        let channel_end = self.pipe_channel_end(guest, fd);
6269        let lock_tracked = self.lock_tracked_descriptions(guest, fd..=fd);
6270        let res = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await;
6271        let fd_was_released = !matches!(res, Err(Errno::EBADF) | Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS));
6272        if fd_was_released {
6273            if let Some(open_file_id) = guest.thread_state_mut().remove_fd(fd) {
6274                self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
6275            }
6276            self.report_lock_references(guest, lock_tracked).await;
6277            if let Ok(fd) = u32::try_from(fd) {
6278                crate::tool_global::descriptors_replaced(guest, fd, fd).await;
6279            }
6280            trace!("Closed {}", fd);
6281            self.note_channel_end_closed(guest, channel_end).await;
6282        }
6283        res.map_err(Error::from)
6284    }

6286    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
6287    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-838): Review close_range descriptor-table synchronization.
6288    /// Close a contiguous descriptor range and mirror successful closes in Detcore.
6289    ///
6290    /// The pinned Reverie revision exposes close_range as `Syscall::Other`. The
6291    /// common flags=0 operation cannot block and is deterministic for the
6292    /// process-local descriptor table. CLOSE_RANGE_UNSHARE and
6293    /// CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC need separate shared-table modeling, so return ENOSYS
6294    /// for nonzero flags rather than letting strict execution silently diverge.
6295    pub async fn handle_close_range<G: Guest<Self>>(
6296        &self,
6297        guest: &mut G,
6298        call: Syscall,
6299    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
6300        let Syscall::Other(_, args) = call else {
6301            unreachable!("close_range unexpectedly gained a typed variant")
6302        };
6303        let first = args.arg0 as u32;
6304        let last = args.arg1 as u32;
6305        let flags = args.arg2 as u32;
6306        if flags != 0 {
6307            return Err(Errno::ENOSYS.into());
6308        }
6309        if first <= last
6310            && let Some(refusal) = self
6311                .refuse_close_of_waited_listener(guest, Sysno::close_range, first..=last)
6312                .await
6313        {
6314            return refusal;
6315        }
6316
6317        let channel_ends = self.pipe_channel_ends_in(guest, first, last);
6318        let lock_tracked = match (i32::try_from(first), i32::try_from(last)) {
6319            (Ok(first), Ok(last)) => self.lock_tracked_descriptions(guest, first..=last),
6320            (Ok(first), Err(_)) => self.lock_tracked_descriptions(guest, first..=RawFd::MAX),
6321            _ => Vec::new(),
6322        };
6323        let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await;
6324        if result.is_ok() {
6325            let released = guest.thread_state_mut().remove_fd_range(first, last);
6326            for open_file_id in released {
6327                self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
6328            }
6329            self.report_lock_references(guest, lock_tracked).await;
6330            crate::tool_global::descriptors_replaced(guest, first, last).await;
6331            for end in channel_ends {
6332                self.note_channel_end_closed(guest, Some(end)).await;
6333            }
6334        }
6335        result.map_err(Error::from)
6336    }

6338    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
6339    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#2373)
6340    /// Advisory whole-file locks, forwarded to the kernel.
6341    ///
6342    /// This was previously an unconditional no-op success, justified by the
6343    /// claim that "an advisory whole-file lock is never contended within the
6344    /// serialized container". That is false: serializing guest threads stops
6345    /// them EXECUTING simultaneously, it does not stop their lock HOLD
6346    /// INTERVALS from overlapping. A holder that is descheduled -- because it
6347    /// blocked, forked, or simply used up its timeslice -- keeps holding while
6348    /// another process runs and observes the lock. Measured before this change,
6349    /// on both ptrace and DBI, two processes held the same `LOCK_EX`
6350    /// simultaneously while native correctly returned `EWOULDBLOCK`.
6351    ///
6352    /// A no-op is the wrong failure direction for a determinism tool. It is
6353    /// deterministically wrong, so double-run verification cannot see it, and it
6354    /// silently removes mutual exclusion from every guest that uses a lockfile.
6355    ///
6356    /// Forwarding is what `fcntl` already does for POSIX record locks, which is
6357    /// why those work. The guest's descriptor is a real host descriptor, so the
6358    /// kernel supplies the whole contract for free and consistently with itself:
6359    /// shared vs exclusive, `LOCK_NB`, upgrade/downgrade (which Linux performs
6360    /// non-atomically -- see below, this handler compensates), release on
6361    /// `LOCK_UN`, release when the last descriptor for the open file
6362    /// description is closed, and release on process exit.
6363    ///
6364    /// Determinism, scoped to what is actually true. When every contender is
6365    /// inside the container the outcome is a function of which guest holds the
6366    /// lock, and that is fixed by Detcore's deterministic schedule, so a given
6367    /// program and seed produce the same acquisition outcome every run.
6368    ///
6369    /// The scope is not decoration. Because this forwards to the kernel, a
6370    /// process OUTSIDE the container holding a lock on a guest-visible file
6371    /// does change the guest's result -- measured: with a host `flock -x`
6372    /// holder, a guest `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` returns `EWOULDBLOCK`, and acquires
6373    /// without one. That is a host-state leak, it is faithful to Linux, and it
6374    /// is the same leak `fcntl` record locks have always had here. Hermit
6375    /// already declines to make a mutating external filesystem deterministic,
6376    /// and lock state on a shared file is part of that state. Do not restate
6377    /// this as "no host state enters the decision": it does, and the previous
6378    /// bug in this very function came from writing down a determinism argument
6379    /// that was broader than the truth.
6380    ///
6381    /// Note that the no-op this replaced was not host-independent in any useful
6382    /// sense either -- it was host-independent by being wrong in all cases.
6383    ///
6384    /// # Why a blocking request is probed non-blockingly, and what that costs
6385    ///
6386    /// A guest thread parked inside a kernel `flock` is not visible to the
6387    /// deterministic scheduler as blocked, so nothing runs to release the lock
6388    /// and the whole container wedges -- measured: a four-way contention guest
6389    /// that completes natively hung indefinitely under a plain forwarding
6390    /// implementation. So a blocking operation is rewritten to `LOCK_NB` and,
6391    /// if it turns out to be contended, refused rather than hung.
6392    ///
6393    /// That rewrite is not free, and the cost is a *lock the guest already
6394    /// owns*. Linux converts an `flock` lock in place and the conversion is not
6395    /// atomic: `flock_lock_inode` deletes this open file description's existing
6396    /// lock **before** it scans for a conflict, so a contended `LOCK_SH` ->
6397    /// `LOCK_EX` conversion leaves the caller holding nothing and then reports
6398    /// `EWOULDBLOCK`. Natively the guest never observes that intermediate
6399    /// state, because a *blocking* request would sleep and eventually acquire.
6400    /// Under the rewrite it would: the guest asked to wait, got told "no", and
6401    /// silently lost the shared lock it was already relying on.
6402    ///
6403    /// So this handler restores the prior mode before refusing a *blocking*
6404    /// conversion, making the refusal side-effect-free. It deliberately does
6405    /// **not** restore when the guest itself passed `LOCK_NB`: there the drop is
6406    /// exactly what Linux does, and re-acquiring would be a divergence in the
6407    /// other direction. `DetFd::flock_mode` is what makes the two cases
6408    /// distinguishable -- it records the mode Detcore last saw the kernel grant
6409    /// for this open file description, so a first acquisition (nothing to lose)
6410    /// is not confused with a conversion (something to lose).
6411    ///
6412    /// That cache covers locks Detcore granted while it had sole knowledge of
6413    /// the open file description. State becomes permanently unknown when the
6414    /// descriptor is inherited across a process fork, discovered after tracing
6415    /// begins, or received through `SCM_RIGHTS` (recorded unobserved), because another process can
6416    /// change that shared kernel lock without updating this cache. A blocking
6417    /// conversion in unknown state is refused before the nonblocking probe, so
6418    /// the refusal cannot destroy a lock Detcore cannot restore.
6419    pub async fn handle_flock<G: Guest<Self>>(
6420        &self,
6421        guest: &mut G,
6422        call: syscalls::Flock,
6423    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
6424        // A flock belongs to its open file description. Whatever the call
6425        // did (took, converted, released, or, refused, dropped a lock in a
6426        // non-atomic conversion), the description's own fdinfo now says which
6427        // locks it holds (`procfs::locks`).
6428        let fd = call.fd();
6429        let result = self.flock_through_the_kernel(guest, call).await;
6430        self.refresh_description_locks(guest, fd, LockCall::Flock)
6431            .await?;
6432        result
6433    }
6434
6435    /// [`Self::handle_flock`]'s call itself.
6436    async fn flock_through_the_kernel<G: Guest<Self>>(
6437        &self,
6438        guest: &mut G,
6439        call: syscalls::Flock,
6440    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
6441        const LOCK_NB: i32 = libc::LOCK_NB;
6442        /// `LOCK_SH`/`LOCK_EX`/`LOCK_UN` with `LOCK_NB` (and any padding) masked off.
6443        const MODE_MASK: i32 = libc::LOCK_SH | libc::LOCK_EX | libc::LOCK_UN;
6444
6445        let (fd, operation) = (call.fd(), call.operation());
6446        let requested = operation & MODE_MASK;
6447        let caller_wants_nonblocking = operation & LOCK_NB != 0;
6448        let releasing = requested == libc::LOCK_UN;
6449        let valid_operation = operation & !(MODE_MASK | LOCK_NB) == 0
6450            && matches!(requested, libc::LOCK_SH | libc::LOCK_EX | libc::LOCK_UN);
6451        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
6452
6453        // Preserve kernel validation for malformed operations. In particular,
6454        // an unknown descriptor with an invalid mode must report EINVAL rather
6455        // than being mistaken for a valid blocking request and refused with
6456        // ENOLCK.
6457        if !valid_operation {
6458            return self
6459                .record_or_replay(guest, call)
6460                .await
6461                .map_err(Error::from);
6462        }
6463
6464        // The mode Detcore last saw the kernel grant this open file description.
6465        let known_held = guest
6466            .thread_state()
6467            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.known_flock_mode())
6468            .unwrap_or(None);
6469
6470        // A nonblocking conversion is allowed to have Linux's documented
6471        // non-atomic side effect. A blocking conversion is not: if this open
6472        // file description was inherited or received and its prior mode is
6473        // unknown, probing could silently drop a lock we cannot restore.
6474        // Validate the descriptor without changing lock state, then refuse the
6475        // uncertain blocking operation before issuing flock at all.
6476        if !caller_wants_nonblocking && !releasing && known_held.is_none() {
6477            guest
6478                .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Fcntl(
6479                    syscalls::Fcntl::new().with_fd(fd).with_cmd(F_GETFD),
6480                ))
6481                .await?;
6482            report_flock_refusal(&format!(
6483                "[dtid {dettid}] blocking flock(fd={fd}, operation={operation:#x}) refused: \
6484                 this open file description existed before Detcore observed its lock state, \
6485                 so a nonblocking probe could destroy a lock that cannot be restored. \
6486                 {FLOCK_REFUSAL_ADVICE}"
6487            ));
6488            return self
6489                .refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::flock, Errno::ENOLCK)
6490                .await;
6491        }
6492        let held = known_held.flatten();
6493
6494        // LOCK_UN cannot block, so it is forwarded exactly as the guest wrote it.
6495        let probe_operation = if releasing {
6496            operation
6497        } else {
6498            operation | LOCK_NB
6499        };
6500        let result = self
6501            .record_or_replay(guest, call.with_operation(probe_operation))
6502            .await;
6503        // A backend that cannot apply flock faithfully refuses it with a typed
6504        // refusal and no lock effect (the KVM backend refuses every lock
6505        // operation: https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1069). Ask
6506        // before anything else is injected, since the next injection replaces
6507        // the backend's record. The refusal is reported as a refusal, never
6508        // handed to the guest as the backend's raw ENOSYS.
6509        let refusal = if result.is_err() {
6510            guest.take_unsupported_refusal()
6511        } else {
6512            None
6513        };
6514        if let Some(refusal) = refusal {
6515            let message = format!(
6516                "[dtid {dettid}] flock(fd={fd}, operation={operation:#x}) refused by the backend: {}. \
6517                 No lock was taken or released.",
6518                refusal.diagnostic
6519            );
6520            report_flock_refusal(&message);
6521            if !self.cfg.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls {
6522                crate::tool_global::report_unsupported_syscall(guest, Sysno::flock).await;
6523            }
6524            return self
6525                .refuse_unserviceable_operation_because(
6526                    guest,
6527                    Sysno::flock,
6528                    Errno::ENOLCK,
6529                    refusal.diagnostic,
6530                )
6531                .await;
6532        }
6533
6534        match result {
6535            Ok(value) => {
6536                let granted = if releasing { None } else { Some(requested) };
6537                let _ = guest
6538                    .thread_state()
6539                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_flock_mode(granted));
6540                trace!(
6541                    "flock(fd={}, operation={:#x}) served, open file now holds {:?}",
6542                    fd, operation, granted
6543                );
6544                Ok(value)
6545            }
6546            Err(Errno::EWOULDBLOCK) if caller_wants_nonblocking => {
6547                // Exactly what the guest asked for, including Linux's own
6548                // non-atomic conversion behavior: if this was a conversion, the
6549                // kernel really did drop the prior lock on the way to failing,
6550                // so the cache must forget it rather than claim a lock the
6551                // guest no longer holds.
6552                if held.is_some_and(|held| held != requested) {
6553                    let _ = guest
6554                        .thread_state()
6555                        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_flock_mode(None));
6556                }
6557                trace!("flock(fd={}, operation={:#x}) would block", fd, operation);
6558                Err(Errno::EWOULDBLOCK.into())
6559            }
6560            Err(Errno::EWOULDBLOCK) => {
6561                // The guest asked to wait, and Detcore substituted a probe.
6562                // Undo the probe's collateral damage before refusing.
6563                if let Some(previous) = held.filter(|previous| *previous != requested) {
6564                    let restore = call.with_operation(previous | LOCK_NB);
6565                    match self.record_or_replay(guest, restore).await {
6566                        Ok(_) => {
6567                            warn!(
6568                                "[dtid {dettid}] contended blocking flock(fd={fd}, \
6569                                 operation={operation:#x}) refused; restored this open file's \
6570                                 prior {previous:#x} lock, which Linux's non-atomic conversion \
6571                                 had dropped. The guest holds exactly what it held before the \
6572                                 call."
6573                            );
6574                        }
6575                        Err(err) => {
6576                            let _ = guest
6577                                .thread_state()
6578                                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_flock_mode(None));
6579                            error!(
6580                                "[dtid {dettid}] contended blocking flock(fd={fd}, \
6581                                 operation={operation:#x}) refused, AND this open file's prior \
6582                                 {previous:#x} lock could not be restored ({err}). Linux's \
6583                                 non-atomic conversion dropped it and something outside this \
6584                                 container took it in the interval. The guest has lost a lock \
6585                                 it held; treat any mutual exclusion it was protecting as \
6586                                 broken."
6587                            );
6588                        }
6589                    }
6590                }
6591                // Waiting faithfully needs a wait queue owned by the
6592                // deterministic scheduler, the way futexes are handled; until
6593                // that exists, refuse loudly. Returning success would recreate
6594                // the mutual-exclusion bug this handler was written to fix, and
6595                // blocking in the kernel would deadlock the container.
6596                report_flock_refusal(&format!(
6597                    "[dtid {dettid}] blocking flock(fd={fd}, operation={operation:#x}) is \
6598                     contended, and Detcore cannot yet park a thread on a file lock \
6599                     deterministically. Refusing rather than granting a lock another guest \
6600                     holds. {FLOCK_REFUSAL_ADVICE}"
6601                ));
6602                self.refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::flock, Errno::ENOLCK)
6603                    .await
6604            }
6605            Err(err) => {
6606                trace!(
6607                    "flock(fd={}, operation={:#x}) refused: {}",
6608                    fd, operation, err
6609                );
6610                Err(err.into())
6611            }
6612        }
6613    }
6614
6615    async fn snapshot_procfs<G: Guest<Self>>(
6616        &self,
6617        guest: &mut G,
6618        call: syscalls::Read,
6619    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error> {
6620        // A backend-owned read may have advanced the kernel cursor without
6621        // passing through Detcore's logical procfs cursor (KVM does this for
6622        // worker-shared descriptors). Rewind before taking the initial snapshot
6623        // so a later intercepted pread cannot snapshot from EOF.
6624        //
6625        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
6626        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#1903): ESPIPE is not a failure here. Several procfs
6627        // files are legitimately non-seekable -- `/proc/net/*` single-release
6628        // seq_files return ESPIPE from `llseek` on the host, verified natively:
6629        // `lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET)` on `/proc/net/sockstat` gives ESPIPE while the
6630        // subsequent `read(2)` returns data. Propagating that ESPIPE made the
6631        // GUEST's `read` fail on a file Linux reads fine (`cat
6632        // /proc/net/sockstat` -> "Illegal seek"), which is a deviation from Linux
6633        // semantics, not a determinism requirement: the rewind is an internal
6634        // correction Detcore performs for its own benefit and the guest never
6635        // asked for it. A non-seekable fd also cannot have been advanced behind
6636        // our back by a seek, and a freshly opened one is already at offset 0, so
6637        // skipping the rewind loses nothing the rewind was protecting.
6638        match guest
6639            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Lseek(
6640                syscalls::Lseek::new()
6641                    .with_fd(call.fd())
6642                    .with_offset(0)
6643                    .with_whence(Whence::SEEK_SET),
6644            ))
6645            .await
6646        {
6647            Ok(_) => {}
6648            Err(Errno::ESPIPE) => {}
6649            Err(err) => return Err(err.into()),
6650        }
6651
6652        // Capture into scratch memory, never into the caller's buffer. The
6653        // caller receives only the sanitized bytes, so every host byte a
6654        // capture read left in its buffer past that length would stay visible
6655        // after the read returns: all of a host `/proc/modules` chunk behind
6656        // its empty sanitized view
6657        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3815). Saving and
6658        // restoring the caller's buffer cannot cover every destination the
6659        // kernel may write, such as a PROT_WRITE-only page that the save
6660        // cannot read. The caller's buffer sees only the sanitized
6661        // publication, which checks its protection as the kernel's copy does.
6662        let (lists_address_space, lists_locks) =
6663            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
6664                (
6665                    detfd.procfs_lists_address_space(),
6666                    detfd.procfs_lists_locks(),
6667                )
6668            })?;
6669        if lists_address_space {
6670            self.capture_procfs_on_stack(guest, call, lists_locks).await
6671        } else {
6672            self.capture_procfs_in_mapping(guest, call, lists_locks)
6673                .await
6674        }
6675    }
6676
6677    /// Capture through a private anonymous mapping that is unmapped before
6678    /// returning, so no host byte stays in guest memory.
6679    async fn capture_procfs_in_mapping<G: Guest<Self>>(
6680        &self,
6681        guest: &mut G,
6682        call: syscalls::Read,
6683        lists_locks: bool,
6684    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error> {
6685        const CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;
6686
6687        let mapped = guest
6688            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
6689                syscalls::Mmap::new()
6690                    .with_addr(None)
6691                    .with_len(CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES)
6692                    .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
6693                    .with_flags(MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS)
6694                    .with_fd(-1)
6695                    .with_offset(0),
6696            ))
6697            .await?;
6698        let mapping = usize::try_from(mapped)
6699            .ok()
6700            .and_then(AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw)
6701            .ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
6702        let result = self
6703            .drain_procfs(guest, call, mapping, CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES, lists_locks)
6704            .await;
6705        guest
6706            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
6707                syscalls::Munmap::new()
6708                    .with_addr(Some(Addr::from(mapping).cast()))
6709                    .with_len(CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES),
6710            ))
6711            .await?;
6712        result
6713    }
6714
6715    /// Capture a file that lists the address space (`maps`, `smaps`,
6716    /// `numa_maps`, `smaps_rollup`) through the guest stack scratch. A
6717    /// capture mapping would be listed in the snapshot, or merged into a
6718    /// neighbouring row, and then be unmapped before the guest sees it. The
6719    /// stack scratch changes no mapping; its original bytes are put back, so
6720    /// no host byte stays below the stack pointer either.
6721    ///
6722    /// The scratch below the red zone is not always there: a thread, fiber or
6723    /// alternate signal stack may put the stack pointer just above a guard page
6724    /// or the end of its mapping (compare [`Self::inject_fstat`]). The read
6725    /// needs no stack, so that must not fail it. The capture then goes through
6726    /// the caller's buffer, which this read writes anyway, with the same save
6727    /// and restore before the output is copied. If not even its first byte can
6728    /// be read and written, Linux copies nothing and the read fails `EFAULT`;
6729    /// it does so here without taking the snapshot.
6730    async fn capture_procfs_on_stack<G: Guest<Self>>(
6731        &self,
6732        guest: &mut G,
6733        call: syscalls::Read,
6734        lists_locks: bool,
6735    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error> {
6736        const CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 512;
6737
6738        let mut original = [0_u8; CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES];
6739        {
6740            let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
6741            let scratch = stack.reserve::<[u8; CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES]>().cast::<u8>();
6742            // `commit` writes the reserved bytes, so save them before it.
6743            if save_procfs_scratch(&mut guest.memory(), scratch, &mut original)
6744                && let Ok(guard) = stack.commit()
6745            {
6746                let result = self
6747                    .drain_procfs(guest, call, scratch, CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES, lists_locks)
6748                    .await;
6749                guest.memory().write_exact(scratch, &original)?;
6750                drop(guard);
6751                return result;
6752            }
6753        }
6754
6755        let buffer = call.buf().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
6756        for chunk in [call.len().min(CAPTURE_CHUNK_BYTES), 1] {
6757            let original = &mut original[..chunk];
6758            if save_procfs_scratch(&mut guest.memory(), buffer, original) {
6759                let result = self
6760                    .drain_procfs(guest, call, buffer, chunk, lists_locks)
6761                    .await;
6762                guest.memory().write_exact(buffer, original)?;
6763                return result;
6764            }
6765        }
6766        Err(Errno::EFAULT.into())
6767    }
6768
6769    /// Read the host file to EOF through `scratch`, `chunk` bytes at a time.
6770    ///
6771    /// For `/proc/locks` (`lists_locks`), each record that reads after the one
6772    /// whose length shows it reached the end of the kernel's lock list return
6773    /// is dropped, waiters and all, when its granted lock is one already read
6774    /// (`procfs::locks::locks_capture_without_repeats`): such records are rows
6775    /// the kernel prints again when the host adds a lock between two reads, at
6776    /// moments the host decides. Any other record is kept. Those reads are still made,
6777    /// through the recorder, until one returns 0, and the decision reads only
6778    /// their recorded lengths and bytes, so a replay drops the same bytes.
6779    async fn drain_procfs<G: Guest<Self>>(
6780        &self,
6781        guest: &mut G,
6782        call: syscalls::Read,
6783        scratch: AddrMut<'_, u8>,
6784        chunk: usize,
6785        lists_locks: bool,
6786    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error> {
6787        const MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
6788
6789        let capture = call.with_buf(Some(scratch)).with_len(chunk);
6790        let mut contents = Vec::new();
6791        let mut reads = Vec::new();
6792        loop {
6793            let bytes_read = self.record_or_replay(guest, capture).await? as usize;
6794            if bytes_read == 0 {
6795                break;
6796            }
6797            if contents.len() + bytes_read > MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES {
6798                return Err(Errno::EFBIG.into());
6799            }
6800            let start = contents.len();
6801            contents.resize(start + bytes_read, 0);
6802            read_guest_exact(&guest.memory(), scratch, &mut contents[start..])?;
6803            reads.push(bytes_read);
6804        }
6805        if lists_locks {
6806            let kept =
6807                crate::procfs::locks::locks_capture_without_repeats(&contents, &reads, chunk);
6808            if kept.len() < contents.len() {
6809                // Not INFO: whether the host moved a lock between the reads is
6810                // host-timed, and INFO is compared between verified runs.
6811                tracing::debug!(
6812                    "[detcore] /proc/locks capture: dropped {} bytes of rows that reads after \
6813                     the end of the kernel's list printed again (reads {:?})",
6814                    contents.len() - kept.len(),
6815                    reads
6816                );
6817                return Ok(kept);
6818            }
6819        }
6820        Ok(contents)
6821    }
6822
6823    /// The procfs directory that the kernel beneath the backend names for
6824    /// descriptor `fd`, which this guest thread just opened: its
6825    /// `/proc/thread-self/fd/<fd>` link, read by a `readlinkat` injected in
6826    /// the guest thread, which the host kernel answers under ptrace and DBT
6827    /// and the KVM executor answers for its own `/proc`, if that names a
6828    /// directory Detcore may record (`procfs_directory_link`). `None`
6829    /// otherwise, and where the guest stack scratch cannot hold the call's
6830    /// buffers, the call fails, or the link does not fit in 256 bytes: every
6831    /// path accepted is far shorter, and a truncated one must not match.
6832    async fn procfs_directory_named_for<G: Guest<Self>>(
6833        guest: &mut G,
6834        fd: RawFd,
6835    ) -> Option<PathBuf> {
6836        let named = Self::descriptor_kernel_link(guest, fd).await?;
6837        procfs_directory_link(&named).then_some(named)
6838    }
6839
6840    /// The `/proc/thread-self/fd/<fd>` link of descriptor `fd`, which this
6841    /// guest thread holds, as the kernel beneath the backend reads it (one
6842    /// `readlinkat` injected in the guest thread; the host kernel under ptrace
6843    /// and DBT, the KVM executor for its own `/proc`). `None` where the guest
6844    /// stack scratch cannot hold the call's buffers, the call fails, or the
6845    /// link does not fit in 256 bytes.
6846    async fn descriptor_kernel_link<G: Guest<Self>>(guest: &mut G, fd: RawFd) -> Option<PathBuf> {
6847        const LINK_CAPACITY: usize = 40;
6848        const TARGET_CAPACITY: usize = 256;
6849        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
6850        let link = stack.push(rendered_procfs::c_string::<LINK_CAPACITY>(
6851            format!("/proc/thread-self/fd/{fd}").as_bytes(),
6852        ));
6853        let target = stack.reserve::<[u8; TARGET_CAPACITY]>();
6854        let stack_guard = stack.commit().ok()?;
6855        let length = guest
6856            .inject(
6857                syscalls::Readlinkat::new()
6858                    .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
6859                    .with_path(PathPtr::from_ptr(link.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char))
6860                    .with_buf(Some(target.cast::<libc::c_char>()))
6861                    .with_buf_len(TARGET_CAPACITY),
6862            )
6863            .await;
6864        let bytes = match length.map(|length| length as usize) {
6865            Ok(length) if length < TARGET_CAPACITY => {
6866                let mut bytes = vec![0; length];
6867                guest
6868                    .memory()
6869                    .read_exact(target.cast::<u8>(), &mut bytes)
6870                    .ok()
6871                    .map(|()| bytes)
6872            }
6873            _ => None,
6874        };
6875        drop(stack_guard);
6876        Some(PathBuf::from(
6877            <std::ffi::OsString as std::os::unix::ffi::OsStringExt>::from_vec(bytes?),
6878        ))
6879    }
6880
6881    /// Whether the descriptor `fd` an open just returned is one of Linux's
6882    /// random devices (`crate::fd::is_random_device`), by the host `fstat`
6883    /// the open already took (`stat`, when metadata is virtualized) or by one
6884    /// `fstat` through the recording ([`Self::recorded_fstat`]). Under record
6885    /// and replay the latter is always used: replay's descriptor is a
6886    /// placeholder, so only the recorded result names the device.
6887    async fn opened_random_device<G: Guest<Self>>(
6888        &self,
6889        guest: &mut G,
6890        fd: RawFd,
6891        stat: Option<&libc::stat>,
6892    ) -> Result<bool, StatFailure> {
6893        let stat = match stat {
6894            Some(stat) if !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes => *stat,
6895            _ => self.recorded_fstat(guest, fd).await?,
6896        };
6897        Ok(crate::fd::is_random_device(stat.st_mode, stat.st_rdev))
6898    }
6899
6900    /// [`Self::recorded_fstat`] of a descriptor an `SCM_RIGHTS` receive
6901    /// installed (`Detcore::record_received_descriptors`). A failed call,
6902    /// recorded or not, is its errno, which leaves the descriptor unrecorded.
6903    /// Under record and replay a buffer that cannot be prepared ends the run
6904    /// instead, as an open's classification does: it recorded no event, so
6905    /// the other run could consume a different one.
6906    pub(crate) async fn received_descriptor_fstat<G: Guest<Self>>(
6907        &self,
6908        guest: &mut G,
6909        raw_fd: RawFd,
6910    ) -> Result<libc::stat, Error> {
6911        match self.recorded_fstat(guest, raw_fd).await {
6912            Ok(stat) => Ok(stat),
6913            Err(StatFailure::Scratch(errno)) if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes => {
6914                Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
6915                    "cannot record descriptor {raw_fd}, received over SCM_RIGHTS, under \
6916                     record and replay: no buffer for its fstat ({errno})"
6917                )))
6918            }
6919            Err(failure) => Err(failure.errno().into()),
6920        }
6921    }
6922
6923    /// `fstat(fd)` through the recording, with [`Self::inject_fstat`]'s buffer
6924    /// placement and retry: recorded under record, served from the recording
6925    /// under replay, injected otherwise. Every attempt, including an
6926    /// interrupted one, is a recorded event. The buffer's placement consumes
6927    /// no event: the stack scratch is used or not by the guest's own stack
6928    /// pointer and mappings, which replay reproduces, and the transient page
6929    /// is an unrecorded private mapping of the same address space. If that
6930    /// mapping fails, `StatFailure::Scratch` reports it, so the caller can
6931    /// refuse to continue a recording or replay rather than consume a
6932    /// different event than the other run did.
6933    async fn recorded_fstat<G: Guest<Self>>(
6934        &self,
6935        guest: &mut G,
6936        raw_fd: RawFd,
6937    ) -> Result<libc::stat, StatFailure> {
6938        info!(
6939            "Taking fstat through the recording to classify fd {}.",
6940            raw_fd
6941        );
6942        let fstat = move |statptr: StatPtr<'_>| {
6943            Syscall::Fstat(
6944                syscalls::Fstat::new()
6945                    .with_fd(raw_fd)
6946                    .with_stat(Some(statptr)),
6947            )
6948        };
6949        Self::stat_with_fallback(guest, raw_fd, fstat, Some(self)).await
6950    }
6951
6952    /// Close descriptor `fd`, which an open just returned but Detcore could
6953    /// not classify, through the recording, and then forget it. A close that
6954    /// provably never ran (ERESTARTSYS: a signal stopped the injection before
6955    /// its `syscall` instruction) is retried; one that ran is not, as Linux
6956    /// releases the descriptor even when `close` reports EINTR or EIO. A close
6957    /// still refused after the retries, or refused otherwise, ends the run:
6958    /// the descriptor would stay open in the guest with no model.
6959    async fn close_unclassified<G: Guest<Self>>(
6960        &self,
6961        guest: &mut G,
6962        fd: RawFd,
6963    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
6964        const ATTEMPTS: usize = 16;
6965        let mut last = Errno::ERESTARTSYS;
6966        for _ in 0..ATTEMPTS {
6967            match self
6968                .record_or_replay(guest, syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd))
6969                .await
6970            {
6971                Ok(_) | Err(Errno::EINTR | Errno::EIO) => {
6972                    guest.thread_state().remove_fd(fd);
6973                    return Ok(());
6974                }
6975                Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS) => last = Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
6976                Err(errno) => {
6977                    last = errno;
6978                    break;
6979                }
6980            }
6981        }
6982        Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
6983            "cannot close fd {fd}, which an open returned but Detcore could not \
6984             classify: close answered {last}"
6985        )))
6986    }
6987
6988    /// What descriptor `fd` of the calling process names, as its
6989    /// `/proc/thread-self/fd` link reads, through the recording
6990    /// ([`Self::recorded_descriptor_link`]): `None` for an anonymous target,
6991    /// a link that cannot be read, one too long for the 256 bytes read (every
6992    /// path Detcore classifies is far shorter, and a truncated one must not
6993    /// match), or one Detcore had no buffer to read into, which must never
6994    /// fail the guest's open.
6995    async fn recorded_open_path<G: Guest<Self>>(
6996        &self,
6997        guest: &mut G,
6998        fd: RawFd,
6999    ) -> Result<Option<PathBuf>, Error> {
7000        let bytes = self
7001            .recorded_descriptor_link(guest, fd)
7002            .await
7003            .unwrap_or(None);
7004        Ok(bytes.and_then(|bytes| {
7005            let path = PathBuf::from(
7006                <std::ffi::OsString as std::os::unix::ffi::OsStringExt>::from_vec(bytes),
7007            );
7008            path.is_absolute().then_some(path)
7009        }))
7010    }
7011
7012    /// The bytes of descriptor `fd`'s `/proc/thread-self/fd` link, through the
7013    /// recording ([`Self::recorded_readlink`]): the recording reads the
7014    /// kernel's link and keeps its bytes, and replay, whose slot may hold a
7015    /// stand-in eventfd, returns the same bytes. `None` for a link that cannot
7016    /// be read or fills the 256 bytes read.
7017    ///
7018    /// The link's name and the buffer go in the guest stack scratch, below the
7019    /// red zone, or, where that memory is not writable (a stack pointer just
7020    /// above a guard page or the lowest page of the main-thread stack), in a
7021    /// transient private page, as `inject_fstat` does
7022    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3328>). Neither placement
7023    /// consumes an event. `Err` when neither could be prepared: no readlink
7024    /// ran, so no event was recorded or consumed, and a caller under record
7025    /// and replay decides whether that may end the run.
7026    pub(crate) async fn recorded_descriptor_link<G: Guest<Self>>(
7027        &self,
7028        guest: &mut G,
7029        fd: RawFd,
7030    ) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, Errno> {
7031        const LINK_CAPACITY: usize = 32;
7032        const TARGET_CAPACITY: usize = 256;
7033        let link_name = rendered_procfs::c_string::<LINK_CAPACITY>(
7034            format!("/proc/thread-self/fd/{fd}").as_bytes(),
7035        );
7036        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
7037        let link = stack.push(link_name);
7038        let target = stack.reserve::<[u8; TARGET_CAPACITY]>();
7039        match stack.commit() {
7040            Ok(stack_guard) => {
7041                let bytes = self
7042                    .recorded_readlink(guest, link.as_raw(), target.as_raw(), TARGET_CAPACITY)
7043                    .await;
7044                drop(stack_guard);
7045                Ok(bytes)
7046            }
7047            Err(_) => {
7048                info!(
7049                    "Guest stack scratch cannot hold the link of fd {}; using a transient page \
7050                     instead.",
7051                    fd
7052                );
7053                let len = LINK_CAPACITY + TARGET_CAPACITY;
7054                let mapped = guest
7055                    .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
7056                        syscalls::Mmap::new()
7057                            .with_addr(None)
7058                            .with_len(len)
7059                            .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
7060                            .with_flags(MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS)
7061                            .with_fd(-1)
7062                            .with_offset(0),
7063                    ))
7064                    .await;
7065                let page = mapped.and_then(|mapped| {
7066                    usize::try_from(mapped)
7067                        .ok()
7068                        .and_then(AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw)
7069                        .ok_or(Errno::ENOMEM)
7070                })?;
7071                let bytes = if let Err(errno) = guest.memory().write_exact(page, &link_name) {
7072                    Err(errno)
7073                } else {
7074                    Ok(self
7075                        .recorded_readlink(
7076                            guest,
7077                            page.as_raw(),
7078                            page.as_raw() + LINK_CAPACITY,
7079                            TARGET_CAPACITY,
7080                        )
7081                        .await)
7082                };
7083                if let Err(errno) = guest
7084                    .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
7085                        syscalls::Munmap::new()
7086                            .with_addr(Some(page.cast::<libc::c_void>().into()))
7087                            .with_len(len),
7088                    ))
7089                    .await
7090                {
7091                    warn!(
7092                        "[detcore] could not unmap the transient link page: {}",
7093                        errno
7094                    );
7095                }
7096                bytes
7097            }
7098        }
7099    }
7100
7101    /// `readlink(link, target, capacity)` through the recording, both at guest
7102    /// addresses: the bytes it read, or `None` if it failed or filled the
7103    /// buffer (a link that may be truncated). Retried while a signal stops it
7104    /// before it runs; every attempt is an event, so replay retries as the
7105    /// recording did.
7106    async fn recorded_readlink<G: Guest<Self>>(
7107        &self,
7108        guest: &mut G,
7109        link: usize,
7110        target: usize,
7111        capacity: usize,
7112    ) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
7113        const ATTEMPTS: usize = 64;
7114        let target = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(target)?;
7115        let path = PathPtr::from_ptr(link as *const libc::c_char);
7116        let buf = Some(target.cast::<libc::c_char>());
7117        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
7118        let call = syscalls::Readlink::new()
7119            .with_path(path)
7120            .with_buf(buf)
7121            .with_bufsize(capacity);
7122        // aarch64 has only `readlinkat`.
7123        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
7124        let call = syscalls::Readlinkat::new()
7125            .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
7126            .with_path(path)
7127            .with_buf(buf)
7128            .with_buf_len(capacity);
7129        let mut answer = Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
7130        for _ in 0..ATTEMPTS {
7131            answer = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await;
7132            if !matches!(answer, Err(Errno::EINTR | Errno::ERESTARTSYS)) {
7133                break;
7134            }
7135        }
7136        let length = answer.ok()?;
7137        let length = usize::try_from(length)
7138            .ok()
7139            .filter(|length| *length < capacity)?;
7140        let mut bytes = vec![0; length];
7141        guest.memory().read_exact(target, &mut bytes).ok()?;
7142        Some(bytes)
7143    }
7144
7145    /// A `read` (`offset` `None`, at the shared cursor, which it advances by
7146    /// the bytes copied) or a `pread64` (at `offset`) of the rendered
7147    /// `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` open as `fd`, in `vfs_read`'s order
7148    /// (fs/read_write.c): a descriptor that cannot read is EBADF; a buffer
7149    /// beyond the user address limit is EFAULT; `rw_verify_area` refuses a
7150    /// count above `SSIZE_MAX` or a position whose end overflows (EINVAL);
7151    /// then the file's own read, even for a count of zero, which still finds
7152    /// its task (ESRCH once it is gone), with the count cut to
7153    /// `MAX_RW_COUNT` (`Detcore::read_rendered_cmdline`).
7154    async fn read_rendered_cmdline_call<G: Guest<Self>>(
7155        &self,
7156        guest: &mut G,
7157        fd: RawFd,
7158        buf: Option<AddrMut<'_, u8>>,
7159        len: usize,
7160        offset: Option<u64>,
7161    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
7162        let status = guest
7163            .thread_state()
7164            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.status_flags())?;
7165        if !can_read(status) {
7166            return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
7167        }
7168        validate_procfs_destination(
7169            || crate::iovecs::UserAddressLimit::from_query(guest.user_address_limit()),
7170            buf,
7171            len,
7172        )?;
7173        let pos = match offset {
7174            Some(offset) => offset,
7175            None => {
7176                self.adopt_rendered_procfs_position(guest, fd).await?;
7177                guest
7178                    .thread_state()
7179                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.procfs_position())?
7180                    .map_or(0, |(position, _)| position) as u64
7181            }
7182        };
7183        let ends = i64::try_from(len)
7184            .ok()
7185            .and_then(|len| i64::try_from(pos).ok()?.checked_add(len));
7186        if ends.is_none() {
7187            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
7188        }
7189        let destination = buf.map_or(0, |buf| buf.as_raw());
7190        let copied = self
7191            .read_rendered_cmdline(
7192                guest,
7193                fd,
7194                destination,
7195                len.min(crate::page::max_rw_count()),
7196                pos,
7197            )
7198            .await?;
7199        if offset.is_none() {
7200            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
7201                detfd.commit_procfs_read(pos as usize, copied);
7202            })?;
7203            self.sync_rendered_procfs_position(guest, fd).await?;
7204        }
7205        Ok(copied as i64)
7206    }
7207
7208    async fn initialize_procfs_snapshot<G: Guest<Self>>(
7209        &self,
7210        guest: &mut G,
7211        call: syscalls::Read,
7212    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
7213        let format = guest
7214            .thread_state()
7215            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |fd| fd.procfs_private_mapping_format())?;
7216        let maps_target = if let Some(format) = format
7217            && guest.runtime_private_memory_regions().is_some()
7218        {
7219            let name = format.name();
7220            if !guest.config().sequentialize_threads {
7221                return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7222                    "runtime-private {name} view unavailable: capture is not sequentialized"
7223                )));
7224            }
7225            let target = guest
7226                .thread_state()
7227                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |fd| fd.procfs_maps_target())?
7228                .ok_or_else(|| {
7229                    Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7230                        "runtime-private {name} view unavailable: opened target image is unbound"
7231                    ))
7232                })?;
7233            if !guest.runtime_private_memory_is_current(&target.private) {
7234                return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7235                    "runtime-private {name} view unavailable: target ownership retired"
7236                )));
7237            }
7238            Some((format, target))
7239        } else {
7240            None
7241        };
7242        let template = guest
7243            .thread_state()
7244            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_rendering_template())?;
7245        // A process's `mountinfo` or `mounts`, in a run with a container
7246        // mount table: the table's bytes, whoever opened the file.
7247        let mount_table = self.mount_table_snapshot(guest, call.fd())?;
7248        let raw_contents = match template {
7249            // A descriptor that cannot read (`O_PATH`, write-only, or access
7250            // mode 3) reads nothing (EBADF), as the kernel's read of it,
7251            // which a rendered snapshot does not make, would answer.
7252            Some(_)
7253                if !can_read(
7254                    guest
7255                        .thread_state()
7256                        .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.status_flags())?,
7257                ) =>
7258            {
7259                return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
7260            }
7261            Some(template) => {
7262                // A per-process file's `show` finds its task again: a task
7263                // that is gone, or whose pid another task now holds, is ESRCH.
7264                // At position 0 only: a description that has no snapshot at
7265                // another position is one rebuilt from a placeholder whose
7266                // first read happened in another process
7267                // (`adopt_received_placeholder`, `adopt_placeholder`), where
7268                // Linux reads on from the buffer that read filled, without
7269                // looking for the task.
7270                let position = guest
7271                    .thread_state()
7272                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_position())?
7273                    .map_or(0, |(offset, _)| offset);
7274                if position == 0 {
7275                    self.require_rendered_task(guest, call.fd()).await?;
7276                }
7277                mount_table.unwrap_or_else(|| template.to_vec())
7278            }

7280            // kernel's bytes, which the table replaces; a descriptor that
7281            // cannot read reads nothing (EBADF), as the kernel's read of it
7282            // would answer.

7284                if !can_read(
7285                    guest
7286                        .thread_state()
7287                        .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.status_flags())?,
7288                ) {
7289                    return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
7290                }
7291                table
7292            }
7293            None => {
7294                if let Some((crate::procfs::private_maps::Format::NumaMaps, target)) = &maps_target
7295                {
7296                    if !can_read(
7297                        guest
7298                            .thread_state()
7299                            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |fd| fd.status_flags())?,
7300                    ) {
7301                        return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
7302                    }
7303                    crate::tool_global::mapping_capture::capture(guest, target)?
7304                } else {
7305                    self.snapshot_procfs(guest, call).await?
7306                }
7307            }
7308        };
7309        let raw_contents = if let Some((format, target)) = maps_target {
7310            let name = format.name();
7311            if !guest.runtime_private_memory_is_current(&target.private) {
7312                return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7313                    "runtime-private {name} view unavailable: target ownership changed during capture"
7314                )));
7315            }
7316            if format == crate::procfs::private_maps::Format::NumaMaps {
7317                // The synchronous capture already projected its coherent pair
7318                // with this exact ownership fact. The existing initializer
7319                // below applies the unchanged NUMA sanitizer exactly once.
7320                raw_contents
7321            } else {
7322                format
7323                    .project(&raw_contents, &target.private.regions)
7324                    .map_err(|reason| {
7325                        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7326                            "runtime-private {name} view unavailable: {reason}"
7327                        ))
7328                    })?
7329            }
7330        } else {
7331            raw_contents
7332        };
7333        // The guest mount view is the launch namespace (guest mount/unshare/
7334        // setns are refused under Detcore). Ephemeral host FUSE seed rows
7335        // (per-process and named-tool seeds) are other tenants' propagated
7336        // runtime state, not part of that namespace; exclude the class at
7337        // capture so snapshot identity assignment and every later read agree
7338        // on the same membership.
7339        let contents = if guest
7340            .thread_state()
7341            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_needs_mountinfo_identities())?
7342        {
7343            crate::procfs::exclude_ephemeral_host_seed_mounts(&raw_contents)
7344        } else {
7345            raw_contents
7346        };

7349        // guest's numbers (slice B3a-4 of
7350        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4266).
7351        let held = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
7352            detfd.procfs_kernel_numbers_held(&contents)

7355        // keep the numbers the kernel gives them, as their paths do. Which
7356        // process's file it is, the kernel's name for the descriptor says
7357        // where the tool shares the guest's descriptors (DBT), whatever path
7358        // reached it.
7359        let path = if guest.config().backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table {
7360            std::fs::read_link(format!("/proc/thread-self/fd/{}", call.fd())).ok()
7361        } else {
7362            guest
7363                .thread_state()
7364                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.path())?
7365        };
7366        let init = path.is_some_and(|path| crate::procfs::ids::names_init(&path));
7367        let held = if init { Vec::new() } else { held };
7368        if let Some(numbers) = Self::guest_procfs_numbers(guest, &held).await {
7369            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
7370                detfd.set_procfs_guest_numbers(numbers.clone())
7371            })?;
7372        }
7373        let virtual_uptime_seconds = self.calculate_procfs_uptime(guest).await?;

7375        // read of the same open file took its snapshot at, which a process
7376        // without Detcore's state of it (after `exec` or `fork` where the
7377        // tool runs in each guest process) finds on the placeholder.
7378        let virtual_uptime_seconds = match guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
7379            detfd
7380                .procfs_rendered_at_first_read()
7381                .then(|| detfd.procfs_rendered_path())
7382                .flatten()
7383        })? {
7384            Some(path) => {
7385                self.first_read_uptime(guest, call.fd(), path, virtual_uptime_seconds)

7387            }
7388            None => virtual_uptime_seconds,
7389        };

7391        // an unrepresentable boot instant refuse unrelated files such as
7392        // `/proc/uptime`.

7394            .thread_state()
7395            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_needs_boot_time())?;
7396        let virtual_boot_time_seconds = needs_boot_time
7397            .then(|| self.calculate_procfs_boot_time())
7398            .transpose()?;
7399        let virtual_realtime_seconds = i64::try_from(thread_observe_time(guest).await.as_secs())
7400            .map_err(|_| Errno::EOVERFLOW)?;

7402        let virtual_pid = guest.inject(syscalls::Getpid::new()).await? as i32;
7403        let virtual_ppid = guest.inject(syscalls::Getppid::new()).await? as i32;

7405            std::path::Path::new("/dev/ptmx"),
7406            std::path::Path::new("/dev/pts/ptmx"),
7407        ]);
7408        let target_fd = guest
7409            .thread_state()
7410            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_target_fd())?;
7411        // The kernel's fdinfo for a procfs file Detcore renders describes the
7412        // memfd standing in for it. Linux's names the file: Detcore's cursor,
7413        // the guest's procfs mount and the file's inode. The cursor is the one
7414        // processes sharing the open file share.
7415        if let Some(target_fd) = target_fd {
7416            self.adopt_rendered_procfs_position(guest, target_fd)
7417                .await?;
7418        }
7419        let rendered_target = match target_fd {
7420            Some(target_fd) => guest
7421                .thread_state()
7422                .with_detfd(target_fd, |detfd| {
7423                    detfd.procfs_rendered_path().map(|path| {
7424                        (
7425                            path,
7426                            detfd.procfs_position().map_or(0, |(offset, _)| offset),
7427                        )
7428                    })
7429                })
7430                .ok()
7431                .flatten(),
7432            None => None,
7433        };

7435        // placeholder: its tag as the position, its tmpfs mount and inode.
7436        // Linux's names the directory it stands for: Detcore's position, the
7437        // guest's procfs mount and the directory's inode
7438        // (`descriptor_directory`).
7439        // Boxed, so that this call's future holds its answer alone.
7440        let placeholder = match target_fd {
7441            Some(target_fd) if rendered_target.is_none() => {
7442                Box::pin(self.placeholder_fdinfo(guest, target_fd)).await?
7443            }
7444            _ => None,
7445        };
7446        let placeholder_inode = placeholder.as_ref().map(|(_, inode)| *inode);

7448            (Some((_, offset)), _) => format!(
7449                "pos:\t{offset}\nflags:\t0\nmnt_id:\t{}\nino:\t0\n",
7450                rendered_procfs::guest_procfs_mount_id()?

7452            .into_bytes(),
7453            (None, Some((placeholder, _))) => placeholder,
7454            (None, None) => contents,
7455        };

7457            let (cached_stat, logical_flags, open_file_id, fd_type, inode_override) =
7458                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(target_fd, |detfd| {
7459                    (
7460                        detfd.stat(),
7461                        detfd.status_flags(),
7462                        detfd.open_file_id(),
7463                        detfd.ty(),
7464                        deterministic_stdio_inode_for_resource(target_fd, detfd.resource()),
7465                    )
7466                })?;

7468                Some(stat) => stat,
7469                None => DetStat::from(self.inject_fstat(guest, target_fd).await?),

7473                Some(inode) => inode,
7474                // Detcore numbered it when it rendered the file.

7479                // numbers it.

7482                    let procfs =
7483                        Self::procfs_entry(guest, &stat, StatTarget::Descriptor(target_fd)).await;
7484                    let files = self.rendered_files(guest);
7485                    if let Some(path) =
7486                        rendered_entry(&procfs, &stat, guest.config().recordreplay_modes, files)
7487                    {
7488                        DetInode::mint(procfs_inode::rendered_inode(path))
7489                    } else {
7490                        determinize_inode_observing_mtime(
7491                            guest,
7492                            stat.raw_inode(),
7493                            procfs.name(stat.dev),
7494                            ObservedMtime::Unobserved,
7495                            InodeSighting::Descriptor,
7496                        )
7497                        .await
7498                        .0
7499                    }
7500                }
7501            };

7503                detcore_model::procfs::parse_fdinfo_mount_id(&contents).ok_or_else(|| {
7504                    Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7505                        "kernel returned malformed /proc/*/fdinfo without one numeric mnt_id"
7506                    ))
7507                })?;

7509            // row order. Replay intentionally retains the recording-time raw
7510            // IDs because ReadV2 supplies recording-time fdinfo bytes.
7511            let has_configured_mount_ids = guest.config().mountinfo_mount_ids_captured;
7512            let virtual_mount_id = if raw_mount_id == 0 {
7513                // Linux uses zero for anonymous objects such as memfd. Key the
7514                // equivalence on the observed value, not our descriptor type.
7515                0
7516            } else if !has_configured_mount_ids {
7517                // Public non-container callers have no pre-captured provenance.
7518                // Mount/unshare/setns are refused once Detcore starts, so a
7519                // tracer-side snapshot of this task's namespace is immutable.
7520                let mountinfo_path = format!("/proc/{}/mountinfo", guest.pid().as_raw());
7521                let mountinfo_contents = std::fs::read(&mountinfo_path).map_err(|error| {
7522                    Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7523                        "failed to read {mountinfo_path} while validating fdinfo mnt_id: {error}"
7524                    ))
7525                })?;

7527                // ephemeral host seed rows are not guest namespace members

7532                    crate::procfs::parse_mountinfo(&mountinfo_contents).ok_or_else(|| {
7533                        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7534                            "kernel returned malformed {mountinfo_path} while validating fdinfo mnt_id"
7535                        ))
7536                    })?;
7537                let snapshot = MountInfoSnapshot::new(
7538                    mountinfo_rows,
7539                    &[],
7540                    false,
7541                    BTreeMap::new(),
7542                    BTreeMap::new(),
7543                )
7544                .ok_or_else(|| {
7545                    Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7546                        "{mountinfo_path} failed strict identity validation for fdinfo"
7547                    ))
7548                })?;
7549                determinize_mount_id(guest, raw_mount_id, Some(snapshot.raw_mount_id_order()))

7551                    .ok_or_else(|| {
7552                        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7553                            "mountinfo mount-ID order changed after the identity snapshot while resolving fdinfo mnt_id {raw_mount_id} for {fd_type:?} from {mountinfo_path}"

7555                    })?

7558                // its nearest shown ancestor (`ContainerMountTable::select`).

7561                    .await
7562                    .ok_or_else(|| {
7563                        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(

7565                        ))
7566                    })?
7567            };

7569                // Determinized immediately above (stdio-special or
7570                // `determinize_inode`); lowered to an integer only here, at the

7572                virtual_inode.as_raw(),
7573                logical_flags,
7574                open_file_id.deterministic_socket_cookie(),
7575                virtual_mount_id,
7576            ))
7577        } else {
7578            None
7579        };
7580        // The guest's CPUID instruction is answered from Detcore's table
7581        // exactly when CPUID is virtualized and the backend delivers the
7582        // instruction to Detcore (`handle_cpuid_event`), on ptrace and KVM
7583        // alike; without CPUID interception the guest sees the host's CPU,
7584        // and so does this file. There Detcore renders the file itself
7585        // (`ProcfsFile::rendered_path`); this is for a /proc/cpuinfo the
7586        // kernel opened: through a symbolic link, after `chroot`, or under
7587        // record and replay.

7589        // session renders the file, is rendered from the table: it holds no
7590        // other bytes.
7591        let (is_cpuinfo, placeholder) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
7592            (
7593                detfd.procfs_is_cpuinfo(),
7594                detfd.procfs_rendered_path().is_some(),
7595            )
7596        })?;
7597        let virtual_cpuinfo = (is_cpuinfo && (placeholder || self.rendered_files(guest).cpuinfo))
7598            .then(|| {
7599                self.virtual_cpuid()
7600                    .cpuinfo(guest.config().virtual_cpu_count())
7601            });
7602        let needs_random_uuid = guest
7603            .thread_state()
7604            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_needs_random_uuid())?;
7605        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
7606        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-955): Review deterministic kernel UUID generation.
7607        let random_uuid =
7608            needs_random_uuid.then(|| guest.thread_state_mut().thread_prng().random::<[u8; 16]>());

7611        // The sanitizers in `crate::procfs` are pure functions of content and
7612        // hold no guest handle, so they cannot reach `InodePool`/`DevicePool`.
7613        // Minting an identity down there would make the maps column stable and
7614        // STILL DISAGREE with `stat` -- deterministic, reproducible and wrong.
7615        // This mirrors how `fdinfo_identity` is built a few lines above:
7616        // determinize with `determinize_inode`/`determinize_device`, then hand

7623            .thread_state()
7624            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_needs_mapping_identities())?;

7627            // A mapping backed by stdio must report the SAME inode fdinfo
7628            // reports for that fd, which is the fixed `deterministic_stdio_inode`

7630            // from the cached stat only: injecting an fstat here would add
7631            // syscalls to every maps read and perturb the very traces this
7632            // change is meant to keep consistent.
7633            //
7634            // The lowest descriptor wins a shared identity, as in
7635            // `deterministic_stdio_inode_for_raw`. Detcore gives all three
7636            // inherited descriptors the stat of its own stdin (`setup_stdio`),

7638            // that file is a mapping of fd 0, and must report the 1000 that
7639            // fd 0's fdinfo reports, not stderr's 1002.
7640            let mut stdio_by_raw_inode: BTreeMap<RawInode, DetInode> = BTreeMap::new();

7642                let cached = guest
7643                    .thread_state()
7644                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
7645                        let inode = deterministic_stdio_inode_for_resource(fd, detfd.resource())?;
7646                        detfd.stat().map(|stat| (stat.raw_inode(), inode))
7647                    })
7648                    .ok()
7649                    .flatten();

7652                }
7653            }

7655            // (address order, which the guest's own mmaps decide), repeats and
7656            // stdio-backed lines included. The pool numbers files in request
7657            // order and every request consumes a number, so sorting by raw
7658            // `(dev, ino)` would let a host inode decide which file gets which
7659            // number, and skipping lines whose host pair repeats (hard-linked
7660            // libraries) or matches stdio would let host identity decide how
7661            // many numbers a read consumes
7662            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/2897).
7663            //
7664            // The device a mapping names is the filesystem's own, which on
7665            // btrfs is not the per-subvolume device `stat` reports; the pair is
7666            // the identity either way, as it is for the device determinized
7667            // below.
7668            let raw_pairs: Vec<(u64, u64)> = String::from_utf8_lossy(&contents)
7669                .lines()
7670                .filter_map(crate::procfs::mapping_header_identity)
7671                .collect();

7673                guest,
7674                raw_pairs
7675                    .iter()
7676                    .map(|&(raw_dev, raw_inode)| RawInode::new(raw_dev, raw_inode))
7677                    .collect(),
7678            )
7679            .await;
7680            for (&(raw_dev, raw_inode), pooled) in raw_pairs.iter().zip(pooled) {
7681                if mapping_identities.contains_key(&(raw_dev, raw_inode)) {
7682                    continue;
7683                }
7684                let det_inode = stdio_by_raw_inode
7685                    .get(&RawInode::new(raw_dev, raw_inode))
7686                    .copied()
7687                    .unwrap_or(pooled);
7688                // The device pool numbers first sightings only, so a repeated
7689                // device request changes nothing.
7690                let det_dev = determinize_device(guest, raw_dev).await;
7691                mapping_identities.insert((raw_dev, raw_inode), (det_dev, det_inode.as_raw()));

7693        }

7695            .thread_state()
7696            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_needs_mountinfo_identities())?
7697        {
7698            let mut rows = crate::procfs::parse_mountinfo(&contents).ok_or_else(|| {
7699                Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7700                    "kernel returned malformed /proc/*/mountinfo"
7701                ))
7702            })?;
7703            let mut device_rewrites = BTreeMap::new();
7704            for &(mountinfo_device, metadata_device) in &guest.config().mountinfo_device_rewrites {
7705                if device_rewrites
7706                    .insert(mountinfo_device, metadata_device)
7707                    .is_some()
7708                {
7709                    return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7710                        "duplicate proven mountinfo device rewrite for raw device {mountinfo_device}"
7711                    )));
7712                }
7713            }
7714            for row in &mut rows {
7715                if let Some(metadata_device) = device_rewrites.get(&row.raw_device) {
