7717                }
7718            }
7719            let mut raw_devices = Vec::new();
7720            let mut seen_devices = BTreeSet::new();
7721            for row in &rows {
7722                if seen_devices.insert(row.raw_device) {
7723                    raw_devices.push(row.raw_device);
7724                }
7725            }
7726            let mut devices = BTreeMap::new();
7727            let virtualize_metadata = guest.config().virtualize_metadata;
7728            if virtualize_metadata {
7729                // Intentionally use snapshot row order to pre-populate the
7730                // same run-global DevicePool used by stat/statx. This makes
7731                // every later observation of a device agree within the run.
7732                // It does not promise that unlike host filesystem layouts
7733                // expose the same device equivalence classes or order.
7734                for raw in raw_devices {
7735                    devices.insert(raw, determinize_device(guest, raw).await);
7736                }
7737            }
7738            let mut root_rewrites = BTreeMap::new();
7739            for rewrite in &guest.config().mountinfo_root_rewrites {
7740                if root_rewrites
7741                    .insert(rewrite.raw_mount_id, rewrite.clone())
7742                    .is_some()
7743                {
7744                    return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7745                        "duplicate proven mountinfo root rewrite for mount ID {}",
7746                        rewrite.raw_mount_id
7747                    )));
7748                }
7749            }
7750            let mut snapshot = MountInfoSnapshot::new(
7751                rows,
7752                if guest.config().mountinfo_mount_ids_captured {
7753                    &guest.config().mountinfo_mount_ids
7754                } else {
7755                    &[]
7756                },
7757                virtualize_metadata,
7758                devices,
7759                root_rewrites,
7760            )
7761            .ok_or_else(|| {
7762                Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7763                    "mountinfo snapshot failed strict identity validation"
7764                ))
7765            })?;
7766            // Number this view's mount IDs through the same run-global pool
7767            // as fdinfo. IDs the run has already shown keep their numbers;
7768            // the rest are numbered in the order this view presents them
7769            // (rows, then parent-only IDs). The canonical order, which may
7770            // follow the captured namespace, only validates the view.
7771            let observation_order = snapshot.raw_mount_id_observation_order();
7772            let Some(virtual_ids) = resolve_mountinfo_identities(
7773                guest,
7774                snapshot.raw_mount_id_order(),
7775                observation_order.clone(),
7776            )
7777            .await
7778            else {
7779                return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7780                    "mountinfo mount-ID order changed after the run-global identity snapshot"
7781                )));
7782            };
7783            if !snapshot.use_run_mount_ids(&observation_order, &virtual_ids) {
7784                return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
7785                    "run-global mount identities do not cover this mountinfo snapshot"
7786                )));
7787            }
7788            Some(snapshot)
7789        } else {
7790            None
7791        };
7792        // `/proc/locks` keeps the guest's own rows only: an OFD lock has no
7793        // owning task, so Linux shows every process's OFD locks from every
7794        // PID namespace (`procfs::locks`). Decided before the sanitizer
7795        // numbers identities, so a dropped row shifts no remaining id. The
7796        // capture above and this decision are two steps of one turn: with
7797        // sequentialized threads no other guest thread's lock call (and its
7798        // fdinfo record) runs between them. Parallel execution would need
7799        // them taken as one.
7800        let lock_rows_kept = if guest
7801            .thread_state()
7802            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_lists_locks())?
7803        {
7804            match crate::procfs::locks::lock_rows(&contents) {
7805                Some(rows) => match crate::tool_global::guest_lock_rows(guest, rows).await {
7806                    Ok(kept) => Some(kept),
7807                    Err(reason) => {
7808                        let reason = format!(
7809                            "/proc/locks: {reason}; that description's rows cannot be told \
7810                             from another process's"
7811                        );
7812                        self.refuse_lock_bookkeeping(guest, reason).await
7813                    }
7814                },
7815                // Rows that do not parse: the sanitizer refuses the snapshot.
7816                None => None,
7817            }
7818        } else {
7819            None
7820        };
7821        let machine = crate::machine::MachineDescription::of(guest.config());
7822        // A status reports the guest's own mask of a thread Detcore holds
7823        // under a private blocking mask, which that thread published to the
7824        // scheduler; the kernel's `SigBlk` is Detcore's mask (Codex review of
7825        // R2b-2 stage 2, P2; https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273).
7826        // Masks are published only where the scheduler models signal targets,
7827        // and under the in-guest delivery gate, where each request publishes
7828        // the guest's mask (A5 step 3c.1b) and the kernel's may be the in-guest
7829        // runtime's (`publishes_guest_masks`). With nothing published for the
7830        // thread, the kernel's `SigBlk` is reported, as before.
7831        let mask_thread = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
7832            detfd.procfs_status_mask_thread(&contents)
7833        })?;
7834        let mask_facts = status_published_sigblk(guest, mask_thread).await?;
7835        // Under `--virtual-cpus` a status reports the CPU affinity of the
7836        // thread it describes. A thread the scheduler no longer knows (one
7837        // reaped while the file was open) shows every CPU.
7838        let cpus_allowed = match (self.cfg.virtual_cpus, mask_thread) {
7839            (Some(cpus), Some(thread)) => Some(
7840                crate::tool_global::cpu_affinity(guest, crate::types::DetTid::from_raw(thread))
7841                    .await
7842                    .cpus(cpus.get())
7843                    .unwrap_or_else(|_| crate::cpu_set::CpuSet::first(cpus.get())),
7844            ),
7845            _ => None,
7846        };
7847        // A task's `schedstat` shows its runtime where it is a thread of the
7848        // reader's own process (`Detcore::same_process_task_runtime`).
7849        let schedstat_thread = guest
7850            .thread_state()
7851            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_schedstat_thread())?;
7852        let schedstat_runtime = match schedstat_thread {
7853            Some(thread) => self.same_process_task_runtime(guest, thread).await,
7854            None => None,
7855        };
7856        // A process's `stat` or `comm` Detcore opened renders its task's
7857        // record in the process table as of this read (`procfs::task_stat`).
7858        let task_stat = self
7859            .rendered_task_stat(guest, call.fd(), virtual_ppid)
7860            .await?;
7861        guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
7862            detfd.initialize_procfs(
7863                contents.clone(),
7864                ProcfsSnapshotContext {
7865                    mapping_identities: mapping_identities.clone(),
7866                    mountinfo: mountinfo.clone(),
7867                    virtual_uptime_seconds,
7868                    virtual_boot_time_seconds,
7869                    virtual_realtime_seconds,
7870                    virtual_pid,
7871                    virtual_ppid,
7872                    virtual_pty_count,
7873                    fdinfo_identity,
7874                    random_uuid,
7875                    virtual_cpuinfo: virtual_cpuinfo.clone(),
7876                    machine: machine.clone(),
7877                    schedstat_runtime,
7878                    published_sigblk: mask_facts.sigblk,
7879                    // A5 step 3c.1d, design D37: the pending ignored signals
7880                    // the guest's mask lets in are left out, under the gate
7881                    // only; those a temporary-mask publication keeps from its
7882                    // call's entry stay, each queue by its own held mask (A5
7883                    // step 3c.1e A).
7884                    status_hides_ignored: guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery,
7885                    status_held_ignored: (mask_facts.held_private, mask_facts.held_shared),
7886                    cpus_allowed,
7887                    lock_rows_kept: lock_rows_kept.clone(),
7888                    task_stat,
7889                },
7890            );
7891        })?;
7892        Ok(())
7893    }
7894
7895    /// The bytes of the procfs file open as `fd`, if it is a process's
7896    /// `mountinfo` or `mounts` and the run has a container mount table
7897    /// (`Config::container_mount_table`): the table's `mountinfo`, with raw
7898    /// identities that the snapshot then numbers as it numbers the kernel's,
7899    /// or its `mounts`. Wherever the file was opened from: rendered by Detcore,
7900    /// or opened by the kernel (under record and replay, through a spelling
7901    /// Detcore does not resolve, on a backend's own procfs), except one the
7902    /// kernel opened after the process it names changed its root, whose view
7903    /// the kernel decides (`chroot` keeps the kernel's path, as for every
7904    /// rendered file). `None` for every other file.
7905    fn mount_table_snapshot<G: Guest<Self>>(
7906        &self,
7907        guest: &G,
7908        fd: RawFd,
7909    ) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, Errno> {
7910        let Some(table) = guest.config().container_mount_table.as_ref() else {
7911            return Ok(None);
7912        };
7913        let (rendering, rendered, pinned) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
7914            (
7915                detfd.procfs_mount_table_rendering(),
7916                detfd.procfs_rendered_path().is_some(),
7917                detfd.procfs_pinned_mount_view(),
7918            )
7919        })?;
7920        let Some(rendering) = rendering else {
7921            return Ok(None);
7922        };
7923        // A rendered file is the table, as its open decided. A file the kernel
7924        // opened reads the view its open pinned; one nothing pinned (a
7925        // descriptor Detcore learned of otherwise), the reader's.
7926        let kernel_view = !rendered
7927            && pinned.unwrap_or_else(|| {
7928                guest
7929                    .thread_state()
7930                    .changed_root
7931                    .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
7932            });
7933        if kernel_view {
7934            return Ok(None);
7935        }
7936        Ok(Some(match rendering {
7937            crate::procfs::MountTableRendering::Mountinfo => table.mountinfo(),
7938            crate::procfs::MountTableRendering::Mounts => {
7939                table.mounts(&guest.config().mountinfo_root_rewrites)
7940            }
7941        }))
7942    }
7943
7944    /// The runtime of `thread`, its user plus system time, where it is the
7945    /// reader or another thread of the reader's own process
7946    /// (`ThreadState::task_cpu_time`, the accounting the CPU-time clocks
7947    /// read), and Detcore renders the reader's own `stat`, so that the two
7948    /// files agree: `None` under record and replay, after `chroot` and in a
7949    /// nested PID namespace, where the kernel serves `stat` with its CPU
7950    /// times zeroed, and for a thread of another process, whose accounting
7951    /// Detcore keeps in that process's own threads.
7952    async fn same_process_task_runtime<G: Guest<Self>>(
7953        &self,
7954        guest: &mut G,
7955        thread: crate::types::DetTid,
7956    ) -> Option<crate::types::LogicalTime> {
7957        if !self.renders_procfs(guest) || guest.thread_state().nested_pid_namespace {
7958            return None;
7959        }
7960        if thread != guest.thread_state().dettid {
7961            let own = guest.thread_state().detpid?;
7962            let process = crate::tool_global::signal_target_process(guest, thread).await;
7963            if process != Some(own) {
7964                return None;
7965            }
7966        }
7967        let (user, system) = guest.thread_state().task_cpu_time(thread);
7968        Some(user + system)
7969    }
7970
7971    /// Whether the process's `mountinfo` or `mounts` the kernel opened as
7972    /// `file` reads the kernel's view: the task the path names has a changed
7973    /// root (`tool_global::root_changed`, which follows filesystem groups
7974    /// shared through CLONE_FS), or Detcore cannot tell which task it names.
7975    /// As on Linux, where `mounts_open_common` takes the target task's root,
7976    /// the reader's own root does not decide it. The kernel's view is
7977    /// Linux's own answer for whatever task the path names, so it is the
7978    /// answer whenever the task is unknown: never the launch table.
7979    async fn mount_view_is_kernel<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &mut G, file: &ProcfsFile) -> bool {
7980        // In a nested PID namespace the path's numbers are that namespace's
7981        // (a child that kept a `/proc` directory descriptor across
7982        // CLONE_NEWPID and opens `self/mountinfo` through it, for one), and
7983        // Detcore does not map them here.
7984        let Some((pid, tid)) = self.procfs_caller_ids(guest) else {
7985            return true;
7986        };
7987        let mut bound = file.clone();
7988        bound.bind_task(pid, tid);
7989        match bound.bound_task() {
7990            Some(task) => {
7991                crate::tool_global::root_changed(
7992                    guest,
7993                    detcore_model::pid::DetPid::from_raw(task.thread.unwrap_or(task.process)),
7994                )
7995                .await
7996            }
7997            None => true,
7998        }
7999    }
8000
8001    /// The raw mount ID a file on mount `raw_mount_id` reports to the guest:
8002    /// with a container mount table, and until the process changes its root,
8003    /// a hidden mount's nearest shown ancestor
8004    /// (`ContainerMountTable::shown_mount_id`); otherwise the mount itself.
8005    pub(crate) fn shown_mount_id<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &G, raw_mount_id: u64) -> u64 {
8006        match guest.config().container_mount_table.as_ref() {
8007            Some(table)
8008                if !guest
8009                    .thread_state()
8010                    .changed_root
8011                    .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) =>
8012            {
8013                table.shown_mount_id(raw_mount_id)
8014            }
8015            _ => raw_mount_id,
8016        }
8017    }
8018
8019    /// Write `stat`, a procfs file Detcore renders, as `statx`'s result, with
8020    /// the guest's procfs mount's ID, as its fdinfo `mnt_id` shows it.
8021    async fn write_rendered_statx<G: Guest<Self>>(
8022        &self,
8023        guest: &mut G,
8024        call: syscalls::Statx,
8025        stat: DetStat,
8026    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
8027        let statptr = call.statx().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
8028        let mut statx: reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx = stat.into();
8029        let raw_mount_id = rendered_procfs::guest_procfs_mount_id().ok();
8030        let unique = statx_requested_mask(call) & STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE != 0;
8031        self.fill_statx_mount_id(guest, &mut statx, raw_mount_id, unique)
8032            .await;
8033        guest.memory().write_value(statptr.0, &statx)?;
8034        Ok(0)
8035    }
8036
8037    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4213):
8038    // Review STATX_MNT_ID numbered as fdinfo's mnt_id, a hidden mount's file
8039    // reporting its nearest shown ancestor.
8040    /// Fill `statx`'s mount ID for a file on mount `raw_mount_id` (a classic
8041    /// ID), as Linux fills it whether or not the caller asked for it
8042    /// (`vfs_statx_path`, v6.12 fs/stat.c:248-259): the number its fdinfo
8043    /// `mnt_id` and its `mountinfo` row show, through the run's mount-ID
8044    /// pool, a hidden mount's file showing its nearest shown ancestor's
8045    /// ([`Self::shown_mount_id`]), with `STATX_MNT_ID`. If the caller asked
8046    /// for `STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE` (`unique`), Linux reports the mount's unique
8047    /// ID and that bit instead; here that is the same number plus
8048    /// [`MNT_UNIQUE_ID_OFFSET`], which is above every classic ID, the same
8049    /// for every file of the mount, different for every other mount, and
8050    /// the first valid unique ID for the first mount numbered. Where there is
8051    /// no such number (no mount provenance to number it by, outside Hermit's
8052    /// container, or no mount ID from the kernel), the field is 0 and both
8053    /// mask bits are cleared, so no caller reads a number that names nothing.
8054    ///
8055    /// Where this differs from Linux: the pool is keyed by classic IDs, which
8056    /// Linux can give a new mount after an unmount (an IDA), while a unique
8057    /// ID is never reused. A mount made after another's unmount, on the
8058    /// freed classic ID, shows that mount's unique ID here too.
8059    async fn fill_statx_mount_id<G: Guest<Self>>(
8060        &self,
8061        guest: &mut G,
8062        statx: &mut reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx,
8063        raw_mount_id: Option<u64>,
8064        unique: bool,
8065    ) {
8066        let guest_mount_id = match raw_mount_id {
8067            Some(raw_mount_id) if guest.config().mountinfo_mount_ids_captured => {
8068                let raw_mount_id = self.shown_mount_id(guest, raw_mount_id);
8069                determinize_mount_id(guest, raw_mount_id, None).await
8070            }
8071            _ => None,
8072        };
8073        let reported = match guest_mount_id {
8074            Some(id) if unique => id
8075                .checked_add(MNT_UNIQUE_ID_OFFSET)
8076                .map(|id| (id, STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE)),
8077            Some(id) => Some((id, reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::STATX_MNT_ID)),
8078            None => None,
8079        };
8080        statx.stx_mask &= !(reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::STATX_MNT_ID | STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE);
8081        match reported {
8082            Some((id, bit)) => {
8083                statx.stx_mnt_id = id;
8084                statx.stx_mask |= bit;
8085            }
8086            None => statx.stx_mnt_id = 0,
8087        }
8088    }
8089
8090    /// SYS_read system call (MAYHANG).
8091    pub async fn handle_read<G: Guest<Self>>(
8092        &self,
8093        guest: &mut G,
8094        call: syscalls::Read,
8095    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
8096        if self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?.is_some() {
8097            return self
8098                .read_timer_slack(guest, call.fd(), call.buf(), call.len())
8099                .await;
8100        }
8101        // A rendered `cmdline`: every read, of any count, reads memory.
8102        if guest
8103            .thread_state()
8104            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_reads_memory_at_every_read())
8105            .unwrap_or(false)
8106        {
8107            return self
8108                .read_rendered_cmdline_call(guest, call.fd(), call.buf(), call.len(), None)
8109                .await;
8110        }
8111
8112        if call.len() == 0 {
8113            if let Ok(Some(status_flags)) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8114                (detfd.ty() == FdType::Rng).then(|| detfd.status_flags())
8115            }) {
8116                // Replay reserves random-device fd slots with eventfds. A
8117                // physical zero-length read of that placeholder returns EINVAL
8118                // even though the logical random-device read must return zero.
8119                require_random_device_read_access(status_flags)?;
8120                let limit =
8121                    crate::iovecs::UserAddressLimit::from_query(guest.user_address_limit())?;
8122                // vfs_read still checks access_ok for a zero-length buffer:
8123                // NULL is valid, but an address beyond TASK_SIZE is EFAULT.
8124                limit.validate(&[crate::iovecs::ImportedIovec {
8125                    base: call.buf().map_or(0, |address| address.as_raw()),
8126                    len: 0,
8127                }])?;
8128                return Ok(0);
8129            }
8130            // A zero-count read transfers nothing on a file or stream, but on a
8131            // datagram or SEQPACKET socket it consumes a pending message. Its
8132            // result goes through record/replay: a replayed descriptor may be
8133            // a placeholder whose own zero-count read fails differently.
8134            // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
8135            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3601)
8136            return self
8137                .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
8138                .await;
8139        }
8140
8141        let (serves_procfs_snapshot, cannot_read) =
8142            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8143                (
8144                    detfd.procfs_serves_snapshot(),
8145                    !can_read(detfd.status_flags()),
8146                )
8147            })?;
8148        // A descriptor that cannot read (`O_PATH`, write-only, access mode 3)
8149        // reads nothing (EBADF), before its buffer is looked at, as Linux's
8150        // `vfs_read` checks, whether or not a rendered file's snapshot is
8151        // taken yet (`/proc/uptime`'s is taken at its first read).
8152        if serves_procfs_snapshot && cannot_read {
8153            return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
8154        }
8155        if serves_procfs_snapshot {
8156            validate_procfs_destination(
8157                || crate::iovecs::UserAddressLimit::from_query(guest.user_address_limit()),
8158                call.buf(),
8159                call.len(),
8160            )?;
8161        }
8162        // A rendered `stat` renders anew where the read does not continue
8163        // the sequence: after a `pread` or a `preadv` moved it, the shared
8164        // cursor is elsewhere (`ProcfsFile::drop_stale_task_snapshot`). Only
8165        // after `vfs_read`'s checks: the descriptor's access (above), the
8166        // destination (`access_ok`, above) and the range (`rw_verify_area`:
8167        // a cursor plus count past LLONG_MAX is EINVAL).
8168        let task_record_cursor = if guest
8169            .thread_state()
8170            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_renders_task_record())?
8171        {
8172            self.adopt_rendered_procfs_position(guest, call.fd())
8173                .await?;
8174            let cursor = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8175                detfd.procfs_position().map_or(0, |(offset, _)| offset)
8176            })?;
8177            verify_procfs_read_range(cursor, call.len())?;
8178            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8179                detfd.procfs_drop_stale_task_snapshot(cursor)
8180            })?;
8181            Some(cursor)
8182        } else {
8183            None
8184        };
8185        // A task's `schedstat` shows the runtime anew at a read at 0
8186        // (`ProcfsFile::drop_schedstat_snapshot_for_read_at`).
8187        guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8188            let cursor = detfd.procfs_position().map_or(0, |(offset, _)| offset);
8189            detfd.procfs_drop_schedstat_snapshot_for_read_at(cursor as u64)
8190        })?;
8191        let needs_procfs_snapshot = guest
8192            .thread_state()
8193            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_needs_snapshot())?;
8194        if needs_procfs_snapshot {
8195            let rendered = self.initialize_procfs_snapshot(guest, call).await;
8196            if let Some(cursor) = task_record_cursor {
8197                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8198                    detfd.procfs_note_task_record_rendered(cursor, rendered.is_ok())
8199                })?;
8200            }
8201            rendered?;
8202        }
8203
8204        self.adopt_rendered_procfs_position(guest, call.fd())
8205            .await?;
8206        // Like a seq_file read, advance the shared cursor only by the bytes
8207        // actually copied: a read that faults before copying anything leaves
8208        // it where it was.
8209        let procfs_preview = guest
8210            .thread_state()
8211            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.preview_procfs(call.len()))?;
8212        if let Some((offset, bytes)) = procfs_preview {
8213            let faults_on_a_short_copy = guest
8214                .thread_state()
8215                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_faults_on_a_short_copy())?;
8216            let copied = copy_procfs_read(
8217                &mut guest.memory(),
8218                call.buf(),
8219                &bytes,
8220                faults_on_a_short_copy,
8221            )?;
8222            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8223                detfd.commit_procfs_read(offset, copied);
8224            })?;
8225            self.sync_rendered_procfs_position(guest, call.fd()).await?;
8226            return Ok(copied as i64);
8227        }
8228
8229        self.fifo_polls_if_a_guest_holds_its_peer(guest, call.fd(), FifoPeer::Writer)
8230            .await;
8231        let (fd_type, resource, descriptor) =
8232            guest.thread_state_mut().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8233                (detfd.ty(), detfd.resource(), detfd.clone())
8234            })?;
8235
8236        if let Some(resource) = resource {
8237            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::R);
8238            resource_request(guest, request).await;
8239        }
8240
8241        let res = match fd_type {
8242            FdType::Rng => {
8243                trace!("Read call RNG fd {}, simulating...", call.fd());
8244                let status_flags = descriptor.status_flags();
8245                let stream = descriptor.random_device_stream();
8246                descriptor
8247                    .with_random_device_stream(|offset| {
8248                        require_random_device_read_access(status_flags)?;
8249                        let remote_buf = call.buf().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
8250                        self.fill_random_device_bytes(guest, stream, remote_buf, call.len(), offset)
8251                    })
8252                    .map(|n| n as i64)
8253            }
8254            FdType::Regular | FdType::Pipe if descriptor.inherited_external_read().is_some() => {
8255                // An authenticated controller input or terminal can block
8256                // after this Device grant.
8257                // Announce one external kernel read even when our cached flags
8258                // say nonblocking: a fork/exec peer can change the shared OFD's
8259                // flags while the process-local model remains stale (the
8260                // pre-existing https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3520).
8261                // The kernel keeps its actual O_NONBLOCK semantics, including
8262                // immediate EAGAIN. Never fill an external short read to len.
8263                self.record_or_replay_blocking(guest, call.into()).await
8264            }
8265            FdType::Regular => {
8266                if guest.config().deterministic_io {
8267                    self.deterministic_read(guest, call).await
8268                } else {
8269                    Ok(self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?)
8270                }
8271            }
8272            FdType::Signalfd
8273                if call.len() >= 2 * crate::syscalls::signal::SIGNALFD_RECORD
8274                    && self.signalfd_reads_per_record(guest, call.fd()).await =>
8275            {
8276                self.read_signalfd_per_record(guest, call).await
8277            }
8278            FdType::Signalfd => self.read_signalfd(guest, call, true).await,
8279            FdType::Timerfd => {
8280                trace!("Possibly blocking read call on timerfd {}", call.fd());
8281                // Expirations up to this thread's virtual now make the host
8282                // descriptor readable before a nonblocking read's one attempt;
8283                // a blocking read's retries publish again at each turn.
8284                crate::syscalls::timerfd::publish_expired(guest).await;
8285                let result = self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
8286                crate::syscalls::timerfd::finish_read(guest, call.fd(), call.buf(), result)
8287            }
8288            FdType::Eventfd => {
8289                trace!(
8290                    "Possibly blocking read call on notification fd {}, type {:?}",
8291                    call.fd(),
8292                    fd_type
8293                );
8294                self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await
8295            }
8296            FdType::Inotify => {
8297                trace!(
8298                    "Possibly blocking read call on notification fd {}, type {:?}",
8299                    call.fd(),
8300                    fd_type
8301                );
8302                let destination = crate::syscalls::inotify::Destination::buffer(
8303                    call.buf().map_or(0, |buf| buf.as_raw()),
8304                    call.len(),
8305                );
8306                let queued = crate::syscalls::inotify::queued_before(guest, call.fd(), call).await;
8307                let result = self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
8308                crate::syscalls::inotify::finish(
8309                    guest,
8310                    Sysno::read,
8311                    call.fd(),
8312                    Some(destination),
8313                    queued,
8314                    result,
8315                )
8316                .await
8317            }
8318            FdType::Memfd | FdType::Pidfd | FdType::Userfaultfd | FdType::Epoll => {
8319                trace!("Read call on unusual fd {}, type {:?}", call.fd(), fd_type);
8320                Ok(self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?)
8321            }
8322
8323            FdType::Socket | FdType::Pipe => {
8324                trace!(
8325                    "Possibly blocking read call on {:?} fd {}",
8326                    fd_type,
8327                    call.fd()
8328                );
8329                self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await
8330            }
8331        };
8332        // O2: a signalfd read (even one that faulted copying out a record
8333        // it had already dequeued) may have taken the process's ITIMER_REAL
8334        // copy (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139).
8335        if fd_type == FdType::Signalfd {
8336            crate::tool_global::reconcile_alarm(guest).await;
8337        }
8338        resource_release_all(guest).await;
8339        res
8340    }
8341
8342    /// One read of signalfd `call`, as the kernel answers it, with each
8343    /// record put through the child-exit ledger and the discarded-at-send
8344    /// record (`reconcile_signalfd_records`). A read whose every record was
8345    /// dropped reads again if `may_read_again`, as if those copies had never
8346    /// been queued; otherwise it answers 0.
8347    async fn read_signalfd<G: Guest<Self>>(
8348        &self,
8349        guest: &mut G,
8350        call: syscalls::Read,
8351        may_read_again: bool,
8352    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
8353        loop {
8354            trace!("Possibly blocking read call on signalfd {}", call.fd());
8355            let extents = [(call.buf().map_or(0, |buf| buf.as_raw()), call.len())];
8356            let before =
8357                crate::syscalls::signal::capture_signalfd_buffer(guest, &extents, call.len());
8358            let result = self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
8359            // A SIGCHLD read here goes through the child-exit ledger as
8360            // one delivered to a handler does. A read whose every record
8361            // was a dropped duplicate reads again, as if those copies had
8362            // never been queued.
8363            match (result, call.buf()) {
8364                (Ok(read), Some(buf))
8365                    if read > 0 && self.cfg.backend.reports_child_exit_publication =>
8366                {
8367                    let Some(kept) = self
8368                        .reconcile_signalfd_records(guest, buf, read as usize, &before)
8369                        .await
8370                    else {
8371                        break self
8372                            .refuse_unrestorable_signalfd_record(guest, Sysno::read)
8373                            .await;
8374                    };
8375                    if self
8376                        .settle_faulted_signalfd_record(
8377                            guest,
8378                            call.fd(),
8379                            &extents,
8380                            Some(read as usize),
8381                        )
8382                        .await
8383                    {
8384                        break self
8385                            .refuse_faulted_signalfd_discard(guest, Sysno::read)
8386                            .await;
8387                    }
8388                    if kept > 0 {
8389                        break Ok(kept as i64);
8390                    }
8391                    if !may_read_again {
8392                        break Ok(0);
8393                    }
8394                }
8395                (Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EFAULT)), _) => {
8396                    if self
8397                        .settle_faulted_signalfd_record(guest, call.fd(), &extents, None)
8398                        .await
8399                    {
8400                        break self
8401                            .refuse_faulted_signalfd_discard(guest, Sysno::read)
8402                            .await;
8403                    }
8404                    break Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
8405                }
8406                (result, _) => break result,
8407            }
8408        }
8409    }
8410
8411    /// Whether a signalfd read of `fd` takes one record per kernel read
8412    /// (4262 design §4.4): some signal it covers has an entry behind the
8413    /// front of its list, or a stale timer entry, in the calling thread's or
8414    /// its process's queue. A read must then dequeue one record at a time:
8415    /// sending a list's next entry before the next record, as Linux's
8416    /// `signalfd_dequeue` loop takes them in its order, and refilling the slot
8417    /// of a stale record it drops, as Linux skips such an entry inside the
8418    /// dequeue. With only single valid entries, every entry is physically
8419    /// queued and none is dropped, so one kernel read returns what Linux
8420    /// returns, in count and in order.
8421    async fn signalfd_reads_per_record<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &mut G, fd: i32) -> bool {
8422        use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalAnswer;
8423        use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalControl;
8424        if !crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::records(guest.config()) {
8425            return false;
8426        }
8427        let Some(mask) = crate::syscalls::signal::signalfd_mask(guest.pid().as_raw(), fd) else {
8428            return false;
8429        };
8430        matches!(
8431            crate::tool_global::discarded_signal(guest, DiscardedSignalControl::Queued).await,
8432            DiscardedSignalAnswer::Bits { thread, process } if (thread | process) & mask != 0
8433        )
8434    }
8435
8436    /// A signalfd read taken one record at a time
8437    /// (`signalfd_reads_per_record`): the first record's read may block, as
8438    /// the call would; each later one is read only while a signal the
8439    /// descriptor covers is pending, so it never blocks (fs/signalfd.c reads
8440    /// later records without waiting). A fault after k records returns
8441    /// k records, as the kernel's copy-out does.
8442    async fn read_signalfd_per_record<G: Guest<Self>>(
8443        &self,
8444        guest: &mut G,
8445        call: syscalls::Read,
8446    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
8447        const RECORD: usize = crate::syscalls::signal::SIGNALFD_RECORD;
8448        let Some(buf) = call.buf() else {
8449            return self.read_signalfd(guest, call, true).await;
8450        };
8451        let mask = crate::syscalls::signal::signalfd_mask(guest.pid().as_raw(), call.fd());
8452        let mut done = 0usize;
8453        // A read whose records were all dropped (stale timer entries) frees
8454        // its slot. Each such read dequeued a physical record and popped its
8455        // entry, and the lists are finite, so the refills end without a cap
8456        // (the Codex re-review of
8457        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4491, P2: 80 stale entries).
8458        while done + RECORD <= call.len() {
8459            if done > 0 {
8460                let pending =
8461                    crate::syscalls::threads::read_kernel_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())
8462                        .map(|state| state.thread_pending | state.shared_pending)
8463                        .unwrap_or(0);
8464                if mask.is_none_or(|mask| pending & mask == 0) {
8465                    break;
8466                }
8467            }
8468            // A guest address, never dereferenced here.
8469            let at = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(buf.as_raw() + done);
8470            let record = syscalls::Read::new()
8471                .with_fd(call.fd())
8472                .with_buf(at)
8473                .with_len(RECORD);
8474            match self.read_signalfd(guest, record, done == 0).await {
8475                Ok(read) if read > 0 => done += read as usize,
8476                Ok(read) if done == 0 => return Ok(read),
8477                // Linux skips a stale entry inside the dequeue and fills the
8478                // slot with the next pending signal (the Claude review of
8479                // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4491, P2-1).
8480                Ok(_) => {}
8481                Err(error) if done == 0 => return Err(error),
8482                Err(_) => break,
8483            }
8484        }
8485        Ok(done as i64)
8486    }
8487
8488    /// SYS_pread64 system call.
8489    pub async fn handle_pread64<G: Guest<Self>>(
8490        &self,
8491        guest: &mut G,
8492        call: syscalls::Pread64,
8493    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
8494        if self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?.is_some() {
8495            return self
8496                .pread_timer_slack(guest, call.fd(), call.buf(), call.len(), call.offset())
8497                .await;
8498        }
8499        // A rendered `cmdline`: `ksys_pread64` refuses a negative position
8500        // first, then every read, of any count, reads memory.
8501        if guest
8502            .thread_state()
8503            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_reads_memory_at_every_read())
8504            .unwrap_or(false)
8505        {
8506            let offset = u64::try_from(call.offset()).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
8507            return self
8508                .read_rendered_cmdline_call(guest, call.fd(), call.buf(), call.len(), Some(offset))
8509                .await;
8510        }
8511
8512        if call.len() == 0 {
8513            // As for read, a zero-count pread's result goes through
8514            // record/replay.
8515            // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
8516            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3601)
8517            return self
8518                .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
8519                .await;
8520        }
8521
8522        let offset = usize::try_from(call.offset()).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
8523        let (serves_procfs_snapshot, cannot_read, renders_task_record) =
8524            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8525                (
8526                    detfd.procfs_serves_snapshot(),
8527                    !can_read(detfd.status_flags()),
8528                    detfd.procfs_renders_task_record(),
8529                )
8530            })?;
8531        // A descriptor that cannot read (`O_PATH`, write-only, access mode 3)
8532        // reads nothing (EBADF), before its buffer is looked at, as Linux's
8533        // `vfs_read` checks, whether or not a rendered file's snapshot is
8534        // taken yet (`/proc/uptime`'s is taken at its first read).
8535        if serves_procfs_snapshot && cannot_read {
8536            return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
8537        }
8538        if serves_procfs_snapshot {
8539            validate_procfs_destination(
8540                || crate::iovecs::UserAddressLimit::from_query(guest.user_address_limit()),
8541                call.buf(),
8542                call.len(),
8543            )?;
8544        }
8545        // A rendered `stat` renders anew where the read does not continue
8546        // the sequence (`ProcfsFile::drop_stale_task_snapshot`), only after
8547        // `vfs_read`'s checks: access, destination (above) and range
8548        // (`rw_verify_area`: a position plus count past LLONG_MAX is EINVAL).
8549        if renders_task_record {
8550            verify_procfs_read_range(offset, call.len())?;
8551            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8552                detfd.procfs_drop_stale_task_snapshot(offset)
8553            })?;
8554        }
8555        // A task's `schedstat` shows the runtime anew at a read at 0
8556        // (`ProcfsFile::drop_schedstat_snapshot_for_read_at`).
8557        guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8558            detfd.procfs_drop_schedstat_snapshot_for_read_at(offset as u64)
8559        })?;
8560        let needs_procfs_snapshot = guest
8561            .thread_state()
8562            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_needs_snapshot())?;
8563        if needs_procfs_snapshot {
8564            let read = syscalls::Read::new()
8565                .with_fd(call.fd())
8566                .with_buf(call.buf())
8567                .with_len(call.len());
8568            let rendered = self.initialize_procfs_snapshot(guest, read).await;
8569            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8570                detfd.procfs_note_task_record_rendered(offset, rendered.is_ok())
8571            })?;
8572            rendered?;
8573        } else if serves_procfs_snapshot
8574            && !renders_task_record
8575            && guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8576                detfd
8577                    .procfs_position()
8578                    .is_some_and(|(position, _)| position != offset)
8579            })?
8580        {
8581            // A read at a position the buffered snapshot does not start at
8582            // runs a per-process file's `show` again (`traverse`).
8583            self.require_rendered_task(guest, call.fd()).await?;
8584        }
8585
8586        let procfs_bytes = guest
8587            .thread_state()
8588            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.take_procfs_at(offset, call.len()))?;
8589        if let Some(bytes) = procfs_bytes {
8590            let faults_on_a_short_copy = guest
8591                .thread_state()
8592                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_faults_on_a_short_copy())?;
8593            let copied = copy_procfs_read(
8594                &mut guest.memory(),
8595                call.buf(),
8596                &bytes,
8597                faults_on_a_short_copy,
8598            )?;
8599            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8600                detfd.procfs_note_read_end(offset + copied)
8601            })?;
8602            return Ok(copied as i64);
8603        }
8604
8605        let (fd_type, resource, status_flags, stream) =
8606            guest.thread_state_mut().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8607                (
8608                    detfd.ty(),
8609                    detfd.resource(),
8610                    detfd.status_flags(),
8611                    detfd.random_device_stream(),
8612                )
8613            })?;
8614
8615        if let Some(resource) = resource {
8616            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::R);
8617            resource_request(guest, request).await;
8618        }
8619
8620        let res = match fd_type {
8621            FdType::Rng => (|| -> Result<i64, Error> {
8622                trace!("Pread64 call RNG fd {}, simulating...", call.fd());
8623                // A random device open for writing only reads nothing
8624                // (EBADF), before its buffer is looked at, as `vfs_read`
8625                // checks FMODE_READ first; read and readv already check.
8626                require_random_device_read_access(status_flags)?;
8627                let remote_buf = call.buf().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
8628                let n = self.fill_random_device_bytes(
8629                    guest,
8630                    stream,
8631                    remote_buf,
8632                    call.len(),
8633                    offset as u64,
8634                )?;
8635                Ok(n as i64)
8636            })(),
8637            FdType::Regular if guest.config().deterministic_io => {
8638                self.deterministic_pread64(guest, call).await
8639            }
8640            _ => match self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await {
8641                Ok(value) => Ok(value),
8642                Err(error) => Err(error.into()),
8643            },
8644        };
8645
8646        resource_release_all(guest).await;
8647        res
8648    }
8649
8650    /// Whether `fd`, whose open recorded the host stat `cached`, is a
8651    /// directory that is not on procfs (see [`Self::handle_lseek`]). procfs
8652    /// keeps the host's seek behavior, as it keeps the host's sizes. A
8653    /// descriptor's type and device never change, so the stat its open took
8654    /// answers without another `fstat` (Claude re-check of
8655    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4369). Its block size can (a
8656    /// FUSE server reports it), so it only rules procfs out: the kernel's
8657    /// procfs always has 1024-byte blocks, and a directory that may be procfs
8658    /// is proved so by naming its entry, as a stat does. (KVM's `/proc`
8659    /// directories are Detcore's placeholders, which answer `lseek`
8660    /// themselves.) Under DBT, where
8661    /// Detcore names no entries, one with procfs's stat fields keeps the
8662    /// host's seek unproved ([`procfs_inode::unprovable_procfs_signature`]).
8663    /// With metadata virtualized every descriptor the guest opened has a stat;
8664    /// those without are Detcore's own pipes and sockets.
8665    async fn is_seekable_directory<G: Guest<Self>>(
8666        guest: &mut G,
8667        fd: RawFd,
8668        cached: Option<DetStat>,
8669    ) -> bool {
8670        let Some(stat) = cached.filter(|stat| stat.mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFDIR) else {
8671            return false;
8672        };
8673        if procfs_inode::unprovable_procfs_signature(
8674            &guest.config().backend,
8675            guest.thread_state().physical_tid,
8676            stat.dev,
8677            stat.blksize,
8678        ) {
8679            return false;
8680        }
8681        !Self::procfs_entry(guest, &stat, StatTarget::Descriptor(fd))
8682            .await
8683            .is_procfs()
8684    }
8685
8686    /// SYS_lseek system call.
8687    pub async fn handle_lseek<G: Guest<Self>>(
8688        &self,
8689        guest: &mut G,
8690        call: syscalls::Lseek,
8691    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
8692        let timer_slack_binding = self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?;
8693        // A seek must not move the position under a `getdents` that is
8694        // reading or serving this open file's directory.
8695        let directory_lock = guest
8696            .thread_state()
8697            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.directory_lock())?;
8698        let _seeking = directory_lock.lock().await;
8699        self.adopt_rendered_procfs_position(guest, call.fd())
8700            .await?;
8701        let (fd_type, status_flags, procfs_position, resource, directory_stream, host_order) =
8702            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8703                (
8704                    detfd.ty(),
8705                    detfd.status_flags(),
8706                    detfd.procfs_position(),
8707                    detfd.resource(),
8708                    detfd.has_directory_stream(),
8709                    detfd.directory_in_host_order(),
8710                )
8711            })?;
8712        if fd_type == FdType::Rng {
8713            return random_device_lseek_result(status_flags, call.whence()).map_err(Into::into);
8714        }
8715        if is_inherited_container_output(resource) {
8716            return Err(Errno::ESPIPE.into());
8717        }
8718        if timer_slack_binding.is_some() && status_flags & libc::O_PATH != 0 {
8719            return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
8720        }
8721        if directory_stream {
8722            // Positions in a sorted directory stream are entry indices (see
8723            // `DirectoryStream`), not host cookies. The kernel position only
8724            // follows the stream, for descriptors Detcore does not track. Like
8725            // tmpfs's `dcache_dir_lseek`, only SEEK_SET and SEEK_CUR are
8726            // accepted; SEEK_END, SEEK_DATA and SEEK_HOLE get `EINVAL`, where
8727            // ext4 and btrfs accept SEEK_END
8728            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3724).
8729            let current = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8730                detfd.with_directory_stream(|stream| stream.position())
8731            })??;
8732            let requested = i128::from(call.offset());
8733            let position = match call.whence() {
8734                Whence::SEEK_SET => requested,
8735                Whence::SEEK_CUR => i128::from(current) + requested,
8736                _ => return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into()),
8737            };
8738            let result = i64::try_from(position)
8739                .ok()
8740                .filter(|position| *position >= 0)
8741                .ok_or(Errno::EINVAL)?;
8742            let target = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8743                detfd.with_directory_stream(|stream| {
8744                    stream.seek(result as u64);
8745                    stream.kernel_target()
8746                })
8747            })??;
8748            self.move_directory_kernel_position(guest, call.fd() as RawFd, target)
8749                .await;
8750            return Ok(result);
8751        }
8752        let Some((current, snapshot_len)) = procfs_position else {
8753            // A directory without a stream yet: SEEK_END would return the
8754            // host directory's size, which st_size no longer reports and
8755            // which changes as anything outside the run adds or removes an
8756            // entry (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4372). Answer
8757            // as a stream does (above, tmpfs's `dcache_dir_lseek`), from the
8758            // descriptor's first use. An `O_PATH` descriptor goes on to the
8759            // kernel, which refuses its seek with EBADF whatever the whence.
8760            if guest.config().virtualize_metadata
8761                && status_flags & libc::O_PATH == 0
8762                && matches!(
8763                    call.whence(),
8764                    Whence::SEEK_END | Whence::SEEK_DATA | Whence::SEEK_HOLE
8765                )
8766            {
8767                let cached = guest
8768                    .thread_state()
8769                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.stat())?;
8770                if Self::is_seekable_directory(guest, call.fd(), cached).await {
8771                    return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
8772                }
8773            }
8774            // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
8775            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#1044): Regular-file lseek must
8776            // flow through record_or_replay, exactly as handle_read does for
8777            // FdType::Regular. Injecting the seek live here is correct for run
8778            // and --verify (the inner NoopTool just re-injects), but under
8779            // record/replay the replay descriptor is a virtual placeholder
8780            // whose kernel position never advances (reads are served from the
8781            // log, not the file). A live SEEK_CUR then returned Ok(0) on replay
8782            // versus the recorded offset (e.g. glibc's __tzfile_read rewinds
8783            // /etc/localtime with lseek(fd, -N, SEEK_CUR)), diverging the
8784            // guest's control flow and desynchronizing the event stream. Routing
8785            // through record_or_replay records the offset once and substitutes
8786            // the recorded value on replay, keeping the two runs identical.
8787            // A placeholder descriptor Detcore does not know is never moved
8788            // into the range of the positions that tag one
8789            // (`descriptor_directory`), where it would pass for another.

8791                .seek_would_place_a_tag(

8793                    call.fd() as RawFd,

8802            if host_order && position == 0 {

8804                // directory again and serve it as a sorted stream.
8805                guest
8806                    .thread_state()
8807                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.use_directory_stream())?;

8815            // virtual open-file description even before the first read.

8821            };

8829                    .await?;
8830            }

8832                .thread_state()
8833                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.set_procfs_offset(new_offset))?;

8838        // descriptor has no position (EBADF), before the seek's arguments are
8839        // looked at; otherwise a sysctl file's `default_llseek` on a file of
8840        // size 0, whatever the snapshot holds, or a `seq_file`'s `seq_lseek`,
8841        // which seeks only from the start or the position.
8842        let files = self.rendered_files(guest);
8843        let rendered = guest
8844            .thread_state()
8845            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_renderable_path(files))?;
8846        if let Some(rendered) = rendered {

8849            }

8851                RenderedSeek::SeqFile
8852            } else if crate::procfs::per_process_name(rendered)
8853                .is_some_and(|name| matches!(name.filename, "auxv" | "cmdline"))
8854            {
8855                RenderedSeek::Generic
8856            } else {
8857                RenderedSeek::Default
8858            };

8860            let result = i64::try_from(new_offset).map_err(|_| Errno::EOVERFLOW)?;
8861            // A rendered `stat` traverses at the seek wherever the sequence
8862            // is not (`ProcfsFile::seek_task_record`): to a positive position
8863            // its record is rendered here, in the seeking thread's turn, and
8864            // a failed `show` (ESRCH, or the named refusal) leaves the cursor
8865            // and the sequence at 0, as `seq_lseek` does.
8866            if guest
8867                .thread_state()
8868                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_renders_task_record())?
8869            {
8870                let renders = guest
8871                    .thread_state()
8872                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.seek_procfs_task_record(new_offset))?;
8873                if renders
8874                    && let Err(error) = self
8875                        .initialize_procfs_snapshot(guest, syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(call.fd()))
8876                        .await
8877                {
8878                    guest
8879                        .thread_state()
8880                        .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.reset_procfs_task_record())?;
8881                    self.sync_rendered_procfs_position(guest, call.fd()).await?;
8882                    return Err(error);
8883                }
8884                self.sync_rendered_procfs_position(guest, call.fd()).await?;
8885                return Ok(result);
8886            }
8887            // seq_lseek to another positive position traverses the file,
8888            // which runs a per-process file's `show` (ESRCH once its task is
8889            // gone); a rewind or a no-op does not.
8890            if new_offset != 0 && new_offset != current {
8891                self.require_rendered_task(guest, call.fd()).await?;
8892            }
8893            guest
8894                .thread_state()
8895                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.seek_procfs(new_offset))?;
8896            self.sync_rendered_procfs_position(guest, call.fd()).await?;

8900        let Some(snapshot_len) = snapshot_len else {
8901            let offset = guest.inject(Syscall::from(call)).await?;
8902            let offset = usize::try_from(offset).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
8903            guest
8904                .thread_state()
8905                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.set_procfs_offset(offset))?;
8906            return Ok(offset as i64);
8907        };
8908
8909        // A `seq_file` seeks only from the start or the position, before and
8910        // after the snapshot (`ProcfsFile::seeks_only_from_start_or_position`).
8911        let seq_file = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
8912            detfd.procfs_seeks_only_from_start_or_position()
8913        })?;
8914        let requested = i128::from(call.offset());
8915        let new_offset = match call.whence() {
8916            Whence::SEEK_SET => requested,
8917            Whence::SEEK_CUR => current as i128 + requested,
8918            _ if seq_file => return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into()),
8919            Whence::SEEK_END => snapshot_len as i128 + requested,
8920            Whence::SEEK_DATA => {
8921                if requested < 0 || requested >= snapshot_len as i128 {
8922                    return Err(Errno::ENXIO.into());
8923                }
8924                requested
8925            }
8926            Whence::SEEK_HOLE => {
8927                if requested < 0 || requested >= snapshot_len as i128 {
8928                    return Err(Errno::ENXIO.into());
8929                }
8930                snapshot_len as i128
8931            }
8932            _ => return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into()),
8933        };
8934        let new_offset = usize::try_from(new_offset).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
8935        let result = i64::try_from(new_offset).map_err(|_| Errno::EOVERFLOW)?;
8936        guest
8937            .thread_state()
8938            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.set_procfs_offset(new_offset))?;
8939        self.sync_rendered_procfs_position(guest, call.fd()).await?;
8940        Ok(result)
8941    }

8943    /// Helper for performing a deterministic read that retries until it gets all its
8944    /// bytes.
8945    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
8946    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#689): Confirm partial reads take precedence over later errors.
8947    async fn deterministic_read<G: Guest<Self>>(
8948        &self,
8949        guest: &mut G,
8950        mut call: syscalls::Read,
8951    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
8952        let mut total_read_bytes = 0;
8953        let mut remaining_buf = call.len();
8954
8955        trace!(
8956            "[detcore/det_io]: Requested read buffer size: {:?}",
8957            remaining_buf
8958        );
8959
8960        loop {
8961            match guest.inject_with_retry(call).await {
8962                Ok(res) => {
8963                    remaining_buf -= res as usize;
8964                    total_read_bytes += res;
8965
8966                    trace!(
8967                        "[detcore/det_io]: Remaining read buffer size: {:?}",
8968                        remaining_buf
8969                    );
8970
8971                    if res == 0 || remaining_buf == 0 {
8972                        break Ok(total_read_bytes);
8973                    }
8974
8975                    // Buf is guaranteed to exist as we already issued a syscall.
8976                    let old_ptr = call.buf().unwrap().as_raw();
8977                    call = call
8978                        .with_len(remaining_buf)
8979                        .with_buf(AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(old_ptr + res as usize));
8980                }
8981                Err(error) if total_read_bytes > 0 => {
8982                    trace!("[detcore/det_io]: returning {total_read_bytes} bytes before {error}");
8983                    break Ok(total_read_bytes);
8984                }
8985                Err(error) => break Err(error.into()),
8986            }
8987        }
8988    }

9001            remaining_buf

9007                    remaining_buf -= res as usize;
9008                    total_read_bytes += res;

9010                    trace!(
9011                        "[detcore/det_io]: Remaining pread64 buffer size: {:?}",

9035    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-838): Review regular-file sendfile mediation.
9036    /// Copy data between tracked regular files or memfds.
9037    ///
9038    /// The kernel advances the input offset (or the explicit offset pointer) and
9039    /// destination offset atomically with the copy. Detcore serializes destination
9040    /// writes while the strict scheduler orders the stable input read, and routes
9041    /// the syscall through record/replay so that the result and offset update stay
9042    /// ordered with other file operations. Socket and pipe destinations can block
9043    /// and need the nonblocking scheduler path; return ENOSYS for those endpoint
9044    /// types so libc/application fallbacks use Detcore's existing read/write
9045    /// handlers instead.
9046    pub async fn handle_sendfile<G: Guest<Self>>(
9047        &self,
9048        guest: &mut G,
9049        call: syscalls::Sendfile,
9050    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9051        let in_type = guest
9052            .thread_state()
9053            .with_detfd(call.in_fd(), |detfd| detfd.ty())?;
9054        let (out_type, out_resource, out_inode) =
9055            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.out_fd(), |detfd| {
9056                (
9057                    detfd.ty(),
9058                    detfd.resource(),
9059                    detfd.stat().map(|stat| stat.raw_inode()),
9060                )
9061            })?;
9062
9063        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
9064        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-973): Refuse sendfile from a procfs input so it
9065        // cannot bypass the deterministic ProcfsFile snapshot. A procfs fd is
9066        // classified `FdType::Regular`, so it would otherwise pass the type
9067        // guard below and copy live kernel bytes straight to the output fd,
9068        // reintroducing the nondeterminism the mediated read()/write() path
9069        // sanitizes. Failing closed with ENOSYS makes callers fall back to
9070        // that mediated path (glibc's sendfile does exactly this).
9071        let in_is_procfs = guest
9072            .thread_state()
9073            .with_detfd(call.in_fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_position().is_some())?;
9074        if in_is_procfs {
9075            return Err(Errno::ENOSYS.into());
9076        }
9077
9078        if !matches!(in_type, FdType::Regular | FdType::Memfd)
9079            || !matches!(out_type, FdType::Regular | FdType::Memfd)
9080        {
9081            return Err(Errno::ENOSYS.into());
9082        }
9083
9084        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
9085        let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
9086        // `out_inode` is the fd's cached HOST inode, so it must be
9087        // determinized before naming a resource. It is deliberately left raw
9088        // for the `touch_file` call below, which takes a `RawInode`.
9089        let out_resource = match out_resource {
9090            Some(resource) => Some(resource),
9091            None => match out_inode {
9092                Some(raw_ino) => Some(ResourceID::FileContents(
9093                    determinize_inode(guest, raw_ino).await.0,
9094                )),
9095                None => None,
9096            },
9097        };
9098        if let Some(resource) = out_resource {
9099            resources.insert(resource, Permission::W);
9100        }
9101        resources.fyi("sendfile");
9102        resource_request(guest, resources).await;
9103
9104        let result = self
9105            .record_or_replay(guest, call)
9106            .await
9107            .map_err(Error::from);
9108        if guest.config().virtualize_metadata && matches!(&result, Ok(copied) if *copied > 0) {
9109            let inode = out_inode.expect("virtualized metadata requires stat data for sendfile");
9110            touch_file(guest, inode).await;
9111        }
9112        resource_release_all(guest).await;
9113        result
9114    }

9116    /// SYS_write system call.
9117    pub async fn handle_write<G: Guest<Self>>(
9118        &self,
9119        guest: &mut G,
9120        mut call: syscalls::Write,
9121    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {

9123        // kernel-run call (execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall's blocking branch
9124        // files it), and its virtual mtime bump below (touch_file) is a
9125        // guest-visible effect a call not run must not leave; a default-fatal
9126        // signal deliverable here arrived before the call, a schedule Linux
9127        // permits for any write. The check at the filing point stays for a
9128        // signal sent while this call waits for its turn below.
9129        if let Some(refused) = super::helpers::kernel_run_entry_refusal(guest)? {
9130            return Err(refused);
9131        }
9132        if self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?.is_some() {
9133            return self
9134                .write_timer_slack(guest, call.fd(), call.buf(), call.len())
9135                .await;
9136        }
9137
9138        if call.len() > 0 {
9139            self.fifo_polls_if_a_guest_holds_its_peer(guest, call.fd(), FifoPeer::Reader)
9140                .await;
9141        }
9142        let (
9143            fd_type,
9144            physically_nonblocking,
9145            logically_nonblocking,
9146            open_file_id,
9147            resource,
9148            raw_ino,
9149        ) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
9150            (
9151                detfd.ty(),
9152                detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
9153                detfd.is_nonblocking(),
9154                detfd.open_file_id(),
9155                detfd.resource(),
9156                detfd.stat().map(|x| x.raw_inode()),
9157            )
9158        })?;
9159        // It doesn't matter much where the linearization point for this mtime bump falls:
9160        if guest.config().virtualize_metadata {

9162                raw_ino.expect("Expect that when virtualize_metadata, DetFd's stat is populated!");
9163            touch_file(guest, r).await;

9167            let container_output = crate::sigalrm_phase1::is_container_output(&resource);
9168            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::W);
9169            resource_request(guest, request).await;
9170            // Signal phase 1, design closure 1: a write to inherited stdout or
9171            // stderr may sleep with no scheduler admission. Once the grant is
9172            // taken no SIGALRM commits until this call ends, so one already due
9173            // is the only one it can strand: recorded as a determinism loss.
9174            if guest.thread_state().sigalrm_handled && container_output {

9181        // sequential mode, including record/replay, so their logically blocking writes use
9182        // the completion helper below. A physically blocking fd instead uses the original
9183        // synchronous path: treating an internal pipe as BlockingExternalIO would assume the
9184        // writer and reader were independent and could deadlock the scheduler.

9189            && matches!(fd_type, FdType::Socket | FdType::Pipe | FdType::Eventfd)

9191            self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await
9192        } else if guest.config().deterministic_io {
9193            let mut total_written_bytes = 0;
9194            let mut remaining_buf = call.len();
9195
9196            trace!(
9197                "[detcore/det_io]: Requested write buffer size: {:?}",
9198                remaining_buf
9199            );

9201            loop {
9202                match self
9203                    .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9204                    .await
9205                {
9206                    Ok(res) => {
9207                        remaining_buf -= res as usize;
9208                        total_written_bytes += res;
9209
9210                        trace!(
9211                            "[detcore/det_io]: Remaining write buffer size: {:?}",
9212                            remaining_buf
9213                        );
9214
9215                        if res == 0 || remaining_buf == 0 {
9216                            break Ok(total_written_bytes);
9217                        }
9218
9219                        // Buf is guaranteed to exist as we already issued a syscall.
9220                        let old_ptr = call.buf().unwrap().as_raw();
9221                        call = call
9222                            .with_len(remaining_buf)
9223                            .with_buf(Addr::<u8>::from_raw(old_ptr + res as usize));

9225                    Err(error) => {

9228                }

9233        };

9259        // straight from `fstat`/`statx`), so it must be determinized before it

9261        // to type-check only because `DetInode` was an alias for `RawInode`.

9263            Some(resource) => Some(resource),
9264            None => match raw_ino {
9265                Some(raw_ino) => Some(ResourceID::FileContents(
9266                    determinize_inode(guest, raw_ino).await.0,
9267                )),
9268                None => None,
9269            },
9270        };

9272        if let Some(resource) = resource {
9273            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::W);
9274            resource_request(guest, request).await;
9275        }

9278            let mut total_written = 0_i64;
9279            let mut remaining = call.len();
9280

9282                match self
9283                    .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9284                    .await
9285                {
9286                    Ok(written) => {
9287                        let Ok(written) = usize::try_from(written) else {
9288                            break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
9289                        };
9290                        let Ok(written_i64) = i64::try_from(written) else {
9291                            break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
9292                        };

9294                            break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
9295                        }

9308                        };

9313                            break Err(Errno::EFBIG.into());

9315                        let Some(next_buf) = Addr::<u8>::from_raw(next_buf) else {
9316                            break Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
9317                        };

9319                            .with_buf(Some(next_buf))
9320                            .with_len(remaining)
9321                            .with_offset(next_offset);

9323                    Err(error) => {
9324                        break finish_partial_record_or_replay_write(total_written, error);

9326                }
9327            }
9328        } else {
9329            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)

9344    /// SYS_writev system call.
9345    ///
9346    /// Preserve the initial writev as one kernel operation so its iovec order remains intact.
9347    /// Detcore adds open-file resource ordering and nonblocking scheduler integration; a
9348    /// blocking pipe short write is completed by the helper because Hermit injected O_NONBLOCK.
9349    pub async fn handle_writev<G: Guest<Self>>(
9350        &self,
9351        guest: &mut G,
9352        call: syscalls::Writev,
9353    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9354        if self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?.is_some() {
9355            self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, call.fd(), true)?;
9356            let iovecs = read_iovecs(&guest.memory(), call.iov(), call.len())?;
9357            return self.writev_timer_slack(guest, call.fd(), iovecs, 0).await;
9358        }
9359
9360        self.fifo_polls_if_a_guest_holds_its_peer(guest, call.fd(), FifoPeer::Reader)
9361            .await;
9362        let (
9363            fd_type,
9364            physically_nonblocking,
9365            logically_nonblocking,
9366            open_file_id,
9367            resource,
9368            raw_ino,
9369        ) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
9370            (
9371                detfd.ty(),
9372                detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
9373                detfd.is_nonblocking(),
9374                detfd.open_file_id(),
9375                detfd.resource(),
9376                detfd.stat().map(|x| x.raw_inode()),
9377            )
9378        })?;
9379
9380        if let Some(resource) = resource {
9381            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::W);
9382            resource_request(guest, request).await;
9383        }
9384
9385        let result = if physically_nonblocking && fd_type == FdType::Pipe && !logically_nonblocking
9386        {
9387            self.execute_blocking_pipe_writev(guest, call, open_file_id)
9388                .await
9389        } else if physically_nonblocking
9390            && matches!(fd_type, FdType::Socket | FdType::Pipe | FdType::Eventfd)
9391        {
9392            self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await
9393        } else {
9394            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9395                .await
9396        };
9397
9398        if guest.config().virtualize_metadata && matches!(&result, Ok(written) if *written > 0) {
9399            let inode =
9400                raw_ino.expect("virtualized metadata requires stat data for every tracked fd");
9401            touch_file(guest, inode).await;
9402        }
9403
9404        resource_release_all(guest).await;
9405        result
9406    }
