9408    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
9409    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#794)
9410    /// A vectored read (`readv`, or `preadv2` at the current offset) of a
9411    /// signalfd, whose
9412    /// SIGCHLD records go through the child-exit ledger as `read`'s do
9413    /// (`reconcile_signalfd_extents`).
9414    ///
9415    /// Linux imports the `count` iovecs at `address` before it writes any record,
9416    /// and the records can overwrite the array itself, so the geometry is
9417    /// captured here, before the read, and used for the reconciliation and
9418    /// for the output observation (`observed`) alike (Codex re-check #6 of
9419    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4031). A read whose every
9420    /// record is dropped reads again, with the array's bytes put back first.
9421    /// An array the tracer cannot read is a proven kernel failure (EINVAL, or
9422    /// EFAULT with some byte outside every mapping: the kernel copies the whole
9423    /// array), forwarded unchanged; a wholly mapped one it cannot read, or one
9424    /// whose mappings cannot be listed, is refused by name, so no record is
9425    /// returned unreconciled.
9426    async fn vectored_signalfd_read<G: Guest<Self>, C>(
9427        &self,
9428        guest: &mut G,
9429        sysno: Sysno,
9430        call: C,
9431        address: usize,
9432        count: usize,
9433        observed: &mut Option<Vec<crate::io_buffers::BufferExtent>>,
9434    ) -> Result<i64, Error>
9435    where
9436        C: Into<Syscall> + Copy,
9437    {
9438        const IOVEC: usize = std::mem::size_of::<libc::iovec>();
9439        let fd = match call.into() {
9440            Syscall::Readv(call) => call.fd(),
9441            Syscall::Preadv2(call) => call.fd(),
9442            _ => -1,
9443        };
9444        // Linux passes the count on as an `unsigned int` (Codex re-check #7).
9445        let count = crate::io_buffers::linux_iovec_count(count as u64);
9446        if count > libc::UIO_MAXIOV as usize {
9447            return self
9448                .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9449                .await;
9450        }
9451        let mut raw = vec![0u8; count * IOVEC];
9452        if count > 0 {
9453            let read = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(address)
9454                .is_some_and(|at| guest.memory().read_exact(at, &mut raw).is_ok())
9455                || {
9456                    use std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;
9457                    std::fs::File::open(format!("/proc/{}/mem", guest.tid().as_raw()))
9458                        .and_then(|mem| mem.read_exact_at(&mut raw, address as u64))
9459                        .is_ok()
9460                };
9461            if !read {
9462                // A maps listing that cannot be read decides nothing: refuse.
9463                let maps = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{}/maps", guest.tid().as_raw()));
9464                if let Ok(maps) = &maps
9465                    && !signalfd_range_is_mapped(maps, address, raw.len())
9466                {
9467                    return self
9468                        .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9469                        .await;
9470                }
9471                tracing::error!(
9472                    "[detcore, dtid {}] {} of a signalfd with its iovec array at {:#x} is not \
9473                     supported: the memory is mapped, but Hermit cannot read it to reconcile \
9474                     the SIGCHLD records (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994)",
9475                    guest.thread_state().dettid,
9476                    sysno,
9477                    address,
9478                );
9479                return self
9480                    .refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, sysno, Errno::ENOSYS)
9481                    .await;
9482            }
9483        }
9484        let extents: Vec<(usize, usize)> = raw
9485            .chunks(IOVEC)
9486            .map(|iovec| {
9487                let word = |at: usize| {
9488                    usize::from_ne_bytes(iovec[at..at + 8].try_into().expect("eight bytes"))
9489                };
9490                (word(0), word(8))
9491            })
9492            .collect();
9493        // A vectored read of a signalfd covering a signal with an entry behind
9494        // its list's front would need one record per kernel read, each into
9495        // its own sub-extents (`read_signalfd_per_record`), which Detcore does
9496        // not do for a vector; refused by name rather than return records out
9497        // of Linux's order (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4262>).
9498        let total: usize = extents.iter().map(|(_, len)| *len).sum();
9499        if total >= 2 * crate::syscalls::signal::SIGNALFD_RECORD
9500            && self.signalfd_reads_per_record(guest, fd).await
9501        {
9502            tracing::error!(
9503                "[detcore, dtid {}] {} of a signalfd while a signal it covers has a POSIX timer's entry queued behind another is not supported: Linux returns them one by one in its dequeue order, which Detcore produces only for read (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4262)",
9504                guest.thread_state().dettid,
9505                sysno,
9506            );
9507            return self
9508                .refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, sysno, Errno::ENOSYS)
9509                .await;
9510        }
9511        loop {
9512            let before =
9513                crate::syscalls::signal::capture_signalfd_buffer(guest, &extents, usize::MAX);
9514            let result = self
9515                .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9516                .await;
9517            match result {
9518                Ok(read) if read > 0 => {
9519                    let Some(kept) = self
9520                        .reconcile_signalfd_extents(guest, &extents, read as usize, &before)
9521                        .await
9522                    else {
9523                        break self.refuse_unrestorable_signalfd_record(guest, sysno).await;
9524                    };
9525                    if self
9526                        .settle_faulted_signalfd_record(guest, fd, &extents, Some(read as usize))
9527                        .await
9528                    {
9529                        break self.refuse_faulted_signalfd_discard(guest, sysno).await;
9530                    }
9531                    if kept > 0 {
9532                        *observed = Some(
9533                            crate::syscalls::signal::signalfd_extent_pieces(&extents, kept)
9534                                .into_iter()
9535                                .map(|(addr, len)| crate::io_buffers::BufferExtent {
9536                                    addr: addr as u64,
9537                                    len: len as u64,
9538                                })
9539                                .collect(),
9540                        );
9541                        break Ok(kept as i64);
9542                    }
9543                    if let Some(at) = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(address)
9544                        && guest.memory().write_exact(at, &raw).is_err()
9545                    {
9546                        break Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
9547                    }
9548                }
9549                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EFAULT)) => {
9550                    if self
9551                        .settle_faulted_signalfd_record(guest, fd, &extents, None)
9552                        .await
9553                    {
9554                        break self.refuse_faulted_signalfd_discard(guest, sysno).await;
9555                    }
9556                    break Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
9557                }
9558                result => break result,
9559            }
9560        }
9561    }
9562
9563    /// Linux's signalfd read dequeues each signal before it copies its record
9564    /// out, and stops at the first copy that faults, so that signal is lost:
9565    /// the read fails with EFAULT if it was the first record, or returns the
9566    /// records before it. The SIGCHLD such a record may have held is settled
9567    /// with the child-exit ledger as a faulted `rt_sigtimedwait`'s is
9568    /// (`WaitFaulted`; the Codex re-check of
9569    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131 at 8692836e). `extents`
9570    /// are the read's buffers and `read` the bytes it returned, or `None` for
9571    /// an EFAULT.
9572    ///
9573    /// An EFAULT dequeued nothing when a buffer is not a user address at all
9574    /// (`access_ok`, checked before any dequeue). After a positive read, a
9575    /// record was lost only if the buffers had room for another and some
9576    /// byte of it is not writable; even then no signal may have been left to
9577    /// take, so the shared queue's pending bit decides that case.
9578    ///
9579    /// Returns whether a record may have been lost that way, and its copy may
9580    /// have been one Linux discarded when it was sent, which it would never
9581    /// have dequeued: the caller refuses the call by name
9582    /// (`refuse_faulted_signalfd_discard`), since the copy cannot be told
9583    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4293>).
9584    async fn settle_faulted_signalfd_record<G: Guest<Self>>(
9585        &self,
9586        guest: &mut G,
9587        fd: i32,
9588        extents: &[(usize, usize)],
9589        read: Option<usize>,
9590    ) -> bool {
9591        if !self.cfg.backend.reports_child_exit_publication || !guest.config().sequentialize_threads
9592        {
9593            return false;
9594        }
9595        match read {
9596            None => {
9597                let user_end = user_address_end();
9598                if extents.iter().any(|(address, len)| {
9599                    address.checked_add(*len).is_none_or(|end| end > user_end)
9600                }) {
9601                    return false;
9602                }
9603            }
9604            Some(read) => {
9605                let Some(next) = signalfd_next_record(extents, read) else {
9606                    return false;
9607                };
9608                let Ok(maps) =
9609                    std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{}/maps", guest.tid().as_raw()))
9610                else {
9611                    return false;
9612                };
9613                if next
9614                    .iter()
9615                    .all(|(address, len)| signalfd_range_is_writable(&maps, *address, *len))
9616                {
9617                    return false;
9618                }
9619            }
9620        }
9621        let mask = signalfd_sigmask(guest.pid().as_raw(), fd);
9622        let lost_a_discarded_copy = {
9623            use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalAnswer;
9624            use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalControl;
9625            use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::STANDARD_SIGNALS;
9626            matches!(
9627                crate::tool_global::discarded_signal(guest, DiscardedSignalControl::Bits).await,
9628                DiscardedSignalAnswer::Bits { thread, process }
9629                    if (thread | process) & mask.unwrap_or(!0) & STANDARD_SIGNALS != 0
9630            )
9631        };
9632        let sigchld = crate::syscalls::threads::kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
9633        if mask.is_some_and(|mask| mask & sigchld == 0) {
9634            return lost_a_discarded_copy;
9635        }
9636        let Ok(state) =
9637            crate::syscalls::threads::read_thread_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())
9638        else {
9639            return lost_a_discarded_copy;
9640        };
9641        // A failed read of a descriptor for SIGCHLD alone took a SIGCHLD.
9642        let shared_pending = if read.is_none() && mask == Some(sigchld) {
9643            false
9644        } else {
9645            state.shared_pending & sigchld != 0
9646        };
9647        crate::tool_global::child_exit_sigchld(
9648            guest,
9649            crate::scheduler::child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl::WaitFaulted {
9650                private_pending: state.thread_pending & sigchld != 0,
9651                shared_pending,
9652            },
9653        )
9654        .await;
9655        lost_a_discarded_copy
9656    }
9657
9658    /// Refuse by name a signalfd `sysno` whose copy-out faulted after a
9659    /// dequeue that may have taken a copy Linux discarded when it was sent
9660    /// (`settle_faulted_signalfd_record`): Linux would not have taken it, and
9661    /// which copy the lost record held cannot be told.
9662    async fn refuse_faulted_signalfd_discard<G: Guest<Self>>(
9663        &self,
9664        guest: &mut G,
9665        sysno: Sysno,
9666    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9667        tracing::error!(
9668            "[detcore, dtid {}] {} of a signalfd faulted copying out a record that may hold a \
9669             signal Linux discarded when it was sent, which Linux would never have dequeued; \
9670             Hermit cannot tell which copy was lost \
9671             (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4293)",
9672            guest.thread_state().dettid,
9673            sysno,
9674        );
9675        self.refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, sysno, Errno::ENOSYS)
9676            .await
9677    }
9678
9679    /// Refuse by name a signalfd `sysno` that read a record to drop (a copy
9680    /// Linux discarded at send, or a duplicate child-exit copy) whose bytes
9681    /// the capture before the read does not reach: more records than
9682    /// `SIGNALFD_CAPTURED` holds, which only real-time signals can make.
9683    /// Linux would leave those bytes as they were, and Hermit does not invent
9684    /// them (the Codex re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4351,
9685    /// P2-2).
9686    async fn refuse_unrestorable_signalfd_record<G: Guest<Self>>(
9687        &self,
9688        guest: &mut G,
9689        sysno: Sysno,
9690    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9691        tracing::error!(
9692            "[detcore, dtid {}] {} of a signalfd read a record Hermit drops, beyond the bytes \
9693             captured before the read, so it cannot leave the caller's buffer as Linux would \
9694             (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4293)",
9695            guest.thread_state().dettid,
9696            sysno,
9697        );
9698        self.refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, sysno, Errno::ENOSYS)
9699            .await
9700    }
9701
9702    /// SYS_readv system call: the vectored form of `read`.
9703    ///
9704    /// Mirrors [`Self::handle_writev`] for the read direction. Detcore adds
9705    /// open-file resource ordering and, for physically nonblocking pipe/socket
9706    /// fds, the nonblocking scheduler integration. Random devices use the shared
9707    /// canonical cursor; other descriptors retain their recorded kernel operation.
9708    pub async fn handle_readv<G: Guest<Self>>(
9709        &self,
9710        guest: &mut G,
9711        call: syscalls::Readv,
9712    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9713        self.handle_readv_with_output(guest, call, &mut None).await
9714    }
9715
9716    /// Import after the resource wait and retain that geometry through copyout.
9717    /// The shared-cursor closure is synchronous and takes no metadata locks.
9718    fn read_random_vectors<G: Guest<Self>>(
9719        &self,
9720        guest: &mut G,
9721        detfd: &DetFd,
9722        request: RandomVectoredRead,
9723        rng_output: &mut Option<Vec<crate::io_buffers::BufferExtent>>,
9724    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9725        require_random_device_read_access(detfd.status_flags())?;
9726        let iovecs = crate::iovecs::import_read_iovecs(
9727            &guest.memory(),
9728            request.address,
9729            request.count,
9730            || crate::iovecs::UserAddressLimit::from_query(guest.user_address_limit()),
9731        )?;
9732        let total = iovecs.iter().map(|iov| iov.len).sum();
9733        validate_random_vector_read(request.offset, total, request.flags)?;
9734        let stream = detfd.random_device_stream();
9735        let written = if let Some(offset) = request.offset {
9736            self.fill_random_device_iovecs(guest, stream, &iovecs, offset)?
9737        } else {
9738            detfd.with_random_device_stream(|offset| {
9739                self.fill_random_device_iovecs(guest, stream, &iovecs, offset)
9740            })?
9741        };
9742        if written > 0 && self.cfg.detlog_io_buffers && crate::detlog_observed!() {
9743            *rng_output = Some(crate::io_buffers::rng_readv_extents(&iovecs, written)?);
9744        }
9745        Ok(written as i64)
9746    }
9747
9748    pub(crate) async fn handle_readv_with_output<G: Guest<Self>>(
9749        &self,
9750        guest: &mut G,
9751        call: syscalls::Readv,
9752        rng_output: &mut Option<Vec<crate::io_buffers::BufferExtent>>,
9753    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9754        if self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?.is_some() {
9755            self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, call.fd(), false)?;
9756            let iovecs = read_iovecs(&guest.memory(), call.iov(), call.len())?;
9757            return self
9758                .readv_timer_slack(guest, call.fd(), iovecs, None, 0)
9759                .await;
9760        }
9761        let files = self.rendered_files(guest);
9762        if guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
9763            detfd.procfs_renderable_path(files).is_some()
9764        })? {
9765            let address = call.iov().map_or(0, |address| address.as_raw());
9766            return self
9767                .readv_rendered_procfs(guest, call.fd(), address, call.len(), None, 0)
9768                .await;
9769        }
9770
9771        let is_procfs = guest
9772            .thread_state()
9773            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_position().is_some())?;
9774        if is_procfs {
9775            return Err(Errno::ENOSYS.into());
9776        }
9777
9778        self.fifo_polls_if_a_guest_holds_its_peer(guest, call.fd(), FifoPeer::Writer)
9779            .await;
9780        let (fd_type, physically_nonblocking, resource, detfd) =
9781            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
9782                (
9783                    detfd.ty(),
9784                    detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
9785                    detfd.resource(),
9786                    detfd.clone(),
9787                )
9788            })?;
9789
9790        if let Some(resource) = resource {
9791            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::R);
9792            resource_request(guest, request).await;
9793        }
9794
9795        let res = if fd_type == FdType::Rng {
9796            self.read_random_vectors(
9797                guest,
9798                &detfd,
9799                RandomVectoredRead {
9800                    address: call.iov().map_or(0, |addr| addr.as_raw()),
9801                    count: call.len(),
9802                    offset: None,
9803                    flags: 0,
9804                },
9805                rng_output,
9806            )
9807        } else if detfd.inherited_external_read().is_some() {
9808            // The same one-kernel-read rule as scalar input: preserve the
9809            // kernel's iovec/short-read/error semantics and announce blocking.
9810            self.record_or_replay_blocking(guest, call.into()).await
9811        } else if fd_type == FdType::Timerfd && crate::syscalls::timerfd::enabled(guest) {
9812            // As `read` of a timerfd on virtual time: publish its expirations,
9813            // retry a logically blocking read in turns, and return the
9814            // virtual count (`crate::syscalls::timerfd`).
9815            crate::syscalls::timerfd::publish_expired(guest).await;
9816            let result = self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
9817            crate::syscalls::timerfd::finish_readv(guest, call.fd(), call.iov(), call.len(), result)
9818        } else if physically_nonblocking
9819            && matches!(fd_type, FdType::Socket | FdType::Pipe | FdType::Eventfd)
9820        {
9821            self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await
9822        } else if fd_type == FdType::Signalfd && self.cfg.backend.reports_child_exit_publication {
9823            // The SIGCHLD records a vectored read scatters go through the
9824            // child-exit ledger as `read`'s do (`reconcile_signalfd_extents`).
9825            self.vectored_signalfd_read(
9826                guest,
9827                Sysno::readv,
9828                call,
9829                call.iov().map_or(0, |iov| iov.as_raw()),
9830                call.len(),
9831                rng_output,
9832            )
9833            .await
9834        } else if fd_type == FdType::Inotify {
9835            let destination = crate::syscalls::inotify::Destination::iovecs(
9836                &guest.memory(),
9837                call.iov().map_or(0, |iov| iov.as_raw()),
9838                call.len(),
9839            );
9840            let queued = crate::syscalls::inotify::queued_before(guest, call.fd(), call).await;
9841            let result = self
9842                .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9843                .await;
9844            crate::syscalls::inotify::finish(
9845                guest,
9846                Sysno::readv,
9847                call.fd(),
9848                destination,
9849                queued,
9850                result,
9851            )
9852            .await
9853        } else {
9854            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9855                .await
9856        };
9857
9858        // O2: a signalfd read (even one that faulted copying out a record
9859        // it had already dequeued) may have taken the process's ITIMER_REAL
9860        // copy (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139).
9861        if fd_type == FdType::Signalfd {
9862            crate::tool_global::reconcile_alarm(guest).await;
9863        }
9864        resource_release_all(guest).await;
9865        res
9866    }

9870    /// SYS_preadv system call: the vectored form of `pread64`.
9871    ///
9872    /// RNG reads use the canonical stream at the explicit offset without
9873    /// advancing its shared cursor. Other files retain their kernel operation.
9874    pub async fn handle_preadv<G: Guest<Self>>(
9875        &self,
9876        guest: &mut G,

9882    pub(crate) async fn handle_preadv_with_output<G: Guest<Self>>(
9883        &self,
9884        guest: &mut G,
9885        call: syscalls::Preadv,
9886        rng_output: &mut Option<Vec<crate::io_buffers::BufferExtent>>,
9887    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9888        // Linux rejects negative offsets before descriptor lookup or import.
9889        let offset = vectored_offset(call.pos_l(), call.pos_h());
9890        if offset < 0 {
9891            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
9892        }
9893        if self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?.is_some() {
9894            self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, call.fd(), false)?;
9895            let iovecs = read_iovecs(&guest.memory(), call.iov(), call.iov_len())?;
9896            return self
9897                .readv_timer_slack(guest, call.fd(), iovecs, Some(offset), 0)
9898                .await;
9899        }
9900        let files = self.rendered_files(guest);
9901        if guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
9902            detfd.procfs_renderable_path(files).is_some()
9903        })? {
9904            let address = call.iov().map_or(0, |address| address.as_raw());
9905            return self
9906                .readv_rendered_procfs(guest, call.fd(), address, call.iov_len(), Some(offset), 0)
9907                .await;
9908        }
9909
9910        let is_procfs = guest
9911            .thread_state()
9912            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_position().is_some())?;
9913        if is_procfs {
9914            return Err(Errno::ENOSYS.into());
9915        }
9916
9917        let detfd = guest
9918            .thread_state()
9919            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.clone())?;
9920
9921        if let Some(resource) = detfd.resource() {
9922            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::R);
9923            resource_request(guest, request).await;
9924        }
9925
9926        let res = if detfd.ty() == FdType::Rng {
9927            self.read_random_vectors(
9928                guest,
9929                &detfd,
9930                RandomVectoredRead {
9931                    address: call.iov().map_or(0, |addr| addr.as_raw()),
9932                    count: call.iov_len(),
9933                    offset: Some(offset as u64),
9934                    flags: 0,
9935                },
9936                rng_output,
9937            )
9938        } else {
9939            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
9940                .await
9941        };
9942        resource_release_all(guest).await;
9943        res
9944    }

9952        guest: &mut G,

9959    pub(crate) async fn handle_preadv2_with_output<G: Guest<Self>>(
9960        &self,
9961        guest: &mut G,
9962        call: syscalls::Preadv2,
9963        rng_output: &mut Option<Vec<crate::io_buffers::BufferExtent>>,
9964    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
9965        let offset = vectored_offset(call.pos_l(), call.pos_h());
9966        if offset < -1 {
9967            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
9968        }
9969        if self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?.is_some() {
9970            self.require_timer_slack_access(guest, call.fd(), false)?;
9971            let count = usize::try_from(call.iov_len()).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
9972            let iovecs = read_iovecs(&guest.memory(), call.iov(), count)?;
9973            return if offset == -1 {
9974                self.readv_timer_slack(guest, call.fd(), iovecs, None, call.flags())
9975                    .await
9976            } else {
9977                self.readv_timer_slack(guest, call.fd(), iovecs, Some(offset), call.flags())
9978                    .await
9979            };
9980        }
9981        let files = self.rendered_files(guest);
9982        if guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
9983            detfd.procfs_renderable_path(files).is_some()
9984        })? {
9985            let address = call.iov().map_or(0, |address| address.as_raw());
9986            let offset = (offset != -1).then_some(offset);
9987            return self
9988                .readv_rendered_procfs(
9989                    guest,
9990                    call.fd(),
9991                    address,
9992                    call.iov_len() as usize,
9993                    offset,
9994                    call.flags(),
9995                )
9996                .await;
9997        }
9998
9999        let is_procfs = guest
10000            .thread_state()
10001            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_position().is_some())?;
10002        if is_procfs {
10003            return Err(Errno::ENOSYS.into());
10004        }
10005
10006        // At the current position (-1) and with no flags, `preadv2` is
10007        // `readv` (`preadv2` calls `do_readv`). On a descriptor whose blocking
10008        // read Detcore runs in turns it is run as one, so it waits as `readv`
10009        // does: the single kernel attempt below fails with EAGAIN on the
10010        // descriptor Detcore made physically nonblocking
10011        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4822).
10012        if offset == -1 && call.flags() == 0 && self.waits_in_turns(guest, call.fd()) {
10013            let readv = syscalls::Readv::new()
10014                .with_fd(call.fd())
10015                .with_iov(call.iov())
10016                .with_len(call.iov_len() as usize);
10017            return self
10018                .handle_readv_with_output(guest, readv, rng_output)
10019                .await;
10020        }
10021
10022        let detfd = guest
10023            .thread_state()
10024            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.clone())?;
10025
10026        if let Some(resource) = detfd.resource() {
10027            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::R);
10028            resource_request(guest, request).await;
10029        }
10030
10031        let res = if detfd.ty() == FdType::Rng {
10032            self.read_random_vectors(
10033                guest,
10034                &detfd,
10035                RandomVectoredRead {
10036                    address: call.iov().map_or(0, |addr| addr.as_raw()),
10037                    count: call.iov_len() as usize,
10038                    offset: (offset != -1).then_some(offset as u64),
10039                    flags: call.flags(),
10040                },
10041                rng_output,
10042            )
10043        } else if detfd.ty() == FdType::Signalfd
10044            && offset == -1
10045            && self.cfg.backend.reports_child_exit_publication
10046        {
10047            // At the current offset (-1) a signalfd reads as `readv` does,
10048            // and its records go through the child-exit ledger
10049            // (`reconcile_signalfd_extents`). At any other offset, as with
10050            // `preadv`, the kernel fails with ESPIPE before it imports the
10051            // array, so that call goes to it unchanged below.
10052            self.vectored_signalfd_read(
10053                guest,
10054                Sysno::preadv2,
10055                call,
10056                call.iov().map_or(0, |iov| iov.as_raw()),
10057                usize::try_from(call.iov_len()).unwrap_or(0),
10058                rng_output,
10059            )
10060            .await
10061        } else if detfd.ty() == FdType::Inotify && offset == -1 {
10062            // At the current offset (-1) an inotify descriptor reads as
10063            // `readv` does (`do_preadv2` calls `do_readv`), so its rename
10064            // cookies are renumbered as `readv`'s are. At any other offset
10065            // the kernel fails with ESPIPE (an anonymous inode has no
10066            // FMODE_PREAD), so that call goes to it unchanged below.
10067            let destination = crate::syscalls::inotify::Destination::iovecs(
10068                &guest.memory(),
10069                call.iov().map_or(0, |iov| iov.as_raw()),
10070                call.iov_len() as usize,
10071            );
10072            let queued = crate::syscalls::inotify::queued_before(guest, call.fd(), call).await;
10073            let result = self
10074                .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
10075                .await;
10076            crate::syscalls::inotify::finish(
10077                guest,
10078                Sysno::preadv2,
10079                call.fd(),
10080                destination,
10081                queued,
10082                result,
10083            )
10084            .await
10085        } else {
10086            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
10087                .await
10088        };
10089        // O2: a signalfd read (even one that faulted copying out a record
10090        // it had already dequeued) may have taken the process's ITIMER_REAL
10091        // copy (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139).
10092        if detfd.ty() == FdType::Signalfd {
10093            crate::tool_global::reconcile_alarm(guest).await;
10094        }
10095        resource_release_all(guest).await;
10096        res
10097    }

10101    /// SYS_pwritev system call: the vectored form of `pwrite64`.
10102    ///
10103    /// Positioned writes target seekable files and do not block, so this mirrors
10104    /// [`Self::handle_pwrite64`]'s ordering, records/replays the single kernel
10105    /// operation, and bumps the virtual mtime on a successful write.
10106    pub async fn handle_pwritev<G: Guest<Self>>(
10107        &self,
10108        guest: &mut G,
10109        call: syscalls::Pwritev,
10110    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
10111        if self.timer_slack_binding(guest, call.fd())?.is_some() {
10112            let offset = vectored_offset(call.pos_l(), call.pos_h());
10113            return if offset < 0 {
10114                Err(Errno::EINVAL.into())
10115            } else {
10116                Err(Errno::ESPIPE.into())
10117            };
10118        }
10119
10120        let (resource, raw_ino) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
10121            (detfd.resource(), detfd.stat().map(|stat| stat.raw_inode()))
10122        })?;
10123        // The fd's cached `DetStat` carries the HOST inode (`DetStat` is built
10124        // straight from `fstat`/`statx`), so it must be determinized before it
10125        // can name a guest-visible resource. Passing it through directly used
10126        // to type-check only because `DetInode` was an alias for `RawInode`.
10127        let resource = match resource {
10128            Some(resource) => Some(resource),
10129            None => match raw_ino {
10130                Some(raw_ino) => Some(ResourceID::FileContents(
10131                    determinize_inode(guest, raw_ino).await.0,
10132                )),
10133                None => None,
10134            },
10135        };
10136
10137        if let Some(resource) = resource {
10138            let request = guest.thread_state().mk_request(resource, Permission::W);
10139            resource_request(guest, request).await;
10140        }
10141
10142        let result = self
10143            .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
10144            .await;
10145
10146        if guest.config().virtualize_metadata && matches!(&result, Ok(written) if *written > 0) {
10147            let inode = raw_ino.expect("virtualized metadata requires stat data for tracked fds");
10148            touch_file(guest, inode).await;
10149        }
10150
10151        resource_release_all(guest).await;
10152        result
10153    }

10155    /// Whether a blocking transfer on `fd` waits in Detcore's turns, or may
10156    /// once the `readv` and `writev` handlers look at it: an internal pipe,
10157    /// socket or eventfd Detcore made physically nonblocking, whose `readv`
10158    /// and `writev` it polls (`execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall`,
10159    /// `execute_blocking_pipe_writev`); a blocking FIFO opened by path, which
10160    /// those handlers poll as a pipe once they find a guest at its other end
10161    /// (`fifo_polls_if_a_guest_holds_its_peer`); or a timerfd on virtual time.
10162    /// A descriptor Detcore cannot look up is left to the kernel.
10163    fn waits_in_turns<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &G, fd: RawFd) -> bool {
10164        guest
10165            .thread_state()
10166            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
10167                (detfd.physically_nonblocking()
10168                    && matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Socket | FdType::Pipe | FdType::Eventfd))
10169                    || (detfd.fifo_awaiting_guest_peer() && !detfd.is_nonblocking())
10170                    || (detfd.ty() == FdType::Timerfd && crate::syscalls::timerfd::enabled(guest))
10171            })
10172            .unwrap_or(false)
10173    }

10251    /// SYS_mmap system call.
10252    pub async fn handle_mmap<G: Guest<Self>>(
10253        &self,
10254        guest: &mut G,
10255        call: syscalls::Mmap,
10256    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
10257        enum SharedBacking {
10258            Anonymous,
10259            File {
10260                object: SharedMemoryObjectId,
10261                offset: u64,
10262            },
10263        }
10264
10265        let backing = if call.flags().contains(MapFlags::MAP_SHARED) {
10266            if call.fd() == -1 {
10267                Some(SharedBacking::Anonymous)
10268            } else {
10269                let offset = u64::try_from(call.offset()).map_err(|_| Errno::EINVAL)?;
10270                guest
10271                    .thread_state()
10272                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |fd| {
10273                        let object = fd.stat().map_or_else(
10274                            || SharedMemoryObjectId::OpenFile {
10275                                id: fd.open_file_id(),
10276                            },
10277                            |stat| SharedMemoryObjectId::File {
10278                                device: stat.dev,
10279                                inode: stat.inode,
10280                            },
10281                        );
10282                        SharedBacking::File { object, offset }
10283                    })
10284                    .ok()
10285            }
10286        } else {
10287            None
10288        };
10289        let len = call.len();
10290        let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
10291        let start = usize::try_from(result).expect("a successful mmap must return an address");
10292
10293        guest.thread_state().unmap_memory(start, len);
10294        match backing {
10295            Some(SharedBacking::Anonymous) => {
10296                guest.thread_state().map_shared_anonymous(start, len);
10297            }
10298            Some(SharedBacking::File { object, offset }) => {
10299                guest
10300                    .thread_state()
10301                    .map_shared_object(start, len, object, offset);
10302            }
10303            None => {}
10304        }
10305        Ok(result)
10306    }

10308    /// SYS_munmap system call.
10309    pub async fn handle_munmap<G: Guest<Self>>(
10310        &self,
10311        guest: &mut G,
10312        call: syscalls::Munmap,
10313    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
10314        let start = call.addr().map(Addr::as_raw).unwrap_or(0);
10315        let len = call.len();
10316        let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
10317        guest.thread_state().unmap_memory(start, len);
10318        Ok(result)
10319    }

10321    /// SYS_mremap system call.
10322    pub async fn handle_mremap<G: Guest<Self>>(
10323        &self,
10324        guest: &mut G,
10325        call: syscalls::Mremap,
10326    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
10327        let old_start = call.addr().map(AddrMut::as_raw).unwrap_or(0);
10328        let old_len = call.old_len();
10329        let new_len = call.new_len();
10330        // MREMAP_DONTUNMAP (Linux 5.7): the old mapping stays in place.
10331        let keep_source = call.flags() & 4 != 0;
10332        let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
10333        let new_start =
10334            usize::try_from(result).expect("a successful mremap must return an address");
10335        guest
10336            .thread_state()
10337            .remap_memory(old_start, old_len, new_start, new_len, keep_source);
10338        Ok(result)
10339    }

10341    /// What Detcore learns of the file `stat` describes, which the guest
10342    /// named as `target`, as a procfs entry: its path within procfs when its
10343    /// device is a procfs mount in the guest's mount table (see
10344    /// [`procfs_inode`]). A failure to tell or to name a procfs entry records
10345    /// a determinism loss, as the entry's number then depends on whether the
10346    /// host rebuilt it.
10347    ///
10348    /// Never under record and replay, which reproduces the recorded host
10349    /// numbers instead: Replayer's descriptor is a placeholder, and its guest
10350    /// has no `/proc`. Nor when the guest's thread IDs do not name host tasks
10351    /// (see [`procfs_inode::guest_tids_name_host_tasks`]), as there is then no
10352    /// `/proc/<tid>` to read.
10353    ///
10354    /// Nor without sequentialized threads (see [`Self::name_procfs_entry`]).
10355    ///
10356    /// Naming a path injects an `openat` and a `close` into the guest (see
10357    /// [`Self::with_object_link`]), and Detcore trusts the host kernel to run
10358    /// them as Linux defines them. A
10359    /// seccomp filter the guest inherited from whatever started it (which
10360    /// `Config::inherited_seccomp` records) may refuse them with an error,
10361    /// such as `EPERM`, and Detcore then names nothing and records a
10362    /// determinism loss. A filter, or a user-space supervisor
10363    /// (`SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF`), that returns a result without running the
10364    /// call stands in for the kernel, which Detcore does not support.
10365    ///
10366    /// The `O_PATH` descriptor that names a path is open in the guest for one
10367    /// turn. A call the scheduler runs in the background meanwhile, such as
10368    /// an `accept` on a descriptor Detcore does not track, can allocate a
10369    /// descriptor in the same table at a moment the host chooses, and so take
10370    /// another number than without the stat, as it can beside any other
10371    /// descriptor allocation (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3988).
10372    ///
10373    /// The guest's `errno` is what it was: under SaBRe, Detcore shares libc,
10374    /// and so `errno`, with the guest thread it handles (see
10375    /// [`procfs_inode::preserving_errno`]).
10376    async fn procfs_entry<G: Guest<Self>>(
10377        guest: &mut G,
10378        stat: &DetStat,
10379        target: StatTarget<'_>,
10380    ) -> ProcfsEntry {
10381        procfs_inode::preserving_errno(Self::name_procfs_entry(guest, stat, target)).await
10382    }
10383
10384    /// Maps/Smaps ownership needs the actual opened object even where scheduler
10385    /// IDs are virtual. Use the existing same-view task directory capability;
10386    /// never pass a virtual TID to the host-only procfs naming path.
10387    async fn maps_descriptor_entry<G: Guest<Self>>(
10388        &self,
10389        guest: &G,
10390        stat: &DetStat,
10391        fd: RawFd,
10392    ) -> ProcfsEntry {
10393        procfs_inode::preserving_errno(async {
10394            if guest.config().recordreplay_modes || !guest.config().sequentialize_threads {
10395                return ProcfsEntry::Unknown;
10396            }
10397            let Some(task) = self.guest_task_directory(guest) else {
10398                return ProcfsEntry::Unknown;
10399            };
10400            match procfs_inode::descriptor_procfs_path(&task, fd, stat.dev, stat.inode) {
10401                Ok(Some(within)) => ProcfsEntry::At(within),
10402                Ok(None) => ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs,
10403                Err(_) => ProcfsEntry::Unknown,
10404            }
10405        })
10406        .await
10407    }
10408
10409    async fn maps_guest_target<G: Guest<Self>>(
10410        &self,
10411        guest: &mut G,
10412        actual: &Path,
10413    ) -> Option<crate::procfs::BoundTask> {
10414        let numbers = if Self::translates_procfs_numbers(guest) {
10415            let ids = crate::procfs::ids::named_ids(actual);
10416            Some(Self::guest_procfs_numbers(guest, &ids).await?)
10417        } else {
10418            None
10419        };
10420        let (pid, tid) = self.procfs_caller_ids(guest)?;
10421        Self::maps_target_with_numbers(actual, numbers.as_ref(), pid, tid)
10422    }
10423
10424    /// Preserve an authenticated spelling when its complete numeric mapping
10425    /// is the identity. Missing target components cannot authorize a binding.
10426    fn maps_target_with_numbers(
10427        actual: &Path,
10428        numbers: Option<&BTreeMap<i32, i32>>,
10429        pid: i32,
10430        tid: i32,
10431    ) -> Option<crate::procfs::BoundTask> {
10432        let translated;
10433        let actual = if let Some(numbers) = numbers {
10434            if crate::procfs::ids::named_ids(actual)
10435                .iter()
10436                .any(|id| !numbers.contains_key(id))
10437            {
10438                return None;
10439            }
10440            translated = crate::procfs::ids::translate(actual, |id| numbers.get(&id).copied());
10441            translated.as_deref().unwrap_or(actual)
10442        } else {
10443            actual
10444        };
10445        crate::procfs::maps_task_at(actual, pid, tid)
10446    }
10447
10448    /// [`Self::procfs_entry`], which restores the guest's `errno` afterwards.
10449    ///
10450    /// Without sequentialized threads, another guest thread can change what a
10451    /// descriptor, the working directory or a path leads to between any two
10452    /// of the steps that name an entry, and under SaBRe it shares the
10453    /// descriptor table Detcore reads the mount table through. So Detcore
10454    /// names nothing then, before any of those steps, and records a
10455    /// determinism loss for any file that may be on procfs (see
10456    /// [`procfs_inode::may_be_procfs`]), devpts files among them.
10457    async fn name_procfs_entry<G: Guest<Self>>(
10458        guest: &mut G,
10459        stat: &DetStat,
10460        target: StatTarget<'_>,
10461    ) -> ProcfsEntry {
10462        if guest.config().recordreplay_modes
10463            || !procfs_inode::guest_tids_name_host_tasks(
10464                &guest.config().backend,
10465                guest.thread_state().physical_tid,
10466            )
10467            || !procfs_inode::may_be_procfs(stat.dev, stat.blksize)
10468        {
10469            return ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs;
10470        }
10471        if !guest.config().sequentialize_threads {
10472            Self::record_procfs_loss(
10473                guest,
10474                "the guest's threads are not sequentialized, so Detcore does not name procfs files"
10475                    .into(),
10476            )
10477            .await;
10478            return ProcfsEntry::Unknown;
10479        }
10480        let tid = guest.tid().as_raw();
10481        let mounts = match procfs_inode::procfs_mounts(tid, stat.dev, false) {
10482            Ok(Some(mounts)) => mounts,
10483            // No procfs mount in the guest's mount table is on the device, but
10484            // a procfs file can be, opened outside the guest's mounts: one
10485            // inherited from Hermit's own `/proc`, or received through
10486            // SCM_RIGHTS. It has no path within the guest's procfs, so it goes
10487            // unnamed. Its filesystem type tells.
10488            Ok(None) => {
10489                let on_procfs = Self::with_object_link(guest, target, |link| {
10490                    procfs_inode::is_on_procfs(link, stat.dev, stat.inode)
10491                })
10492                .await;
10493                return match on_procfs {
10494                    Ok(false) => ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs,
10495                    Ok(true) => {
10496                        Self::record_procfs_loss(
10497                            guest,
10498                            "a procfs file outside the guest's procfs mounts".into(),
10499                        )
10500                        .await;
10501                        ProcfsEntry::Unnamed
10502                    }
10503                    Err(reason) => {
10504                        Self::record_procfs_loss(guest, reason).await;
10505                        ProcfsEntry::Unknown
10506                    }
10507                };
10508            }
10509            Err(error) => {
10510                Self::record_procfs_loss(
10511                    guest,
10512                    format!(
10513                        "cannot read the guest's mount table: {}",
10514                        crate::util::describe_io_error(&error)
10515                    ),
10516                )
10517                .await;
10518                return ProcfsEntry::Unknown;
10519            }
10520        };
10521        let (canonical, mount_id) = match Self::procfs_canonical_path(guest, stat, target).await {
10522            Ok(found) => found,
10523            Err(reason) => {
10524                Self::record_procfs_loss(guest, reason).await;
10525                return ProcfsEntry::Unnamed;
10526            }
10527        };
10528        let reread = || procfs_inode::procfs_mounts(tid, stat.dev, true);
10529        match procfs_inode::path_within(
10530            &mounts,
10531            mount_id,
10532            &canonical,
10533            reread,
10534            procfs_inode::mount_root,
10535        ) {
10536            Ok(within) => ProcfsEntry::At(within),
10537            // The guest reached the file through a mount that its mount
10538            // table, read again, does not list at a mount point where Detcore
10539            // finds the mount: one outside the guest's root, or one whose
10540            // mount point reads in another frame than the file's path.
10541            Err(reason) => {
10542                Self::record_procfs_loss(guest, reason).await;
10543                ProcfsEntry::Unnamed
10544            }
10545        }
10546    }
10547
10548    /// The canonical path of the procfs file `stat` describes, which the
10549    /// guest named as `target`, from a magic link to it (see
10550    /// [`Self::with_object_link`]), if that is still the file `stat`
10551    /// describes, and the ID of the mount it was reached through. An entry
10552    /// the host rebuilt between the guest's stat and an `O_PATH` open, a
10553    /// window of one injected call, is not, and goes unnamed.
10554    async fn procfs_canonical_path<G: Guest<Self>>(
10555        guest: &mut G,
10556        stat: &DetStat,
10557        target: StatTarget<'_>,
10558    ) -> Result<(PathBuf, u64), String> {
10559        Self::with_object_link(guest, target, |link| {
10560            procfs_inode::inspect_link(link, stat.dev, stat.inode)
10561        })
10562        .await
10563    }
10564
10565    /// Run `inspect` on a magic link to the file the guest named as
10566    /// `target`: that of the descriptor or working directory in the guest
10567    /// thread's `/proc/<tid>`. For a path, Detcore opens an `O_PATH`
10568    /// descriptor in the guest with the guest's own path, directory and
10569    /// flags, which resolves `self` and `thread-self` to the guest, and
10570    /// closes it again (see [`Self::open_object_descriptor`] and
10571    /// [`Self::close_object_descriptor`]). An error is the reason Detcore
10572    /// learned nothing, or that the guest's descriptors may have changed.
10573    ///
10574    /// It runs only with sequentialized threads (see
10575    /// [`Self::name_procfs_entry`]). Only then do the open, the look at the
10576    /// link and the close run in one turn, and does the guest's descriptor or
10577    /// working directory lead to one file throughout; otherwise another guest
10578    /// thread can close the descriptor Detcore opened and take its number for
10579    /// one of its own in between, which Detcore would then read, and close.
10580    async fn with_object_link<G: Guest<Self>, R>(
10581        guest: &mut G,
10582        target: StatTarget<'_>,
10583        inspect: impl FnOnce(&Path) -> Result<R, String>,
10584    ) -> Result<R, String> {
10585        let tid = guest.tid().as_raw();
10586        match target {
10587            StatTarget::Descriptor(fd) => inspect(Path::new(&format!("/proc/{tid}/fd/{fd}"))),
10588            StatTarget::Cwd => inspect(Path::new(&format!("/proc/{tid}/cwd"))),
10589            StatTarget::Overwritten => Err("the call's result overwrote the guest's path".into()),
10590            StatTarget::Path {
10591                dirfd,
10592                path,
10593                follow,
10594            } => {
10595                let mut flags = OFlag::O_PATH | OFlag::O_CLOEXEC;
10596                if !follow {
10597                    flags |= OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW;
10598                }
10599                let open = syscalls::Openat::new()
10600                    .with_dirfd(dirfd)
10601                    .with_path(path)
10602                    .with_flags(flags);
10603                let fd = Self::open_object_descriptor(guest, open).await?;
10604                let found = inspect(Path::new(&format!("/proc/{tid}/fd/{fd}")));
10605                Self::close_object_descriptor(guest, fd).await?;
10606                found
10607            }
10608        }
10609    }
10610
10611    /// Open the `O_PATH` descriptor `open` describes in the guest. An open
10612    /// that opened no descriptor and reported a restart or `EINTR` (see
10613    /// [`procfs_inode::read_open`]) is tried again, but only
10614    /// `OBJECT_DESCRIPTOR_ATTEMPTS` times, as a seccomp filter the guest
10615    /// inherited can return a restart every time without running the call.
10616    async fn open_object_descriptor<G: Guest<Self>>(
10617        guest: &mut G,
10618        open: syscalls::Openat,
10619    ) -> Result<RawFd, String> {
10620        let mut last = Errno::EINTR.to_string();
10621        for _ in 0..OBJECT_DESCRIPTOR_ATTEMPTS {
10622            // The guest's path, respelled for this injection where it leads
10623            // below a descriptor directory, as the guest's own call is
10624            // (`Self::inject_translated`).
10625            match procfs_inode::read_open(Self::inject_translated(guest, Syscall::from(open)).await)
10626            {
10627                procfs_inode::Injected::Ran(fd) => return Ok(fd),
10628                procfs_inode::Injected::NotRun(reported) => last = reported,
10629                procfs_inode::Injected::Failed(reason) => return Err(reason),
10630            }
10631        }
10632        Err(format!(
10633            "cannot open the guest's path again: {last} in each of {OBJECT_DESCRIPTOR_ATTEMPTS} attempts"
10634        ))
10635    }
10636
10637    /// Close the `O_PATH` descriptor `fd` that Detcore opened in the guest. A
10638    /// close that did not run (see [`procfs_inode::read_close`]) is tried
10639    /// again, but only `OBJECT_DESCRIPTOR_ATTEMPTS` times. One that failed
10640    /// leaves the descriptor open, where it changes the numbers the guest's
10641    /// later descriptors take, so it is an error.
10642    async fn close_object_descriptor<G: Guest<Self>>(
10643        guest: &mut G,
10644        fd: RawFd,
10645    ) -> Result<(), String> {
10646        let close = syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd);
10647        for _ in 0..OBJECT_DESCRIPTOR_ATTEMPTS {
10648            match procfs_inode::read_close(guest.inject(close).await) {
10649                procfs_inode::Injected::Ran(()) => return Ok(()),
10650                procfs_inode::Injected::NotRun(_) => {}
10651                procfs_inode::Injected::Failed(reason) => return Err(reason),
10652            }
10653        }
10654        Err(format!(
10655            "close of the guest's O_PATH descriptor did not run in {OBJECT_DESCRIPTOR_ATTEMPTS} attempts"
10656        ))
10657    }
10658
10659    /// Records the determinism loss of a procfs entry Detcore could not name,
10660    /// once per process, through the global tool, whose process is the one
10661    /// whose losses verification reads under every backend.
10662    async fn record_procfs_loss<G: Guest<Self>>(guest: &mut G, reason: String) {
10663        static RECORDED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
10664        if !RECORDED.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
10665            report_determinism_loss(guest, format!("procfs inode numbers: {reason}")).await;
10666        }
10667    }
10668
10669    // Determinize stat by doing:
10670    //   - using virtual inode instead of real inodes. The virtual inodes
10671    //     increase monolitically and won't be re-used (like ext4)
10672    //   - use logical modtime which could be used by program like GNU make
10673    //     to determine file changes. A file first seen with a canonical host
10674    //     mtime (`CANONICAL_FILE_MTIME_SECONDS`, e.g. the Nix store's 1) keeps
10675    //     it; any other first-seen file reports the epoch.
10676    //   - atime, ctime and btime always report the epoch: the kernel sets ctime
10677    //     and btime itself, so even for a Nix store file they are real
10678    //     timestamps, and Hermit keeps no per-file atime.
10679    async fn determinize_stat<G, S>(
10680        &self,
10681        guest: &mut G,
10682        stat: S,
10683        inode_override: Option<DetInode>,
10684        procfs: ProcfsEntry,
10685    ) -> Result<DetStat, Error>
10686    where
10687        G: Guest<Self>,
10688        S: Into<DetStat>,
10689    {
10690        // The two fields this reads, copied: cloning the whole Config here
10691        // copied its mount-table lists, one allocation per container mount, on
10692        // every stat-family call.
10693        let recordreplay_modes = guest.config().recordreplay_modes;
10694        let epoch = guest.config().epoch;
10695
10696        let mut stat: DetStat = stat.into();
10697        // Detcore's placeholder, however the guest reached it: the rendered
10698        // file it stands in for.
10699        if inode_override.is_none()
10700            && !recordreplay_modes
10701            && let Some(path) = rendered_procfs::placeholder_identity(stat.dev, stat.inode)
10702        {
10703            return self.rendered_metadata(guest, path).await;
10704        }
10705        let (d_ino, global_mtime) = match inode_override {
10706            // The container's stdio streams have fixed inodes and always
10707            // report the epoch: whatever backs them on the host (a pipe, a
10708            // terminal, a redirected file) is not part of the guest's view.
10709            Some(inode) => {
10710                let nanos = epoch
10711                    .timestamp_nanos_opt()
10712                    .expect("epoch cannot be represented in nanoseconds")
10713                    as u64;
10714                (inode, LogicalTime::from_nanos(nanos))
10715            }
10716            None => {
10717                // statx fills stx_mtime only when it reports STATX_MTIME.
10718                let observed = if stat.mask.contains(StatxMask::STATX_MTIME) {
10719                    ObservedMtime::from_host_mtime(stat.mtime.tv_sec, stat.mtime.tv_nsec)
10720                } else {
10721                    ObservedMtime::Unobserved
10722                };
10723                // A file with a link cannot be one a retired mapping describes:
10724                // Linux refuses to link an unlinked file again (only an
10725                // `O_TMPFILE` file, which is never retired, may get a name).
10726                // So a nonzero link count is a name sighting however the file
10727                // was reached, by path, descriptor or working directory, and a
10728                // zero count (`fstat` after `unlink`, `/proc/self/fd/N`) is not.
10729                let sighting = if stat.mask.contains(StatxMask::STATX_NLINK) && stat.nlink > 0 {
10730                    InodeSighting::Name
10731                } else {
10732                    InodeSighting::Descriptor
10733                };
10734                // A procfs root counts the host's processes as its links.
10735                // Report 1, which file systems that do not count a
10736                // directory's links report, so that a walker such as `find`
10737                // infers nothing from it.
10738                if procfs.is_procfs()
10739                    && stat.inode == procfs_inode::PROC_ROOT_INO
10740                    && stat.mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFDIR
10741                    && stat.mask.contains(StatxMask::STATX_NLINK)
10742                {
10743                    stat.nlink = 1;
10744                }
10745                match rendered_entry(
10746                    &procfs,
10747                    &stat,
10748                    recordreplay_modes,
10749                    self.rendered_files(guest),
10750                ) {
10751                    // A file Detcore renders, reached through a spelling the
10752                    // kernel resolved (a symbolic link): the number its path
10753                    // names, and the epoch.
10754                    Some(path) => {
10755                        let nanos = epoch
10756                            .timestamp_nanos_opt()
10757                            .expect("epoch cannot be represented in nanoseconds")
10758                            as u64;
10759                        (
10760                            DetInode::mint(procfs_inode::rendered_inode(path)),
10761                            LogicalTime::from_nanos(nanos),
10762                        )
10763                    }
10764                    None => {
10765                        determinize_inode_observing_mtime(
10766                            guest,
10767                            stat.raw_inode(),
10768                            procfs.name(stat.dev),
10769                            observed,
10770                            sighting,
10771                        )
10772                        .await
10773                    }
10774                }
10775            }
10776        };
10777        let host_inode = stat.inode;
10778        stat.inode = d_ino.as_raw(); // Reveal only the deterministic inode.
10779
10780        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
10781        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1056): Deterministic st_dev remapping.
10782        // The raw st_dev leaks the kernel's host-wide anonymous block-device
10783        // number for procfs/sysfs/tmpfs mounts, which drifts between runs (and
10784        // between the two runs of `--verify`). Reveal only a deterministic
10785        // device id.
10786        let host_device = stat.dev;
10787        stat.dev = determinize_device(guest, stat.dev).await;
10788        // A procfs root that Detcore could not name (`ProcfsEntry::Unknown`, as
10789        // on a backend that does not read the guest's mount table) reaches here
10790        // with the host's process count as its link count, which changes
10791        // whenever a host process starts or exits. Its device is Detcore's
10792        // procfs device by now, so it reports 1 like a named one (above).
10793        // Measured on DBT: two runs of one guest saw 6724 and 6770.
10794        if stat.dev == procfs_inode::VIRTUAL_PROC_DEVICE
10795            && host_inode == procfs_inode::PROC_ROOT_INO
10796            && stat.mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFDIR
10797            && stat.mask.contains(StatxMask::STATX_NLINK)
10798        {
10799            stat.nlink = 1;
10800        }
10801
10802        // A directory's size is whatever its file system makes of its
10803        // entries: btrfs sums the names' lengths, tmpfs counts entries, ext4
10804        // rounds up to its blocks. So it changes whenever any process adds or
10805        // removes an entry, and differs between file systems. Builds stat
10806        // every ancestor of their working directory (kbuild, configure,
10807        // cargo, CMake's look at $HOME), so the host's value broke
10808        // `--verify --verify-strict` of ordinary builds on a shared machine
10809        // and reproducibility across hosts
10810        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4162). Report one
10811        // 4096-byte block, as ext4 does for a small directory, whatever the
10812        // directory holds; btrfs reports an empty directory as 0, so even
10813        // an empty one is set. A procfs directory keeps the host's value
10814        // (0, or a descriptor count for /proc/<pid>/fd), which Detcore
10815        // already virtualizes there. Only a proved procfs directory keeps
10816        // it: one whose entry Detcore names (`ProcfsEntry`, on the backends
10817        // whose guest threads are host tasks). (KVM's `/proc` directories are
10818        // Detcore's placeholders, whose stat Detcore answers.) Its stat fields alone
10819        // prove nothing: an anonymous device with 1024-byte blocks is also
10820        // devpts, autofs or a FUSE mount reporting those blocks (Codex
10821        // re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4369). Under
10822        // DBT, where Detcore names no procfs entries, such a directory keeps
10823        // the host's value unproved
10824        // (`procfs_inode::unprovable_procfs_signature`). sysfs and cgroup
10825        // directories, which Linux also reports as 0, report 4096.
10826        if stat.mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFDIR
10827            && stat.mask.contains(StatxMask::STATX_SIZE)
10828            && !procfs.is_procfs()
10829            && !procfs_inode::unprovable_procfs_signature(
10830                &guest.config().backend,
10831                guest.thread_state().physical_tid,
10832                host_device,
10833                stat.blksize,
10834            )
10835        {
10836            stat.size = 4096;
10837            if stat.mask.contains(StatxMask::STATX_BLOCKS) {
10838                stat.blocks = 8;
10839            }
10840        }
10841
10842        // A directory's link count is the same kind of host value: on file
10843        // systems that count a directory's links (ext4, and tmpfs too) it
10844        // is two plus the number of subdirectories, so it changes whenever
10845        // any process adds or removes a subdirectory; only file systems
10846        // that do not count them (btrfs) report 1 for every directory. The
10847        // ancestors a build stats include shared directories such as
10848        // `/home`, whose subdirectory count churns under parallel work on
10849        // a shared machine, so the host's count broke the same `--verify`
10850        // comparisons as the size above, through the hashed stat buffer
10851        // the io-buffer log records. Report 1, as the procfs root above
10852        // already does. GNU find's leaf optimization expects `nlink - 2`
10853        // subdirectories and stats entries until it has seen that many;
10854        // a count below 2 disables the optimization, so 1 makes a walker
10855        // infer nothing and stat every entry -- the safe direction.
10856        //
10857        // Unlike the size pin above, this pin does not inherit the
10858        // unprovable-procfs exclusion: a procfs directory's size 0 matters
10859        // to SEEK_END, but its link count has no such consumer, and the
10860        // procfs root already reports 1 on every backend, so 1 cannot be
10861        // wrong for a directory that might be procfs. An anonymous-device
10862        // directory with 1024-byte blocks (autofs `/home`, devpts, a FUSE
10863        // mount) is therefore pinned on DBT too, where the size pin still
10864        // leaves it alone. Only a proved procfs directory keeps its host
10865        // count: one Detcore knows is procfs (`ProcfsEntry::At` or
10866        // `ProcfsEntry::Unnamed`; see `ProcfsEntry::is_procfs`). For
10867        // example `/proc/<pid>/fd` reports nlink 2 and carries its
10868        // descriptor count in its size, and both are preserved here.
10869        // Synthetic procfs directories Detcore serves itself (the
10870        // `descriptor_directory` placeholders answered by
10871        // `rendered_procfs_stat` before `determinize_stat` runs) bypass
10872        // this pin entirely and keep their synthesized metadata.
10873        //
10874        // A deleted directory keeps 0: `mkdir`, `open(O_DIRECTORY)`,
10875        // `rmdir`, then `fstat` reports `st_nlink == 0` on Linux (ext4's
10876        // rmdir clears the count), and that zero is guest-visible state,
10877        // not host churn. Only a positive count is pinned.
10878        if stat.mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFDIR
10879            && stat.mask.contains(StatxMask::STATX_NLINK)
10880            && stat.nlink >= 1
10881            && !procfs.is_procfs()
10882        {
10883            stat.nlink = 1;
10884        }
10885
10886        let epoch_tp = Timespec {
10887            tv_sec: epoch.timestamp(),
10888            tv_nsec: epoch.timestamp_subsec_nanos() as i64,
10889        };
10890
10891        let mtime: Timespec = global_mtime.into();
10892        stat.atime = epoch_tp;
10893        stat.ctime = epoch_tp;
10894        stat.btime = epoch_tp;
10895
10896        stat.mtime = mtime;
10897
10898        Ok(stat)
10899    }
10900
10901    /// Handles all stat syscalls.
10902    pub async fn handle_stat_family<G: Guest<Self>>(
10903        &self,
10904        guest: &mut G,
10905        call: StatFamily,
10906    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
10907        if guest.config().virtualize_metadata {
10908            // NB: let kernel handle error codes, it's not easy to do so without
10909            // kernel because there're many corner cases. i.e.: even access
10910            // filepath from tracer may cause tracer to hang under certain fuse
10911            // filesystem (squashfs_ll).
10912            // The target is found before the call, which can overwrite its path.
10913            // A procfs file Detcore renders is answered from the path as named,
10914            // as Linux reads the path before it writes the result, once the
10915            // call's own arguments passed.
10916            let target = stat_family_target(&guest.memory(), &call);
10917            if !stat_family_arguments_valid(&guest.memory(), &call) {
10918                if !matches!(self.rendered_procfs_stat(guest, target).await, Ok(None)) {
10919                    return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
10920                }
10921            } else if let Some(stat) = self.rendered_procfs_stat(guest, target).await? {
10922                let statptr = call.stat().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
10923                guest.memory().write_value(statptr.0, &stat.into())?;
10924                return Ok(0);
10925            }
10926            let target = match call.stat() {
10927                Some(result) => target.unless_overwritten(
10928                    &guest.memory(),
10929                    result.0.as_raw(),
10930                    std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>(),
10931                ),
10932                None => target,
10933            };
10934            let before = Self::stat_buffer_before(
10935                guest,
10936                call.stat().map(|result| result.0.as_raw()),
10937                std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>(),
10938            );
10939            Self::inject_translated(guest, Syscall::from(call)).await?;
10940            let statptr = call.stat().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
10941            let inode_override = target
10942                .descriptor()
10943                .and_then(|fd| stdio_inode_override(guest, fd));
10944            let stat: libc::stat = guest.memory().read_value(statptr.0)?;
10945            // The placeholder directory, reached through a spelling the
10946            // `--proc` level table could not resolve: hidden, as `/proc/fs`
10947            // is (`descriptor_directory`). Until its identity is learnt, the
10948            // question is asked in a boxed future, after which the result is
10949            // read again, so that no stat is kept across it.
10950            let (mode, dev, ino) = (stat.st_mode, stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino);
10951            let stat = match Self::hidden_placeholder_known(guest, mode, dev, ino) {
10952                Some(true) => {
10953                    return Self::hidden_placeholder_stat(guest, statptr.0.as_raw(), before);
10954                }
10955                Some(false) => stat,
10956                None => {
10957                    if Box::pin(Self::hidden_placeholder_reached(guest, mode, dev, ino)).await {
10958                        return Self::hidden_placeholder_stat(guest, statptr.0.as_raw(), before);
10959                    }
10960                    guest.memory().read_value(statptr.0)?
10961                }
10962            };
10963            let mut memory = guest.memory();
10964            // A placeholder another process made, or an earlier image of this
10965            // one, becomes known by its identity (`determinize_stat`).
10966            if inode_override.is_none() {
10967                let _ = self
10968                    .recognize_placeholder(guest, &DetStat::from(&stat), target)
10969                    .await;
10970            }
10971            let procfs = match inode_override {
10972                Some(_) => ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs,
10973                None => Self::procfs_entry(guest, &DetStat::from(&stat), target).await,
10974            };
10975            let stat = self
10976                .determinize_stat(guest, stat, inode_override, procfs)
10977                .await?;
10978            memory.write_value(statptr.0, &stat.into())?;
10979            Ok(0)
10980        } else {
10981            // A procfs file Detcore renders has no kernel object to ask.
10982            let target = stat_family_target(&guest.memory(), &call);
10983            if !stat_family_arguments_valid(&guest.memory(), &call) {
10984                if !matches!(self.rendered_procfs_stat(guest, target).await, Ok(None)) {
10985                    return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
10986                }
10987            } else if let Some(stat) = self.rendered_procfs_stat(guest, target).await? {
10988                let statptr = call.stat().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
10989                guest.memory().write_value(statptr.0, &stat.into())?;
10990                return Ok(0);
10991            }
10992            let before = Self::stat_buffer_before(
10993                guest,
10994                call.stat().map(|result| result.0.as_raw()),
10995                std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>(),
10996            );
10997            let ret = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
10998            // The placeholder directory is hidden here too (record and replay
10999            // have none, so a recording is unchanged).
11000            if ret == 0
11001                && before.is_some()
11002                && let Some(statptr) = call.stat()
11003            {
11004                let stat: libc::stat = guest.memory().read_value(statptr.0)?;
11005                let (mode, dev, ino) = (stat.st_mode, stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino);
11006                if Self::reaches_hidden_placeholder(guest, mode, dev, ino).await {
11007                    return Self::hidden_placeholder_stat(guest, statptr.0.as_raw(), before);
11008                }
11009            }
11010            Ok(ret)
11011        }
11012    }
11013
11014    /// statx system call
11015    pub async fn handle_statx<G: Guest<Self>>(
11016        &self,
11017        guest: &mut G,
11018        call: syscalls::Statx,
11019    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
11020        // Whether `statx` accepts its arguments, which it checks before it
11021        // looks at any file.
11022        let renderable = statx_arguments_valid(
11023            call.flags().bits(),
11024            call.mask().bits(),
11025            names_no_path(&guest.memory(), call.path(), call.flags()),
11026        );
11027        if guest.config().virtualize_metadata {
11028            // NB: let kernel handle error codes, it's not easy to do so without kernel
11029            // because there're many corner cases. i.e.: even access filepath from tracer
11030            // may cause tracer to hang under certain fuse filesystem (squashfs_ll).
11031            // The target is found before the call, which can overwrite its path.
11032            // A procfs file Detcore renders is answered from the path as named,
11033            // as Linux reads the path before it writes the result, once the
11034            // call's own arguments passed (which `statx` checks before it
11035            // looks up any file).
11036            let target = StatTarget::at(&guest.memory(), call.dirfd(), call.path(), call.flags());
11037            if !renderable {
11038                if !matches!(self.rendered_procfs_stat(guest, target).await, Ok(None)) {
11039                    return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
11040                }
11041            } else if let Some(stat) = self.rendered_procfs_stat(guest, target).await? {
11042                return self.write_rendered_statx(guest, call, stat).await;
11043            }
11044            let target = match call.statx() {
11045                Some(result) => target.unless_overwritten(
11046                    &guest.memory(),
11047                    result.0.as_raw(),
11048                    std::mem::size_of::<reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx>(),
11049                ),
11050                None => target,
11051            };
11052            // A call that asks for the unique mount ID asks the kernel for the
11053            // classic one: the run's mount-ID pool numbers classic IDs, the
11054            // ones mountinfo and fdinfo show, and the guest's unique ID is
11055            // derived from that number (`fill_statx_mount_id`). Linux fills
11056            // both mount-ID fields in `vfs_statx_path` (v6.12
11057            // fs/stat.c:248-259) after the filesystem's getattr, which sees
11058            // `STATX_MNT_ID` in place of `STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE`.
11059            let unique = statx_requested_mask(call) & STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE != 0;
11060            let before = Self::stat_buffer_before(
11061                guest,
11062                call.statx().map(|result| result.0.as_raw()),
11063                std::mem::size_of::<reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx>(),
11064            );
11065            Self::inject_translated(guest, Syscall::from(statx_asking_classic_mount_id(call)))
11066                .await?;
11067            let statptr = call.statx().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
11068            let inode_override = target
11069                .descriptor()
11070                .and_then(|fd| stdio_inode_override(guest, fd));
11071            let stat: reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx = guest.memory().read_value(statptr.0)?;
11072            // The placeholder directory, reached through a spelling the
11073            // `--proc` level table could not resolve: hidden, as `/proc/fs`
11074            // is (`descriptor_directory`), asked as for the other stat calls
11075            // (`handle_stat_family`).
11076            let (mode, dev, ino) = {
11077                let identity = DetStat::from(stat);
11078                (identity.mode, identity.dev, identity.inode)
11079            };
11080            let stat = match Self::hidden_placeholder_known(guest, mode, dev, ino) {
11081                Some(true) => {
11082                    return Self::hidden_placeholder_stat(guest, statptr.0.as_raw(), before);
11083                }
11084                Some(false) => stat,
11085                None => {
11086                    if Box::pin(Self::hidden_placeholder_reached(guest, mode, dev, ino)).await {
11087                        return Self::hidden_placeholder_stat(guest, statptr.0.as_raw(), before);
11088                    }
11089                    guest.memory().read_value(statptr.0)?
11090                }
11091            };
11092            let mut memory = guest.memory();
11093            // A placeholder another process made, or an earlier image of this
11094            // one, becomes known by its identity (`determinize_stat`).
11095            let placeholder = match inode_override {
11096                None => {
11097                    self.recognize_placeholder(guest, &DetStat::from(stat), target)
11098                        .await
11099                }
11100                Some(_) => None,
11101            };
11102            let procfs = match inode_override {
