11103                Some(_) => ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs,
11104                None => Self::procfs_entry(guest, &DetStat::from(stat), target).await,
11105            };
11106            // A rendered file reached through any spelling (a symbolic link to
11107            // its descriptor link) is on the guest's procfs mount, not on the
11108            // placeholder's memfd's.
11109            let raw_mount_id = match placeholder {
11110                Some(_) => rendered_procfs::guest_procfs_mount_id().ok(),
11111                None => (stat.stx_mask & reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::STATX_MNT_ID != 0)
11112                    .then_some(stat.stx_mnt_id),
11113            };
11114            let stat = self
11115                .determinize_stat(guest, stat, inode_override, procfs)
11116                .await?;
11117            let mut statx: reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx = stat.into();
11118            self.fill_statx_mount_id(guest, &mut statx, raw_mount_id, unique)
11119                .await;
11120            memory.write_value(statptr.0, &statx)?;
11121            Ok(0)
11122        } else {
11123            // A procfs file Detcore renders has no kernel object to ask.
11124            let target = StatTarget::at(&guest.memory(), call.dirfd(), call.path(), call.flags());
11125            // Arguments `statx` refuses before it looks up any file, here a
11126            // file Detcore renders.
11127            if !renderable {
11128                if !matches!(self.rendered_procfs_stat(guest, target).await, Ok(None)) {
11129                    return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
11130                }
11131            } else if let Some(stat) = self.rendered_procfs_stat(guest, target).await? {
11132                return self.write_rendered_statx(guest, call, stat).await;
11133            }
11134            let before = Self::stat_buffer_before(
11135                guest,
11136                call.statx().map(|result| result.0.as_raw()),
11137                std::mem::size_of::<reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx>(),
11138            );
11139            let ret = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
11140            // The same in recording, in replay and without either: a recording
11141            // keeps only the fields Detcore models, so what else the kernel
11142            // wrote must not reach the guest when it is recorded either.
11143            if ret == 0
11144                && let Some(statptr) = call.statx()
11145            {
11146                // The placeholder directory is hidden here too
11147                // (`handle_stat_family`), before the tail is canonicalized.
11148                if before.is_some() {
11149                    let stat: reverie::syscalls::linux_abi::Statx =
11150                        guest.memory().read_value(statptr.0)?;
11151                    let identity = DetStat::from(stat);
11152                    let (mode, dev, ino) = (identity.mode, identity.dev, identity.inode);
11153                    if Self::reaches_hidden_placeholder(guest, mode, dev, ino).await {
11154                        return Self::hidden_placeholder_stat(guest, statptr.0.as_raw(), before);
11155                    }
11156                }
11157                canonicalize_statx_tail(&mut guest.memory(), statptr.0.as_raw())?;
11158            }
11159            Ok(ret)
11160        }
11161    }
11162
11163    /// Whether a guest's F_SETFL or FIONBIO on this descriptor changes only its
11164    /// logical (guest-visible) O_NONBLOCK, leaving it physically nonblocking for
11165    /// the scheduler's nonblockize-and-retry.
11166    ///
11167    /// Outside record/replay that holds for every scheduler-managed type. In
11168    /// record/replay it holds only for a container-internal channel that is
11169    /// already physically nonblocking: a pipe, which is how `handle_pipe2`
11170    /// leaves every guest-created pipe in both phases, or an internal socket (a
11171    /// socketpair endpoint, which is how `handle_socketpair` leaves both ends, or
11172    /// a socket whose peer `classify_socket_peer` found to be a guest, which it
11173    /// makes physically nonblocking). Forwarding the guest's
11174    /// clear would make the recording's next read on that channel a blocking
11175    /// read on an fd that `syscall_targets_internal_fd` calls internal, which
11176    /// deadlocks the sequentialized scheduler while the writer waits for its
11177    /// turn. Both phases take the same branch, because `fd_type`,
11178    /// `internal_socket` and `physically_nonblocking` are Detcore
11179    /// bookkeeping that record and replay evolve identically: an F_SETFL is
11180    /// still recorded and replayed, with the kernel given `flags | O_NONBLOCK`
11181    /// in record and the recorded result returned in replay; a FIONBIO returns
11182    /// before `record_or_replay`, so neither phase records or applies it. Other
11183    /// sockets and eventfds stay external in record/replay. A pipe whose
11184    /// physical O_NONBLOCK came from the guest rather than from Detcore is also
11185    /// kept nonblocking; in record/replay the only such pipes are `pipe2` pipes,
11186    /// which Detcore has already made nonblocking.
11187    fn keeps_physically_nonblocking(
11188        &self,
11189        fd_type: FdType,
11190        internal_socket: bool,
11191        physically_nonblocking: bool,
11192        inherited_external_read: bool,
11193    ) -> bool {
11194        self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets()
11195            && !inherited_external_read
11196            && match fd_type {
11197                FdType::Pipe => !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes || physically_nonblocking,
11198                FdType::Socket if internal_socket => {
11199                    !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes || physically_nonblocking
11200                }
11201                FdType::Socket | FdType::Eventfd => !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes,
11202                _ => false,
11203            }
11204    }
11205
11206    /// fcntl system call
11207    pub async fn handle_fcntl<G: Guest<Self>>(
11208        &self,
11209        guest: &mut G,
11210        call: syscalls::Fcntl,
11211    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
11212        let fd = call.fd();
11213        // A reserved in-guest signal as the descriptor's I/O signal; 0, the
11214        // default SIGIO, is never reserved. Like the owner screen below, it
11215        // comes first, so a refused call has no other effect. Linux's fdget
11216        // comes before it: a descriptor the guest does not hold, or an O_PATH
11217        // one (which `check_fcntl_cmd` admits only for F_DUPFD*, F_GETFD,
11218        // F_SETFD and F_GETFL), is EBADF.
11219        if let F_SETSIG(signal) = call.cmd()
11220            && guest.config().reserves_in_guest_signal(signal.into())
11221        {
11222            let o_path = guest
11223                .thread_state()
11224                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.status_flags() & libc::O_PATH != 0)?;
11225            if o_path {
11226                return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
11227            }
11228            Self::refuse_reserved_signal_arming(
11229                guest,
11230                crate::refused_signal_controls::ReservedArming::FcntlSetsig,
11231                signal.into(),
11232            )?;
11233        }
11234        // On an in-guest run's default route, the one operation that would
11235        // complete a host-timed signal producer (D28), before the call reaches
11236        // the kernel. It comes before the owner screen below, so that its own
11237        // reads of the descriptor's state finish before the screen takes its
11238        // copy of an `F_SETOWN_EX` owner on the scratch stack: one scratch
11239        // frame at a time. It reads that owner from guest memory itself; the
11240        // screen's later copy is the same value, since only a thread of the
11241        // caller's process could change it in between, and the in-guest
11242        // backends, the only ones that refuse producers, run no second thread
11243        // (they refuse thread creation).
11244        if let Some((arming, owner)) = self.fcntl_producer_arming(guest, call) {
11245            self.refuse_host_timed_producer(guest, fd, arming, owner)
11246                .await?;
11247        }
11248        // Before anything else, so a refused call has no other effect.
11249        let (call, _owner_copy) = self.screen_fcntl_owner(guest, call).await?;
11250        // The owner of an asynchronous-I/O descriptor may be any process or
11251        // process group, and Linux signals it when data arrives, at a moment
11252        // set by host timing. Record the signals in this turn, before the call
11253        // reaches the kernel, for every process of the container, and never
11254        // forget them (`Scheduler::record_host_timed_signals`).
11255        let signals = fcntl_host_timed_signals(call.cmd());
11256        if signals & kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGALRM) != 0 {
11257            refuse_sigalrm(guest, SigalrmControl::ArmProducer).await?;
11258        }
11259        // A lease makes another process's open of the file wait for the
11260        // lease break, interruptibly, with no scheduler admission.
11261        if matches!(call.cmd(), F_SETLEASE(lease) if lease != libc::F_UNLCK) {
11262            refuse_sigalrm(guest, SigalrmControl::ArmProducer).await?;
11263        }
11264        if signals != 0 && guest.config().backend.host_timed_signals_are_physical {
11265            record_host_timed_signals(guest, HostTimedSignalScope::Container, signals).await;
11266        }
11267        let o_cloexec = match call.cmd() {
11268            F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC(_) => OFlag::O_CLOEXEC,
11269            _ => OFlag::empty(),
11270        };
11271        match call.cmd() {
11272            F_GETFL => {
11273                let physical_flags = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
11274                let (logical_nonblocking, rendered_nofollow) =
11275                    guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
11276                        (
11277                            detfd.is_nonblocking(),
11278                            detfd.procfs_rendered_path().is_some()
11279                                && detfd.status_flags() & libc::O_NOFOLLOW != 0,
11280                        )
11281                    })?;
11282                // A rendered procfs file's placeholder was reopened without
11283                // the guest's `O_NOFOLLOW`, which Linux keeps.
11284                let physical_flags = if rendered_nofollow {
11285                    physical_flags | i64::from(libc::O_NOFOLLOW)
11286                } else {
11287                    physical_flags
11288                };
11289                let nonblocking = i64::from(OFlag::O_NONBLOCK.bits());
11290                if logical_nonblocking {
11291                    Ok(physical_flags | nonblocking)
11292                } else {
11293                    Ok(physical_flags & !nonblocking)
11294                }
11295            }
11296            F_SETFL(flags) => {
11297                let (fd_type, internal_socket, physically_nonblocking, inherited_external_read) =
11298                    guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
11299                        (
11300                            detfd.ty(),
11301                            detfd.is_internal_socket(),
11302                            detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
11303                            detfd.inherited_external_read().is_some(),
11304                        )
11305                    })?;
11306                let force_nonblocking = self.keeps_physically_nonblocking(
11307                    fd_type,
11308                    internal_socket,
11309                    physically_nonblocking,
11310                    inherited_external_read,
11311                );
11312                let physical_flags = if force_nonblocking {
11313                    flags | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK.bits()
11314                } else {
11315                    flags
11316                };
11317                let result = self
11318                    .record_or_replay(guest, call.with_cmd(F_SETFL(physical_flags)))
11319                    .await?;
11320                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
11321                    // Record the guest's *logical* status flags (derives logical
11322                    // nonblocking); when we forced O_NONBLOCK physically without the
11323                    // guest asking, mark the description physically nonblocking too.
11324                    detfd.set_status_flags(flags);
11325                    if force_nonblocking {
11326                        detfd.set_physically_nonblocking();
11327                    }
11328                })?;
11329                Ok(result)
11330            }
11331            F_DUPFD(_) | F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC(_) => {
11332                let newfd = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await? as RawFd;
11333                let lock_tracked = self.lock_tracked_descriptions(guest, newfd..=newfd);
11334                let replaced = guest.thread_state_mut().dup_fd(fd, newfd, o_cloexec)?;
11335                if let Some(open_file_id) = replaced {
11336                    self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
11337                }
11338                self.report_lock_references(guest, lock_tracked).await;
11339                Ok(newfd as i64)
11340            }
11341            F_SETFD(flags) => {
11342                let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
11343                let cloexec = flags & libc::FD_CLOEXEC != 0;
11344                // A descriptor Detcore lists without modelling keeps its flag
11345                // too (`FileMetadata::present_unmodelled`).
11346                if !guest.thread_state().set_unmodelled_cloexec(fd, cloexec) {
11347                    guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
11348                        detfd.set_cloexec(cloexec);
11349                    })?;
11350                }
11351                Ok(result)
11352            }
11353            // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
11354            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-2568): Review refusing guest pipe growth.
11355            // Raising a pipe above the pinned capacity is the ONE syscall that
11356            // defeats the pin, and whether it succeeds is decided by the host's
11357            // `/proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size`. On a default host (1 MiB ceiling)
11358            // the guest gets a 1048576-byte pipe; on a hardened host (64 KiB)
11359            // the identical guest gets EPERM and keeps 8192. Same binary, same
11360            // `--strict`, guest-visible return value and pipe capacity decided
11361            // by a host sysctl -- a determinism leak by this project's own
11362            // definition, and it survived because the capacity pin was applied
11363            // at creation and never defended afterwards.
11364            //
11365            // Refuse deterministically instead of asking Linux. EPERM is the
11366            // errno Linux itself returns when that ceiling binds, so the guest
11367            // sees a shape it must already handle rather than a novel one, and
11368            // it is the answer the hardened host would have given.
11369            //
11370            // SHRINKING IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. It is always permitted for
11371            // an unprivileged process, it is process-local with no host-derived
11372            // input, and `tests/c/pipe_capacity.c` locks
11373            // it as a guest-visible contract: that fixture shrinks to one page
11374            // and requires the value to round-trip. Clamping every
11375            // `F_SETPIPE_SZ` to the pinned capacity would break that contract
11376            // while fixing nothing that is actually nondeterministic.
11377            // A host-backed pipe's capacity is host state
11378            // (`reported_pipe_capacity`); the guest reads it no larger than
11379            // the ceiling it may raise a pipe to.
11380            F_GETPIPE_SZ => {
11381                let host = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
11382                if !host_pipe_floor() {
11383                    self.refuse_below_two_page_pipe_floor(
11384                        guest,
11385                        &format!("F_GETPIPE_SZ on fd {fd} read {host} bytes"),
11386                    )
11387                    .await;
11388                }
11389                Ok(reported_pipe_capacity(host))
11390            }
11391            F_SETPIPE_SZ(requested) if pipe_capacity_request_exceeds_ceiling(requested) => {
11392                trace!(
11393                    "[detcore] refusing F_SETPIPE_SZ({}) above the deterministic pipe ceiling {}",
11394                    requested,
11395                    deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()
11396                );
11397                Err(Errno::EPERM.into())
11398            }
11399            // An OFD lock belongs to its open file description, and Linux
11400            // shows it in `/proc/locks` from every PID namespace, the host's
11401            // included, as owner -1. After each call, the description's own
11402            // fdinfo says which locks it holds (`procfs::locks`); the lock
11403            // itself is the kernel's, as for POSIX locks.
11404            F_OFD_SETLK(_) | F_OFD_SETLKW(_) => {
11405                let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
11406                self.refresh_description_locks(guest, fd, LockCall::Fcntl)
11407                    .await?;
11408                Ok(result)
11409            }
11410            _ => {
11411                trace!(
11412                    "[detcore-finishme]: fcntl unhandled cases: {:?}",
11413                    call.cmd()
11414                );
11415                Ok(self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?)
11416            }
11417        }
11418    }
11419
11420    /// Record which OFD and flock locks the open file description `fd` names
11421    /// holds now, after a call through it that may have changed them
11422    /// (`procfs::locks`), from the `lock:` lines of its fdinfo, which name
11423    /// exactly that description's locks with the device `/proc/locks`
11424    /// prints. A descriptor Detcore keeps no model of is left out.
11425    ///
11426    /// The fdinfo is read only through an anchor proved to be procfs, by a
11427    /// sequence of calls through the recorder ([`Self::read_own_fdinfo`]):
11428    /// the `/proc/locks` rows a replay filters are the recording's, and
11429    /// replay takes no real lock, so the locks they are matched against must
11430    /// be the recording's too. A recording therefore holds, after each such
11431    /// call, the anchor's `openat`, `fstatfs` and `fstat`, the entry's
11432    /// `openat2`, `fstatfs` and `fstat`, the reads and two `close`s
11433    /// (hermit-cli's `RECORD_VERSION` names the change).
11434    ///
11435    /// The guest's `call` is never affected. A read that fails for a cause
11436    /// the guest's own filesystem view or the backend decides (no `/proc`,
11437    /// not procfs, an entry outside it or across a mount, a backend's
11438    /// refusal) makes the description untrackable: it contributes no lock. A
11439    /// read that fails for ambient or resource state (a full descriptor table
11440    /// or file table, no memory, an interruption, an I/O error, a kernel
11441    /// without `openat2`, a permission refusal) leaves its locks unknown, and
11442    /// a later `/proc/locks` read
11443    /// refuses while a guest table references the description
11444    /// (`procfs::locks::LockLedger::unknown`).
11445    ///
11446    /// A lock or unlock through a descriptor whose description the ledger
11447    /// may know under another identity (one Detcore keeps no model of, such
11448    /// as a descriptor received over `SCM_RIGHTS` and not recorded
11449    /// (`Detcore::record_received_descriptors`), or one recorded on
11450    /// reception as a second model of the sender's description, not one that
11451    /// joined an open file its table models) can leave that other
11452    /// identity's entry stale, so no lock on that file's inode number counts
11453    /// from then on (`procfs::locks::LockLedger::alias_inode`): hidden, never
11454    /// a host's row admitted. If that descriptor's fdinfo cannot be read for
11455    /// ambient or resource state, every later `/proc/locks` read refuses
11456    /// instead ([`Self::note_alias`]).
11457    pub(crate) async fn refresh_description_locks<G: Guest<Self>>(
11458        &self,
11459        guest: &mut G,
11460        fd: RawFd,
11461        call: LockCall,
11462    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
11463        let model = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
11464            detfd.set_lock_tracked();
11465            if matches!(
11466                call,
11467                LockCall::Recvmsg | LockCall::Recvmmsg | LockCall::BinderWriteRead
11468            ) {
11469                detfd.set_received_for_locks();
11470            }
11471            if call == LockCall::Fcntl {
11472                detfd.set_may_hold_ofd_lock();
11473            }
11474            (detfd.open_file_id(), detfd.is_received_for_locks())
11475        });
11476        let Ok((open_file, received)) = model else {
11477            if call.changes_locks() {
11478                let fdinfo = self.read_own_fdinfo(guest, fd, call.name()).await?;
11479                Self::note_alias(guest, &fdinfo).await;
11480            }
11481            return Ok(());
11482        };
11483        let fdinfo = self.read_own_fdinfo(guest, fd, call.name()).await?;
11484        if received && call.changes_locks() {
11485            Self::note_alias(guest, &fdinfo).await;
11486        }
11487        let held = matches!(&fdinfo, FdinfoRead::Contents(_));
11488        let locks = match fdinfo {
11489            FdinfoRead::Contents(contents) => {
11490                Ok(crate::procfs::locks::held_locks_in_fdinfo(&contents))
11491            }
11492            FdinfoRead::Unknown(reason) => Err(reason),
11493            // Hidden, never admitted: the description contributes no lock
11494            // until a later read through a proved procfs.
11495            FdinfoRead::Untrackable(reason) => {
11496                info!("[detcore] /proc/locks: {reason}; its locks are not shown");
11497                Ok(Vec::new())
11498            }
11499        };
11500        if !held
11501            || locks
11502                .as_ref()
11503                .is_ok_and(|locks| locks.iter().any(|lock| lock.class == "OFDLCK"))
11504        {
11505            let _ = guest
11506                .thread_state()
11507                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_may_hold_ofd_lock());
11508        }
11509        let slots = guest.thread_state().slots_naming(open_file);
11510        crate::tool_global::note_description_locks(guest, open_file, locks, slots).await;
11511        Ok(())
11512    }
11513
11514    /// After a lock or unlock through a descriptor whose description the
11515    /// ledger may know under another identity: no lock on its inode number
11516    /// counts from now on (`procfs::locks::LockLedger::alias_inode`). If its
11517    /// fdinfo could not be read for ambient or resource state, which
11518    /// identities it changed is unknown, and every later `/proc/locks`
11519    /// snapshot is refused by name (`procfs::locks::LockLedger::refuse`); if
11520    /// the guest's `/proc` could not be proved to be procfs, no lock counts
11521    /// at all (an inode of `None`), which only hides.
11522    async fn note_alias<G: Guest<Self>>(guest: &mut G, fdinfo: &FdinfoRead) {
11523        match fdinfo {
11524            FdinfoRead::Unknown(reason) => {
11525                crate::tool_global::note_lock_ledger_refused(guest, reason.clone()).await;
11526            }
11527            FdinfoRead::Contents(_) | FdinfoRead::Untrackable(_) => {
11528                crate::tool_global::note_aliased_inode(guest, fdinfo.inode()).await;
11529            }
11530        }
11531    }
11532
11533    /// The descriptions named by the slots `fds` of this thread's table
11534    /// whose locks `procfs::locks::LockLedger` follows, taken before a close
11535    /// or replacement of those slots.
11536    fn lock_tracked_descriptions<G: Guest<Self>>(
11537        &self,
11538        guest: &G,
11539        fds: std::ops::RangeInclusive<RawFd>,
11540    ) -> Vec<OpenFileId> {
11541        let thread = guest.thread_state();
11542        let candidates = if fds.start() == fds.end() {
11543            vec![*fds.start()]
11544        } else {
11545            thread
11546                .open_fds()
11547                .into_iter()
11548                .filter(|fd| fds.contains(fd))
11549                .collect()
11550        };
11551        let mut tracked = candidates
11552            .into_iter()
11553            .filter_map(|fd| {
11554                thread
11555                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
11556                        detfd.is_lock_tracked().then(|| detfd.open_file_id())
11557                    })
11558                    .ok()
11559                    .flatten()
11560            })
11561            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
11562        tracked.sort();
11563        tracked.dedup();
11564        tracked
11565    }
11566
11567    /// After a close or replacement of slots that named `descriptions`,
11568    /// report how many slots of this thread's table still name each
11569    /// (`procfs::locks::LockLedger::release`).
11570    async fn report_lock_references<G: Guest<Self>>(
11571        &self,
11572        guest: &mut G,
11573        descriptions: Vec<OpenFileId>,
11574    ) {
11575        for open_file in descriptions {
11576            let remaining = guest.thread_state().slots_naming(open_file);
11577            crate::tool_global::note_table_released(guest, open_file, remaining).await;
11578        }
11579    }
11580
11581    /// The text of `/proc/thread-self/fdinfo/<fd>`, read through the guest's
11582    /// procfs only, by a recorded sequence staged in a private page mapped for
11583    /// this call and unmapped before it returns ([`Self::read_staged_fdinfo`]).
11584    ///
11585    /// The guest chooses its own root, so a path alone proves nothing: under a
11586    /// `chroot` its `/proc` can be any tree, with any text where an fdinfo is
11587    /// expected, and lock lines that matched a host's lock would admit the
11588    /// host's `/proc/locks` row. So the read starts from an anchor, the
11589    /// guest's `/proc`, which must be procfs (`fstatfs`), opens the entry
11590    /// below it with `openat2`'s `RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_XDEV` (no step
11591    /// out of the anchor, no mount crossed, so nothing bound over an entry),
11592    /// and requires the entry itself on procfs and on the anchor's device
11593    /// (`fstatfs` and `fstat` of both). Every step goes through the
11594    /// recorder, so record and replay decide alike. The read holds two
11595    /// descriptors at once, the anchor and the entry. These checks rely on
11596    /// the serialized schedule, under which no other guest thread runs
11597    /// between the calls; with concurrent threads the entry check narrows a
11598    /// `dup2` race on the descriptor numbers but does not close it
11599    /// ([`Self::read_opened_entry`]).
11600    ///
11601    /// No page for a guest that mapped its whole address space away, and a
11602    /// failed step whose errno is ambient or resource state
11603    /// ([`fdinfo_failure_hides`] is false), leave the description's locks
11604    /// unknown ([`FdinfoRead::Unknown`], whose reason names the guest's
11605    /// `call`, [`fdinfo_refusal`]). Every other outcome that gives no proved
11606    /// fdinfo (no `/proc`, not procfs, an entry outside it or across a
11607    /// mount, a device mismatch, a guest-decided or backend-decided errno)
11608    /// makes the description untrackable ([`FdinfoRead::Untrackable`]).
11609    async fn read_own_fdinfo<G: Guest<Self>>(
11610        &self,
11611        guest: &mut G,
11612        fd: RawFd,
11613        call: &str,
11614    ) -> Result<FdinfoRead, Error> {
11615        let mapped = guest
11616            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
11617                syscalls::Mmap::new()
11618                    .with_addr(None)
11619                    .with_len(FDINFO_PAGE)
11620                    .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
11621                    .with_flags(MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS)
11622                    .with_fd(-1)
11623                    .with_offset(0),
11624            ))
11625            .await;
11626        let Some(page) = mapped
11627            .ok()
11628            .and_then(|mapped| usize::try_from(mapped).ok())
11629            .filter(|page| *page != 0)
11630        else {
11631            return Ok(FdinfoRead::Unknown(format!(
11632                "after {call} on fd {fd}, Detcore could not map the page it reads that \
11633                 descriptor's fdinfo through ({mapped:?}), so it does not know which locks \
11634                 the description holds"
11635            )));
11636        };
11637        let result = self.read_staged_fdinfo(guest, page, fd).await;
11638        if let Err(errno) = guest
11639            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
11640                syscalls::Munmap::new()
11641                    .with_addr(Addr::from_raw(page))
11642                    .with_len(FDINFO_PAGE),
11643            ))
11644            .await
11645        {
11646            warn!(
11647                "[detcore] could not unmap the transient fdinfo page: {}",
11648                errno
11649            );
11650        }
11651        Ok(match result? {
11652            Ok(contents) => FdinfoRead::Contents(contents),
11653            // Ambient or resource state says nothing about the locks.
11654            Err(FdinfoFailure::Failed(step, errno)) if !fdinfo_failure_hides(errno) => {
11655                FdinfoRead::Unknown(fdinfo_refusal(call, fd, step, errno))
11656            }
11657            Err(FdinfoFailure::Failed(step, errno)) => FdinfoRead::Untrackable(format!(
11658                "after {call} on fd {fd}, the guest's /proc did not give a procfs fdinfo \
11659                 ({step}: {errno})"
11660            )),
11661            Err(FdinfoFailure::NotProcfs(why)) => FdinfoRead::Untrackable(format!(
11662                "after {call} on fd {fd}, the guest's /proc did not give a procfs fdinfo \
11663                 ({why})"
11664            )),
11665        })
11666    }
11667
11668    /// Stop the run, by name, with the policy-refusal exit, because Detcore
11669    /// cannot tell a `/proc/locks` snapshot's guest rows from a host's while a
11670    /// description whose locks it could not read is referenced
11671    /// (`procfs::locks::LockLedger::unknown`).
11672    async fn refuse_lock_bookkeeping<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &mut G, reason: String) -> ! {
11673        error!("[detcore] {reason}");
11674        crate::tool_global::report_policy_refusal(guest, reason).await;
11675        crate::tool_global::unrecoverable_shutdown(guest, detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT)
11676            .await
11677    }
11678
11679    /// [`Self::read_own_fdinfo`]'s recorded sequence, in the mapped `page`
11680    /// (layout: the path at [`FDINFO_PATH`], `openat2`'s `struct open_how` at
11681    /// [`FDINFO_HOW`], `fstatfs` and `fstat` buffers at [`FDINFO_STAT`], the
11682    /// read buffer from [`FDINFO_READ`]): open the anchor, prove it procfs,
11683    /// open the entry beneath it on its mount, compare devices, read, and
11684    /// close both descriptors.
11685    async fn read_staged_fdinfo<G: Guest<Self>>(
11686        &self,
11687        guest: &mut G,
11688        page: usize,
11689        fd: RawFd,
11690    ) -> Result<Result<Vec<u8>, FdinfoFailure>, Error> {
11691        // A backend whose `/proc` is its own (KVM) gives no procfs anchor:
11692        // nothing is opened there, and the description is untrackable, as an
11693        // anchor that is not procfs makes it.
11694        if !procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors(&self.cfg.backend) {
11695            return Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::NotProcfs(
11696                "the backend's /proc is not the kernel's procfs",
11697            )));
11698        }
11699        let path_ptr =
11700            PathPtr::from_ptr((page + FDINFO_PATH) as *const libc::c_char).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
11701        self.write_fdinfo_path(guest, page, "/proc")?;
11702        let anchor = syscalls::Openat::new()
11703            .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
11704            .with_path(Some(path_ptr))
11705            .with_flags(OFlag::O_PATH | OFlag::O_DIRECTORY | OFlag::O_CLOEXEC)
11706            .with_mode(None);
11707        let anchor = match self.record_or_replay(guest, Syscall::Openat(anchor)).await {
11708            Ok(anchor) => anchor as RawFd,
11709            Err(errno) => return Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::Failed("open", errno))),
11710        };
11711        let result = self.read_beneath_anchor(guest, page, anchor, fd).await;
11712        if let Err(errno) = self
11713            .record_or_replay(guest, syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(anchor))
11714            .await
11715        {
11716            trace!("[detcore] closing the fdinfo anchor failed: {errno}");
11717        }
11718        result
11719    }
11720
11721    /// [`Self::read_staged_fdinfo`] once its `anchor` is open.
11722    async fn read_beneath_anchor<G: Guest<Self>>(
11723        &self,
11724        guest: &mut G,
11725        page: usize,
11726        anchor: RawFd,
11727        fd: RawFd,
11728    ) -> Result<Result<Vec<u8>, FdinfoFailure>, Error> {
11729        let anchor_device = match self.recorded_procfs_device(guest, page, anchor).await? {
11730            Ok(device) => device,
11731            Err(failure) => return Ok(Err(failure)),
11732        };
11733        self.write_fdinfo_path(guest, page, &format!("thread-self/fdinfo/{fd}"))?;
11734        // struct open_how { u64 flags; u64 mode; u64 resolve; }
11735        let how = (libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_CLOEXEC) as u64;
11736        let mut open_how = [0u8; FDINFO_HOW_SIZE];
11737        open_how[..8].copy_from_slice(&how.to_ne_bytes());
11738        open_how[16..].copy_from_slice(&FDINFO_RESOLVE.to_ne_bytes());
11739        let how_ptr = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(page + FDINFO_HOW).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
11740        guest.memory().write_exact(how_ptr, &open_how)?;
11741        let opened = match self
11742            .record_or_replay(
11743                guest,
11744                Syscall::from_raw(
11745                    Sysno::openat2,
11746                    procfs_levels::raw_args([
11747                        anchor as usize,
11748                        page + FDINFO_PATH,
11749                        page + FDINFO_HOW,
11750                        FDINFO_HOW_SIZE,
11751                        0,
11752                        0,
11753                    ]),
11754                ),
11755            )
11756            .await
11757        {
11758            Ok(opened) => opened as RawFd,
11759            // The entry is outside the anchor or across a mount.
11760            Err(Errno::EXDEV) => {
11761                return Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::NotProcfs(
11762                    "the entry is outside /proc or across a mount",
11763                )));
11764            }
11765            Err(errno) => return Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::Failed("open", errno))),
11766        };
11767        // Closed on every path, the error ones included.
11768        let result = self
11769            .read_opened_entry(guest, page, opened, anchor_device)
11770            .await;
11771        if let Err(errno) = self
11772            .record_or_replay(guest, syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(opened))
11773            .await
11774        {
11775            trace!("[detcore] closing fdinfo failed: {errno}");
11776        }
11777        result
11778    }
11779
11780    /// The text of the `opened` fdinfo entry, once it too is shown to be on
11781    /// procfs and on the anchor's device. The checks run on the entry's own
11782    /// descriptor, so a sibling thread that replaces the anchor's descriptor
11783    /// number between calls (`dup2` of a fake directory) cannot pass them.
11784    ///
11785    /// The defence relies on Detcore's serialized schedule: no other guest
11786    /// thread runs between these injected calls. Under
11787    /// `--no-sequentialize-threads` a sibling could still `dup2` onto the
11788    /// entry's own descriptor number between its checks and the read; the
11789    /// entry check narrows that race but does not close it.
11790    async fn read_opened_entry<G: Guest<Self>>(
11791        &self,
11792        guest: &mut G,
11793        page: usize,
11794        opened: RawFd,
11795        anchor_device: u64,
11796    ) -> Result<Result<Vec<u8>, FdinfoFailure>, Error> {
11797        match self.recorded_procfs_device(guest, page, opened).await? {
11798            Ok(device) if device == anchor_device => {}
11799            Ok(_) => {
11800                return Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::NotProcfs(
11801                    "the entry is not on /proc's device",
11802                )));
11803            }
11804            Err(failure) => return Ok(Err(failure)),
11805        }
11806        let scratch = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(page + FDINFO_READ).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
11807        match self
11808            .drain_procfs(
11809                guest,
11810                syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(opened),
11811                scratch,
11812                FDINFO_PAGE - FDINFO_READ,
11813                false,
11814            )
11815            .await
11816        {
11817            Ok(contents) => Ok(Ok(contents)),
11818            Err(Error::Errno(errno)) => Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::Failed("read", errno))),
11819            Err(error) => Err(error),
11820        }
11821    }
11822
11823    /// The device of the descriptor `fd`, once `fstatfs` shows it is on
11824    /// procfs, both through the recorder into the stat buffer of the fdinfo
11825    /// page. A failed call keeps its errno, for the common classification
11826    /// ([`fdinfo_failure_hides`]).
11827    async fn recorded_procfs_device<G: Guest<Self>>(
11828        &self,
11829        guest: &mut G,
11830        page: usize,
11831        fd: RawFd,
11832    ) -> Result<Result<u64, FdinfoFailure>, Error> {
11833        let stat = page + FDINFO_STAT;
11834        if let Err(errno) = self
11835            .record_or_replay(
11836                guest,
11837                Syscall::from_raw(
11838                    Sysno::fstatfs,
11839                    procfs_levels::raw_args([fd as usize, stat, 0, 0, 0, 0]),
11840                ),
11841            )
11842            .await
11843        {
11844            return Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::Failed("fstatfs", errno)));
11845        }
11846        // `f_type` is the first field of `struct statfs`.
11847        if self.read_fdinfo_word(guest, stat)? != libc::PROC_SUPER_MAGIC as u64 {
11848            return Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::NotProcfs("not procfs")));
11849        }
11850        if let Err(errno) = self
11851            .record_or_replay(
11852                guest,
11853                Syscall::from_raw(
11854                    Sysno::fstat,
11855                    procfs_levels::raw_args([fd as usize, stat, 0, 0, 0, 0]),
11856                ),
11857            )
11858            .await
11859        {
11860            return Ok(Err(FdinfoFailure::Failed("fstat", errno)));
11861        }
11862        // `st_dev` is the first field of `struct stat`.
11863        Ok(Ok(self.read_fdinfo_word(guest, stat)?))
11864    }
11865
11866    /// Write `path`, NUL-terminated, at the fdinfo page's path slot.
11867    fn write_fdinfo_path<G: Guest<Self>>(
11868        &self,
11869        guest: &mut G,
11870        page: usize,
11871        path: &str,
11872    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
11873        assert!(
11874            path.len() < FDINFO_HOW - FDINFO_PATH,
11875            "fdinfo path {path:?} outgrew its room"
11876        );
11877        let start = AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(page + FDINFO_PATH).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
11878        let mut bytes = path.as_bytes().to_vec();
11879        bytes.push(0);
11880        guest.memory().write_exact(start, &bytes)?;
11881        Ok(())
11882    }
11883
11884    /// The first 8 bytes at `address`, a native-endian `u64`.
11885    fn read_fdinfo_word<G: Guest<Self>>(
11886        &self,
11887        guest: &mut G,
11888        address: usize,
11889    ) -> Result<u64, Error> {
11890        let mut word = [0u8; 8];
11891        let start = Addr::<u8>::from_raw(address).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
11892        guest.memory().read_exact(start, &mut word)?;
11893        Ok(u64::from_ne_bytes(word))
11894    }
11895
11896    /// Refuse with EPERM a call that would make one of Hermit's tasks the
11897    /// owner of a descriptor's signals (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4083).
11898    /// Linux would accept it and later signal Hermit whenever the descriptor is
11899    /// ready; with `F_SETSIG(SIGTERM)` that ended Hermit's run. Refusing is a
11900    /// policy, the answer `pidfd_open` of Hermit's process gets.
11901    async fn refuse_hermit_owner<G: Guest<Self>>(
11902        &self,
11903        guest: &mut G,
11904        fd: RawFd,
11905        command: &str,
11906        owner: libc::c_int,
11907    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
11908        if owner <= 0 || !crate::tool_global::names_hermit_task(guest, None, owner).await {
11909            return Ok(());
11910        }
11911        tracing::info!(
11912            "[detcore, dtid {}] {command} on fd {fd} names task {owner}, one of Hermit's own, \
11913             as the owner of its signals: refused with EPERM \
11914             (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4083)",
11915            guest.thread_state().dettid,
11916        );
11917        Err(Errno::EPERM.into())
11918    }
11919
11920    /// The operation `call`, an `fcntl` as the kernel will receive it, would
11921    /// perform that can complete a host-timed signal producer
11922    /// ([`crate::host_timed_producers`]), where the run refuses them
11923    /// (`Config::in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers`); `None` for every
11924    /// other call, for every disarm (an owner of 0, `F_SETLEASE` with
11925    /// `F_UNLCK`, `F_NOTIFY` with no event bit, `F_SETFL` without `O_ASYNC`), for
11926    /// arguments the kernel refuses before it arms anything (`F_SETOWN` of
11927    /// `INT_MIN`, an unknown `F_SETOWN_EX` type or lease type), and always
11928    /// where the run does not refuse them. `F_SETSIG` alone completes nothing:
11929    /// it changes which signal an owner gets. With an owner-setting command
11930    /// comes the pid number the kernel looks up for the owner (`find_vpid`):
11931    /// `F_SETOWN`'s owner, negated for a process group, and `F_SETOWN_EX`'s
11932    /// pid as given.
11933    fn fcntl_producer_arming<G: Guest<Self>>(
11934        &self,
11935        guest: &mut G,
11936        call: syscalls::Fcntl,
11937    ) -> Option<(
11938        crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerArming,
11939        Option<crate::host_timed_producers::OwnerLookup>,
11940    )> {
11941        use crate::host_timed_producers::F_OWNER_PGRP;
11942        use crate::host_timed_producers::F_OWNER_PID;
11943        use crate::host_timed_producers::F_OWNER_TID;
11944        use crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerArming;
11945        // dnotify's event bits, `DN_ACCESS` through `DN_ATTRIB`: the only ones
11946        // `convert_arg` turns into events (`fs/notify/dnotify/dnotify.c:201-221`);
11947        // every other bit (`DN_MULTISHOT`, an unknown one) makes none.
11948        const DN_EVENTS: libc::c_int = 0x3f;
11949        if !guest.config().in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers {
11950            return None;
11951        }
11952        match call.cmd() {
11953            F_SETOWN => {
11954                let owner = call.into_parts().1.arg2 as libc::c_int;
11955                (owner != 0 && owner != libc::c_int::MIN).then_some((
11956                    ProducerArming::SetOwner("fcntl(F_SETOWN)"),
11957                    Some(crate::host_timed_producers::OwnerLookup::of_setown(owner)),
11958                ))
11959            }
11960            F_SETOWN_EX(Some(owner)) => {
11961                let owner: Addr<[libc::c_int; 2]> = owner.cast();
11962                let [kind, pid] = guest.memory().read_value(owner).ok()?;
11963                ([F_OWNER_TID, F_OWNER_PID, F_OWNER_PGRP].contains(&kind) && pid != 0).then_some((
11964                    ProducerArming::SetOwner("fcntl(F_SETOWN_EX)"),
11965                    Some(crate::host_timed_producers::OwnerLookup {
11966                        who: pid,
11967                        group: kind == F_OWNER_PGRP,
11968                    }),
11969                ))
11970            }
11971            F_SETFL(flags) => (flags & libc::O_ASYNC != 0)
11972                .then_some((ProducerArming::SetAsync("fcntl(F_SETFL)"), None)),
11973            F_SETLEASE(lease) => [libc::F_RDLCK, libc::F_WRLCK]
11974                .contains(&lease)
11975                .then_some((ProducerArming::Lease, None)),
11976            F_NOTIFY(mask) => (mask & DN_EVENTS != 0).then_some((ProducerArming::Notify, None)),
11977            _ => None,
11978        }
11979    }
11980
11981    /// As [`Self::fcntl_producer_arming`], for an `ioctl` as the kernel will
11982    /// receive it: `FIOSETOWN` or `SIOCSPGRP` with a nonzero owner, with the
11983    /// pid number the kernel looks up for it (`f_setown`), and `FIOASYNC`
11984    /// turning `O_ASYNC` on. An unreadable argument is left to the kernel,
11985    /// which answers EBADF or EFAULT and arms nothing.
11986    fn ioctl_producer_arming<G: Guest<Self>>(
11987        &self,
11988        guest: &mut G,
11989        call: syscalls::Ioctl,
11990    ) -> Option<(
11991        crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerArming,
11992        Option<crate::host_timed_producers::OwnerLookup>,
11993    )> {
11994        use crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerArming;
11995        if !guest.config().in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers {
11996            return None;
11997        }
11998        let (call_name, owner) = match call.request() {
11999            syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIOASYNC(on) => {
12000                let on: libc::c_int = guest.memory().read_value(on?).ok()?;
12001                return (on != 0).then_some((ProducerArming::SetAsync("ioctl(FIOASYNC)"), None));
12002            }
12003            syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIOSETOWN(owner) => ("ioctl(FIOSETOWN)", owner),
12004            syscalls::ioctl::Request::SIOCSPGRP(owner) => ("ioctl(SIOCSPGRP)", owner),
12005            _ => return None,
12006        };
12007        let owner: libc::c_int = guest.memory().read_value(owner?).ok()?;
12008        (owner != 0 && owner != libc::c_int::MIN).then_some((
12009            ProducerArming::SetSocketOwner(call_name),
12010            Some(crate::host_timed_producers::OwnerLookup::of_setown(owner)),
12011        ))
12012    }
12013
12014    /// Refuses with EPERM and a WARN `arming` on descriptor `fd` if it would
12015    /// complete a host-timed signal producer
12016    /// ([`crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerArming::completes`]), reading
12017    /// the descriptor's state in the caller's turn
12018    /// ([`Self::descriptor_producer_state`]). Linux's answers that come
12019    /// before any arming come first: EBADF for a descriptor the caller does
12020    /// not hold or an `O_PATH` one, ENOTDIR for `F_NOTIFY` on a file that is
12021    /// not a directory (`fcntl_dirnotify`, `fs/notify/dnotify/dnotify.c:288-292`)
12022    /// and EINVAL for a lease on a file that is not regular (`vfs_setlease`,
12023    /// `fs/locks.c:2021-2022`). An owner-setting operation naming an owner
12024    /// no signal can reach (`owner`, [`Self::owner_can_be_signalled`])
12025    /// completes nothing, and is left to the kernel, which answers ESRCH for
12026    /// one that does not exist, as `f_setown` and `f_setown_ex` do, and sets
12027    /// one that exists but can never be signalled. Called only where the run
12028    /// refuses producers.
12029    async fn refuse_host_timed_producer<G: Guest<Self>>(
12030        &self,
12031        guest: &mut G,
12032        fd: RawFd,
12033        arming: crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerArming,
12034        owner: Option<crate::host_timed_producers::OwnerLookup>,
12035    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
12036        use crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerArming;
12037        let (state, file_type) = self.descriptor_producer_state(guest, fd).await?;
12038        match arming {
12039            ProducerArming::Notify if file_type != libc::S_IFDIR => {
12040                return Err(Errno::ENOTDIR.into());
12041            }
12042            ProducerArming::Lease if file_type != libc::S_IFREG => {
12043                return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
12044            }
12045            _ => {}
12046        }
12047        if !arming.completes(state) {
12048            return Ok(());
12049        }
12050        if let Some(owner) = owner
12051            && !self.owner_can_be_signalled(guest, owner).await?
12052        {
12053            return Ok(());
12054        }
12055        tracing::warn!(
12056            "{}",
12057            crate::host_timed_producers::producer_refused_warning(
12058                arming,
12059                state,
12060                fd,
12061                guest.thread_state().dettid.as_raw(),
12062            )
12063        );
12064        Err(Errno::EPERM.into())
12065    }
12066
12067    /// Whether a signal for `owner`, the owner an owner-setting call names,
12068    /// can reach a guest process, now or after a later call of the guest's,
12069    /// so that setting it would complete a producer. Two questions are kept
12070    /// apart. The kernel sets any owner whose pid number a task, process
12071    /// group or session still holds (`find_vpid`; ESRCH otherwise: `f_setown`,
12072    /// `fs/fcntl.c:177-181`, and `f_setown_ex`, `:251-253`). Whether a signal
12073    /// can then reach anyone depends on the owner's type (`send_sigio`,
12074    /// `fs/fcntl.c:917-928`):
12075    /// - a process or thread owner (`F_OWNER_PID`, `F_OWNER_TID`, a positive
12076    ///   `F_SETOWN`) reaches the task with that pid, asked by `kill(who, 0)`.
12077    ///   A number that only a group or session holds names no task, and none
12078    ///   can take it while the owner holds it, so it can never be signalled.
12079    /// - a process-group owner reaches the members of that group
12080    ///   (`fs/fcntl.c:923-928`). It can be signalled when the group exists,
12081    ///   asked by `kill(-who, 0)`, and also when only a live task with that
12082    ///   pid exists, asked by `kill(who, 0)` and Detcore's exit model: that
12083    ///   task can still form the group, by `setpgid(0, 0)` or `setsid()`
12084    ///   (whose new group is the task's own pid, `kernel/sys.c:1128`), which
12085    ///   Detcore admits on every backend, and Linux would then signal it, so
12086    ///   arming it now completes a producer that a later call activates. A
12087    ///   number no task holds as its pid or group (one a session alone still
12088    ///   holds), or one only an exited task holds (a zombie), can never be
12089    ///   signalled.
12090    ///   `kill(-1, 0)` names every process, not group 1, so group 1 is asked
12091    ///   by `getpgid(1)`: pid 1 is Hermit's container init on the in-guest
12092    ///   backends, which never forms a group of its own later, so group 1
12093    ///   exists exactly when its leader is pid 1 (a group outside the PID
12094    ///   namespace reads as 0).
12095    ///
12096    /// Each probe sends nothing and runs in the caller's turn through
12097    /// `record_or_replay`. A probe answered (0, or EPERM for a task the
12098    /// caller may not signal) means it exists; ESRCH means it does not; any
12099    /// other errno (a security module's refusal, say) fails closed: the owner
12100    /// counts as reachable, so the call is refused by name rather than armed
12101    /// unchecked.
12102    async fn owner_can_be_signalled<G: Guest<Self>>(
12103        &self,
12104        guest: &mut G,
12105        owner: crate::host_timed_producers::OwnerLookup,
12106    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
12107        let who = owner.who;
12108        if who <= 0 {
12109            return Ok(false);
12110        }
12111        let mut probe = async |sysno: Sysno, target: libc::c_int| {
12112            let call = Syscall::from_raw(
12113                sysno,
12114                procfs_levels::raw_args([target as isize as usize, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]),
12115            );
12116            self.record_or_replay(&mut *guest, call).await
12117        };
12118        let answered = |result: Result<i64, Errno>| !matches!(result, Err(Errno::ESRCH));
12119        if owner.group && who == 1 {
12120            return Ok(match probe(Sysno::getpgid, 1).await {
12121                Ok(leader) => leader == 1,
12122                Err(Errno::ESRCH) => false,
12123                Err(_) => true,
12124            });
12125        }
12126        if owner.group && answered(probe(Sysno::kill, -who).await) {
12127            return Ok(true);
12128        }
12129        if !answered(probe(Sysno::kill, who).await) {
12130            return Ok(false);
12131        }
12132        if !owner.group {
12133            return Ok(true);
12134        }
12135        // A task holds the number as its pid, but leads no group: it can form
12136        // the group later only while it lives. One Detcore saw exit (a zombie
12137        // its parent has not reaped, or one already gone) never will, so its
12138        // number as a group owner can never be signalled. A task Detcore does
12139        // not model (none of the guest's) counts as able to.
12140        let (targets, exited) =
12141            crate::tool_global::resolve_kill_targets_and_exit(guest, DetPid::from_raw(who)).await;
12142        Ok(!targets.is_empty() || exited.is_none())
12143    }
12144
12145    /// What descriptor `fd` already arms toward a host-timed signal producer,
12146    /// and its file type (`st_mode & S_IFMT`), read in the caller's turn by
12147    /// `F_GETFL`, `F_GETOWN_EX` and `fstat`, each through `record_or_replay`,
12148    /// so a replay reads the recorded answers. The guest's own calls set a
12149    /// descriptor's owner and status flags in their turns (an inherited
12150    /// producer is refused at launch), and the reads run in the caller's
12151    /// turn, so the answers are the same in every run. The exception is an
12152    /// open file description the guest shares with a process outside the
12153    /// container (an inherited descriptor whose other holder is still
12154    /// running), which that process can change at a moment host timing
12155    /// decides: outside input of the same class as an external kill, which
12156    /// Hermit does not make deterministic. A descriptor the caller does not
12157    /// hold is EBADF from the first read, and an `O_PATH` one is EBADF, as
12158    /// Linux answers every arming command on one (`check_fcntl_cmd`,
12159    /// `fs/fcntl.c:556-568` and `:571-591`).
12160    async fn descriptor_producer_state<G: Guest<Self>>(
12161        &self,
12162        guest: &mut G,
12163        fd: RawFd,
12164    ) -> Result<(crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerState, libc::mode_t), Error> {
12165        let fcntl = |command: libc::c_int, address: usize| {
12166            Syscall::from_raw(
12167                Sysno::fcntl,
12168                procfs_levels::raw_args([fd as usize, command as usize, address, 0, 0, 0]),
12169            )
12170        };
12171        let flags = self
12172            .record_or_replay(guest, fcntl(libc::F_GETFL, 0))
12173            .await? as libc::c_int;
12174        if flags & libc::O_PATH != 0 {
12175            return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
12176        }
12177        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
12178        let owner = stack.reserve::<[libc::c_int; 2]>();
12179        let stat = stack.reserve::<libc::stat>();
12180        let guard = stack.commit()?;
12181        self.record_or_replay(
12182            guest,
12183            fcntl(crate::host_timed_producers::F_GETOWN_EX, owner.as_raw()),
12184        )
12185        .await?;
12186        self.record_or_replay(
12187            guest,
12188            Syscall::from_raw(
12189                Sysno::fstat,
12190                procfs_levels::raw_args([fd as usize, stat.as_raw(), 0, 0, 0, 0]),
12191            ),
12192        )
12193        .await?;
12194        let [kind, pid] = guest.memory().read_value(Addr::from(owner))?;
12195        let stat: libc::stat = guest.memory().read_value(Addr::from(stat))?;
12196        drop(guard);
12197        let file_type = stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT;
12198        Ok((
12199            crate::host_timed_producers::ProducerState {
12200                o_async: flags & libc::O_ASYNC != 0,
12201                owner: crate::host_timed_producers::names_an_owner(kind, pid),
12202                socket: file_type == libc::S_IFSOCK,
12203            },
12204            file_type,
12205        ))
12206    }
12207
12208    /// `call`, unless it is an `fcntl` that sets a descriptor's signal owner
12209    /// to one of Hermit's tasks ([`Self::refuse_hermit_owner`]): `F_SETOWN`
12210    /// with a positive pid, or `F_SETOWN_EX` naming a thread (`F_OWNER_TID`)
12211    /// or a process (`F_OWNER_PID`).
12212    ///
12213    /// `F_SETOWN` passes the owner by value; it is read from the raw argument,
12214    /// because the pinned Reverie's typed `FcntlCmd::F_SETOWN` carries none.
12215    /// `F_SETOWN_EX` passes it through guest memory, which another guest
12216    /// thread could change between this check and the kernel's own read, so
12217    /// the `f_owner_ex` is read once and the kernel is handed Detcore's copy,
12218    /// on this thread's scratch stack. An `f_owner_ex` that cannot be read is
12219    /// EFAULT here, as the kernel would answer, rather than a pointer passed
12220    /// on for the kernel to read later. The returned guard keeps the copy
12221    /// alive (SaBRe's scratch stack is an arena it owns) and must be held
12222    /// until the call has run.
12223    async fn screen_fcntl_owner<G: Guest<Self>>(
12224        &self,
12225        guest: &mut G,
12226        call: syscalls::Fcntl,
12227    ) -> Result<(syscalls::Fcntl, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>), Error> {
12228        // Linux's include/uapi/asm-generic/fcntl.h; the pinned libc lacks them.
12229        const F_OWNER_TID: libc::c_int = 0;
12230        const F_OWNER_PID: libc::c_int = 1;
12231        match call.cmd() {
12232            F_SETOWN => {
12233                let (_, args) = call.into_parts();
12234                self.refuse_hermit_owner(guest, call.fd(), "F_SETOWN", args.arg2 as libc::c_int)
12235                    .await?;
12236                Ok((call, None))
12237            }
12238            F_SETOWN_EX(owner) => {
12239                let owner: Addr<[libc::c_int; 2]> = owner.ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?.cast();
12240                let copy = guest.memory().read_value(owner)?;
12241                if matches!(copy[0], F_OWNER_TID | F_OWNER_PID) {
12242                    self.refuse_hermit_owner(guest, call.fd(), "F_SETOWN_EX", copy[1])
12243                        .await?;
12244                }
12245                let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
12246                let copied: Addr<[libc::c_int; 2]> = stack.push(copy);
12247                let guard = stack.commit()?;
12248                Ok((call.with_cmd(F_SETOWN_EX(Some(copied.cast()))), Some(guard)))
12249            }
12250            _ => Ok((call, None)),
12251        }
12252    }
12253
12254    /// `call`, unless it is an `ioctl` that sets a descriptor's signal owner
12255    /// to one of Hermit's tasks ([`Self::refuse_hermit_owner`]): `FIOSETOWN`
12256    /// or `SIOCSPGRP` with a positive pid, which set the owner as `F_SETOWN`
12257    /// does. The owner is passed through guest memory, so, as for
12258    /// `F_SETOWN_EX` ([`Self::screen_fcntl_owner`]), it is read once and the
12259    /// kernel is handed Detcore's copy, kept alive by the returned guard;
12260    /// an unreadable one is EFAULT.
12261    async fn screen_ioctl_owner<G: Guest<Self>>(
12262        &self,
12263        guest: &mut G,
12264        call: syscalls::Ioctl,
12265    ) -> Result<(syscalls::Ioctl, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>), Error> {
12266        let (command, owner) = match call.request() {
12267            syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIOSETOWN(owner) => ("FIOSETOWN", owner),
12268            syscalls::ioctl::Request::SIOCSPGRP(owner) => ("SIOCSPGRP", owner),
12269            _ => return Ok((call, None)),
12270        };
12271        let copy: libc::c_int = guest.memory().read_value(owner.ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?)?;
12272        self.refuse_hermit_owner(guest, call.fd(), command, copy)
12273            .await?;
12274        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
12275        let copied = stack.push(copy);
12276        let guard = stack.commit()?;
12277        let request = match call.request() {
12278            syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIOSETOWN(_) => {
12279                syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIOSETOWN(Some(copied))
12280            }
12281            _ => syscalls::ioctl::Request::SIOCSPGRP(Some(copied)),
12282        };
12283        Ok((call.with_request(request), Some(guard)))
12284    }
12285
12286    /// ioctl system call
12287    pub async fn handle_ioctl<G: Guest<Self>>(
12288        &self,
12289        guest: &mut G,
12290        call: syscalls::Ioctl,
12291    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
12292        let fd = call.fd();
12293        // Setting a virtual timerfd's host tick count would make the host
12294        // disagree with Detcore's count (`crate::syscalls::timerfd`).
12295        if Syscall::Ioctl(call).into_parts().1.arg1 as u64
12296            == crate::syscalls::timerfd::TFD_IOC_SET_TICKS
12297            && crate::syscalls::timerfd::enabled(guest)
12298            && crate::syscalls::timerfd::is_timerfd(guest, fd)
12299        {
12300            crate::syscalls::timerfd::refuse(format_args!(
12301                "ioctl(TFD_IOC_SET_TICKS) on timerfd {fd} would set the host's tick count"
12302            ));
12303        }
12304        // As in `handle_fcntl`: the one request that would complete a
12305        // host-timed signal producer, on an in-guest run's default route,
12306        // before the owner screen takes its copy on the scratch stack.
12307        if let Some((arming, owner)) = self.ioctl_producer_arming(guest, call) {
12308            self.refuse_host_timed_producer(guest, fd, arming, owner)
12309                .await?;
12310        }
12311        // Before anything else, so a refused call has no other effect.
12312        let (call, _owner_copy) = self.screen_ioctl_owner(guest, call).await?;
12313        // As in `handle_fcntl`: an asynchronous-I/O owner, and a session whose
12314        // controlling terminal hangs up, are signalled at a moment set by host
12315        // timing, so hold their signals in every process.
12316        let signals = ioctl_host_timed_signals(call.request());
12317        if signals != 0 && guest.config().backend.host_timed_signals_are_physical {
12318            record_host_timed_signals(guest, HostTimedSignalScope::Container, signals).await;
12319        }
12320        let (cloexec, nonblocking) = match call.request() {
12321            // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
12322            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1142): Review deterministic SIOCETHTOOL rejection.
12323            // Ethernet link state belongs to the host network namespace and can change between
12324            // runs. Match record/replay's established policy instead of exposing that state.
12325            syscalls::ioctl::Request::SIOCETHTOOL(_) => return Err(Errno::ENODEV.into()),
12326            syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIOCLEX => (Some(true), None),
12327            syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIONCLEX => (Some(false), None),
12328            syscalls::ioctl::Request::FIONBIO(value) => {
12329                let enabled = guest.memory().read_value(value.ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?)? != 0;
12330                (None, Some(enabled))
12331            }
12332            _ => (None, None),
12333        };
12334
12335        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
12336        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1013): Review logical FIONBIO handling for forced fds.
12337        // Detcore already keeps scheduler-managed fds physically nonblocking. Satisfy
12338        // FIONBIO logically instead of forwarding it: some backends cannot apply the
12339        // ioctl to their proxied pipe fd, and clearing it would violate the scheduler's
12340        // nonblockize-and-retry invariant. This mirrors F_SETFL's forced state split.
12341        if let Some(enabled) = nonblocking {
12342            let (fd_type, internal_socket, physically_nonblocking, inherited_external_read) =
12343                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
12344                    (
12345                        detfd.ty(),
12346                        detfd.is_internal_socket(),
12347                        detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
12348                        detfd.inherited_external_read().is_some(),
12349                    )
12350                })?;
12351            if self.keeps_physically_nonblocking(
12352                fd_type,
12353                internal_socket,
12354                physically_nonblocking,
12355                inherited_external_read,
12356            ) && physically_nonblocking
12357            {
12358                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
12359                    detfd.set_logical_nonblocking(enabled);
12360                })?;
12361                return Ok(0);
12362            }
12363        }
12364
12365        let request = Syscall::Ioctl(call).into_parts().1.arg1 as u64;
12366        let argument = Syscall::Ioctl(call).into_parts().1.arg2;
12367        // A binder read can install descriptors the transaction carried, which
12368        // no call names as new (`crate::syscalls::binder`). Read the call's
12369        // read_consumed before it runs, so only the commands it writes are
12370        // parsed; the in-guest backends discover such a descriptor
12371        // themselves, and parse nothing here.
12372        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
12373        // Record/replay restores only the outer ioctl structure, not the
12374        // nested command buffer or installed descriptors. Preserve that
12375        // existing Binder limitation without adding receipt-probe events.
12376        let binder_read = crate::syscalls::binder::is_write_read(request)
12377            && !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
12378            && !self.discovers_received_descriptors(guest);
12379        let already_consumed = if binder_read {
12380            crate::syscalls::binder::consumed_before(&guest.memory(), argument)
12381        } else {
12382            0
12383        };
12384        let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
12385        // `handle_ioctl` runs the call in the caller's turn, so no other
12386        // task can have closed or replaced a delivered number yet.
12387        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-4736)
12388        if binder_read && result >= 0 {
12389            let delivered =
12390                crate::syscalls::binder::delivered(&guest.memory(), argument, already_consumed);
12391            let recorded = self
12392                .record_received_descriptors(
12393                    guest,
12394                    &delivered,
12395                    crate::syscalls::scm_rights::Channel::Binder,
12396                    true,
12397                    // Binder installs every descriptor it delivers
12398                    // close-on-exec (`binder_apply_fd_fixups`).
12399                    true,
12400                    crate::syscalls::scm_rights::ReceivedFrom {
12401                        socket: fd,
12402                        peek: false,
12403                    },
12404                )
12405                .await?;
12406            self.refresh_received_locks(guest, &recorded, LockCall::BinderWriteRead)
12407                .await?;
12408        }
12409        // A descriptor Detcore lists without modelling keeps its
12410        // close-on-exec flag too (`FileMetadata::present_unmodelled`).
12411        let unmodelled =
12412            cloexec.is_some_and(|enabled| guest.thread_state().set_unmodelled_cloexec(fd, enabled));
12413        if !unmodelled && (cloexec.is_some() || nonblocking.is_some()) {
12414            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
12415                if let Some(enabled) = cloexec {
12416                    detfd.set_cloexec(enabled);
12417                }
12418                if let Some(enabled) = nonblocking {
12419                    detfd.set_nonblocking(enabled);
12420                }
12421            })?;
12422        }
12423        Ok(result)
12424    }
12425
12426    /// statfs: report deterministic filesystem statistics.
12427    ///
12428    /// The kernel's `statfs` reflects live host state: the free-block counts
12429    /// (`f_bfree`, `f_bavail`), the free-inode count (`f_ffree`) and the device
12430    /// id (`f_fsid`) all vary between runs as the underlying host filesystem
12431    /// fills and drains, which makes a bare passthrough diverge under `--verify`
12432    /// (e.g. `tar` calls statfs on its target filesystem). The static geometry
12433    /// of the mount (`f_type`, `f_bsize`, `f_blocks`, `f_namelen`, ...) is
12434    /// reproducible, so we run the real syscall and then canonicalize only the
12435    /// volatile fields.
12436    pub async fn handle_statfs<G: Guest<Self>>(
12437        &self,
12438        guest: &mut G,
12439        call: syscalls::Statfs,
12440    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
12441        if let Some(pointer) = call.path() {
12442            let path: PathBuf = pointer.read(&guest.memory())?;
12443            Self::prepare_guest_cwd(guest, libc::AT_FDCWD, &path).await;
12444            let observed = Self::observed_path(guest, libc::AT_FDCWD, &path)?;
12445            if self.rendered_procfs_at(guest, &observed).await?.is_some()
12446                || Box::pin(Self::names_placeholder_directory(guest, &observed)).await
12447                || self
12448                    .placeholder_reached(guest, libc::AT_FDCWD, Some(pointer), true)
12449                    .await
12450                    .is_some()
12451            {
12452                self.write_procfs_statfs(guest, call.buf())?;
12453                return Ok(0);
12454            }
12455        }
12456        let ret = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
12457        self.canonicalize_statfs_buf(guest, call.buf())?;
12458        Ok(ret)
12459    }
12460
12461    /// fstatfs: same determinization as [`Self::handle_statfs`], keyed on an fd.
12462    pub async fn handle_fstatfs<G: Guest<Self>>(
12463        &self,
12464        guest: &mut G,
12465        call: syscalls::Fstatfs,
12466    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
12467        let rendered = guest
12468            .thread_state()
12469            .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.procfs_rendered_path().is_some())
12470            .unwrap_or(false);
12471        if rendered {
12472            self.write_procfs_statfs(guest, call.buf())?;
12473            return Ok(0);
12474        }
12475        let ret = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
12476        self.canonicalize_statfs_buf(guest, call.buf())?;
12477        Ok(ret)
12478    }
12479
12480    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
12481    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#1851): Determinized ownership mutation. Emulate the
12482    // IDENTITY half of the call and let Linux answer the ARGUMENT half.
12483    /// The `chown` family (`chown`, `fchown`, `fchownat`, `lchown`).
12484    ///
12485    /// Detcore presents a fixed virtual-root identity, so the *permission*
12486    /// answer must be the one a real root gets: success, for any uid. But root
12487    /// privilege affects only the ownership permission check — it does not
12488    /// waive pathname, descriptor, or flag errors. A real root's
12489    /// `chown("/does/not/exist", 0, 0)` still fails with `ENOENT`.
12490    ///
12491    /// So this does not fabricate a bare `Ok(0)`. It translates the mutation
12492    /// into a side-effect-free metadata lookup with the same target-selection
12493    /// arguments, and reports success only if that lookup succeeds:
12494    ///
12495    /// * `F_GETFL` validates `fchown`'s descriptor and distinguishes an
12496    ///   `O_PATH` descriptor (valid for `fstat`, invalid for `fchown`);
12497    ///   `newfstatat` performs the corresponding path walk for the three
12498    ///   pathname variants, preserving `ENOENT`, `ENOTDIR`, `ELOOP`,
12499    ///   `ENAMETOOLONG`, `EFAULT`, and `EBADF`;
12500    /// * `fchownat` flags are checked explicitly before the lookup, so an
12501    ///   unsupported flag still returns `EINVAL` rather than being accepted by
12502    ///   a metadata syscall with a wider flag vocabulary;
12503    /// * the ownership assignment itself is not performed, but the *other*
12504    ///   consequences of a successful chown are, because Linux applies them
12505    ///   even when ownership does not change. Measured on this host with
12506    ///   `chown(path, -1, -1)`: mode `06755`, `04755` and `02755` all become
12507    ///   `0755`; `02644` keeps `S_ISGID` because the file is not
12508    ///   group-executable; a directory at `06755` keeps both bits; and ctime
12509    ///   moves in every one of those cases, including the plain `0644` file
12510    ///   with nothing to clear. Skipping that is a privilege-containment
12511    ///   regression, not a bookkeeping one: a guest that builds a setuid
12512    ///   binary and chowns it would see the setuid bit survive under hermit
12513    ///   and be cleared on the kernel.
12514    ///
12515    /// Rather than reimplement that rule, the consequence is delegated to the
12516    /// kernel by reissuing the *same* call from the same family with the
12517    /// `(-1, -1)` sentinel, which is precisely the operation whose only effects
12518    /// are `ATTR_CTIME | ATTR_KILL_SUID | ATTR_KILL_SGID`. Delegation gets the
12519    /// directory exemption, the group-executable condition on `S_ISGID`, and
12520    /// symlink handling right for free, and cannot drift from the kernel the
12521    /// way a transcribed rule would.
12522    ///
12523    /// Routed through `record_or_replay` rather than `inject`, so a replay does
12524    /// not need the guest's filesystem to still exist.
12525    ///
12526    /// **Semantic boundary, stated explicitly.** Detcore does not model
12527    /// per-file ownership, so the success is not observable through a later
12528    /// `stat`. A guest that chowns to a foreign uid and reads the owner back
12529    /// sees the unchanged owner — a divergence a single-uid container cannot
12530    /// avoid, and strictly smaller than the status quo in which the guest
12531    /// believes it is root and cannot chown at all.
12532    ///
12533    /// **Residual, also stated.** This emulates ownership permission and target
12534    /// validation, not every write-time filesystem policy. In particular a
12535    /// target on a read-only mount can pass the metadata lookup where a real
12536    /// chown would return `EROFS`. Path resolution also still requires search
12537    /// permission on the parent directories, so `EACCES` remains a function of
12538    /// the host identity under `--no-namespace`. That exposure is shared with
12539    /// every pass-through filesystem syscall (`open`, `stat`, `chmod`) and is
12540    /// not introduced here; it is recorded so the boundary is not overstated.
12541    ///
12542    /// **Residual introduced by the delegation, stated too.** The sentinel call
12543    /// needs the same `inode_owner_or_capable` permission the mode change does,
12544    /// so on a target the guest does not own it returns `EPERM` and that errno
12545    /// is propagated. Reporting a successful chown while silently failing to
12546    /// apply the consequence the kernel guarantees would be the same defect in
12547    /// a narrower form, so this fails closed instead. It is not a regression:
12548    /// that is exactly the case in which the pass-through implementation also
12549    /// returned `EPERM`. The case this change exists to fix — a guest chowning
12550    /// a file it created — is the owning case, and it succeeds.
12551    ///
12552    /// The behavioural contract is bracketed end to end by
12553    /// `hermit-cli/tests/chown_virtual_root_identity.rs`; the unit tests in
12554    /// `syscall_classification` pin membership only and cannot see this
12555    /// function's result.
12556    pub async fn handle_ownership_change_noop<G: Guest<Self>>(
12557        &self,
12558        guest: &mut G,
12559        call: Syscall,
12560    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
12561        // Unreachable while `is_ownership_change_noop_syscall` and the matches
12562        // below name the same four syscalls. Fail closed if they drift: "not
12563        // attempted" must never be observationally identical to a validated
12564        // emulated success.
12565        let ownership_change = match call {
12566            Syscall::Fchown(_) | Syscall::Fchownat(_) => true,
12567            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
12568            Syscall::Chown(_) | Syscall::Lchown(_) => true,
12569            _ => false,
12570        };
12571        if !ownership_change {
12572            warn!(
12573                "ownership-change no-op reached with an unexpected syscall {:?}; \
12574                 refusing unvalidated success",
12575                call.number()
12576            );
12577            return Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ENOSYS));
12578        }
12579
12580        // Flag errors precede path resolution in the kernel, so check first.
12581        if let Syscall::Fchownat(c) = &call {
12582            let allowed = AtFlags::AT_EMPTY_PATH | AtFlags::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW;
12583            if c.flags().bits() & !allowed.bits() != 0 {
12584                return Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EINVAL));
12585            }
12586        }
12587
12588        // Argument half. `F_GETFL` answers it for `fchown`: it validates the
12589        // descriptor and distinguishes an `O_PATH` descriptor, which `fstat`
12590        // accepts and `fchown` rejects. For the three pathname variants a
12591        // `newfstatat` with the same target-selection arguments performs the
12592        // corresponding path walk.
12593        if let Syscall::Fchown(c) = &call {
12594            let flags = self
12595                .record_or_replay(
12596                    guest,
12597                    syscalls::Fcntl::new().with_fd(c.fd()).with_cmd(F_GETFL),
12598                )
12599                .await?;
12600            if flags & i64::from(OFlag::O_PATH.bits()) != 0 {
