12601                return Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EBADF));
12602            }
12603        } else {
12604            let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
12605            let statptr: StatPtr = StatPtr(stack.reserve());
12606            stack.commit()?;
12607
12608            let validate = match &call {
12609                #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
12610                Syscall::Chown(c) => crate::arch::fstatat_syscall(
12611                    syscalls::Fstatat::new()
12612                        .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
12613                        .with_path(c.path())
12614                        .with_stat(Some(statptr))
12615                        .with_flags(AtFlags::empty()),
12616                ),
12617                #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
12618                Syscall::Lchown(c) => crate::arch::fstatat_syscall(
12619                    syscalls::Fstatat::new()
12620                        .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
12621                        .with_path(c.path())
12622                        .with_stat(Some(statptr))
12623                        .with_flags(AtFlags::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW),
12624                ),
12625                Syscall::Fchownat(c) => crate::arch::fstatat_syscall(
12626                    syscalls::Fstatat::new()
12627                        .with_dirfd(c.dirfd())
12628                        .with_path(c.path())
12629                        .with_stat(Some(statptr))
12630                        .with_flags(c.flags()),
12631                ),
12632                _ => return Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ENOSYS)),
12633            };
12634
12635            // The errno of the side-effect-free validating call is the guest's
12636            // answer; only an actually executed successful validation becomes the
12637            // emulated success. Clear the scratch output on both paths.
12638            let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, validate).await;
12639            guest
12640                .memory()
12641                .write_exact(statptr.0.cast(), &[0; std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>()])?;
12642            result?;
12643        }
12644
12645        // Metadata half, delegated to the kernel. The identity assignment is
12646        // deliberately not performed, but everything else a successful chown
12647        // does is, by reissuing the same call with the `(-1, -1)` sentinel:
12648        // clear `S_ISUID`, clear `S_ISGID` on a group-executable file, exempt
12649        // directories, and move ctime unconditionally. Letting Linux apply its
12650        // own rule keeps it from drifting here.
12651        const KEEP_ID: libc::uid_t = libc::uid_t::MAX;
12652        let consequence = match &call {
12653            Syscall::Fchown(c) => Syscall::Fchown(
12654                syscalls::Fchown::new()
12655                    .with_fd(c.fd())
12656                    .with_owner(KEEP_ID)
12657                    .with_group(KEEP_ID),
12658            ),
12659            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
12660            Syscall::Chown(c) => Syscall::Chown(
12661                syscalls::Chown::new()
12662                    .with_path(c.path())
12663                    .with_owner(KEEP_ID)
12664                    .with_group(KEEP_ID),
12665            ),
12666            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
12667            Syscall::Lchown(c) => Syscall::Lchown(
12668                syscalls::Lchown::new()
12669                    .with_path(c.path())
12670                    .with_owner(KEEP_ID)
12671                    .with_group(KEEP_ID),
12672            ),
12673            Syscall::Fchownat(c) => Syscall::Fchownat(
12674                syscalls::Fchownat::new()
12675                    .with_dirfd(c.dirfd())
12676                    .with_path(c.path())
12677                    .with_owner(KEEP_ID)
12678                    .with_group(KEEP_ID)
12679                    .with_flags(c.flags()),
12680            ),
12681            _ => return Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ENOSYS)),
12682        };
12683        self.record_or_replay(guest, consequence).await?;
12684        Ok(0)
12685    }
12686
12687    /// Overwrite the host-varying fields of a `statfs` result buffer with fixed
12688    /// values, leaving the static per-mount geometry intact. Shared by statfs
12689    /// and fstatfs. A null buffer (only possible on an error return, which the
12690    /// caller has already propagated) is a no-op.
12691    fn canonicalize_statfs_buf<G: Guest<Self>>(
12692        &self,
12693        guest: &mut G,
12694        buf: Option<AddrMut<libc::statfs>>,
12695    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
12696        // Fixed *caps* for the volatile counters. The exact values are
12697        // arbitrary; they only need to be constant so repeated runs agree. We
12698        // clamp each free count to the mount's (static) total so we never report
12699        // the impossible "free > total": a filesystem may be smaller than the
12700        // cap, and some (e.g. overlayfs) report no inode accounting at all
12701        // (`f_files == 0`).
12702        const FREE_BLOCKS_CAP: libc::fsblkcnt_t = 1_000_000;
12703        const FREE_INODES_CAP: libc::fsfilcnt_t = 500_000;
12704
12705        if let Some(buf) = buf {
12706            let mut sf = guest.memory().read_value(buf)?;
12707            let free_blocks = FREE_BLOCKS_CAP.min(sf.f_blocks);
12708            sf.f_bfree = free_blocks;
12709            sf.f_bavail = free_blocks;
12710            // `f_files == 0` means the filesystem does not track inodes; keep the
12711            // free count at 0 rather than inventing free inodes on a mount that
12712            // reports none.
12713            sf.f_ffree = if sf.f_files == 0 {
12714                0
12715            } else {
12716                FREE_INODES_CAP.min(sf.f_files)
12717            };
12718            // f_fsid is a device-dependent filesystem identifier; zero it. An
12719            // all-zero bit pattern is a valid `fsid_t` (a POD id pair).
12720            sf.f_fsid = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
12721            guest.memory().write_value(buf, &sf)?;
12722        }
12723        Ok(())
12724    }
12725
12726    /// dup system call.
12727    pub async fn handle_dup<G: Guest<Self>>(
12728        &self,
12729        guest: &mut G,
12730        call: syscalls::Dup,
12731    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
12732        let old_fd = call.oldfd();
12733        let new_fd = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await? as RawFd;
12734        let lock_tracked = self.lock_tracked_descriptions(guest, new_fd..=new_fd);
12735        let replaced = guest
12736            .thread_state_mut()
12737            .dup_fd(old_fd, new_fd, OFlag::empty())?;
12738        if let Some(open_file_id) = replaced {
12739            self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
12740        }
12741        self.report_lock_references(guest, lock_tracked).await;
12742        Ok(new_fd as i64)
12743    }
12744
12745    /// dup2 system call.
12746    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
12747    pub async fn handle_dup2<G: Guest<Self>>(
12748        &self,
12749        guest: &mut G,
12750        call: syscalls::Dup2,
12751    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
12752        let old_fd = call.oldfd();
12753        let new_fd = call.newfd();
12754        if let Some(refusal) = self
12755            .refuse_dup_over_waited_listener(guest, Sysno::dup2, old_fd, new_fd)
12756            .await
12757        {
12758            return refusal;
12759        }
12760        // `dup2` over another open descriptor closes it.
12761        let closed_end = (old_fd != new_fd)
12762            .then(|| self.pipe_channel_end(guest, new_fd))
12763            .flatten();
12764        let res = self
12765            .record_or_replay(guest, call)
12766            .await
12767            .inspect_err(|errno| Self::note_failed_dup(guest, old_fd, new_fd, *errno))?;
12768        // Reported as soon as the kernel replaced `new_fd`, before Detcore's
12769        // own table update, which can still fail for a descriptor it does not
12770        // track (`Scheduler::note_descriptors_replaced`).
12771        if old_fd != new_fd
12772            && let Ok(new_fd) = u32::try_from(new_fd)
12773        {
12774            crate::tool_global::descriptors_replaced(guest, new_fd, new_fd).await;
12775        }
12776        let lock_tracked = if old_fd == new_fd {
12777            Vec::new()
12778        } else {
12779            self.lock_tracked_descriptions(guest, new_fd..=new_fd)
12780        };
12781        let replaced = self
12782            .dup_fd_after_replacement(guest, old_fd, new_fd, OFlag::empty(), lock_tracked.clone())
12783            .await?;
12784        if let Some(open_file_id) = replaced {
12785            self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
12786        }
12787        self.report_lock_references(guest, lock_tracked).await;
12788        self.note_channel_end_closed(guest, closed_end).await;
12789        Ok(res)
12790    }
12791
12792    /// A `dup2` or `dup3` of `old_fd` to `new_fd` that failed with `errno`:
12793    /// one that failed with `EBADF` for an old descriptor that is not open
12794    /// grew the table to hold `new_fd` first, as `ksys_dup3` expands it
12795    /// before it looks `old_fd` up
12796    /// (<https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.17/fs/file.c#L1408-L1415>),
12797    /// unless `new_fd` was at or above `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, which it refuses
12798    /// first (`ThreadState::note_failed_dup_target`). The flags, and the same
12799    /// descriptor twice, are refused before (`EINVAL`).
12800    fn note_failed_dup<G: Guest<Self>>(guest: &G, old_fd: RawFd, new_fd: RawFd, errno: Errno) {
12801        if errno == Errno::EBADF && old_fd != new_fd {
12802            guest.thread_state().note_failed_dup_target(new_fd);
12803        }
12804    }
12805
12806    /// Detcore's table update after the kernel's `dup2` or `dup3` put
12807    /// `old_fd`'s description in slot `new_fd`. If Detcore keeps no model of
12808    /// `old_fd` (one received over `SCM_RIGHTS` and not recorded,
12809    /// `Detcore::record_received_descriptors`), the update fails,
12810    /// but the kernel replaced the slot all the same: its old description is
12811    /// dropped from the model and `lock_tracked` (what the slot named) is
12812    /// reported to `procfs::locks::LockLedger`, so no stale entry can admit
12813    /// a host's identical `/proc/locks` row. The error is returned as before.
12814    async fn dup_fd_after_replacement<G: Guest<Self>>(
12815        &self,
12816        guest: &mut G,
12817        old_fd: RawFd,
12818        new_fd: RawFd,
12819        flags: OFlag,
12820        lock_tracked: Vec<OpenFileId>,
12821    ) -> Result<Option<OpenFileId>, Error> {
12822        match guest.thread_state_mut().dup_fd(old_fd, new_fd, flags) {
12823            Ok(replaced) => Ok(replaced),
12824            Err(errno) => {
12825                if old_fd != new_fd {
12826                    let displaced = guest.thread_state().remove_fd(new_fd);
12827                    if let Some(open_file_id) = displaced {
12828                        self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
12829                    }
12830                    self.report_lock_references(guest, lock_tracked).await;
12831                }
12832                Err(errno.into())
12833            }
12834        }
12835    }
12836
12837    /// Refuse a `dup2` or `dup3` that would close `new_fd` while a blocking
12838    /// accept waits on it. With `old_fd == new_fd` neither call closes
12839    /// anything. The check comes before the call, so a call that would fail
12840    /// for another reason (a bad `old_fd`) is refused as well.
12841    async fn refuse_dup_over_waited_listener<G: Guest<Self>>(
12842        &self,
12843        guest: &mut G,
12844        sysno: Sysno,
12845        old_fd: RawFd,
12846        new_fd: RawFd,
12847    ) -> Option<Result<i64, Error>> {
12848        if old_fd == new_fd {
12849            return None;
12850        }
12851        let new_fd = u32::try_from(new_fd).ok()?;
12852        self.refuse_close_of_waited_listener(guest, sysno, new_fd..=new_fd)
12853            .await
12854    }
12855
12856    /// dup3 system call.
12857    pub async fn handle_dup3<G: Guest<Self>>(
12858        &self,
12859        guest: &mut G,
12860        call: syscalls::Dup3,
12861    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
12862        let old_fd = call.oldfd();
12863        let new_fd = call.newfd();
12864        let flags = call.flags();
12865        if let Some(refusal) = self
12866            .refuse_dup_over_waited_listener(guest, Sysno::dup3, old_fd, new_fd)
12867            .await
12868        {
12869            return refusal;
12870        }
12871        // `dup3` over another open descriptor closes it.
12872        let closed_end = (old_fd != new_fd)
12873            .then(|| self.pipe_channel_end(guest, new_fd))
12874            .flatten();
12875        let res = self
12876            .record_or_replay(guest, call)
12877            .await
12878            .inspect_err(|errno| Self::note_failed_dup(guest, old_fd, new_fd, *errno))?;
12879        // Reported before Detcore's own table update, as for `dup2`.
12880        if let Ok(new_fd) = u32::try_from(new_fd) {
12881            crate::tool_global::descriptors_replaced(guest, new_fd, new_fd).await;
12882        }
12883        let lock_tracked = self.lock_tracked_descriptions(guest, new_fd..=new_fd);
12884        let replaced = self
12885            .dup_fd_after_replacement(guest, old_fd, new_fd, flags, lock_tracked.clone())
12886            .await?;
12887        if let Some(open_file_id) = replaced {
12888            self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
12889        }
12890        self.report_lock_references(guest, lock_tracked).await;
12891        self.note_channel_end_closed(guest, closed_end).await;
12892        Ok(res)
12893    }
12894
12895    /// pipe2 system call.
12896    pub async fn handle_pipe2<G: Guest<Self>>(
12897        &self,
12898        guest: &mut G,
12899        call: syscalls::Pipe2,
12900    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
12901        // Pipes are unambiguously container-internal: both endpoints are owned by
12902        // guest processes. Make them physically nonblocking whenever we sequentialize
12903        // threads -- INCLUDING record/replay modes. This lets a potentially-blocking
12904        // pipe read follow the deterministic nonblockize-and-retry (InternalIOPolling)
12905        // path instead of being descheduled as BlockingExternalIO. A pipe reader and
12906        // its paired writer are NOT independent, so treating an internal pipe as
12907        // "external blocking IO" (safe to run in the background and rejoin whenever)
12908        // deadlocks the sequentialized scheduler in R/R (the documented pipe hang). The
12909        // physical O_NONBLOCK is Detcore-internal and invisible to the guest (F_GETFL is
12910        // virtualized), and mirrors what `hermit run --strict` already does for pipes.
12911        let internally_nonblocking = self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets();
12912        let injected = if internally_nonblocking {
12913            call.with_flags(call.flags() | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK)
12914        } else {
12915            call
12916        };
12917        // NO PRE-CALL READ OF `pipefd`. This is load-bearing on three backends, not a style
12918        // choice. `record_or_replay` below returns early on failure, so every guest memory
12919        // access AFTER it runs only when pipe2 SUCCEEDED -- and a successful pipe2 means the
12920        // kernel itself wrote two ints there, which proves the address valid. A pre-call
12921        // snapshot would be the only access to a kernel-UNVALIDATED address, and `LocalMemory`
12922        // (reverie-dbt, reverie-e9patch, reverie-liteinst) implements reads as an unsafe
12923        // `copy_nonoverlapping` that always returns `Ok`: a bad pointer is a hardware fault
12924        // that `Result::ok` cannot catch, so the guest would die with SIGSEGV before Linux
12925        // could report EFAULT. Letting the kernel touch `pipefd` first is also what keeps its
12926        // argument-validation precedence intact -- flags are checked before the pointer, so a
12927        // bad pointer with bad flags is EINVAL and with good flags EFAULT.
12928        // A C guest asserting that precedence directly is being added separately.
12929        let res = self.record_or_replay(guest, injected).await?;
12930        let memory = guest.memory();
12931
12932        if let Some(pipefd) = call.pipefd() {
12933            let fds: [i32; 2] = memory.read_value(pipefd)?;
12934            if internally_nonblocking {
12935                // Where host load decides a new pipe's size, no pin is the same in every
12936                // run, even one that happens to succeed (a pipe created under the quota
12937                // already has two pages).
12938                let capacity_result = if host_pipe_floor() {
12939                    guest
12940                        .inject(
12941                            syscalls::Fcntl::new()
12942                                .with_fd(fds[0])
12943                                .with_cmd(F_SETPIPE_SZ(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes())),
12944                        )
12945                        .await
12946                } else {
12947                    error!(
12948                        "{}",
12949                        below_two_page_pipe_floor("a new pipe cannot be pinned")
12950                    );
12951                    Err(Errno::EPERM)
12952                };
12953                if let Some(failure) = pipe_capacity_failure(fds, capacity_result) {
12954                    // Release the descriptors Linux already created, THEN stop the run.
12955                    //
12956                    // Returning `Err` here -- what this code did before -- unwinds without
12957                    // closing them. `pipe2` has already succeeded, so both descriptors are
12958                    // live in the guest and are not yet registered with `add_fd`, which means
12959                    // Detcore's own bookkeeping never learns they exist. Closing them is the
12960                    // only way the guest's descriptor table matches Detcore's model.
12961                    //
12962                    // We do NOT fabricate a `pipe2` errno. Linux leaves `pipefd` untouched
12963                    // when `pipe2` fails, so inventing a failure would oblige us to restore
12964                    // the caller's buffer, which needs the pre-call snapshot the comment above
12965                    // explains we must never take. And returning success with an unpinned pipe
12966                    // silently restores exactly the host-dependent capacity this path exists
12967                    // to remove. An unpinnable pipe means determinism is unavailable for this
12968                    // run, so fail closed and loudly rather than quietly.
12969                    //
12970                    // Defensive, not expected: pinning on a freshly created EMPTY pipe is a
12971                    // shrink or a no-op. EBUSY needs buffered data and EPERM needs to exceed
12972                    // `pipe-max-size`; neither can hold here (below a two-page
12973                    // `pipe-max-size` the pin is refused before it is tried).
12974                    for close in failure.close_syscalls() {
12975                        let _ = guest.inject(close).await;
12976                    }
12977                    error!(
12978                        "[detcore] cannot pin scheduler-managed pipe to {} bytes (fds {:?}): {}. \
12979                         Determinism is unavailable for this run.",
12980                        deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes(),
12981                        failure.created_fds,
12982                        failure.error,
12983                    );
12984                    // Fail-closed policy: determinism is unavailable for this run.
12985                    unrecoverable_shutdown(guest, detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT).await;
12986                }
12987            }
12988            self.add_fd(guest, fds[0], call.flags(), FdType::Pipe)
12989                .await?;
12990            self.add_fd(guest, fds[1], call.flags(), FdType::Pipe)
12991                .await?;
12992            // The guest holds both ends (`DetFd::is_guest_held`).
12993            for fd in fds {
12994                guest
12995                    .thread_state()
12996                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_guest_held())?;
12997            }
12998            if internally_nonblocking {
12999                self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fds[0]);
13000                self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fds[1]);
13001            }
13002            // Both ends name the pipe by the read end's open file description,
13003            // for `--pipe-wake-latency` only (`crate::pipe_wake`).
13004            if self.cfg.pipe_wake_latency_in_effect().is_some() {
13005                let read_end = guest
13006                    .thread_state()
13007                    .with_detfd(fds[0], |detfd| detfd.open_file_id())?;
13008                let channel = crate::pipe_wake::ChannelId::Pipe(read_end);
13009                for (fd, reads) in [(fds[0], true), (fds[1], false)] {
13010                    let end = crate::pipe_wake::ChannelEnd {
13011                        channel,
13012                        reads,
13013                        writes: !reads,
13014                    };
13015                    guest
13016                        .thread_state()
13017                        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_channel(end))?;
13018                }
13019            }
13020        }
13021
13022        Ok(res)
13023    }
13024
13025    /// utime syscall: update access/modification time on a file
13026    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
13027    pub async fn handle_utime<G: Guest<Self>>(
13028        &self,
13029        guest: &mut G,
13030        call: syscalls::Utime,
13031    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
13032        let times = match call.times() {
13033            None => {
13034                let now: Timespec = thread_observe_time(guest).await.into();
13035                [now, now]
13036            }
13037            Some(times) => {
13038                let utimbuf = guest.memory().read_value(times)?;
13039                [
13040                    Timespec {
13041                        tv_sec: utimbuf.actime,
13042                        tv_nsec: 0,
13043                    },
13044                    Timespec {
13045                        tv_sec: utimbuf.modtime,
13046                        tv_nsec: 0,
13047                    },
13048                ]
13049            }
13050        };
13051
13052        let utimensat = syscalls::Utimensat::new()
13053            .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
13054            .with_path(call.path());
13055
13056        self.set_file_times(guest, utimensat, Some(times)).await
13057    }
13058
13059    /// utimes syscall
13060    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
13061    pub async fn handle_utimes<G: Guest<Self>>(
13062        &self,
13063        guest: &mut G,
13064        call: syscalls::Utimes,
13065    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
13066        let utimensat = syscalls::Utimensat::new()
13067            .with_dirfd(libc::AT_FDCWD)
13068            .with_path(call.filename());
13069
13070        match call.times() {
13071            None => {
13072                let now: Timespec = thread_observe_time(guest).await.into();
13073                self.set_file_times(guest, utimensat, Some([now, now]))
13074                    .await
13075            }
13076            Some(times) => {
13077                // Convert the timeval array to a timespec array.
13078                let mut memory = guest.memory();
13079                let tvs = memory.read_value(times)?;
13080                let tp: Addr<[Timespec; 2]> = times.cast();
13081
13082                // Safety: The address could point to read-only memory and the
13083                // write below could fail.
13084                let tp = unsafe { tp.into_mut() };
13085
13086                memory.write_value(tp, &[tvs[0].into(), tvs[1].into()])?;
13087                self.set_file_times(guest, utimensat.with_times(Some(tp.into())), None)
13088                    .await
13089            }
13090        }
13091    }

13093    /// ustimensat syscall
13094    pub async fn handle_utimensat<G: Guest<Self>>(
13095        &self,
13096        guest: &mut G,
13097        call: syscalls::Utimensat,
13098    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
13099        self.set_file_times(guest, call, None).await
13100    }
13101
13102    /// Performs a utimensat call and copies the mtime it sets into the virtual
13103    /// mtime. With `staged` the times are first pushed onto the guest's scratch
13104    /// stack and replace the call's `times` pointer; utime and utimes(NULL)
13105    /// build their times that way.
13106    async fn set_file_times<G: Guest<Self>>(
13107        &self,
13108        guest: &mut G,
13109        call: syscalls::Utimensat,
13110        staged: Option<[Timespec; 2]>,
13111    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
13112        if !guest.config().virtualize_metadata {
13113            return self.utimensat_without_lookup(guest, call, staged).await;
13114        }
13115        // Without thread sequentialization another guest thread can swap the
13116        // target away and back around the call, so that both lookups name a
13117        // file the kernel did not update. No lookup can tell the two apart,
13118        // so the virtual mtime is left alone.
13119        if !guest.config().sequentialize_threads {
13120            return self.utimensat_without_lookup(guest, call, staged).await;
13121        }
13122        // The scratch stack starts 128 bytes below the stack pointer and its
13123        // addresses are computed by subtraction, so a stack pointer too close
13124        // to zero to hold the staged times and the lookup buffer would stop
13125        // Hermit rather than reach Linux.
13126        let scratch = 128
13127            + staged.map_or(0, |_| std::mem::size_of::<[Timespec; 2]>())
13128            + std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>();
13129        if usize::try_from(crate::arch::stack_pointer(&guest.regs().await))
13130            .map_or(true, |rsp| rsp <= scratch)
13131        {
13132            info!(
13133                "Guest stack pointer cannot hold the utimensat target lookup; \
13134                 leaving the virtual mtime unchanged."
13135            );
13136            return self.utimensat_without_lookup(guest, call, staged).await;
13137        }
13138
13139        // The staged times and the buffer for the target lookups share one
13140        // scratch stack, and its guard is held until the last injected syscall
13141        // has run, so that neither the kernel's read of the times nor a lookup
13142        // finds the other's bytes, or a restored stack, at its address.
13143        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
13144        let staged_call = match staged {
13145            Some(times) => call.with_times(Some(stack.push(times))),
13146            None => call,
13147        };
13148        let statptr: StatPtr = StatPtr(stack.reserve());
13149        // The scratch stack lies below the guest's red zone, where a raw
13150        // syscall may keep its own path or times. Writing the lookup buffer
13151        // over either would change the call before Linux reads it.
13152        if utimensat_input_overlaps(&guest.memory(), &call, staged.is_none(), statptr) {
13153            info!(
13154                "utimensat inputs overlap the target lookup buffer; \
13155                 leaving the virtual mtime unchanged."
13156            );
13157            drop(stack);
13158            return self.utimensat_without_lookup(guest, call, staged).await;
13159        }
13160        // The buffer's address range can still share its pages with guest data
13161        // through a second shared mapping, which no address comparison sees.
13162        // Its bytes are saved here and put back after the commit and after
13163        // each lookup, so the lookups and the call read their inputs unchanged
13164        // and the guest keeps its memory.
13165        let mut saved = [0u8; std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>()];
13166        if guest
13167            .memory()
13168            .read_exact(statptr.0.cast(), &mut saved)
13169            .is_err()
13170        {
13171            info!(
13172                "Guest stack scratch cannot hold the utimensat target lookup; \
13173                 leaving the virtual mtime unchanged."
13174            );
13175            drop(stack);
13176            return self.utimensat_without_lookup(guest, call, staged).await;
13177        }
13178        let _guard = match stack.commit() {
13179            Ok(guard) => guard,
13180            // The lookup buffer only serves the virtual update, so a scratch
13181            // stack that cannot hold it, for example one next to the guard
13182            // page, must not keep the guest's own call from reaching Linux.
13183            // The commit writes page by page, so it can fail after writing a
13184            // lower writable page; those bytes are put back first.
13185            Err(_) => {
13186                info!(
13187                    "Guest stack scratch cannot hold the utimensat target lookup; \
13188                     leaving the virtual mtime unchanged."
13189                );
13190                restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
13191                return self.utimensat_without_lookup(guest, call, staged).await;
13192            }
13193        };
13194        restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
13195        let call = staged_call;
13196
13197        // The kernel applies the new times to the real file, but the guest
13198        // observes the virtual mtime, which otherwise only moves on writes. Copy
13199        // the requested mtime into it so that `tar` extraction, `cp -p` and
13200        // `touch -r` restore a file's mtime and `make` compares the times the
13201        // build asked for rather than the order in which files were unpacked.
13202        //
13203        // Nothing below may change the syscall's result: an unreadable `times`
13204        // or a failed lookup only skips the virtual update, and the kernel
13205        // reports its own error for the call itself.
13206        let mtime = match (staged, call.times()) {
13207            (Some([_, mtime]), _) => Some(mtime),
13208            (None, None) => Some(Timespec {
13209                tv_sec: 0,
13210                tv_nsec: libc::UTIME_NOW,
13211            }),
13212            (None, Some(times)) => guest
13213                .memory()
13214                .read_value(times)
13215                .ok()
13216                .map(|[_, mtime]| mtime),
13217        }
13218        .filter(|mtime| mtime.tv_nsec != libc::UTIME_OMIT);
13219        let before = match mtime {
13220            Some(_) => self.utimensat_target(guest, &call, statptr).await,
13221            None => None,
13222        };
13223        restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
13224
13225        let res = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
13226
13227        // Update only the inode the kernel modified. No other guest thread
13228        // runs during the call, but a process outside the container can still
13229        // rename, unlink or replace the target; the target is resolved before
13230        // and after the call, and the update is skipped unless both name the
13231        // same file. Equal lookups alone do not show that the kernel updated
13232        // that file: the name may have been swapped away and back during the
13233        // call, or an inode number reused. So an explicit mtime is copied only
13234        // when the file holds it, truncated to the filesystem's granularity,
13235        // and the virtual mtime takes the value the kernel stored, which is
13236        // what stat reports on Linux. `UTIME_NOW` has no such witness.
13237        let (Some(mtime), Some(before)) = (mtime, before) else {
13238            return Ok(res);
13239        };
13240        let after = self.utimensat_target(guest, &call, statptr).await;
13241        restore_lookup_buffer(&mut guest.memory(), statptr, &saved);
13242        let Some(after) = after else {
13243            return Ok(res);
13244        };
13245        if (after.st_dev, after.st_ino) != (before.st_dev, before.st_ino) {
13246            return Ok(res);
13247        }
13248        if mtime.tv_nsec == libc::UTIME_NOW {
13249            touch_file(guest, RawInode::new(after.st_dev, after.st_ino)).await;
13250            return Ok(res);
13251        }
13252        const NANOS_PER_SEC: i128 = 1_000_000_000;
13253        let requested = i128::from(mtime.tv_sec) * NANOS_PER_SEC + i128::from(mtime.tv_nsec);
13254        let stored = i128::from(after.st_mtime) * NANOS_PER_SEC + i128::from(after.st_mtime_nsec);
13255        // Linux truncates the requested time down to the filesystem's
13256        // granularity, at most a second on the filesystems builds use.
13257        if (0..NANOS_PER_SEC).contains(&(requested - stored)) {
13258            let nanos = u64::try_from(stored.max(0)).unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
13259            set_file_mtime(
13260                guest,
13261                RawInode::new(after.st_dev, after.st_ino),
13262                LogicalTime::from_nanos(nanos),
13263            )
13264            .await;
13265        }
13266        Ok(res)
13267    }
13268
13269    /// Performs a utimensat call without the virtual mtime update. Staged
13270    /// times are then the only scratch-stack allocation, as they were before
13271    /// the update existed.
13272    async fn utimensat_without_lookup<G: Guest<Self>>(
13273        &self,
13274        guest: &mut G,
13275        call: syscalls::Utimensat,
13276        staged: Option<[Timespec; 2]>,
13277    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
13278        let Some(times) = staged else {
13279            return self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await;
13280        };
13281        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
13282        let call = call.with_times(Some(stack.push(times)));
13283        let _guard = stack.commit()?;
13284        self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await
13285    }
13286
13287    /// The metadata of the file a utimensat call targets, with the same target
13288    /// selection: the descriptor itself for `futimens` (a NULL path), else a
13289    /// path walk honoring the flags utimensat accepts. `None` if the lookup
13290    /// fails.
13291    async fn utimensat_target<G: Guest<Self>>(
13292        &self,
13293        guest: &mut G,
13294        call: &syscalls::Utimensat,
13295        statptr: StatPtr<'_>,
13296    ) -> Option<libc::stat> {
13297        let lookup = match call.path() {
13298            None => Syscall::Fstat(
13299                syscalls::Fstat::new()
13300                    .with_fd(call.dirfd())
13301                    .with_stat(Some(statptr)),
13302            ),
13303            Some(path) => {
13304                let allowed = libc::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW | libc::AT_EMPTY_PATH;
13305                crate::arch::fstatat_syscall(
13306                    syscalls::Fstatat::new()
13307                        .with_dirfd(call.dirfd())
13308                        .with_path(Some(path))
13309                        .with_stat(Some(statptr))
13310                        .with_flags(AtFlags::from_bits_truncate(call.flags() & allowed)),
13311                )
13312            }
13313        };
13314        self.record_or_replay(guest, lookup).await.ok()?;
13315        statptr.read(&guest.memory()).ok()
13316    }
13317
13318    /// socket system call.
13319    pub async fn handle_socket<G: Guest<Self>>(
13320        &self,
13321        guest: &mut G,
13322        call: syscalls::Socket,
13323    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
13324        // The socket syscall itself is not blocking, but we must decide whether to make the socket
13325        // returned physically nonblocking.
13326        if !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads || self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
13327            // Allow possibly blocking syscall in record mode
13328            let fd = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await? as RawFd;
13329            self.add_fd(
13330                guest,
13331                fd,
13332                OFlag::from_bits_truncate(call.r#type()),
13333                FdType::Socket,
13334            )
13335            .await?;
13336            self.mark_sock_diag_fd(guest, fd, &call);
13337            self.note_unix_socket(guest, fd, call.family(), call.r#type());
13338            self.mark_error_queue_reads(guest, fd, &call)?;
13339            // Linux's SOCK_TYPE_MASK: the type without SOCK_NONBLOCK and SOCK_CLOEXEC.
13340            const SOCK_TYPE_MASK: i32 = 0xf;
13341            if self.accept_in_turn_enabled() && call.r#type() & SOCK_TYPE_MASK == libc::SOCK_STREAM
13342            {
13343                guest
13344                    .thread_state()
13345                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_accept_in_turn_eligible())?;
13346            }
13347            Ok(fd as i64)
13348        } else {
13349            // Under run mode, force all sockets to be registered to be nonblocking in the OS:
13350            let call2 = if self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets() {
13351                call.with_type(call.r#type() | libc::SOCK_NONBLOCK)
13352            } else {
13353                call
13354            };
13355            let fd = self.record_or_replay(guest, call2).await? as RawFd; // Cannot hang.
13356            self.add_fd(
13357                guest,
13358                fd,
13359                OFlag::from_bits_truncate(
13360                    call.r#type() & (libc::SOCK_NONBLOCK | libc::SOCK_CLOEXEC),
13361                ),
13362                FdType::Socket,
13363            )
13364            .await?;
13365            self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fd);
13366            self.mark_sock_diag_fd(guest, fd, &call);
13367            self.note_unix_socket(guest, fd, call.family(), call.r#type());
13368            self.mark_error_queue_reads(guest, fd, &call)?;
13369
13370            Ok(fd as i64)
13371        }
13372    }
13373
13374    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
13375    /// Whether record/replay runs a blocking `accept(2)` on a stream socket
13376    /// the container created in the caller's turn
13377    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3880). The temporary
13378    /// `O_NONBLOCK` around each attempt goes through Detcore's own copy of the
13379    /// listener (`AcceptBracket`), which needs a tool outside the guest's
13380    /// descriptor table, as under ptrace.
13381    pub(crate) fn accept_in_turn_enabled(&self) -> bool {
13382        self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
13383            && self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets()
13384            && !self.cfg.backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table
13385    }
13386
13387    /// Record whether a receive with `MSG_ERRQUEUE` on the socket `call`
13388    /// created never waits (`crate::fd::error_queue_read_never_waits`), so that
13389    /// such a receive runs once even on a socket the guest left blocking.
13390    fn mark_error_queue_reads<G: Guest<Self>>(
13391        &self,
13392        guest: &mut G,

13426                .thread_state()

13431    /// socketpair system call.
13432    pub async fn handle_socketpair<G: Guest<Self>>(
13433        &self,
13434        guest: &mut G,
13435        call: syscalls::Socketpair,
13436    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
13437        let call2 = if self.cfg.sequentialize_threads && !self.cfg.debug_externalize_sockets {
13438            call.with_type(call.r#type() | libc::SOCK_NONBLOCK)
13439        } else {
13440            call
13441        };
13442        let res = self.record_or_replay(guest, call2).await?;
13443        if let Some(usockvec) = call.usockvec() {
13444            let memory = guest.memory();
13445            let fds: [i32; 2] = memory.read_value(usockvec)?;
13446
13447            // Logical flags are as requested:
13448            self.add_fd(
13449                guest,
13450                fds[0],
13451                OFlag::from_bits_truncate(
13452                    call.r#type() & (libc::SOCK_NONBLOCK | libc::SOCK_CLOEXEC),
13453                ),
13454                FdType::Socket,
13455            )
13456            .await?;
13457            self.add_fd(
13458                guest,
13459                fds[1],
13460                OFlag::from_bits_truncate(
13461                    call.r#type() & (libc::SOCK_NONBLOCK | libc::SOCK_CLOEXEC),
13462                ),
13463                FdType::Socket,
13464            )
13465            .await?;
13466
13467            // Both endpoints are container-internal by construction: socketpair(2)
13468            // creates the pair itself, so no peer outside the container can ever
13469            // hold one. Record that here, at the only point where it is known,
13470            // so potentially-blocking I/O on them takes the same
13471            // nonblockize-and-retry path as a pipe rather than being treated as
13472            // external blocking I/O against an fd Detcore just made SOCK_NONBLOCK.
13473            // See `syscall_targets_internal_fd`. Only when the endpoints really
13474            // are physically nonblocking, which is the same condition as `call2`
13475            // above: under `debug_externalize_sockets` they stay external.
13476            if self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets() {
13477                // The guest holds both ends of a stream or seqpacket pair
13478                // (`DetFd::is_guest_held`). A datagram end is not marked: it can
13479                // gain an address, from `bind` or autobind (`SO_PASSCRED`), and
13480                // then receive from any process once its peer is gone.
13481                let kind = call.r#type() & !(libc::SOCK_NONBLOCK | libc::SOCK_CLOEXEC);
13482                let connection = kind == libc::SOCK_STREAM || kind == libc::SOCK_SEQPACKET;
13483                for fd in fds {
13484                    let _ = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
13485                        detfd.set_socketpair_endpoint();
13486                        if connection {
13487                            detfd.set_guest_held();
13488                        }
13489                    });
13490                }
13491            }
13492            self.note_socketpair(guest, fds, call.family(), call.r#type());
13493
13494            self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fds[0]);
13495            self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fds[1]);
13496        }
13497        Ok(res)
13498    }

13509    /// from the same guest memory in both phases.

13511        &self,

13513        call: syscalls::Setsockopt,
13514    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {

13518            && call.level() == libc::SOL_SOCKET
13519            && matches!(call.optname(), libc::SO_RCVTIMEO | SO_RCVTIMEO_NEW))
13520        .then(|| {

13522            call.optval()
13523                .and_then(|value| {
13524                    guest
13525                        .memory()
13526                        .read_value::<_, libc::timeval>(value.cast())
13527                        .ok()
13528                })
13529                .map_or(ReceiveTimeout::Unknown, ReceiveTimeout::set_by)
13530        });
13531        let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
13532        if let Some(timeout) = receive_timeout {
13533            let _ = guest
13534                .thread_state()
13535                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.set_receive_timeout(timeout));
13536        }
13537        Ok(result)
13538    }

13575    /// Return an option value from a tracked socket. Hermit only promises normal

13578    pub async fn handle_getsockopt<G: Guest<Self>>(
13579        &self,

13581        call: syscalls::Getsockopt,

13589                if fd_type == FdType::Socket {
13590                    call.optlen()
13591                        .map(|length| guest.memory().read_value(length))
13592                        .transpose()?

13594                    None
13595                }
13596            } else {
13597                None
13598            };

13600        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-886): Review deterministic SO_COOKIE identities.
13601        let deterministic_cookie =
13602            if call.level() == libc::SOL_SOCKET && call.optname() == libc::SO_COOKIE {
13603                let requested_length = call
13604                    .optlen()
13605                    .map(|length| guest.memory().read_value(length))
13606                    .transpose()?;
13607                let open_file_id = guest
13608                    .thread_state()
13609                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.open_file_id())?;
13610                Some((open_file_id.deterministic_socket_cookie(), requested_length))
13611            } else {
13612                None
13613            };
13614
13615        let result = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?;
13616
13617        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-898): Hermit exposes one virtual CPU, so do not
13618        // leak the host CPU that processed a socket's most recent packet.
13619        if result == 0
13620            && call.level() == libc::SOL_SOCKET
13621            && call.optname() == libc::SO_INCOMING_CPU
13622            && let (Some(optval), Some(optlen)) = (call.optval(), call.optlen())
13623        {
13624            let returned_len: libc::socklen_t = guest.memory().read_value(optlen)?;
13625            let zero_cpu = 0_i32.to_ne_bytes();
13626            let returned_len = (returned_len as usize).min(zero_cpu.len());
13627            guest
13628                .memory()
13629                .write_exact(optval.cast::<u8>(), &zero_cpu[..returned_len])?;
13630        }
13631        if result == 0
13632            && call.level() == libc::IPPROTO_TCP
13633            && call.optname() == libc::TCP_INFO
13634            && let (Some(optval), Some(optlen)) = (call.optval(), call.optlen())

13636            let returned_len: libc::socklen_t = guest.memory().read_value(optlen)?;
13637            let mut info = vec![0; returned_len as usize];
13638            let optval = optval.cast::<u8>();
13639            guest.memory().read_exact(optval, info.as_mut_slice())?;
13640            canonicalize_tcp_info(&mut info);
13641            guest.memory().write_exact(optval, info.as_slice())?;
13642        }
13643        if let Some(requested_length) = requested_length
13644            && let Some(value) = call.optval()
13645        {
13646            let bytes = DETERMINISTIC_NETNS_COOKIE.to_ne_bytes();
13647            let write_length = (requested_length as usize).min(bytes.len());
13648            guest
13649                .memory()
13650                .write_exact(value.cast(), &bytes[..write_length])?;
13651        }
13652        if let Some((cookie, Some(requested_length))) = deterministic_cookie
13653            && let Some(value) = call.optval()
13654        {
13655            let bytes = cookie.to_ne_bytes();
13656            let write_length = (requested_length as usize).min(bytes.len());
13657            guest
13658                .memory()
13659                .write_exact(value.cast(), &bytes[..write_length])?;

13665    /// Half-close the read and/or write direction of an already tracked socket.
13666    /// shutdown never blocks and returns no data; its effect is deterministic
13667    /// given the container's socket state, so it forwards via record_or_replay

13673    /// before it relies on the mark (`finish_after_read_shutdown`), since a TCP
13674    /// disconnect opens the read side again (`tcp_disconnect`).

13676        &self,

13682            && matches!(result, Ok(_) | Err(Errno::ENOTCONN))
13683        {
13684            // An untracked descriptor has no model to mark.
13685            let _ = guest
13686                .thread_state()
13687                .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| detfd.set_read_shutdown_requested());
13688        }
13689        Ok(result?)
13690    }

13920        &self,
13921        guest: &mut G,
13922        call: syscalls::Eventfd2,
13923    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
13924        let internally_nonblocking =
13925            self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets() && !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes;
13926        let injected = if internally_nonblocking {
13927            call.with_flags(call.flags() | syscalls::EfdFlags::EFD_NONBLOCK)
13928        } else {
13929            call
13930        };
13931        let fd = self.record_or_replay(guest, injected).await? as RawFd;
13932        self.add_fd(
13933            guest,
13934            fd,
13935            OFlag::from_bits_truncate(
13936                call.flags().bits() & (libc::EFD_CLOEXEC | libc::EFD_NONBLOCK),
13937            ),
13938            FdType::Eventfd,
13939        )
13940        .await?;
13941        // Only a holder of this descriptor can signal it (`DetFd::is_guest_held`).
13942        guest
13943            .thread_state()
13944            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_guest_held())?;
13945        if internally_nonblocking {
13946            self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fd);
13947        }
13948        Ok(fd as i64)
13949    }

13951    /// signalfd4 system call.
13952    pub async fn handle_signalfd4<G: Guest<Self>>(
13953        &self,
13954        guest: &mut G,
13955        call: syscalls::Signalfd4,
13956    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
13957        // A signalfd of a pending real-time timer expiration that every thread
13958        // blocked when it expired would be readable at once
13959        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089). A mask the kernel
13960        // cannot read fails the call below.
13961        let mask = match call.mask().and_then(|mask| Addr::from_raw(mask.as_raw())) {
13962            Some(mask) => {
13963                // The call's first injection (`restart_if_first_probe_not_run`).
13964                match crate::syscalls::signal::read_kernel_sigset(guest, mask).await {
13965                    Err(error @ Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)) => {
13966                        return crate::syscalls::signal::restart_if_first_probe_not_run(Err(error));
13967                    }
13968                    read => read.ok(),
13969                }
13970            }
13971            None => None,
13972        };
13973        if let Some(mask) = mask {
13974            let pending = crate::syscalls::helpers::pending_real_time_among(guest, mask).await;
13975            crate::syscalls::helpers::act_on_pending_real_time(guest, pending, mask, 0).await;
13976        }
13977        let signalfd = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await? as RawFd;
13978        // A real-time timer expiration this descriptor, or a copy a fork
13979        // inherits, could read is never kept pending
13980        // (`Scheduler::real_time_expiration_fate`), a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID`
13981        // timer's copy of a signal it covers may be taken unobserved
13982        // (`Scheduler::thread_timer_copy_is_observable`), and a process one
13983        // of whose threads blocks in an I/O call while it holds one for
13984        // SIGCHLD does not attribute SIGCHLD through the send window
13985        // (`Scheduler::note_outside_blocker`), since that call may read it
13986        // outside the schedule.
13987        if let Some(mask) = mask
13988            && mask != 0
13989            && let Some(detpid) = guest.thread_state().detpid
13990        {
13991            crate::tool_global::register_signalfd(guest, detpid, mask).await;
13992        }
13993        self.add_fd(
13994            guest,
13995            signalfd,
13996            OFlag::from_bits_truncate(
13997                call.flags().bits() & (libc::SFD_CLOEXEC | libc::SFD_NONBLOCK),
13998            ),
13999            FdType::Signalfd,
14000        )
14001        .await?;
14002        Ok(signalfd as i64)
14003    }

14005    /// Create and register a timer notification descriptor.
14006    ///
14007    /// Determinism: strict execution serializes creation, which exposes only kernel validation,
14008    /// guest-visible flags, and a descriptor number; this operation does not read the clock.
14009    pub async fn handle_timerfd_create<G: Guest<Self>>(
14010        &self,
14011        guest: &mut G,
14012        call: syscalls::TimerfdCreate,
14013    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14014        // A timerfd on virtual time is physically nonblocking, as an eventfd
14015        // is, so a logically blocking read retries in scheduler turns
14016        // (internal IO polling) instead of blocking in the host until a
14017        // host-timed moment (`crate::syscalls::timerfd`).
14018        crate::syscalls::timerfd::refuse_unshared_model(guest);
14019        let internally_nonblocking = crate::syscalls::timerfd::enabled(guest);
14020        let injected = if internally_nonblocking {
14021            call.with_flags(call.flags() | syscalls::TimerFlags::TFD_NONBLOCK)
14022        } else {
14023            call
14024        };
14025        let fd = self.record_or_replay(guest, injected).await? as RawFd;
14026        self.add_fd(
14027            guest,
14028            fd,
14029            OFlag::from_bits_truncate(
14030                call.flags().bits() & (libc::TFD_CLOEXEC | libc::TFD_NONBLOCK),
14031            ),
14032            FdType::Timerfd,
14033        )
14034        .await?;
14035        if internally_nonblocking {
14036            self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fd);
14037        }
14038        Ok(fd as i64)
14039    }

14135    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
14136    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-862): pidfd creation and Detcore FD registration.
14137    /// Create a pidfd through record/replay and synchronize the descriptor with
14138    /// Detcore's metadata before fcntl, poll, close, or waitid can observe it.
14139    pub async fn handle_pidfd_open<G: Guest<Self>>(
14140        &self,
14141        guest: &mut G,
14142        call: syscalls::PidfdOpen,
14143    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14144        let allowed_flags = libc::O_NONBLOCK as u32;
14145        if call.flags() & !allowed_flags != 0 {
14146            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
14147        }
14148        // A pidfd for Hermit's own process, PID 1 of the guest's namespace,
14149        // would let `pidfd_send_signal` signal it and `pidfd_getfd` take its
14150        // descriptors (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4066). Linux
14151        // would open it; refusing it with EPERM is a policy, the answer the
14152        // guest already gets for `ptrace` and `process_vm_readv` on that process.
14153        let pid = call.pid() as i32;
14154        // A nested caller names its own namespace's pid, where none of
14155        // Hermit's tasks is visible; the pidfd records the task it names
14156        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155). A pid no task of
14157        // that namespace has goes to the kernel, which answers ESRCH.
14158        if pid > 0 && guest.thread_state().nested_pid_namespace {
14159            let target = match crate::tool_global::guest_pid(guest, pid).await {
14160                crate::scheduler::pid_namespaces::GuestPidAnswer::Task { task, .. } => Some(task),
14161                crate::scheduler::pid_namespaces::GuestPidAnswer::NoSuchPid => None,
14162                crate::scheduler::pid_namespaces::GuestPidAnswer::Untranslatable(reason) => {
14163                    tracing::error!(
14164                        "[detcore, dtid {}] pidfd_open of pid {} from a nested PID namespace is not supported: {} (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155)",
14165                        guest.thread_state().dettid,
14166                        pid,
14167                        reason,
14168                    );
14169                    return self
14170                        .refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::pidfd_open, Errno::ENOSYS)
14171                        .await;
14172                }
14173            };
14174            let fd = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await? as RawFd;
14175            let flags = OFlag::O_CLOEXEC | OFlag::from_bits_truncate(call.flags() as libc::c_int);
14176            self.add_fd(guest, fd, flags, FdType::Pidfd).await?;
14177            if let Some(target) = target {
14178                guest
14179                    .thread_state()
14180                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_pidfd_target(target))?;
14181            }
14182            return Ok(fd as i64);
14183        }
14184        if pid > 0 && crate::tool_global::names_hermit_task(guest, Some(pid), pid).await {
14185            tracing::info!(
14186                "[detcore, dtid {}] pidfd_open of {}, Hermit's own process: refused with EPERM \
14187                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4066)",
14188                guest.thread_state().dettid,
14189                pid,
14190            );
14191            return Err(Errno::EPERM.into());
14192        }
14193
14194        let fd = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await? as RawFd;
14195        let flags = OFlag::O_CLOEXEC | OFlag::from_bits_truncate(call.flags() as libc::c_int);
14196        self.add_fd(guest, fd, flags, FdType::Pidfd).await?;
14197        let target = DetPid::from_raw(call.pid() as i32);
14198        guest
14199            .thread_state()
14200            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_pidfd_target(target))?;
14201        Ok(fd as i64)
14202    }

14204    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
14205    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1175): pidfd_send_signal(2) determinization.
14206    /// Deliver a signal to the process referred to by a pidfd.
14207    ///
14208    /// `pidfd_send_signal(pidfd, sig, info, flags)` names its target by an open
14209    /// kernel descriptor rather than a numeric PID. Unlike `kill(2)`, there is
14210    /// therefore no host-PID/virtual-PID ambiguity for Detcore to resolve: the
14211    /// pidfd was bound to one specific process at `pidfd_open` time. Signal
14212    /// generation runs inside this thread's serialized scheduler turn, as for
14213    /// `tgkill`/`tkill`/`rt_tgsigqueueinfo`, which forward through record/replay
14214    /// and then tell the scheduler that the signal is pending for its receiver
14215    /// (`notify_cross_task_signal`), so that a receiver parked in a blocking call
14216    /// is woken. This handler does the same for a process with one live thread
14217    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4099>).
14218    ///
14219    /// The flags and the descriptor are decided as Linux decides them, ahead of
14220    /// the forward (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4108>):
14221    /// - an unknown flag bit, or more than one of the three scope flags, is
14222    ///   EINVAL; `PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD_GROUP` is the scope a process pidfd has
14223    ///   anyway, and `PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD` sends to the thread whose id is the
14224    ///   pid, as `tgkill(pid, pid)` does; `PIDFD_SIGNAL_PROCESS_GROUP` is
14225    ///   refused by name, even with signal 0, whose answer would come from the
14226    ///   process group the guest inherits from Hermit;
14227    /// - a descriptor names a process when it is a pidfd from `pidfd_open` or
14228    ///   a `/proc/<pid>` directory of the guest's procfs
14229    ///   (`process_directory_descriptor`); any other file is EBADF, and a
14230    ///   descriptor Detcore cannot classify is refused by name.
14231    ///
14232    /// A process-directed signal to a process with several live threads is
14233    /// refused by name, as `kill` refuses it (`Detcore::process_signal_target`).
14234    ///
14235    /// `call` is the raw `Syscall::Other`; `pidfd`/`flags` are pre-extracted from
14236    /// its arguments by the dispatcher.
14237    pub async fn handle_pidfd_send_signal<G: Guest<Self>>(
14238        &self,
14239        guest: &mut G,
14240        call: Syscall,
14241        pidfd: RawFd,
14242        signal: i32,
14243        flags: u32,
14244    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14245        // Linux checks the flags before it looks at the descriptor.
14246        let mut scope = pidfd_signal_scope(flags)?;
14247        let info = AddrMut::<GuestSiginfo>::from_raw(call.into_parts().1.arg2);
14248        if let Some(refused) = self
14249            .refuse_forged_own_sigchld(guest, Sysno::pidfd_send_signal, signal, info)
14250            .await
14251        {
14252            return refused;
14253        }
14254        // The two sentinels name the caller without a descriptor: its thread
14255        // (`PIDFD_SELF_THREAD`, thread-directed unless a flag says otherwise)
14256        // or its thread group (`PIDFD_SELF_THREAD_GROUP`)
14257        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4147).
14258        let named = if let Some((target, default)) = pidfd_self_target(guest, pidfd) {
14259            if flags == 0 {
14260                scope = default;
14261            }
14262            Some(target)
14263        } else {
14264            // An unknown or closed descriptor is EBADF, and so is any file that is
14265            // neither a pidfd nor an opened path (a pipe, a socket, an eventfd...).
14266            // Linux's fdget skips an O_PATH descriptor, so it is EBADF too.
14267            let kind = guest
14268                .thread_state()
14269                .with_detfd(pidfd, |detfd| match detfd.ty() {
14270                    FdType::Pidfd => Some(Some(detfd.pidfd_target())),
14271                    FdType::Regular if detfd.status_flags() & libc::O_PATH == 0 => Some(None),
14272                    _ => None,
14273                })?;
14274            let Some(kind) = kind else {
14275                return Err(Errno::EBADF.into());
14276            };
14277            // `named` is the pid the descriptor names. A pidfd from `pidfd_open`
14278            // names a process leader; a `/proc/<tid>` directory may name any thread,
14279            // whose process is its leader's (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4094).
14280            match kind {
14281                Some(target) => target,
14282                None => {
14283                    let descriptor = if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
14284                        // Replay holds a placeholder for a reopened file, so the
14285                        // descriptor cannot be read the same way in both.
14286                        ProcessDirectoryDescriptor::Unknown(
14287                            "record and replay do not read what a descriptor names",
14288                        )
14289                    } else if !guest.config().backend.host_task_reads_reach_guest_threads {
14290                        // Only on ptrace are the guest's thread ids the host's, so
14291                        // that its descriptors can be read through /proc/<tid>.
14292                        ProcessDirectoryDescriptor::Unknown(
14293                            "this backend's guest thread ids are not host thread ids",
14294                        )
14295                    } else {
14296                        process_directory_descriptor(guest.tid().as_raw(), pidfd)
14297                    };

14299                        ProcessDirectoryDescriptor::Process(task)
14300                            if crate::tool_global::names_hermit_task(
14301                                guest,
14302                                None,
14303                                task.as_raw(),
14304                            )
14305                            .await =>
14306                        {
14307                            // Any of Hermit's threads, as a `kill` naming one is
14308                            // dropped and `pidfd_open` of Hermit's process is refused
14309                            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4066).
14310                            tracing::info!(
14311                                "[detcore, dtid {}] pidfd_send_signal through /proc/{}, one of \
14312                                 Hermit's own threads: refused with EPERM",
14313                                guest.thread_state().dettid,
14314                                task,
14315                            );
14316                            return Err(Errno::EPERM.into());
14317                        }
14318                        ProcessDirectoryDescriptor::Process(task) => Some(task),
14319                        ProcessDirectoryDescriptor::NotAProcess => return Err(Errno::EBADF.into()),
14320                        ProcessDirectoryDescriptor::Unknown(reason) => {
14321                            tracing::error!(
14322                                "[detcore, dtid {}] pidfd_send_signal through descriptor {} is not \
14323                                 supported: {} (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4108)",
14324                                guest.thread_state().dettid,
14325                                pidfd,
14326                                reason,
14327                            );
14328                            return self
14329                                .refuse_unserviceable_operation(
14330                                    guest,
14331                                    Sysno::pidfd_send_signal,
14332                                    Errno::ENOSYS,
14333                                )
14334                                .await;
14335                        }
14336                    }
14337                }
14338            }
14339        };
14340        if scope == PidfdSignalScope::ProcessGroup {
14341            tracing::error!(
14342                "[detcore, dtid {}] signal {} by pidfd_send_signal with PIDFD_SIGNAL_PROCESS_GROUP \
14343                 is not supported: Detcore does not model process-group membership, and the \
14344                 guest's process group is inherited from Hermit's \
14345                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4108)",
14346                guest.thread_state().dettid,
14347                signal,
14348            );
14349            return self
14350                .refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::pidfd_send_signal, Errno::ENOSYS)
14351                .await;
14352        }
14353        // A reserved in-guest signal to another live process is refused here,
14354        // after the group scope's refusal above and before any path below
14355        // forwards the call; a target with no live thread (a zombie, or gone)
14356        // keeps its answer below.
14357        if let Some(refused) = self
14358            .refuse_reserved_signal_send(
14359                guest,
14360                Sysno::pidfd_send_signal,
14361                signal,
14362                crate::syscalls::signal::ReservedSendTarget::Pidfd {
14363                    named,
14364                    thread: scope == PidfdSignalScope::Thread,
14365                },
14366                crate::syscalls::signal::ReservedSendSiginfo::Pidfd(info.map(|info| info.as_raw())),
14367            )
14368            .await
14369        {
14370            return refused;
14371        }
14372        // D48 (A5 step 3c.1c): a stop signal under the in-guest delivery
14373        // gate, the caller's own process included.
14374        if let Some(refused) = self
14375            .refuse_stop_signal_send(
14376                guest,
14377                Sysno::pidfd_send_signal,
14378                signal,
14379                crate::syscalls::signal::ReservedSendTarget::Pidfd {
14380                    named,
14381                    thread: scope == PidfdSignalScope::Thread,
14382                },
14383                crate::syscalls::signal::ReservedSendSiginfo::Pidfd(info.map(|info| info.as_raw())),
14384            )
14385            .await
14386        {
14387            return refused;
14388        }
14389        let process = match named {
14390            Some(named) => Some(signal_target_process(guest, named).await.unwrap_or(named)),
14391            None => None,
14392        };
