14394        // by the kernel unless the init catches it, SIGKILL always
14395        // (`Detcore::own_namespace_init_drops`): forward it unchanged, with
14396        // nothing to retire or record
14397        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155).
14398        if guest.thread_state().nested_pid_namespace
14399            && let Some(process) = process
14400            && let Ok(Some(local)) = crate::tool_global::local_pid(guest, process).await
14401            && let crate::scheduler::pid_namespaces::GuestPidAnswer::Task {
14402                own_init_caught, ..
14403            } = crate::tool_global::guest_pid(guest, local).await
14404            && Self::own_namespace_init_drops(own_init_caught, signal)
14405        {
14406            return Ok(self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?);
14407        }
14408        // A process Detcore saw exit and that is gone is ESRCH, as Linux
14409        // answers once it is reaped, whatever the host has reaped by now
14410        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4091).
14411        if guest.config().sequentialize_threads
14412            && let Some(process) = process
14413        {
14414            let (targets, zombie) = resolve_kill_targets_and_exit(guest, process).await;
14415            if targets.is_empty() && zombie == Some(false) {
14416                return self.gone_pidfd_signal_answer(guest, call, signal).await;
14417            }
14418        }
14419        // The thread scope sends to the thread whose id is the pid, like
14420        // `tgkill(pid, pid)`; the process scope to its process.
14421        let thread_scope = scope == PidfdSignalScope::Thread;
14422        let receiver_id = if thread_scope { named } else { process };
14423        self.record_orphaned_group_signals(guest, signal).await;
14424        if signal == libc::SIGALRM {
14425            // `pidfd_open` records the process a pidfd names; a pidfd with no
14426            // recorded target is refused while any process handles SIGALRM.
14427            let control = match receiver_id {
14428                Some(target) => SigalrmControl::SendTo(DetTid::from_raw(target.as_raw())),
14429                None => SigalrmControl::SendToUnnamed,
14430            };
14431            refuse_sigalrm(guest, control).await?;
14432        }
14433        // A thread-scoped SIGKILL to a leader that exited while its group
14434        // lives on changes nothing, as `tgkill`'s does
14435        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4445).
14436        let exited_leader = signal == libc::SIGKILL
14437            && guest.config().sequentialize_threads
14438            && thread_scope
14439            && match named {
14440                Some(thread) => {
14441                    crate::syscalls::signal::sigkill_names_an_exited_leader(
14442                        guest,
14443                        DetTid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
14444                    )
14445                    .await
14446                }
14447                None => false,
14448            };
14449        if signal == libc::SIGKILL
14450            && guest.config().sequentialize_threads
14451            && !exited_leader
14452            && let (Some(process), Some(receiver)) = (process, receiver_id)
14453        {
14454            // A SIGKILL ends the whole process whichever thread it names, and
14455            // is retired at this turn as `kill`'s and `tgkill`'s are
14456            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994).
14457            if self
14458                .reserve_controlled_self_sigkill_exit(
14459                    guest,
14460                    signal,
14461                    Some(process),
14462                    thread_scope.then(|| DetTid::from_raw(receiver.as_raw())),
14463                )
14464                .await
14465            {
14466                return Ok(self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?);
14467            }
14468            if let Some(reservation) =
14469                reserve_sigkill(guest, DetTid::from_raw(receiver.as_raw())).await
14470            {
14471                return self.send_reserved_sigkill(guest, reservation, call).await;
14472            }
14473        }
14474        if thread_scope {
14475            // A thread-scoped send queues the copy in the named thread's
14476            // private queue (the Claude re-check of
14477            // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
14478            let value = match (named, process) {
14479                (Some(thread), Some(process)) => {
14480                    self.send_guest_signal(
14481                        guest,
14482                        call,
14483                        DetTid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
14484                        signal,
14485                        Some(process),
14486                        true,
14487                        DetTid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
14488                    )
14489                    .await?
14490                }
14491                _ => self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?,
14492            };
14493            if exited_leader {
14494                return Ok(value);
14495            }
14496            if let (Some(thread), Some(process)) = (named, process) {
14497                let thread = DetTid::from_raw(thread.as_raw());
14498                if signal == libc::SIGKILL {
14499                    crate::tool_global::notify_signal_pending(
14500                        guest,
14501                        thread,
14502                        SigWrapper(libc::SIGKILL),
14503                        Some(process),
14504                        crate::tool_global::SignalScope::Thread,
14505                    )
14506                    .await;
14507                } else {
14508                    self.notify_cross_task_signal(
14509                        guest,
14510                        thread,
14511                        signal,
14512                        Some(process),
14513                        crate::tool_global::SignalScope::Thread,
14514                    )
14515                    .await;
14516                }
14517            }
14518            return Ok(value);
14519        }
14520        // A process-directed signal. To a process with two or more live threads
14521        // it goes to the thread Linux's complete_signal picks, as Detcore
14522        // decides it, or waits in the shared queue when none wants it, as for
14523        // `kill` (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034). Everything
14524        // else is forwarded and the kernel answers: signal 0, which only
14525        // checks that the process exists; a SIGKILL that could not be
14526        // reserved, which kills the whole group whichever thread it reaches
14527        // (the scheduler is told below); a process with one live thread, whose
14528        // receiver the scheduler is then told about, as `kill` does; and a
14529        // process with none (a zombie, which Linux still signals
14530        // successfully).
14531        let mut receiver = None;
14532        if signal != 0
14533            && signal != libc::SIGKILL
14534            && guest.config().sequentialize_threads
14535            && let Some(target) = process
14536        {
14537            // A process-scoped pidfd names the process's leader; a
14538            // `/proc/<tid>` descriptor names its thread.
14539            let named_task = DetTid::from_raw(named.unwrap_or(target).as_raw());
14540            match self
14541                .process_signal_target(
14542                    guest,
14543                    reverie::syscalls::Sysno::pidfd_send_signal,
14544                    target,
14545                    named_task,
14546                    signal,
14547                )
14548                .await
14549            {
14550                Ok(ProcessSignalTarget::Thread(thread)) => receiver = Some((thread, target)),
14551                // Forwarded below, waking no thread: into the shared queue,
14552                // to a zombie, or to a process the kernel answers for.
14553                Ok(ProcessSignalTarget::SharedQueue | ProcessSignalTarget::Zombie)
14554                | Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ESRCH)) => {}
14555                Err(error) => return Err(error),
14556            }
14557        }
14558        let value = match receiver {
14559            Some((thread, process)) => {
14560                // A process-scoped pidfd names the process's leader
14561                // (`pidfd_send_signal` with `PIDTYPE_TGID`).
14562                self.send_guest_signal(
14563                    guest,
14564                    call,
14565                    thread,
14566                    signal,
14567                    Some(process),
14568                    false,
14569                    DetTid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
14570                )
14571                .await?
14572            }
14573            None => self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?,
14574        };
14575        if let Some((thread, process)) = receiver {
14576            // Tell the scheduler, as `kill` does, so a receiver parked in a
14577            // blocking call (pause(), a futex wait) is woken to take it
14578            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4099).
14579            self.notify_cross_task_signal(
14580                guest,
14581                thread,
14582                signal,
14583                Some(process),
14584                crate::tool_global::SignalScope::Process,
14585            )
14586            .await;
14587        }
14588        if signal == libc::SIGKILL {
14589            // A process killed through a pidfd will die; the scheduler must
14590            // not count a wait for it as part of a deadlock
14591            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904).
14592            match process {
14593                Some(target) => {
14594                    crate::tool_global::notify_signal_pending(
14595                        guest,
14596                        DetTid::from_raw(target.as_raw()),
14597                        SigWrapper(libc::SIGKILL),
14598                        Some(target),
14599                        crate::tool_global::SignalScope::Process,
14600                    )
14601                    .await
14602                }
14603                None => crate::tool_global::notify_unresolved_sigkill(guest, None).await,
14604            }
14605        }
14606        Ok(value)
14607    }
14608
14609    /// The answer to a `pidfd_send_signal` whose target Detcore saw exit and
14610    /// that is gone, in Linux's order: a non-NULL `info` is copied and its
14611    /// layout checked against its own `si_signo` (EFAULT, E2BIG), then that
14612    /// `si_signo` against the signal (EINVAL), then a forged `si_code`
14613    /// (EPERM), and only then is the task missing (ESRCH). The copy, the layout
14614    /// check and the `si_code` check are the kernel's: the same `info` goes to
14615    /// `rt_sigqueueinfo` naming a pid no task can have, which makes those
14616    /// checks and sends nothing (as
14617    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4124> does for that call).
14618    /// `rt_sigqueueinfo` checks the layout against the signal it is given, so
14619    /// it is given the info's own `si_signo`.
14620    async fn gone_pidfd_signal_answer<G: Guest<Self>>(
14621        &self,
14622        guest: &mut G,
14623        call: Syscall,
14624        signal: i32,
14625    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14626        let info = match call {
14627            Syscall::Other(_, args) => args.arg2,
14628            _ => 0,
14629        };
14630        let Some(info) = AddrMut::<GuestSiginfo>::from_raw(info) else {
14631            return Err(Errno::ESRCH.into());
14632        };
14633        let signo = guest.memory().read_value(info.cast::<libc::c_int>()).ok();
14634        let probe = syscalls::RtSigqueueinfo::new()
14635            .with_tgid(super::signal::NO_SUCH_PID)
14636            .with_sig(signo.unwrap_or(signal))
14637            .with_siginfo(Some(info.cast()));
14638        let checked = guest.inject(probe).await;
14639        let answer = match checked {
14640            Err(errno @ (Errno::EPERM | Errno::ESRCH)) => errno,
14641            Err(errno) => return Err(errno.into()),
14642            Ok(_) => Errno::ESRCH,
14643        };
14644        // The copy succeeded, so the kernel could read `si_signo`; a page
14645        // only the kernel reaches (`[vvar]`) cannot be decided here.
14646        let Some(signo) = signo else {
14647            tracing::error!(
14648                "[detcore, dtid {}] pidfd_send_signal to a gone process with a siginfo_t at \
14649                 {:#x} is not supported: Hermit cannot read its si_signo \
14650                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4108)",
14651                guest.thread_state().dettid,
14652                info.as_raw(),
14653            );
14654            return self
14655                .refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::pidfd_send_signal, Errno::ENOSYS)
14656                .await;
14657        };
14658        if signo != signal {
14659            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
14660        }
14661        Err(answer.into())
14662    }
14663
14664    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
14665    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1175): pidfd_getfd(2) determinization and the
14666    // FdType of the duplicated descriptor.
14667    /// Duplicate a descriptor from the process referred to by a pidfd.
14668    ///
14669    /// `pidfd_getfd(pidfd, targetfd, flags)` returns a fresh descriptor in the
14670    /// caller that aliases `targetfd` in the target process. The source pidfd
14671    /// names one specific process fixed at `pidfd_open` time, the returned
14672    /// descriptor number is chosen through record/replay (so it is stable across
14673    /// runs), and a successful modeled operation executes inside this thread's
14674    /// serialized turn, so the result is deterministic. For zero flags, Detcore
14675    /// fails closed with `EBADF` unless it models the descriptor as a pidfd.
14676    /// Linux checks the kernel-reserved `flags` first, however, so a nonzero
14677    /// value takes the raw record/replay path and preserves the kernel's exact
14678    /// `EINVAL` across valid and invalid descriptor combinations.
14679    ///
14680    /// The modeled path is narrower than "same process": the caller must be the
14681    /// thread-group leader named by the pidfd. `CLONE_THREAD` does not imply
14682    /// `CLONE_FILES`, so a nonleader can share the target's TGID while using a
14683    /// different descriptor table. Requiring `target == getpid() == gettid()`
14684    /// proves that `targetfd` is resolved in the caller's exact table. The
14685    /// returned descriptor is then modeled as a real alias of the source open
14686    /// file description. Broader support needs a cross-task OFD channel that
14687    /// Detcore does not have today, so every other target is refused with
14688    /// `EOPNOTSUPP`. Failed calls leave descriptor state unchanged.
14689    pub async fn handle_pidfd_getfd<G: Guest<Self>>(
14690        &self,
14691        guest: &mut G,
14692        call: Syscall,
14693        pidfd: RawFd,
14694        targetfd: RawFd,
14695        flags: u32,
14696    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14697        if flags != 0 {
14698            return match self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await {
14699                Err(error) => Err(error.into()),
14700                Ok(fd) => {
14701                    let fd = fd as RawFd;
14702                    let close_result = guest.inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(fd)).await;
14703                    Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
14704                        "pidfd_getfd unexpectedly accepted reserved flags and returned fd {fd}; cleanup close result: {close_result:?}"
14705                    )))
14706                }
14707            };
14708        }
14709
14710        if !guest.config().sequentialize_threads {
14711            return self
14712                .refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::pidfd_getfd, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP)
14713                .await;
14714        }
14715
14716        // A nested caller's own getpid and gettid are its namespace's ids,
14717        // while a pidfd records the task in the container's: compare the
14718        // caller's own DetPid and DetTid then
14719        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155).
14720        let (current_tgid, current_tid) = match guest.thread_state().detpid {
14721            Some(detpid) if guest.thread_state().nested_pid_namespace => {
14722                (detpid, guest.thread_state().dettid)
14723            }
14724            _ => (
14725                DetPid::from_raw(guest.inject(syscalls::Getpid::new()).await? as i32),
14726                DetTid::from_raw(guest.inject(syscalls::Gettid::new()).await? as i32),
14727            ),
14728        };
14729        let source = guest.thread_state().capture_pidfd_getfd_source(
14730            pidfd,
14731            targetfd,
14732            current_tgid,
14733            current_tid,
14734        )?;
14735        let fd = match self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await {
14736            Ok(fd) => fd as RawFd,
14737            Err(error) => {
14738                if let Some(open_file_id) = guest.thread_state().abandon_captured_fd(source) {
14739                    self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
14740                }
14741                return Err(error.into());
14742            }
14743        };
14744        // pidfd_getfd always sets FD_CLOEXEC on the returned descriptor.
14745        let replaced = match guest.thread_state_mut().install_captured_fd(
14746            source,
14747            fd,
14748            OFlag::O_CLOEXEC,
14749        ) {
14750            Ok(replaced) => replaced,
14751            Err(error @ CapturedDetFdInstallError { .. }) => {
14752                let expected_files_id = error.expected_files_id;
14753                let actual_files_id = error.actual_files_id;
14754                let cleanup = error.into_cleanup();
14755                let close_result = guest
14756                    .inject(syscalls::Close::new().with_fd(cleanup.close_fd))
14757                    .await;
14758                if let Some(open_file_id) = cleanup.release_open_file {
14759                    self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
14760                }
14761                if let Err(close_error) = close_result {
14762                    return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
14763                        "pidfd_getfd returned fd {fd}, but its captured source table changed from {expected_files_id:?} to {actual_files_id:?}; cleanup close failed with {close_error}"
14764                    )));
14765                }
14766                warn!(
14767                    "pidfd_getfd returned fd {fd}, but its captured source table changed from {expected_files_id:?} to {actual_files_id:?}; closed the result and refusing with EOPNOTSUPP"
14768                );
14769                return Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP.into());
14770            }
14771        };
14772        if let Some(open_file_id) = replaced {
14773            self.release_port_for_open_file(guest, open_file_id).await;
14774        }
14775        // This process now holds the description too, with any OFD or flock
14776        // lock it holds (`procfs::locks`).
14777        self.refresh_description_locks(guest, fd, LockCall::PidfdGetfd)
14778            .await?;
14779        Ok(fd as i64)
14780    }

14782    /// userfaultfd system call.
14783    pub async fn handle_userfaultfd<G: Guest<Self>>(
14784        &self,
14785        guest: &mut G,
14786        call: syscalls::Userfaultfd,
14787    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14788        let fd = self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await? as RawFd;
14789        self.add_fd(
14790            guest,
14791            fd,
14792            OFlag::from_bits_truncate(call.flags()),
14793            FdType::Userfaultfd,
14794        )
14795        .await?;
14796        Ok(fd as i64)
14797    }

14799    /// accept4 system call (MAYHANG).
14800    ///
14801    /// Category: External OR Internal IO
14802    /// ---------------------------------
14803    /// When do we know?  We only know if an accept4 did an extra-container IO AFTER it returns.
14804    /// I.e. we could accept a connection from another endpoint in the container, or from the outside,
14805    /// and we don't know which at the point where `accept4` is called.
14806    pub async fn handle_accept4<G: Guest<Self>>(
14807        &self,
14808        guest: &mut G,
14809        call: syscalls::Accept4,
14810    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14811        // This option applies both to the socket we're doing the accept call on, and the connection
14812        // that we return. We don't have any smart detection yet to separate internal/external, so
14813        // applies to everything.
14814        //
14815        // Record and replay leave the connection as the guest asked, as `handle_socket` does.
14816        // Their reads and writes on it run as backgrounded blocking calls, and on a physically
14817        // nonblocking connection such a call returns EAGAIN to a guest that asked to block
14818        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3882). The rejoin log orders their results.
14819        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
14820        let physically_nonblocking =
14821            self.cfg.use_nonblocking_sockets() && !self.cfg.recordreplay_modes;
14822        let call2 = if physically_nonblocking {
14823            // Let the socket returned from accept4 be physically nonblocking:
14824            call.with_flags(call.flags() | SockFlag::SOCK_NONBLOCK)
14825        } else {
14826            call
14827        };
14828        let in_turn = self.accept_in_turn_enabled()
14829            && guest
14830                .thread_state()
14831                .with_detfd(call.sockfd(), |detfd| detfd.is_accept_in_turn_listener())
14832                .unwrap_or(false);
14833        let completes_in_turn = in_turn || self.completes_in_turn(guest, call2);
14834        // A connection reads its error queue as its listener does. Read before
14835        // the accept, which may wait while other threads change the table.
14836        let error_queue_never_waits = guest
14837            .thread_state()
14838            .with_detfd(call.sockfd(), |detfd| detfd.error_queue_never_waits())
14839            .unwrap_or(false);
14840        let fd = if in_turn {
14841            // Record and replay run the accept in the caller's turn, so the new descriptor's
14842            // number is allocated deterministically (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3880).
14843            self.accept_in_turn(guest, call2).await? as RawFd
14844        } else {
14845            // This will do blocking/polling as appropriate based on the fd status:
14846            self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call2).await? as RawFd
14847        };
14848
14849        self.add_fd(
14850            guest,
14851            fd,
14852            // This will specify whether the socket returned is logically non-blocking:
14853            oflag_from_sock_bits(call.flags().bits()),
14854            FdType::Socket,
14855        )
14856        .await?;
14857        guest
14858            .thread_state()
14859            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.set_accepted_connection())?;
14860        self.note_unix_accept(guest, call.sockfd(), fd, completes_in_turn);
14861        guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
14862            detfd.set_accepted_connection();
14863            detfd.set_error_queue_never_waits(error_queue_never_waits);
14864        })?;
14865        self.classify_guest_held_peer(guest, fd).await;
14866
14867        if physically_nonblocking {
14868            self.maybe_set_nonblocking_fd(guest, fd);
14869        }
14870        self.classify_socket_peer(guest, fd, SocketRole::Connected)
14871            .await;
14872
14873        Ok(fd as i64)
14874    }

14876    /// getdents system call.
14877    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
14878    pub async fn handle_getdents<G: Guest<Self>>(
14879        &self,
14880        guest: &mut G,
14881        call: syscalls::Getdents,
14882    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14883        let virtualize = guest.config().virtualize_metadata;
14884        if !virtualize
14885            && (call.dirent().is_none()
14886                || !self.is_caller_descriptor_table(guest, call.fd() as i32))
14887        {
14888            return Ok(self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?);
14889        }
14890        let buf = call.dirent().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?.cast::<u8>();
14891        let call = GetdentsCall {
14892            call: Syscall::from(call),
14893            empty: Syscall::from(call.with_count(0)),
14894            fd: call.fd() as i32,
14895            buf,
14896            capacity: call.count() as usize,
14897            format: DirentFormat::Legacy,
14898        };
14899        if virtualize {
14900            self.serve_directory_stream(guest, call).await
14901        } else {
14902            self.project_one_buffer(guest, call).await
14903        }
14904    }

14917            return Ok(self.record_or_replay(guest, call).await?);
14918        }
14919        let buf = call.dirent().ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?.cast::<u8>();
14920        let call = GetdentsCall {
14921            call: Syscall::from(call),
14922            empty: Syscall::from(call.with_count(0)),
14923            fd: call.fd() as i32,
14924            buf,
14925            capacity: call.count() as usize,

14927        };
14928        if virtualize {
