14934
14935    /// Answer a `getdents` call from the open file's sorted directory stream
14936    /// (see [`DirectoryStream`]), reading the host directory first if the
14937    /// stream has no snapshot.
14938    ///
14939    /// Sorting each kernel buffer on its own is not enough: a directory larger
14940    /// than one buffer (about a thousand short names for glibc's 32KiB) would
14941    /// come back as sorted runs whose boundaries, and the host `d_off` cookies
14942    /// inside them, depend on the filesystem's on-disk layout.
14943    async fn serve_directory_stream<G: Guest<Self>>(
14944        &self,
14945        guest: &mut G,
14946        call: GetdentsCall<'_>,
14947    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
14948        let negative = i32::try_from(call.capacity).is_err();
14949        let lock = match guest
14950            .thread_state()
14951            .with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| detfd.directory_lock())
14952        {
14953            Ok(lock) => lock,
14954            // Detcore has no open file description for this descriptor (one
14955            // received through SCM_RIGHTS and not recorded, for example), so there is nowhere
14956            // to keep a stream. Sort the one kernel buffer instead, as before
14957            // directory streams existed; the kernel reports a descriptor that
14958            // is not open at all.
14959            Err(Errno::EBADF) if negative => {
14960                return self.serve_negative_count(guest, call, None).await;
14961            }
14962            Err(Errno::EBADF) => return self.project_one_buffer(guest, call).await,
14963            Err(errno) => return Err(errno.into()),
14964        };
14965        let _serving = lock.lock().await;
14966        let (host_order, needs_snapshot, position) =
14967            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| {
14968                (
14969                    detfd.directory_in_host_order(),
14970                    detfd.directory_needs_snapshot(),
14971                    detfd.with_directory_stream(|stream| stream.position()).ok(),
14972                )
14973            })?;
14974        if negative {
14975            let stream = if host_order {
14976                None
14977            } else {
14978                position.map(|position| (position, needs_snapshot))
14979            };
14980            return self.serve_negative_count(guest, call, stream).await;
14981        }
14982        if host_order {
14983            return self.project_one_buffer(guest, call).await;
14984        }
14985        if !needs_snapshot {
14986            return self.serve_next_batch(guest, call).await;
14987        }
14988        let mark = directory_snapshot_mark(guest).await;
14989        if let Some((entries, inodes, order)) = self.modeled_directory_snapshot(guest, call).await?
14990        {
14991            let mut entries = Some(entries);
14992            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| {
14993                detfd.install_directory_snapshot(
14994                    entries.take().unwrap_or_default(),
14995                    mark,
14996                    inodes.clone(),
14997                    order,
14998                )
14999            })?;
15000            return self.serve_next_batch(guest, call).await;
15001        }
15002        // How to key the entries' numbers is decided with the snapshot, as a
15003        // procfs directory loses its name once its task exits (see
15004        // `DirectoryStream`).
15005        let inodes = self.directory_inodes(guest, call.fd).await?;
15006        match self.snapshot_directory_privately(guest, call).await {
15007            Ok(Some(entries)) => {
15008                let mut entries = Some(entries);
15009                guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| {
15010                    detfd.install_directory_snapshot(
15011                        entries.take().unwrap_or_default(),
15012                        mark,
15013                        inodes.clone(),
15014                        DirectoryOrder::NameBytes,
15015                    )
15016                })?;
15017                self.serve_next_batch(guest, call).await
15018            }
15019            Ok(None) => {
15020                guest
15021                    .thread_state()
15022                    .with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| detfd.use_host_directory_order())?;
15023                self.project_one_buffer(guest, call).await
15024            }
15025            Err(error) => Err(error),
15026        }
15027    }
15028
15029    /// Answer a `getdents` whose count does not fit in an `int`. Linux keeps
15030    /// the count in one, where it is negative, so no entry fits: the call
15031    /// fails with `EINVAL`, or returns 0 at the end of the directory, and
15032    /// moves nothing. It does not look at the buffer, so a count of 0 gets
15033    /// the same answer for any pointer, and the same `EBADF`, `ENOTDIR` or
15034    /// `ENOENT`; that is the call issued, since a backend that does not
15035    /// truncate the guest's count to an `int` would copy host records into
15036    /// the guest's buffer.
15037    ///
15038    /// `stream` is the directory stream's position and whether it needs a
15039    /// snapshot, or `None` when the open file has no stream (it has not been
15040    /// read, is read in host order, or is not tracked). Then the guest's
15041    /// position is the kernel's, so the kernel's answer is Linux's. So it is
15042    /// for a stream rewound to 0, whose kernel position is the start. A
15043    /// stream that has a snapshot decides between `EINVAL` and 0 itself. The
15044    /// kernel position of a stream without a snapshot is moved to the start
15045    /// first, and then to where the snapshot, if made, puts it. A descriptor
15046    /// Detcore does not track that shares the open file, and had moved that
15047    /// position, reads on from there, where on Linux the call moves nothing. A
15048    /// stream rewound and then seeked past 0 needs to know how many entries
15049    /// the directory has, so a snapshot is taken (see
15050    /// [`Self::snapshot_directory_privately`]). If the directory must be
15051    /// read in host order instead, the kernel's answer from the start is
15052    /// returned, which is `EINVAL` even at or past the end; if no mapping can
15053    /// be made for the snapshot, the call fails with `ENOMEM`
15054    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3723).
15055    async fn serve_negative_count<G: Guest<Self>>(
15056        &self,
15057        guest: &mut G,
15058        call: GetdentsCall<'_>,
15059        stream: Option<(u64, bool)>,
15060    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
15061        if let Some((_, true)) = stream {
15062            // Without a snapshot, the kernel position of a stream is the
15063            // start; a descriptor Detcore does not track may have moved it.
15064            self.move_directory_kernel_position(guest, call.fd, 0).await;
15065        }
15066        let kernel = self.record_or_replay(guest, call.empty).await;
15067        match kernel {
15068            Ok(_) | Err(Errno::EINVAL) => {}
15069            Err(errno) => return Err(errno.into()),
15070        }
15071        match stream {
15072            None | Some((0, true)) => return Ok(kernel.map(|_| 0)?),
15073            Some((_, true)) => {
15074                let mark = directory_snapshot_mark(guest).await;
15075                let modeled = self.modeled_directory_snapshot(guest, call).await?;
15076                let (snapshot, inodes, order) = match modeled {
15077                    Some((entries, inodes, order)) => (Ok(Some(entries)), inodes, order),
15078                    None => {
15079                        let inodes = self.directory_inodes(guest, call.fd).await?;
15080                        (
15081                            self.snapshot_directory_privately(guest, call).await,
15082                            inodes,
15083                            DirectoryOrder::NameBytes,
15084                        )
15085                    }
15086                };
15087                match snapshot {
15088                    Ok(Some(entries)) => {
15089                        let mut entries = Some(entries);
15090                        let target = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| {
15091                            detfd.install_directory_snapshot(
15092                                entries.take().unwrap_or_default(),
15093                                mark,
15094                                inodes.clone(),
15095                                order,
15096                            );
15097                            detfd.with_directory_stream(|stream| stream.kernel_target())
15098                        })??;
15099                        self.move_directory_kernel_position(guest, call.fd, target)
15100                            .await;
15101                    }
15102                    Ok(None) => return Ok(kernel.map(|_| 0)?),
15103                    Err(error) => return Err(error),
15104                }
15105            }
15106            Some((_, false)) => {}
15107        }
15108        let batch = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| {
15109            detfd.with_directory_stream(|stream| stream.next_batch(call.format, 0))
15110        })??;
15111        batch?;
15112        Ok(0)
15113    }
15114
15115    /// Return the entries at the stream's position that fit in the guest's
15116    /// buffer, with determinized inodes, keyed as decided when the snapshot
15117    /// was taken, and each `d_off` naming the position after its entry,
15118    /// counting from 1.
15119    ///
15120    /// Whatever the outcome, the kernel position then follows the stream (see
15121    /// [`DirectoryStream::kernel_target`]).
15122    async fn serve_next_batch<G: Guest<Self>>(
15123        &self,
15124        guest: &mut G,
15125        call: GetdentsCall<'_>,
15126    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
15127        let (start, batch, mark, inodes) =
15128            guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| {
15129                detfd.with_directory_stream(|stream| {
15130                    (
15131                        stream.position(),
15132                        stream.next_batch(call.format, call.capacity),
15133                        stream.snapshot_mark(),
15134                        stream.snapshot_inodes(),
15135                    )
15136                })
15137            })??;
15138        let (passed, copied) = match batch {
15139            Ok(batch) => {
15140                // Every snapshot is installed with its keys; a stream without
15141                // them is keyed now.
15142                let inodes = match inodes {
15143                    Some(inodes) => inodes,
15144                    None => self.directory_inodes(guest, call.fd).await?,
15145                };
15146                let mut records = Vec::new();
15147                let mut names = Vec::with_capacity(batch.len());
15148                for (index, entry) in batch.iter().enumerate() {
15149                    let (host, path) = inodes.entry_inode(&entry.name, entry.ino);
15150                    let files = self.rendered_files(guest);
15151                    let d_ino = match self
15152                        .rendered_listed_inode(guest, &inodes, &entry.name, entry.ino, files)
15153                        .await?
15154                    {
15155                        Some(inode) => DetInode::mint(inode),
15156                        None => determinize_listed_inode(guest, host, path, mark).await.0,
15157                    };
15158                    let d_off = i64::try_from(start + index as u64 + 1).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
15159                    call.format
15160                        .encode(entry, d_ino.as_raw(), d_off, &mut records);
15161                    names.push(entry.name.len());
15162                }
15163                copy_records(
15164                    &mut guest.memory(),
15165                    call.buf,
15166                    call.format,
15167                    &records,
15168                    &names,
15169                    start,
15170                )
15171            }
15172            Err(errno) => (0, Err(errno)),
15173        };
15174        // With --no-sequentialize-threads another thread can close the
15175        // descriptor during the copy; like Linux, the call's result stands.
15176        let target = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| {
15177            detfd.with_directory_stream(|stream| {
15178                stream.advance(passed);
15179                stream.kernel_target()
15180            })
15181        });
15182        if let Ok(Ok(target)) = target {
15183            self.move_directory_kernel_position(guest, call.fd, target)
15184                .await;
15185        }
15186        Ok(copied.map(|len| len as i64)?)
15187    }
15188
15189    /// The entries of the `/proc` directory open as `fd`, and how to key their
15190    /// inode numbers, if Detcore lists it from its own model (see
15191    /// [`crate::procfs::listing`]): the root, the level table's other
15192    /// directories, a process's or a thread's directory, or a process's
15193    /// `task`, with processes and threads as the guest numbers them, so that
15194    /// every backend lists the same.
15195    ///
15196    /// The directory is the one the descriptor was opened on: where guest
15197    /// thread IDs name host tasks (ptrace), the kernel's canonical name for
15198    /// it (`procfs_entry`), which bound `self` and `thread-self` to the
15199    /// opener, so an inherited or passed descriptor keeps listing the
15200    /// opener's; on a backend that serves its own `/proc` (KVM), the guest's
15201    /// spelling, and only a directory with no process in its path (the root
15202    /// and the table's system directories), as its process directories cannot
15203    /// be opened yet (slice B3a-4).
15204    ///
15205    /// Each entry is looked up by its spelling below the directory, as the
15206    /// guest's own `lstat` of it would be: on the kernel's procfs an entry the
15207    /// lookup does not find (a name the level lists but this kernel lacks,
15208    /// such as `children` without `CONFIG_PROC_CHILDREN`) is left out, unless
15209    /// Detcore renders it; on a backend's own /proc (KVM), whose lookups
15210    /// follow its executor's process table at host-timed moments, a lookup
15211    /// decides no entry. One the lookup finds is
15212    /// numbered by the inode it reports, which a stat of it pools under too
15213    /// (with the entry's name and its task's incarnation), so the two agree. A
15214    /// file Detcore renders is numbered by its rendered inode
15215    /// ([`Self::serve_next_batch`]), and an entry the backend refuses to look
15216    /// up (KVM) by its path's key.
15217    ///
15218    /// The kernel's directory is still read once, as for any other directory
15219    /// ([`Self::snapshot_directory_privately`]), for its `d_off` cookies: each
15220    /// entry carries the cookie of the host entry of its name, so that the
15221    /// stream leaves the kernel position where a descriptor Detcore does not
15222    /// track reads on from (at the end, the kernel's own end). A descriptor
15223    /// whose position the guest moved before its first read is then read in
15224    /// host order, as any other is.
15225    ///
15226    /// `None`, so that the kernel's listing is served as before: for any other
15227    /// directory; an `O_PATH` descriptor, which lists nothing (the kernel's
15228    /// `EBADF`); under record and replay, where the replayer's descriptor
15229    /// does not name the recorded directory; in a nested PID namespace, whose
15230    /// numbers are not Detcore's; after a guest `chroot`, where `/proc` need
15231    /// not be procfs; for a descriptor not on the guest's procfs (a user bind
15232    /// over part of it); on the in-guest backends whose kernel numbers
15233    /// processes otherwise than Detcore (DBT,
15234    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4009>), where a listed guest
15235    /// pid would open the kernel's process of that number until `/proc/<pid>`
15236    /// is translated (slice B3a-4); and for a process or thread the scheduler
15237    /// does not list, which the kernel's directory then answers for.
15238    async fn modeled_directory_snapshot<G: Guest<Self>>(
15239        &self,
15240        guest: &mut G,
15241        call: GetdentsCall<'_>,
15242    ) -> Result<Option<(Vec<DirEntry>, DirectoryInodes, DirectoryOrder)>, Error> {
15243        let fd = call.fd;
15244        use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
15245
15246        use crate::procfs::listing;
15247        use crate::procfs::listing::ModeledDirectory;
15248        let state = guest.thread_state();
15249        if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
15250            || state.nested_pid_namespace
15251            || state.changed_root.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
15252        {
15253            return Ok(None);
15254        }
15255        let Ok((spelled, status_flags)) =
15256            state.with_detfd(fd, |detfd| (detfd.path(), detfd.status_flags()))
15257        else {
15258            return Ok(None);
15259        };
15260        // Only a descriptor the guest opened by a spelling of such a
15261        // directory is one, which spares every other directory's listing the
15262        // naming below.
15263        if status_flags & libc::O_PATH != 0 {
15264            return Ok(None);
15265        }
15266        // Where numbers are translated (DBT), the kernel's name for the
15267        // descriptor says which directory it is, whatever spelling opened it
15268        // (`/proc/self/fd/N` of a descriptor of `/proc`).
15269        let kernel_named = || {
15270            std::fs::read_link(format!("/proc/thread-self/fd/{fd}"))
15271                .is_ok_and(|kernel| listing::classify(&kernel, 0, 0).is_some())
15272        };
15273        if spelled
15274            .as_deref()
15275            .and_then(|spelled| listing::classify(spelled, 0, 0))
15276            .is_none()
15277            && !(Self::translates_procfs_numbers(guest)
15278                && guest.config().backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table
15279                && kernel_named())
15280        {
15281            return Ok(None);
15282        }
15283        let state = guest.thread_state();
15284        let tid = state.dettid.as_raw();
15285        let names_tasks =
15286            procfs_inode::guest_tids_name_host_tasks(&self.cfg.backend, state.physical_tid);
15287        let pid = self.own_detpid(guest).as_raw();
15288        let cached = guest
15289            .thread_state()
15290            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.stat())
15291            .ok()
15292            .flatten();
15293        let stat = match cached {
15294            Some(stat) => stat,
15295            None => DetStat::from(self.inject_fstat(guest, fd).await?),
15296        };
15297        if stat.mode & libc::S_IFMT != libc::S_IFDIR {
15298            return Ok(None);
15299        }
15300        // Where the kernel numbers processes otherwise than Detcore (DBT),
15301        // the directory is the one the guest's spelling names, which reached
15302        // the kernel's directory of the same process (`procfs_numbers`).
15303        let translates = Self::translates_procfs_numbers(guest)
15304            && rendered_procfs::proc_device() == Some(stat.dev);
15305        let path = if names_tasks && rendered_procfs::proc_device() == Some(stat.dev) {
15306            match Self::procfs_entry(guest, &stat, StatTarget::Descriptor(fd)).await {
15307                ProcfsEntry::At(within) => {
15308                    Path::new("/proc").join(within.strip_prefix("/").unwrap_or(&within))
15309                }
15310                ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs | ProcfsEntry::Unnamed | ProcfsEntry::Unknown => {
15311                    return Ok(None);
15312                }
15313            }
15314        } else if translates {
15315            match Self::guest_procfs_spelling(guest, fd).await {
15316                Some(path) => path,
15317                None => return Ok(None),
15318            }
15319        } else {
15320            return Ok(None);
15321        };
15322        let Some(directory) = listing::classify(&path, pid, tid) else {
15323            return Ok(None);
15324        };
15325        let process = match directory {
15326            ModeledDirectory::System(_) => None,
15327            ModeledDirectory::Process(process)
15328            | ModeledDirectory::Thread(process, _)
15329            | ModeledDirectory::Tasks(process) => Some(DetPid::from_raw(process)),
15330        };
15331        let facts = crate::tool_global::procfs_listing(guest, process).await;
15332        let listed = match directory {
15333            ModeledDirectory::System(_) => true,
15334            // The namespace's init is Hermit's own process unless a guest
15335            // holds pid 1; its threads are the kernel's to list.
15336            ModeledDirectory::Process(process) => {
15337                process == 1 || facts.processes.contains(&process)
15338            }
15339            ModeledDirectory::Thread(_, thread) => facts.threads.contains(&thread),
15340            ModeledDirectory::Tasks(_) => !facts.threads.is_empty(),
15341        };
15342        if !listed {
15343            return Ok(None);
15344        }
15345        let Some(names) = listing::entries(&directory, self.cfg.proc_level, &facts) else {
15346            return Ok(None);
15347        };
15348        // The host's cookies, where the kernel lists the directory.
15349        let Some(host) = self.snapshot_directory_privately(guest, call).await? else {
15350            return Ok(None);
15351        };
15352        // A process or thread number the kernel lists is the kernel's (DBT):
15353        // its cookie is the cookie of the guest's number for it.
15354        let host_numbers = if translates {
15355            let held = host
15356                .iter()
15357                .filter(|entry| {
15358                    crate::procfs::ids::names_an_id(&path, std::ffi::OsStr::from_bytes(&entry.name))
15359                })
15360                .filter_map(|entry| std::str::from_utf8(&entry.name).ok()?.parse::<i32>().ok())
15361                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
15362            Self::guest_procfs_numbers(guest, &held)
15363                .await
15364                .unwrap_or_default()
15365        } else {
15366            BTreeMap::new()
15367        };
15368        // A kernel number that is no guest's has no cookie to give: its name
15369        // may be another guest number's.
15370        let host_cookies: std::collections::HashMap<Vec<u8>, i64> = host
15371            .iter()
15372            .filter_map(|entry| {
15373                if !translates
15374                    || !crate::procfs::ids::names_an_id(
15375                        &path,
15376                        std::ffi::OsStr::from_bytes(&entry.name),
15377                    )
15378                {
15379                    return Some((entry.name.clone(), entry.off));
15380                }
15381                let kernel = std::str::from_utf8(&entry.name).ok()?.parse::<i32>().ok()?;
15382                let guest = host_numbers.get(&kernel)?;
15383                Some((guest.to_string().into_bytes(), entry.off))
15384            })
15385            .collect();
15386        let host_cookie = |name: &[u8]| host_cookies.get(name).copied().unwrap_or(0);
15387        let session_files = self.rendered_files(guest);
15388        let host_end = host.last().map_or(0, |entry| entry.off);
15389        // Looked up from the guest's own descriptor where it names the
15390        // kernel's directory, and by the guest's spelling on DBT, whose lookup
15391        // translates the guest's numbers to the kernel's as the guest's own
15392        // lookup of each would be (`inject_statat`, `procfs_numbers`).
15393        let (lookup_dir, spellings): (RawFd, Vec<PathBuf>) = if translates {
15394            let spellings = names
15395                .iter()
15396                .map(|(name, _)| path.join(std::ffi::OsStr::from_bytes(name)))
15397                .collect();
15398            (libc::AT_FDCWD, spellings)
15399        } else {
15400            let spellings = names
15401                .iter()
15402                .map(|(name, _)| PathBuf::from(std::ffi::OsStr::from_bytes(name)))
15403                .collect();
15404            (fd, spellings)
15405        };
15406        let looked_up = self.looked_up_inodes(guest, lookup_dir, &spellings).await?;
15407        let within = listing::within(&directory);
15408        let entries = names
15409            .into_iter()
15410            .zip(looked_up)
15411            .filter_map(|((name, ty), looked_up)| {
15412                let entry = match name.as_slice() {
15413                    b"." => within.clone(),
15414                    b".." => within.parent().unwrap_or(&within).to_path_buf(),
15415                    name => within.join(std::ffi::OsStr::from_bytes(name)),
15416                };
15417                // A file Detcore renders exists whatever the kernel has. (Not
15418                // a task's `comm` where the kernel serves every one.)
15419                let rendered = crate::procfs::ProcfsFile::from_path(
15420                    &Path::new("/proc").join(entry.strip_prefix("/").unwrap_or(&entry)),
15421                )
15422                .is_some_and(|file| {
15423                    !self.kernel_serves_every_comm(&file)
15424                        && file.rendered_path(session_files).is_some()
15425                });
15426                let ino = match looked_up {
15427                    Ok(ino) => ino,
15428                    Err(Errno::ENOENT) if name != b"." && name != b".." && !rendered => {
15429                        return None;
15430                    }
15431                    Err(_) => procfs_inode::path_inode(stat.dev, &entry).ino,
15432                };
15433                Some(DirEntry {
15434                    ino,
15435                    off: host_cookie(&name),
15436                    ty,
15437                    name,
15438                })
15439            })
15440            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
15441        // In host order, which `DirectoryStream::install` takes them in, and
15442        // ending where the host's listing ends, so the stream's end is the
15443        // kernel's.
15444        let mut entries = entries;
15445        entries.sort_by_key(|entry| entry.off);
15446        if let Some(last) = entries.last_mut() {
15447            last.off = last.off.max(host_end);
15448        }
15449        let inodes = DirectoryInodes::new(stat.dev, Some(ProcfsDirectory::new(within)));
15450        let order = match &directory {
15451            ModeledDirectory::System(names) if names.is_empty() => DirectoryOrder::ProcfsIds,
15452            ModeledDirectory::Tasks(_) => DirectoryOrder::ProcfsIds,
15453            _ => DirectoryOrder::NameBytes,
15454        };
15455        Ok(Some((entries, inodes, order)))
15456    }
15457
15458    /// The inode number a lookup of each of `paths` from the directory open as
15459    /// `dir` (or absolute, with `AT_FDCWD`), without following a final link,
15460    /// gives in the guest, as the guest's own `fstatat` of it would, or the
15461    /// lookup's error. The paths are staged in an
15462    /// anonymous mapping injected for the purpose and unmapped before the guest
15463    /// runs again, as a directory snapshot's reads are (see
15464    /// [`Self::snapshot_directory_privately`]); without one, every lookup is
15465    /// `ENOMEM`. A mapping that cannot be unmapped would be visible to the
15466    /// guest, so that is an error.
15467    async fn looked_up_inodes<G: Guest<Self>>(
15468        &self,
15469        guest: &mut G,
15470        dir: RawFd,
15471        paths: &[PathBuf],
15472    ) -> Result<Vec<Result<u64, Errno>>, Error> {
15473        use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
15474
15475        let mapped = guest
15476            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
15477                syscalls::Mmap::new()
15478                    .with_addr(None)
15479                    .with_len(DIRECTORY_PAGE)
15480                    .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
15481                    .with_flags(MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS)
15482                    .with_fd(-1)
15483                    .with_offset(0),
15484            ))
15485            .await;
15486        let Some(page) = mapped
15487            .ok()
15488            .and_then(|addr| usize::try_from(addr).ok())
15489            .and_then(AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw)
15490        else {
15491            return Ok(vec![Err(Errno::ENOMEM); paths.len()]);
15492        };
15493        let mut inodes = Vec::with_capacity(paths.len());
15494        for path in paths {
15495            let mut bytes = path.as_os_str().as_bytes().to_vec();
15496            bytes.push(0);
15497            let staged =
15498                bytes.len() <= DIRECTORY_PAGE && guest.memory().write_exact(page, &bytes).is_ok();
15499            let staged_path = PathPtr::from_ptr(page.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char);
15500            let inode = match (staged, staged_path) {
15501                (true, Some(staged_path)) => Self::inject_statat(
15502                    guest,
15503                    dir,
15504                    staged_path,
15505                    [Some(staged_path), None],
15506                    AtFlags::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW,
15507                )
15508                .await
15509                .map(|stat| stat.st_ino),
15510                _ => Err(Errno::ENAMETOOLONG),
15511            };
15512            inodes.push(inode);
15513        }
15514        guest
15515            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
15516                syscalls::Munmap::new()
15517                    .with_addr(Some(Addr::from(page).cast()))
15518                    .with_len(DIRECTORY_PAGE),
15519            ))
15520            .await?;
15521        Ok(inodes)
15522    }
15523
15524    /// How to key the inode numbers of the entries of the directory open as
15525    /// `fd`. Every entry is on the directory's host device (a mount point's
15526    /// entry names the directory beneath the mount, on the same device), and
15527    /// a procfs directory's entries also name their paths beneath its
15528    /// canonical path (see [`procfs_inode`]). The directory's stat is the
15529    /// cached one when Detcore tracks `fd`, and an injected `fstat` otherwise.
15530    async fn directory_inodes<G: Guest<Self>>(
15531        &self,
15532        guest: &mut G,
15533        fd: RawFd,
15534    ) -> Result<DirectoryInodes, Errno> {
15535        let cached = guest
15536            .thread_state()
15537            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.stat())
15538            .ok()
15539            .flatten();
15540        let stat = match cached {
15541            Some(stat) => stat,
15542            None => DetStat::from(self.inject_fstat(guest, fd).await?),
15543        };
15544        let procfs = match Self::procfs_entry(guest, &stat, StatTarget::Descriptor(fd)).await {
15545            ProcfsEntry::At(within) => Some(ProcfsDirectory::new(within)),
15546            ProcfsEntry::NotProcfs | ProcfsEntry::Unnamed | ProcfsEntry::Unknown => None,
15547        };
15548        Ok(DirectoryInodes::new(stat.dev, procfs))
15549    }
15550
15551    /// Move the kernel position of the open file behind `fd` to `target`, a
15552    /// [`DirectoryStream::kernel_target`], so that a descriptor Detcore does
15553    /// not track that aliases it reads every entry the stream has not
15554    /// returned. Without this, the snapshot leaves the kernel at the end of
15555    /// the directory, and such a descriptor would read nothing.
15556    ///
15557    /// The guest's own call has already been decided, so a failed seek is not
15558    /// reported to it; the next move of the stream seeks again.
15559    async fn move_directory_kernel_position<G: Guest<Self>>(
15560        &self,
15561        guest: &mut G,
15562        fd: RawFd,
15563        target: i64,
15564    ) {
15565        // A placeholder's kernel position is its tag, which nothing moves:
15566        // Detcore answers its listing and its seeks from its model.
15567        if Self::placeholder_of(guest, fd).is_some() {
15568            return;
15569        }
15570        let seek = syscalls::Lseek::new()
15571            .with_fd(fd)
15572            .with_offset(target)
15573            .with_whence(Whence::SEEK_SET);
15574        let _ = self.record_or_replay(guest, seek).await;
15575    }
15576
15577    /// Drop from `entries`, read from the directory open as `fd`, the CPUs and
15578    /// nodes that the virtual CPUs and single node leave out (see
15579    /// [`is_absent_cpu_entry`]), so that a guest counting
15580    /// `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN` finds the virtual CPUs, as `online` and
15581    /// `sched_getaffinity` report
15582    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4160>); and the `/proc`
15583    /// names outside the run's `--proc` level, which lookups refuse (see
15584    /// [`levels::absent_entry`]).
15585    ///
15586    /// The directory is named by the kernel's path for the descriptor, so a
15587    /// relative or symlinked spelling is recognized too. Not under record and
15588    /// replay, where the replayer's descriptor does not name the recorded
15589    /// directory, so the two runs would not drop alike; Detcore names no
15590    /// procfs entry there either (see [`Self::procfs_entry`]).
15591    async fn drop_absent_entries<G: Guest<Self>>(
15592        &self,
15593        guest: &mut G,
15594        fd: RawFd,
15595        entries: &mut Vec<DirEntry>,
15596    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
15597        if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
15598            return Ok(());
15599        }
15600        let link = format!("{}/fd/{fd}", self.caller_proc_directory(guest));
15601        // Names are dropped as outside the level only from a directory the
15602        // tool sees is on procfs: not from a user bind over part of `/proc`,
15603        // and not where the tool cannot tell (its `/proc` entry for the
15604        // caller is not the caller's where the guest's threads are no host
15605        // tasks, KVM, or is unreadable after a `chroot`).
15606        let tool_sees_caller =
15607            crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors(&self.cfg.backend);
15608        let directory_metadata = tool_sees_caller
15609            .then(|| std::fs::metadata(&link).ok())
15610            .flatten();
15611        let on_procfs = match (&directory_metadata, rendered_procfs::proc_device()) {
15612            (Some(metadata), Some(device)) => metadata.dev() == device,
15613            _ => false,
15614        };
15615        if self.is_caller_descriptor_table(guest, fd) {
15616            entries.retain(|entry| {
15617                !runtime_owned_descriptor_entry(&entry.name, |fd| guest.is_runtime_owned_fd(fd))
15618            });
15619        }
15620        let directory = listed_directory(
15621            tool_sees_caller,
15622            || std::fs::read_link(&link).ok(),
15623            || {
15624                guest
15625                    .thread_state()
15626                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.path())
15627                    .ok()
15628                    .flatten()
15629            },
15630        );
15631        // After a `chroot` into another root, the kernel names the directory
15632        // in the tool's view, below that root.
15633        let directory = match (directory, self.guest_root_in_view(guest)) {
15634            (Some(directory), Some(Some(root))) if !directory.starts_with("/proc") => directory
15635                .strip_prefix(&root)
15636                .ok()
15637                .map(|below| Path::new("/").join(below))
15638                .or(Some(directory)),
15639            (directory, _) => directory,
15640        };
15641        if let Some(directory) = directory {
15642            let level = self.cfg.proc_level;
15643            let cpus = self.cfg.virtual_cpu_count();
15644            // A user bind over a sysfs path keeps its own names. Ask the
15645            // opened descriptor, not its path in the tool's mount namespace.
15646            let has_absent_cpu = entries
15647                .iter()
15648                .any(|entry| is_absent_cpu_entry(&directory, &entry.name, cpus));
15649            let on_sysfs = has_absent_cpu
15650                && self
15651                    .descriptor_is_on_filesystem(guest, fd, libc::SYSFS_MAGIC)
15652                    .await?;
15653            entries.retain(|entry| {
15654                !(on_sysfs && is_absent_cpu_entry(&directory, &entry.name, cpus))
15655                    && !(on_procfs && levels::absent_entry(&directory, &entry.name, level))
15656            });
15657        }
15658        Ok(())
15659    }
15660
15661    /// Whether the opened procfs object names the caller's own descriptor
15662    /// table. Authenticate kernel object identity, not the guest spelling:
15663    /// an inherited directory may belong to a different process. Process and
15664    /// thread aliases have distinct inodes; the process alias requires the
15665    /// existing shared-table proof. Independent of metadata virtualization.
15666    fn is_caller_descriptor_table<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &G, fd: RawFd) -> bool {
15667        if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
15668            || !crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors(&self.cfg.backend)
15669        {
15670            return false;
15671        }
15672        let link = format!("{}/fd/{fd}", self.caller_proc_directory(guest));
15673        std::fs::metadata(link).is_ok_and(|metadata| {
15674            self.is_caller_descriptor_identity(
15675                guest,
15676                (metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()),
15677                &["fd", "fdinfo"],
15678            )
15679        })
15680    }
15681
15682    /// The same object test for an opened directory or a pathname lookup.
15683    /// Readlink accepts only `fd`; listings also accept `fdinfo`.
15684    fn is_caller_descriptor_identity<G: Guest<Self>>(
15685        &self,
15686        guest: &G,
15687        identity: (u64, u64),
15688        kinds: &[&str],
15689    ) -> bool {
15690        if rendered_procfs::proc_device() != Some(identity.0) {
15691            return false;
15692        }
15693        let state = guest.thread_state();
15694        let holds_process_table =
15695            state.dettid == self.own_detpid(guest) || state.holds_process_files();
15696        let process = if self.cfg.backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table {
15697            String::from("/proc/self")
15698        } else {
15699            format!("/proc/{}", guest.pid().as_raw())
15700        };
15701        caller_descriptor_identity_matches(
15702            identity,
15703            &self.caller_proc_directory(guest),
15704            holds_process_table.then_some(process.as_str()),
15705            kinds,
15706        )
15707    }
15708
15709    /// Hide an owner-reported descriptor only after the original pathname's
15710    /// parent resolves to this caller's actual FD directory. A recorded
15711    /// `/proc/self/fd` spelling alone cannot authenticate an inherited,
15712    /// replaced, or invalid directory descriptor.
15713    pub(crate) async fn readlink_names_runtime_fd<G: Guest<Self>>(
15714        &self,
15715        guest: &mut G,
15716        dirfd: RawFd,
15717        path: &Path,
15718    ) -> bool {
15719        use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
15720
15721        use super::namespace::decimal_fd;
15722
15723        let bytes = path.as_os_str().as_bytes();
15724        if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
15725            || !crate::procfs_inode::tool_can_name_guest_descriptors(&self.cfg.backend)
15726            || guest.thread_state().changed_root.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
15727            || bytes.is_empty()
15728            || bytes.len() >= libc::PATH_MAX as usize
15729            || bytes.ends_with(b"/")
15730        {
15731            return false;
15732        }
15733        // Only parse the final raw component. The actual parent object,
15734        // rather than an absolute or recognized spelling, proves whose
15735        // descriptor table this is. In particular, retain interior `..`
15736        // and symlinks for Linux to resolve in order.
15737        let name = bytes.rsplit(|byte| *byte == b'/').next().unwrap();
15738        let Some(fd) = decimal_fd(std::ffi::OsStr::from_bytes(name)) else {
15739            return false;
15740        };
15741        // Keep the original relative lookup and its dirfd, including errors
15742        // such as EBADF and ENOTDIR. The translated injection handles guest
15743        // PID spellings and placeholder directories just as the original
15744        // readlink does. Do not inspect the protected descriptor itself.
15745        let parent = match bytes.iter().rposition(|byte| *byte == b'/') {
15746            Some(0) => &b"/"[..],
15747            Some(end) => &bytes[..end],
15748            None => &b"."[..],
15749        };
15750        let stat_size = std::mem::size_of::<libc::stat>();
15751        let length = stat_size + parent.len() + 1;
15752        let Some(page) = procfs_levels::map_transient(guest, length).await else {
15753            return false;
15754        };
15755        // SAFETY: the mapping contains stat_size + parent.len() + 1 bytes,
15756        // so this u8 offset remains within the successfully mapped region.
15757        let parent_address = unsafe { page.add(stat_size) };
15758        let mut staged = parent.to_vec();
15759        staged.push(0);
15760        let stat = StatPtr(page.cast());
15761        let observed = if guest.memory().write_exact(parent_address, &staged).is_ok() {
15762            let call = syscalls::Newfstatat::new()
15763                .with_dirfd(dirfd)
15764                .with_path(PathPtr::from_ptr(
15765                    parent_address.as_raw() as *const libc::c_char
15766                ))
15767                .with_stat(Some(stat))
15768                .with_flags(AtFlags::empty());
15769            match Self::inject_translated_in_page(guest, Syscall::from(call)).await {
15770                Ok(_) => stat.read(&guest.memory()).ok(),
15771                Err(_) => None,
15772            }
15773        } else {
15774            None
15775        };
15776        procfs_levels::unmap_transient(guest, page, length).await;
15777        observed.is_some_and(|stat| {
15778            stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT == libc::S_IFDIR
15779                && self.is_caller_descriptor_identity(guest, (stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino), &["fd"])
15780                && guest.is_runtime_owned_fd(fd)
15781        })
15782    }
15783
15784    /// Answer `getdents` without a directory stream by issuing the guest's own
15785    /// call. With metadata virtualization, sort that kernel buffer and
15786    /// determinize its inodes. Without it, only omit runtime-owned entries
15787    /// from an authenticated caller descriptor table; keep host order and
15788    /// inodes. The host's `d_off` cookies are kept, so the kernel can
15789    /// still interpret them. A directory larger than one buffer comes back as
15790    /// sorted runs whose boundaries depend on the host.
15791    ///
15792    /// A buffer whose every entry is dropped (see
15793    /// [`Self::drop_absent_entries`]) is not returned empty, which would
15794    /// end the directory: the call is issued again from where the kernel
15795    /// left off. The bytes the kernel wrote past the entries returned, by this
15796    /// call or one it reissued, are zeroed, as they may name the entries
15797    /// dropped; so is a buffer every dropped entry was written to when the
15798    /// directory then ends.
15799    async fn project_one_buffer<G: Guest<Self>>(
15800        &self,
15801        guest: &mut G,
15802        call: GetdentsCall<'_>,
15803    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
15804        // The longest any call wrote: a reissued call can write less than the
15805        // one before it, whose dropped names lie past it.
15806        let virtualize = guest.config().virtualize_metadata;
15807        let mut written = 0;
15808        let mut dropped = false;
15809        let (len, mut entries) = loop {
15810            let len = match self.record_or_replay(guest, call.call).await {
15811                Ok(len) => len as usize,
15812                Err(error) => {
15813                    if written > 0 {
15814                        guest.memory().write_exact(call.buf, &vec![0; written])?;
15815                    }
15816                    return Err(error.into());
15817                }
15818            };
15819            if len == 0 {
15820                if written > 0 {
15821                    guest.memory().write_exact(call.buf, &vec![0; written])?;
15822                }
15823                return Ok(0);
15824            }
15825            written = written.max(len);
15826            let mut entries = match read_records(&guest.memory(), call.buf, len, call.format) {
15827                Ok(entries) => entries,
15828                Err(error) => {
15829                    guest.memory().write_exact(call.buf, &vec![0; written])?;
15830                    return Err(error.into());
15831                }
15832            };
15833            if virtualize {
15834                if let Err(error) = self.drop_absent_entries(guest, call.fd, &mut entries).await {
15835                    // The kernel already wrote these names. A failed identity
15836                    // probe must not leave omitted CPUs visible in the buffer.
15837                    guest.memory().write_exact(call.buf, &vec![0; written])?;
15838                    return Err(error);
15839                }
15840            } else {
15841                let original = entries.len();
15842                entries.retain(|entry| {
15843                    !runtime_owned_descriptor_entry(&entry.name, |fd| guest.is_runtime_owned_fd(fd))
15844                });
15845                if entries.len() == original && !dropped {
15846                    return Ok(len as i64);
15847                }
15848                dropped = true;
15849            }
15850            if !entries.is_empty() {
15851                break (len, entries);
15852            }
15853        };
15854        let inodes = if virtualize {
15855            sort_dir_entries(&mut entries);
15856            Some(self.directory_inodes(guest, call.fd).await?)
15857        } else {
15858            None
15859        };
15860        let mut records = Vec::with_capacity(len);
15861        for entry in &entries {
15862            let Some(inodes) = &inodes else {
15863                call.format
15864                    .encode(entry, entry.ino, entry.off, &mut records);
15865                continue;
15866            };
15867            let (host, path) = inodes.entry_inode(&entry.name, entry.ino);
15868            let files = self.rendered_files(guest);
15869            let d_ino = match self
15870                .rendered_listed_inode(guest, inodes, &entry.name, entry.ino, files)
15871                .await?
15872            {
15873                Some(inode) => DetInode::mint(inode),
15874                None => determinize_named_inode(guest, host, path).await.0,
15875            };
15876            call.format
15877                .encode(entry, d_ino.as_raw(), entry.off, &mut records);
15878        }
15879        let returned = records.len();
15880        // Zero what the kernel wrote past the entries returned.
15881        records.resize(returned.max(written), 0);
15882        if guest.memory().write_exact(call.buf, &records).is_err() {
15883            // The padding after the last name may not be writable, as Linux
15884            // does not write it.
15885            let written = entries.last().map_or(0, |last| {
15886                returned - call.format.record_len(last.name.len())
15887                    + call.format.written_len(last.name.len())
15888            });
15889            guest.memory().write_exact(call.buf, &records[..written])?;
15890        }
15891        Ok(returned as i64)
15892    }
15893
15894    /// Read the whole host directory behind `call.fd` into a private mapping
15895    /// (see [`Self::snapshot_directory`]), and return its entries in host
15896    /// order, less the CPUs and nodes Hermit's single virtual CPU and node
15897    /// leave out and the `/proc` names outside the run's level (see
15898    /// [`Self::drop_absent_entries`]). Every directory
15899    /// snapshot a stream stores comes from here, so none holds them.
15900    ///
15901    /// Linux writes into guest memory only the records a call returns and the
15902    /// fields it stored of one it could not finish, so the reads do not go to
15903    /// the guest's buffer, which may be too small
15904    /// for any entry, unreadable, or partly unmapped, nor to its stack. They
15905    /// go to an anonymous mapping injected for the purpose and unmapped
15906    /// before the guest runs again, as the atomic `writev` does for its
15907    /// iovecs. The mapping is fresh, so the reads leave nothing that the
15908    /// guest could see in memory. On the kvm backend, whose guest allocator
15909    /// fills the lowest hole below a cursor first and moves the cursor past
15910    /// each mapping it makes, the mapping moves that cursor, so a later
15911    /// mapping that fits no hole below it lands elsewhere than on Linux. That
15912    /// follows from the guest's own calls, so it is the same on every run.
15913    ///
15914    /// If a mapping of [`DIRECTORY_DRAIN_COUNT`] bytes cannot be made, one
15915    /// page is used, which still holds any entry. If that cannot be made
15916    /// either (the guest's address space is at its limit), the call fails
15917    /// with `ENOMEM` before anything is read, and the stream stays without a
15918    /// snapshot, so a later call tries again. Linux's `getdents` does not
15919    /// fail so; serving the directory in host order would make the order
15920    /// depend on the host. This divergence is tracked in
15921    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3723.
15922    async fn snapshot_directory_privately<G: Guest<Self>>(
15923        &self,
15924        guest: &mut G,
15925        call: GetdentsCall<'_>,
15926    ) -> Result<Option<Vec<DirEntry>>, Error> {
15927        let mut mapping = None;
15928        for len in [DIRECTORY_DRAIN_COUNT as usize, DIRECTORY_PAGE] {
15929            let mapped = guest
15930                .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
15931                    syscalls::Mmap::new()
15932                        .with_addr(None)
15933                        .with_len(len)
15934                        .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
15935                        .with_flags(MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS)
15936                        .with_fd(-1)
15937                        .with_offset(0),
15938                ))
15939                .await;
15940            if let Some(scratch) = mapped
15941                .ok()
15942                .and_then(|addr| usize::try_from(addr).ok())
15943                .and_then(AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw)
15944            {
15945                mapping = Some((scratch, len));
15946                break;
15947            }
15948        }
15949        let Some((scratch, len)) = mapping else {
15950            return Err(Errno::ENOMEM.into());
15951        };
15952        let snapshot = self
15953            .snapshot_directory(guest, call.into_scratch(scratch, len as u32))
15954            .await;
15955        let unmapped = guest
15956            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
15957                syscalls::Munmap::new()
15958                    .with_addr(Some(Addr::from(scratch).cast()))
15959                    .with_len(len),
15960            ))
15961            .await;
15962        // A mapping left behind would be visible to the guest.
15963        unmapped?;
15964        let mut snapshot = snapshot?;
15965        if let Some(entries) = &mut snapshot {
15966            self.drop_absent_entries(guest, call.fd, entries).await?;
15967        }
15968        Ok(snapshot)
15969    }
15970
15971    /// Read the whole host directory by issuing `call.call` until it returns
15972    /// 0, and return its entries in host order. `call` reads into a private
15973    /// mapping that holds any entry.
15974    ///
15975    /// Every step goes through `record_or_replay`, so a replay reads the same
15976    /// entries from the log. The reads must start at the beginning of the
15977    /// directory: a known directory is rewound there, and before the first
15978    /// snapshot the kernel position must already be 0.
15979    ///
15980    /// The first read fails as the guest's call would at any position: the
15981    /// descriptor is not a directory, or the directory has been removed.
15982    ///
15983    /// Returns `None` when this open file must be read in host order instead,
15984    /// with the kernel position where the guest left it. Either the position
15985    /// was moved before the first `getdents`, to a host cookie that no entry
15986    /// index stands for, or a read after the first failed, so the directory
15987    /// cannot be read to its end. A regular file, pipe or `O_PATH` descriptor
15988    /// whose position is not 0 also lands here, and reading it in host order
15989    /// reports the kernel's error without moving its offset.
15990    async fn snapshot_directory<G: Guest<Self>>(
15991        &self,
15992        guest: &mut G,
15993        call: GetdentsCall<'_>,
15994    ) -> Result<Option<Vec<DirEntry>>, Error> {
15995        let known_directory = guest
15996            .thread_state()
15997            .with_detfd(call.fd, |detfd| detfd.has_directory_stream())?;
15998        let lseek = |offset, whence| {
15999            syscalls::Lseek::new()
16000                .with_fd(call.fd)
16001                .with_offset(offset)
16002                .with_whence(whence)
16003        };
16004        if known_directory {
16005            self.record_or_replay(guest, lseek(0, Whence::SEEK_SET))
16006                .await?;
16007        } else if self
16008            .record_or_replay(guest, lseek(0, Whence::SEEK_CUR))
16009            .await
16010            != Ok(0)
16011        {
16012            return Ok(None);
16013        }
16014
16015        let mut entries = Vec::new();
16016        let mut read_any = false;
16017        let error: Error = loop {
16018            let len = match self.record_or_replay(guest, call.call).await {
16019                Ok(0) => return Ok(Some(entries)),
16020                Ok(len) => len as usize,
16021                Err(error) => break error.into(),
16022            };
16023            read_any = true;
16024            match read_records(&guest.memory(), call.buf, len, call.format) {
16025                Ok(parsed) => entries.extend(parsed),
16026                Err(error) => break error.into(),
16027            }
16028        };
16029        if !read_any {
16030            return Err(error);
16031        }
16032        // The earlier reads moved the position, which the guest's call must
16033        // find where the guest left it: at the start.
16034        self.record_or_replay(guest, lseek(0, Whence::SEEK_SET))
16035            .await?;
16036        Ok(None)
16037    }
16038}
16039
16040/// The size of the private mapping that a snapshot reads the host directory
16041/// into, and so the most bytes one read of it asks for. It holds any entry.
16042const DIRECTORY_DRAIN_COUNT: u32 = 64 * 1024;
16043
16044/// The granularity at which the guest's buffer can stop being writable.
16045const DIRECTORY_PAGE: usize = 4096;
16046
16047/// The most pages one vectored copy names: Linux's `IOV_MAX`.
16048const PAGES_PER_COPY: usize = 1024;
16049
16050/// The pieces of the `len` bytes at guest address `addr`, split where they
16051/// cross a page: the offset and length of each.
16052fn guest_pages(addr: usize, len: usize) -> Vec<(usize, usize)> {
16053    let mut pieces = Vec::with_capacity(len / DIRECTORY_PAGE + 2);
16054    let mut at = 0;
16055    while at < len {
16056        let piece = (DIRECTORY_PAGE - (addr + at) % DIRECTORY_PAGE).min(len - at);
16057        pieces.push((at, piece));
16058        at += piece;
16059    }
16060    pieces
16061}
16062
16063/// Read and decode the `len` bytes of records a `getdents` returned in the
16064/// guest's buffer. Linux does not write the padding after the last record's
16065/// name, which can lie in a page the guest cannot read.
16066fn read_records(
16067    memory: &impl MemoryAccess,
16068    buf: AddrMut<u8>,
16069    len: usize,
16070    format: DirentFormat,
16071) -> Result<Vec<DirEntry>, Errno> {
16072    let mut bytes = vec![0; len];
16073    let readable = match memory.read_exact(buf, &mut bytes) {
16074        Ok(()) => len,
16075        Err(_) => read_guest_prefix(memory, buf, &mut bytes)?,
16076    };
16077    format.parse_written(&mut bytes, readable)
16078}
16079
16080/// Read the start of the guest's buffer into `bytes`, up to the first page the
16081/// guest cannot read, and return how many bytes were read. Only a fault
16082/// (`EFAULT`) ends the copy short; any other error of the copy, such as
16083/// `ESRCH` for a thread that is gone or `EIO` from the backend, is returned.
16084///
16085/// This and [`write_guest_pieces`] use only vectored copies, one page per
16086/// piece, which respect the guest's page protection. Reverie's `read` and
16087/// `write` do not always: on the ptrace backend, a copy of at most 8 bytes goes
16088/// through `PTRACE_PEEKDATA` or `PTRACE_POKEDATA`, which reach a page the guest
16089/// has made inaccessible.
16090pub(crate) fn read_guest_prefix(
16091    memory: &impl MemoryAccess,
16092    buf: AddrMut<u8>,
16093    bytes: &mut [u8],
16094) -> Result<usize, Errno> {
16095    let mut done = 0;
16096    for pages in guest_pages(buf.as_raw(), bytes.len()).chunks(PAGES_PER_COPY) {
16097        let from = pages[0].0;
16098        let len: usize = pages.iter().map(|&(_, len)| len).sum();
16099        let remote: Vec<AddrSlice<u8>> = pages
16100            .iter()
16101            .map(|&(at, len)| unsafe { AddrSlice::from_raw_parts(buf.add(at).into(), len) })
16102            .collect();
16103        let remote: Vec<std::io::IoSlice> = remote
16104            .iter()
16105            .map(|piece| unsafe { piece.as_ioslice() })
16106            .collect();
16107        let mut local = [std::io::IoSliceMut::new(&mut bytes[from..from + len])];
16108        let copied = match memory.read_vectored(&remote, &mut local) {
16109            Err(Errno::EFAULT) => 0,
16110            copied => copied?,
16111        };
16112        done += copied;
16113        if copied < len {
16114            break;
16115        }
16116    }
16117    Ok(done)
16118}
16119
16120/// Write each of `pieces`, an offset in the guest's buffer and the bytes to
16121/// store there, within one page, in the order given, up to the first the
16122/// guest cannot write. Return how many bytes of the pieces were written,
16123/// counted in that order. As in [`read_guest_prefix`], only a fault ends the
16124/// copy short, and any other error is returned.
16125fn write_guest_pieces(
16126    memory: &mut impl MemoryAccess,
16127    buf: AddrMut<u8>,
16128    pieces: &[(usize, &[u8])],
16129) -> Result<usize, Errno> {
16130    let mut done = 0;
16131    for pieces in pieces.chunks(PAGES_PER_COPY) {
16132        let len: usize = pieces.iter().map(|(_, bytes)| bytes.len()).sum();
16133        let mut remote: Vec<AddrSliceMut<u8>> = pieces
16134            .iter()
16135            .map(|&(at, bytes)| unsafe { AddrSliceMut::from_raw_parts(buf.add(at), bytes.len()) })
16136            .collect();
16137        let mut remote: Vec<std::io::IoSliceMut> = remote
16138            .iter_mut()
16139            .map(|piece| unsafe { piece.as_ioslice_mut() })
16140            .collect();
16141        let local: Vec<std::io::IoSlice> = pieces
16142            .iter()
16143            .map(|&(_, bytes)| std::io::IoSlice::new(bytes))
16144            .collect();
16145        let copied = match memory.write_vectored(&local, &mut remote) {
16146            Err(Errno::EFAULT) => 0,
16147            copied => copied?,
16148        };
16149        done += copied;
16150        if copied < len {
16151            break;
16152        }
16153    }
16154    Ok(done)
16155}
16156
16157/// One store that Linux makes into the guest's buffer to copy directory
16158/// records: where in the buffer, the bytes stored (a range of the records,
16159/// or of the first record's placeholder `d_off` after them), and whether the
16160/// CPU makes it as one store, which writes nothing if any byte of it faults.
16161struct DirentStore {
16162    at: usize,
16163    from: std::ops::Range<usize>,
16164    single: bool,
16165}
16166
16167/// The stores Linux makes, in its order, to copy records whose names are
16168/// `names` bytes long, and for each record, how many of the stores precede
16169/// the end of its `filldir`. `placeholder` is where the first record's
16170/// placeholder `d_off` follows the records.
16171///
16172/// For each record, `filldir` (fs/readdir.c) first stores the `d_off` of the
16173/// record before it, which is its own entry's position. The first record of
16174/// a call has none before it, so its own `d_off` gets that position, to be
16175/// overwritten. Then come `d_ino`, `d_reclen`, `d_type`, the NUL after the
16176/// name, and the name. Once no more records are copied, the call stores the
16177/// last one's `d_off`. No padding is written.
16178///
16179/// Linux copies a name in words from its start, after the NUL that follows
16180/// it. A name spans at most two pages, and the NUL's page could be written,
16181/// so if a word of the name faults, the first does, and none of the name is
16182/// written. So it is here, where the name is written page by page.
16183fn dirent_stores(
16184    format: DirentFormat,
16185    names: &[usize],
16186    placeholder: usize,
16187) -> (Vec<DirentStore>, Vec<usize>) {
16188    let field = |at: usize, len: usize| DirentStore {
16189        at,
16190        from: at..at + len,
16191        single: true,
16192    };
16193    let mut stores = Vec::with_capacity(names.len() * 6 + 1);
16194    let mut filled = Vec::with_capacity(names.len());
16195    let mut previous = None;
16196    let mut at = 0;
16197    for &name_len in names {
16198        let reclen = format.record_len(name_len);
16199        let name = at + format.name_offset();
16200        stores.push(match previous {
16201            Some(previous) => field(previous + 8, 8),
16202            None => DirentStore {
16203                at: at + 8,
16204                from: placeholder..placeholder + 8,
16205                single: true,
16206            },
16207        });
16208        stores.push(field(at, 8));
16209        stores.push(field(at + 16, 2));
16210        stores.push(field(at + format.type_offset(reclen), 1));
16211        stores.push(field(name + name_len, 1));
16212        stores.push(DirentStore {
16213            at: name,
16214            from: name..name + name_len,
16215            single: false,
16216        });
16217        filled.push(stores.len());
16218        previous = Some(at);
16219        at += reclen;
16220    }
16221    if let Some(previous) = previous {
16222        stores.push(field(previous + 8, 8));
16223    }
16224    (stores, filled)
16225}
16226
16227/// Copy directory records into the guest's buffer as Linux does: store by
16228/// store (see [`dirent_stores`]), up to the first store the guest cannot
16229/// write. `records` holds the records of entries whose names are `names`
16230/// bytes long, the first at position `start`.
16231///
16232/// Return how many entries the call passes, and its result: the bytes of the
16233/// records whose `filldir` completed. It is `EFAULT` if none did, or if the
16234/// fault hit a `d_off`, which the call's last store would then write again.
16235/// A copy that fails with any error other than a fault passes no entry and
16236/// returns that error, as the call did before directory streams.
16237///
16238/// Each store within one page is written whole or not at all, as Linux's
16239/// are. A single store that crosses into another page, a field of a buffer
16240/// not aligned to 8 bytes, the CPU writes whole or not at all, so its two
16241/// parts are written one after the other and the first is put back if the
16242/// second cannot be written. What is put back is read just before the first
16243/// part is written, after every store before it, which may have changed those
16244/// bytes through another mapping of the same memory. The part written first
16245/// is the one whose bytes Detcore can read to put back: the part in the
16246/// second page, unless only the part in the first page can be read. Where
16247/// neither can be read with a vectored copy, the part in the second page is
16248/// written first, so that a write-only buffer ending at a page the guest
16249/// cannot touch is left as Linux leaves it, and its bytes are read to put
16250/// back with Reverie's `read`, which for at most 8 bytes is `PTRACE_PEEKDATA`
16251/// on the ptrace backend and reads a write-only page. While no other thread
16252/// writes the buffer, only a store from a page the guest can neither read nor
16253/// write into a write-only page that this read cannot reach either leaves
16254/// bytes Linux does not write: up to 7, in the write-only page.
16255fn copy_records(
16256    memory: &mut impl MemoryAccess,
16257    buf: AddrMut<u8>,
16258    format: DirentFormat,
16259    records: &[u8],
16260    names: &[usize],
16261    start: u64,
16262) -> (usize, Result<usize, Errno>) {
16263    if names.is_empty() {
16264        return (0, Ok(0));
16265    }
16266    let mut source = records.to_vec();
16267    let placeholder = source.len();
16268    source.extend_from_slice(&i64::try_from(start).unwrap_or(i64::MAX).to_ne_bytes());
16269    let (stores, filled) = dirent_stores(format, names, placeholder);
16270    // Each piece, within one page: where in the buffer and its bytes, and,
16271    // in `owner`, its store.
16272    let mut pieces: Vec<(usize, &[u8])> = Vec::with_capacity(stores.len());
16273    let mut owner = Vec::with_capacity(stores.len());
16274    // For each single store that crosses pages: its part written first, as an
16275    // index into `pieces`, and whether the guest can read that part's bytes.
16276    let mut crossing = Vec::new();
16277    for (index, store) in stores.iter().enumerate() {
16278        let mut split = guest_pages(buf.as_raw() + store.at, store.from.len());
16279        if store.single && split.len() > 1 {
16280            let readable: Result<Vec<bool>, Errno> = split
16281                .iter()
16282                .map(|&(at, len)| {
16283                    let mut bytes = vec![0; len];
16284                    let addr = unsafe { buf.add(store.at + at) };
16285                    Ok(read_guest_prefix(memory, addr, &mut bytes)? == len)
16286                })
16287                .collect();
16288            let mut readable = match readable {
16289                Ok(readable) => readable,
16290                Err(errno) => return (0, Err(errno)),
16291            };
16292            if readable[1] || !readable[0] {
16293                split.reverse();
16294                readable.reverse();
16295            }
16296            crossing.push((pieces.len(), readable[0]));
16297        }
16298        for (at, len) in split {
16299            let from = store.from.start + at;
16300            pieces.push((store.at + at, &source[from..from + len]));
16301            owner.push(index);
16302        }
16303    }
16304    // Write the pieces in order, stopping before the first part of each
16305    // crossing store to save what the guest has there. The stores before it
16306    // can have changed those bytes through another mapping of the same memory,
16307    // so they are read only once those stores are made.
16308    let mut next = 0;
16309    let mut saved: Option<(usize, Vec<u8>)> = None;
16310    let mut failed = None;
16311    for &(stop, readable) in crossing.iter().chain([(pieces.len(), false)].iter()) {
16312        let segment = &pieces[next..stop];
16313        let written = match write_guest_pieces(memory, buf, segment) {
16314            Ok(written) => written,
16315            Err(errno) => return (0, Err(errno)),
16316        };
16317        let mut end = 0;
16318        if let Some(at) = segment.iter().position(|(_, bytes)| {
16319            end += bytes.len();
16320            end > written
16321        }) {
16322            failed = Some(next + at);
16323            break;
16324        }
16325        if stop == pieces.len() {
16326            break;
16327        }
16328        let (at, bytes) = pieces[stop];
16329        let addr = unsafe { buf.add(at) };
16330        let mut before = vec![0; bytes.len()];
16331        let read = if readable {
16332            match read_guest_prefix(memory, addr, &mut before) {
16333                Ok(read) => read == before.len(),
16334                Err(errno) => return (0, Err(errno)),
16335            }
16336        } else {
16337            // The part in the second page, at its start, which no vectored copy
16338            // can read. Reverie's `read` of at most 8 bytes can on the ptrace
16339            // backend, through `PTRACE_PEEKDATA`, and a read changes nothing
16340            // the guest sees.
16341            memory.read_exact(addr, &mut before).is_ok()
16342        };
16343        saved = read.then_some((stop, before));
16344        next = stop;
16345    }
16346    let Some(failed) = failed else {
16347        return (names.len(), Ok(records.len()));
16348    };
16349    let store = owner[failed];
16350    if failed > 0
16351        && owner[failed - 1] == store
16352        && let Some((first, before)) = &saved
16353        && *first == failed - 1
16354        && let Err(errno) =
16355            write_guest_pieces(memory, buf, &[(pieces[*first].0, before.as_slice())])
16356    {
16357        return (0, Err(errno));
16358    }
16359    // The entry whose `filldir` made the store, or all of them for the call's
16360    // last store, and the first store of that `filldir`.
16361    let entry = filled.partition_point(|&end| end <= store);
16362    let first = entry.checked_sub(1).map_or(0, |before| filled[before]);
16363    let result = if entry == 0 || store == first {
16364        Err(Errno::EFAULT)
16365    } else {
16366        Ok(names[..entry]
16367            .iter()
16368            .map(|&name_len| format.record_len(name_len))
16369            .sum())
16370    };
16371    (entry, result)
16372}
16373
16374/// A guest `getdents` or `getdents64` call.
16375#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
16376struct GetdentsCall<'a> {
16377    /// The call as the guest made it.
16378    call: Syscall,
16379    /// The same call asking for no bytes.
16380    empty: Syscall,
16381    fd: RawFd,
16382    buf: AddrMut<'a, u8>,
16383    /// The guest's buffer size.
16384    capacity: usize,
16385    format: DirentFormat,
16386}
16387
16388impl<'a> GetdentsCall<'a> {
16389    /// The same call reading at most `count` bytes into `buf` instead.
16390    fn into_scratch<'b>(self, buf: AddrMut<'b, u8>, count: u32) -> GetdentsCall<'b> {
16391        let call = match self.call {
16392            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
16393            Syscall::Getdents(call) => {
16394                Syscall::from(call.with_dirent(Some(buf.cast())).with_count(count))
16395            }
16396            Syscall::Getdents64(call) => {
16397                Syscall::from(call.with_dirent(Some(buf.cast())).with_count(count))
16398            }
16399            other => other,
16400        };
16401        GetdentsCall {
16402            call,
16403            empty: self.empty,
16404            fd: self.fd,
16405            buf,
16406            capacity: count as usize,
16407            format: self.format,
16408        }
16409    }
16410}
16411
16412/// Whether every byte of `[address, address + len)` lies in some mapping of a
16413/// `/proc/<pid>/maps` listing (`Detcore::vectored_signalfd_read`).
16414fn signalfd_range_is_mapped(maps: &str, address: usize, len: usize) -> bool {
16415    signalfd_range_is_covered(maps, address, len, false)
16416}
16417
16418/// Whether every byte of `[address, address + len)` lies in some writable
16419/// mapping of a `/proc/<pid>/maps` listing
16420/// (`Detcore::settle_faulted_signalfd_record`).
16421fn signalfd_range_is_writable(maps: &str, address: usize, len: usize) -> bool {
16422    signalfd_range_is_covered(maps, address, len, true)
16423}
16424
16425/// The pieces of the guest buffers `extents` (address, length) that the
16426/// signalfd record after the first `read` bytes would fill, or `None` if
16427/// they have no room for a whole record there (Linux reads only whole ones).
16428fn signalfd_next_record(extents: &[(usize, usize)], read: usize) -> Option<Vec<(usize, usize)>> {
16429    const RECORD: usize = std::mem::size_of::<libc::signalfd_siginfo>();
16430    let capacity = extents
16431        .iter()
16432        .try_fold(0usize, |total, (_, len)| total.checked_add(*len))?;
16433    if capacity / RECORD <= read / RECORD {
16434        return None;
16435    }
16436    let mut skip = read - read % RECORD;
16437    let mut left = RECORD;
16438    let mut pieces = Vec::new();
16439    for (address, len) in extents {
16440        if left == 0 {
16441            break;
16442        }
16443        if skip >= *len {
16444            skip -= len;
16445            continue;
16446        }
16447        let take = (len - skip).min(left);
16448        pieces.push((address + skip, take));
16449        left -= take;
16450        skip = 0;
16451    }
16452    Some(pieces)
16453}
16454
16455/// The end of the user address space, x86-64's `TASK_SIZE_MAX`, above which
16456/// `access_ok` fails a buffer before a call does anything: 2^56 - 4096 where
16457/// the kernel runs five-level page tables, 2^47 - 4096 otherwise. Measured
16458/// once, by asking for a mapping above 2^47, which the kernel grants there
16459/// only with five-level page tables.
16460fn user_address_end() -> usize {
16461    static END: std::sync::OnceLock<usize> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
16462    *END.get_or_init(|| {
16463        const HINT: usize = 1 << 48;
16464        // SAFETY: a fresh anonymous mapping, unmapped at once; the hint is
16465        // only a hint (no MAP_FIXED).
16466        let at = unsafe {
16467            libc::mmap(
16468                HINT as *mut libc::c_void,
16469                4096,
16470                libc::PROT_NONE,
16471                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS,
16472                -1,
16473                0,
16474            )
16475        };
16476        if at == libc::MAP_FAILED {
16477            return (1 << 47) - 4096;
16478        }
16479        // SAFETY: the mapping made above.
16480        unsafe { libc::munmap(at, 4096) };
16481        if at as usize >= 1 << 47 {
16482            (1 << 56) - 4096
16483        } else {
16484            (1 << 47) - 4096
16485        }
16486    })
16487}
16488
16489/// Authenticate the current task's FD/fdinfo directory by kernel object
16490/// identity, including symlink/bind aliases, without interpreting guest PIDs.
16491#[cfg(test)]
16492fn is_caller_descriptor_directory(
16493    observed: &std::fs::Metadata,
16494    caller: &str,
16495    process: Option<&str>,
16496) -> bool {
16497    caller_descriptor_identity_matches(
16498        (observed.dev(), observed.ino()),
16499        caller,
16500        process,
16501        &["fd", "fdinfo"],
16502    )
16503}
16504
16505fn caller_descriptor_identity_matches(
16506    observed: (u64, u64),
16507    caller: &str,
16508    process: Option<&str>,
16509    kinds: &[&str],
16510) -> bool {
16511    [Some(caller), process].into_iter().flatten().any(|owner| {
16512        kinds.iter().any(|kind| {
16513            std::fs::metadata(format!("{owner}/{kind}"))
16514                .is_ok_and(|expected| observed == (expected.dev(), expected.ino()))
16515        })
16516    })
16517}
16518
16519fn runtime_owned_descriptor_entry(name: &[u8], owns: impl FnOnce(RawFd) -> bool) -> bool {
16520    !name.is_empty()
16521        && name.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_digit)
16522        && std::str::from_utf8(name)
16523            .ok()
16524            .and_then(|name| name.parse::<RawFd>().ok())
16525            .is_some_and(owns)
16526}
16527
16528/// The signals a signalfd reads, from its `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo` entry.
16529fn signalfd_sigmask(pid: i32, fd: i32) -> Option<u64> {
16530    let info = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/fdinfo/{fd}")).ok()?;
16531    let mask = info
16532        .lines()
16533        .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("sigmask:"))?;
16534    u64::from_str_radix(mask.trim(), 16).ok()
16535}
16536
16537fn signalfd_range_is_covered(maps: &str, address: usize, len: usize, writable: bool) -> bool {
16538    let mut ranges: Vec<(usize, usize)> = maps
16539        .lines()
16540        .filter_map(|line| {
16541            let mut fields = line.split_whitespace();
16542            let (start, end) = fields.next()?.split_once('-')?;
16543            if writable && !fields.next()?.contains('w') {
16544                return None;
16545            }
16546            Some((
16547                usize::from_str_radix(start, 16).ok()?,
16548                usize::from_str_radix(end, 16).ok()?,
16549            ))
16550        })
16551        .collect();
16552    ranges.sort();
16553    let Some(end) = address.checked_add(len) else {
16554        return false;
16555    };
16556    let mut next = address;
16557    for (start, stop) in ranges {
16558        if start <= next && next < stop {
16559            next = stop;
16560            if next >= end {
16561                return true;
16562            }
16563        }
16564    }
16565    false
16566}
