16568#[cfg(test)]
16569mod guest_proc_visibility_tests {
16570    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
16571
16572    use reverie::BackendCapabilities;
16573
16574    use super::reopens_scheduler_managed_pipe;
16575    use super::resolved_open_path;
16576
16577    /// The open-path helpers read `/proc/<pid>/fd/<fd>` wherever guest
16578    /// threads are host tasks: ptrace (whose facts a DBT run without its
16579    /// configuration keeps), in-guest LiteInst, DBT and SaBRe.
16580    /// With this process's own pipe and file, those read the links. KVM, whose
16581    /// guest is not a host task, never consults them and gives the helpers'
16582    /// "unknown" answers.
16583    #[tokio::test]
16584    async fn host_proc_links_are_read_except_under_kvm() {
16585        let pid = std::process::id() as i32;
16586        let (reader, _writer) = nix::unistd::pipe().unwrap();
16587        let alias = nix::unistd::dup(&reader).unwrap();
16588        let file = std::fs::File::open("/proc/self/exe").unwrap();
16589        let (pipe_fd, alias_fd) = (reader.as_raw_fd(), alias.as_raw_fd());
16590        let file_fd = file.as_raw_fd();
16591
16592        for backend in [
16593            BackendCapabilities::PTRACE,
16594            BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST,
16595            BackendCapabilities::DBT,
16596            BackendCapabilities::SABRE,
16597        ] {
16598            assert!(
16599                reopens_scheduler_managed_pipe(&backend, pid, alias_fd, &[pipe_fd]),
16600                "{backend:?}"
16601            );
16602            assert!(
16603                resolved_open_path(&backend, pid, file_fd).is_some(),
16604                "{backend:?}"
16605            );
16606        }
16607        let kvm = BackendCapabilities::KVM;
16608        assert!(!reopens_scheduler_managed_pipe(
16609            &kvm,
16610            pid,
16611            alias_fd,
16612            &[pipe_fd]
16613        ));
16614        assert_eq!(resolved_open_path(&kvm, pid, file_fd), None);
16615
16616        // Runtime ownership is exact: ordinary high application descriptors
16617        // remain visible, and a directory merely named "fd" is not procfs.
16618        for name in [
16619            b"1023".as_slice(),
16620            b"1025",
16621            b"4096",
16622            b".",
16623            b"..",
16624            b"+1024",
16625            b"2147483648",
16626        ] {
16627            assert!(!super::runtime_owned_descriptor_entry(name, |fd| fd == 1024));
16628        }
16629        assert!(super::runtime_owned_descriptor_entry(b"1024", |fd| fd == 1024));
16630        assert!(!super::runtime_owned_descriptor_entry(b"1024", |_| false));
16631        for kind in ["fd", "fdinfo"] {
16632            let thread = std::fs::metadata(format!("/proc/thread-self/{kind}")).unwrap();
16633            let process = std::fs::metadata(format!("/proc/self/{kind}")).unwrap();
16634            assert!(super::is_caller_descriptor_directory(
16635                &thread,
16636                "/proc/thread-self",
16637                None
16638            ));
16639            assert!(!super::is_caller_descriptor_directory(
16640                &process,
16641                "/proc/thread-self",
16642                None
16643            ));
16644            assert!(super::is_caller_descriptor_directory(
16645                &process,
16646                "/proc/thread-self",
16647                Some("/proc/self")
16648            ));
16649        }
16650        let ordinary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
16651        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(ordinary.path()).unwrap();
16652        assert!(!super::is_caller_descriptor_directory(
16653            &metadata,
16654            "/proc/thread-self",
16655            Some("/proc/self")
16656        ));
16657        super::inject_fstat_scratch::raw_directory_projection().await;
16658    }
16659}

16661#[cfg(test)]
16662mod signalfd_geometry_tests {
16663    use super::signalfd_next_record;
16664    use super::signalfd_range_is_mapped;
16665    use super::signalfd_range_is_writable;
16666
16667    /// A range is mapped only when contiguous mappings cover every byte.
16668    #[test]
16669    fn an_iovec_array_is_mapped_only_when_mappings_cover_every_byte() {
16670        let maps =
16671            "1000-2000 r--p 0 0:0 0\n2000-3000 ---p 0 0:0 0 [vvar]\n5000-6000 rw-p 0 0:0 0\n";
16672        assert!(signalfd_range_is_mapped(maps, 0x1ff0, 32));
16673        assert!(
16674            !signalfd_range_is_mapped(maps, 0x2ff0, 32),
16675            "runs into a hole"
16676        );
16677        assert!(!signalfd_range_is_mapped(maps, 0x4000, 16));
16678        assert!(!signalfd_range_is_mapped(maps, usize::MAX - 4, 16));
16679        assert!(!signalfd_range_is_mapped("", 0x1000, 16));
16680    }
16681
16682    /// The record a signalfd read could have lost after the bytes it
16683    /// returned: only where the buffers hold a whole further record, which
16684    /// may span iovecs, and lost only if some byte of it is not writable.
16685    #[test]
16686    fn the_record_after_a_read_is_where_the_buffers_have_room_for_it() {
16687        assert_eq!(
16688            signalfd_next_record(&[(0x1000, 256)], 128),
16689            Some(vec![(0x1080, 128)])
16690        );
16691        assert_eq!(signalfd_next_record(&[(0x1000, 255)], 128), None);
16692        assert_eq!(signalfd_next_record(&[(0x1000, 128)], 128), None);
16693        assert_eq!(
16694            signalfd_next_record(&[(0x1000, 100), (0x3000, 60), (0x5000, 300)], 128),
16695            Some(vec![(0x3000 + 28, 32), (0x5000, 96)])
16696        );
16697        assert_eq!(
16698            signalfd_next_record(&[(0x1000, usize::MAX), (0x2000, 2)], 0),
16699            None
16700        );
16701        let maps = "1000-2000 rw-p 0 0:0 0\n2000-3000 ---p 0 0:0 0\n";
16702        assert!(signalfd_range_is_writable(maps, 0x1f80, 128));
16703        assert!(!signalfd_range_is_writable(maps, 0x1fc0, 128));
16704        assert!(signalfd_range_is_mapped(maps, 0x1fc0, 128));
16705    }
16706}

16708#[cfg(test)]
16709mod procfs_wiring_guard {
16710    //! The procfs snapshot WIRING, guarded where the wiring lives.
16711    //!
16712    //! WHY THIS IS A SOURCE-LEVEL GUARD AND NOT A BEHAVIOURAL TEST. The thing
16713    //! at risk is not `ProcfsFile`'s logic -- that is exercised elsewhere. It is
16714    //! the CALL from each read handler into the snapshot initialiser. Those
16715    //! handlers are `async fn`s on the `Tool` trait taking a live `Guest`, so a
16716    //! unit test cannot invoke one without standing up a traced guest process;
16717    //! that is exactly why the only thing guarding this today is one heavyweight
16718    //! integration test that compiles a C probe and runs hermit.
16719    //!
16720    //! MEASURED GAP (2026-08-07, hermit 75506005d): deleting the pread64
16721    //! snapshot-initialisation block leaves ALL 386 detcore lib tests green.
16722    //! A mechanism whose only proof of life is one fixture is one deletion away
16723    //! from vanishing unnoticed -- the positioned-read determinism bug this
16724    //! wiring fixes would silently return.
16725    //!
16726    //! These assertions are deliberately narrow: they bind to the CALL, name the
16727    //! mechanism when they fail, and cost nothing to run. They do not claim to
16728    //! verify that the snapshot is correct.
16729
16730    /// The production source only. `include_str!` pulls in THIS module too, so a
16731    /// naive scan counts the guard's own string literals and reports phantom
16732    /// duplicates -- it did exactly that on first run. Truncating at the guard's
16733    /// own header makes every assertion below immune to self-reference.
16734    fn production_source() -> &'static str {
16735        const WHOLE: &str = include_str!("files.rs");
16736        const GUARD: &str = "#[cfg(test)]\nmod procfs_wiring_guard {";
16737        match WHOLE.find(GUARD) {
16738            Some(cut) => &WHOLE[..cut],
16739            None => WHOLE,
16740        }
16741    }
16742
16743    /// The body of `fn <name>` up to the next top-level `    }` at fn indent.
16744    fn handler_body(name: &str) -> &'static str {
16745        let start = production_source()
16746            .find(&format!("fn {}<G: Guest<Self>>", name))
16747            .unwrap_or_else(|| {
16748                panic!(
16749                    "procfs wiring guard: handler `{name}` not found in files.rs.\n\
16750                     TWO VERY DIFFERENT CAUSES, and the guard cannot tell them apart:\n\
16751                       (a) the handler was RENAMED or its signature changed -- the \
16752                     mechanism is fine, update the name in this guard; or\n\
16753                       (b) the handler was DELETED -- the procfs snapshot wiring is gone.\n\
16754                     Check which before editing. This guard binds to source text on \
16755                     purpose: the handlers are async `Tool` methods taking a live Guest, \
16756                     so nothing cheaper can observe the call. It is deliberately loud \
16757                     when it cannot see the code, because silently passing is the \
16758                     failure it exists to prevent."
16759                )
16760            });
16761        let rest = &production_source()[start..];
16762        let end = rest
16763            .find(
16764                "
16765    }
16766",
16767            )
16768            .map(|e| e + 6)
16769            .unwrap_or(rest.len());
16770        &rest[..end]
16771    }
16772
16773    #[test]
16774    fn pread64_initializes_the_procfs_snapshot() {
16775        let body = handler_body("handle_pread64");
16776        assert!(
16777            body.contains("procfs_needs_snapshot") && body.contains("initialize_procfs_snapshot"),
16778            "MISSING MECHANISM: the pread64 handler no longer initialises the procfs \
16779             snapshot. Positioned reads will fall through to LIVE KERNEL BYTES instead of \
16780             the sanitized ProcfsFile snapshot, reintroducing the positioned-read \
16781             nondeterminism that hermit-cli/tests/procfs_positioned_determinism.rs exists \
16782             to catch. Restore the `procfs_needs_snapshot` -> `initialize_procfs_snapshot` \
16783             call in handle_pread64."
16784        );
16785    }
16786
16787    #[test]
16788    fn read_initializes_the_procfs_snapshot() {
16789        let body = handler_body("handle_read");
16790        assert!(
16791            body.contains("procfs_needs_snapshot") && body.contains("initialize_procfs_snapshot"),
16792            "MISSING MECHANISM: the sequential read handler no longer initialises the \
16793             procfs snapshot. Reads of /proc will observe live kernel bytes. Restore the \
16794             `procfs_needs_snapshot` -> `initialize_procfs_snapshot` call in handle_read."
16795        );
16796    }
16797
16798    #[test]
16799    fn both_read_paths_share_one_snapshot_initializer() {
16800        // The original defect was exactly this asymmetry: `read` consumed the
16801        // sanitized snapshot while `pread64` did not. Forking the logic into two
16802        // initialisers is how that asymmetry comes back.
16803        let n = production_source()
16804            .matches("async fn initialize_procfs_snapshot")
16805            .count();
16806        assert_eq!(
16807            n, 1,
16808            "MISSING MECHANISM: expected exactly ONE `initialize_procfs_snapshot` \
16809             definition so every read path shares it; found {n}. Two initialisers is how \
16810             read/pread64 drifted apart in the first place."
16811        );
16812        for handler in ["handle_read", "handle_pread64"] {
16813            assert!(
16814                handler_body(handler).contains("self.initialize_procfs_snapshot("),
16815                "MISSING MECHANISM: `{handler}` does not call the shared \
16816                 initialize_procfs_snapshot."
16817            );
16818        }
16819    }
16820
16821    /// Both mountinfo captures in the snapshot initializer must drop ephemeral
16822    /// host seed rows (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3219): the guest
16823    /// read's capture, for the files that carry mountinfo identities, and the
16824    /// tracer-side capture that validates fdinfo `mnt_id`. Without either, host
16825    /// seed churn reaches guest-visible mountinfo or shifts mount-ID assignment,
16826    /// and no unit test of the filter itself notices.
16827    #[test]
16828    fn snapshot_initializer_excludes_host_seed_mounts_at_both_captures() {
16829        let body = handler_body("initialize_procfs_snapshot");
16830        let calls = body.matches("exclude_ephemeral_host_seed_mounts(").count();
16831        assert_eq!(
16832            calls, 2,
16833            "MISSING MECHANISM: initialize_procfs_snapshot must call \
16834             exclude_ephemeral_host_seed_mounts exactly twice (the guest mountinfo \
16835             capture and the fdinfo mnt_id capture); found {calls}. Without it, \
16836             unrelated host squashfuse seed mounts make /proc/<pid>/mountinfo and \
16837             fdinfo mount IDs depend on host timing."
16838        );
16839        let guest_capture = body
16840            .find("exclude_ephemeral_host_seed_mounts(&raw_contents)")
16841            .expect(
16842                "MISSING MECHANISM: the guest read's procfs capture (`raw_contents`) is \
16843                 no longer filtered for host seed mounts",
16844            );
16845        let gate = body[..guest_capture]
16846            .rfind("let contents = if")
16847            .map(|start| &body[start..guest_capture])
16848            .unwrap_or_default();
16849        assert!(
16850            gate.contains("procfs_needs_mountinfo_identities()"),
16851            "MISSING MECHANISM: the guest capture's seed filter must apply exactly to \
16852             the files that carry mountinfo identities (`let contents = if ... \
16853             procfs_needs_mountinfo_identities()`); found {gate:?}"
16854        );
16855        let fdinfo_capture = body
16856            .find("exclude_ephemeral_host_seed_mounts(&mountinfo_contents)")
16857            .expect(
16858                "MISSING MECHANISM: the fdinfo mnt_id capture (`mountinfo_contents`) is \
16859                 no longer filtered for host seed mounts",
16860            );
16861        let parse = body
16862            .find("parse_mountinfo(&mountinfo_contents)")
16863            .expect("the fdinfo mnt_id capture no longer parses mountinfo_contents");
16864        assert!(
16865            fdinfo_capture < parse,
16866            "MISSING MECHANISM: the fdinfo mnt_id capture parses mountinfo before \
16867             dropping host seed rows"
16868        );
16869    }
16870
16871    #[test]
16872    fn the_guard_can_actually_see_the_handlers() {
16873        // Positive control: if the extractor silently returned empty bodies the
16874        // three assertions above would be vacuous rather than protective.
16875        for handler in ["handle_read", "handle_pread64"] {
16876            let body = handler_body(handler);
16877            assert!(
16878                body.len() > 200 && body.contains("call.fd()"),
16879                "guard extractor did not find a real body for `{handler}` \
16880                 (len {}), so the wiring assertions would be vacuous",
16881                body.len()
16882            );
16883        }
16884    }
16885}

16887#[cfg(test)]
16888mod test {
16889    use nix::fcntl::OFlag;
16890    use reverie::syscalls::FromToRaw;
16891    use reverie::syscalls::LocalMemory;
16892    use reverie::syscalls::Whence;
16893
16894    use super::deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes;
16895    use super::fcntl_host_timed_signals;
16896    use super::ioctl_host_timed_signals;
16897    use super::may_have_acquired_controlling_terminal;
16898    use super::open_can_acquire_controlling_terminal;
16899    use super::opened_controlling_terminal;
16900    use super::pipe_capacity_request_exceeds_ceiling;
16901    use super::terminal_can_become_controlling;
16902    use crate::test_pages::PAGE;
16903    use crate::test_pages::Pages;
16904
16905    /// Run the test named `case` in an isolated child process, returning
16906    /// true when this invocation is the parent and the caller must return
16907    /// at once. Tests that close this process's real descriptors and then
16908    /// assert the numbers are dead race sibling test threads under plain
16909    /// `cargo test`: a sibling can be handed a just-closed number before
16910    /// the assertion reads it. A child process has no sibling threads
16911    /// allocating descriptors.
16912    fn isolated_child(case: &str) -> bool {
16913        const CHILD: &str = "HERMIT_FILES_TEST_CHILD";
16914        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).as_deref() == Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new(case)) {
16915            return false;
16916        }
16917        let output = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
16918            .args(["--exact", case, "--nocapture", "--test-threads=1"])
16919            .env(CHILD, case)
16920            .output()
16921            .unwrap();
16922        assert!(output.status.success(), "{output:?}");
16923        assert!(
16924            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).contains("1 passed"),
16925            "{output:?}"
16926        );
16927        true
16928    }
16929
16930    /// A `/proc/self` or `/proc/thread-self` spelling leads to the opener's
16931    /// task, which a name relative to the descriptor is then looked up below,
16932    /// whoever looks it up.
16933    #[test]
16934    fn a_proc_selector_leads_to_the_openers_task() {
16935        use std::path::Path;
16936
16937        use super::procfs_selector_reached;
16938
16939        let own = Some((3, 5));
16940        for (spelling, reached) in [
16941            ("/proc/self", Some("/proc/3")),
16942            ("/proc/self/", Some("/proc/3")),
16943            ("/proc/self/task", Some("/proc/3/task")),
16944            ("/proc/self/task/5", Some("/proc/3/task/5")),
16945            ("/proc/thread-self", Some("/proc/3/task/5")),
16946            ("/proc/self/fd/7", None),
16947            ("/proc/self/task/05", None),
16948            ("/proc/thread-self/fd/7", None),
16949            ("/proc/self/cwd", None),
16950            ("/proc/3", Some("/proc/3")),
16951            ("/proc/7/", Some("/proc/7")),
16952            ("/proc/7/task", Some("/proc/7/task")),
16953            ("/proc/7/task/9", Some("/proc/7/task/9")),
16954            ("/proc/07", None),
16955            ("/proc/7/task/09", None),
16956            ("/proc/7/fd", None),
16957            ("/proc/7/task/9/fd/1", None),
16958            ("/proc/sys", None),
16959            ("/proc", None),
16960            ("/proc/selfish", None),
16961            ("/dev/fd", None),
16962            ("self", None),
16963        ] {
16964            assert_eq!(
16965                procfs_selector_reached(Path::new(spelling), own).as_deref(),
16966                reached.map(Path::new),
16967                "{spelling}"
16968            );
16969        }
16970        // In a nested PID namespace Detcore does not know the caller's numbers.
16971        assert_eq!(procfs_selector_reached(Path::new("/proc/self"), None), None);
16972        assert_eq!(procfs_selector_reached(Path::new("/proc/3"), None), None);
16973        // The selector links themselves, which an `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW` open
16974        // opens rather than the directory they lead to.
16975        for (spelling, link) in [
16976            ("/proc/self", true),
16977            ("/proc/thread-self", true),
16978            // A trailing slash follows the link (`opens_the_link_itself`).
16979            ("/proc/self/", true),
16980            ("/proc/self/task", false),
16981            ("/proc/3", false),
16982            ("/proc/selfish", false),
16983        ] {
16984            assert_eq!(
16985                super::names_a_selector_link(Path::new(spelling)),
16986                link,
16987                "{spelling}"
16988            );
16989        }
16990        // The task each reached directory is, or is below.
16991        let task = |process, thread| crate::procfs::BoundTask { process, thread };
16992        for (reached, expected) in [
16993            ("/proc/3", Some(task(3, None))),
16994            ("/proc/3/task", Some(task(3, None))),
16995            ("/proc/3/task/5", Some(task(3, Some(5)))),
16996            ("/proc/3/task/5/ns", Some(task(3, Some(5)))),
16997            ("/proc/3/ns", Some(task(3, None))),
16998            ("/proc", None),
16999            ("/proc/sys", None),
17000            ("/proc/0", None),
17001        ] {
17002            assert_eq!(
17003                super::procfs_reached_task(Path::new(reached)),
17004                expected,
17005                "{reached}"
17006            );
17007        }
17008    }
17009
17010    /// A descriptor opened through one of the caller's descriptor links
17011    /// records the path of the descriptor the link names, so a name relative
17012    /// to it is the file Linux finds below that file: `/proc/stat` through a
17013    /// reopened `/proc`, and through a reopened reopening. It keeps its
17014    /// spelling wherever the recorded path could name another file: a link
17015    /// opened itself (`O_NOFOLLOW` without a trailing slash), the process's
17016    /// table where the caller holds a table of its own, a target without an
17017    /// absolute recorded path, and a target that names a per-caller
17018    /// selector. Every other open records its spelling.
17019    #[test]
17020    fn an_open_through_a_descriptor_link_records_the_targets_path() {
17021        use std::path::Path;
17022        use std::path::PathBuf;
17023
17024        use super::DescriptorLinkOpener;
17025        use super::path_to_record_for_open;
17026
17027        let leader = DescriptorLinkOpener {
17028            own: Some((3, 3)),
17029            holds_process_table: true,
17030        };
17031        let read = OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_DIRECTORY;
17032        let table = |fd: i32| match fd {
17033            4 => Some(PathBuf::from("/proc")),
17034            6 => Some(PathBuf::from("relative/dir")),
17035            8 => Some(PathBuf::from("/proc/self")),
17036            9 => Some(PathBuf::from("/proc/thread-self")),
17037            10 => Some(PathBuf::from("/dev/fd")),
17038            11 => Some(PathBuf::from("/proc/12")),
17039            _ => None,
17040        };
17041        for spelling in [
17042            "/proc/self/fd/4",
17043            "/dev/fd/4",
17044            "/proc/thread-self/fd/4",
17045            "/proc/3/fd/4",
17046            "/proc/3/task/3/fd/4",
17047        ] {
17048            let recorded = path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), read, leader, table, None);
17049            assert_eq!(recorded, Path::new("/proc"), "{spelling}");
17050            // A dirfd-relative name below the new descriptor is then the
17051            // rendered file's own path (`Detcore::observed_path`).
17052            assert_eq!(recorded.join("stat"), Path::new("/proc/stat"));
17053            assert_eq!(
17054                recorded.join("sys/kernel/random/uuid"),
17055                Path::new("/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid")
17056            );
17057        }
17058        // An alias of an alias: the second open finds the first's recorded
17059        // path, already the target's.
17060        let first =
17061            path_to_record_for_open(Path::new("/proc/self/fd/4"), read, leader, table, None);
17062        let second = path_to_record_for_open(
17063            Path::new("/dev/fd/9"),
17064            read,
17065            leader,
17066            |fd| (fd == 9).then(|| first.clone()),
17067            None,
17068        );
17069        assert_eq!(second, Path::new("/proc"));
17070        // O_NOFOLLOW opens the link itself (O_PATH) unless a trailing slash
17071        // or `/.` follows it.
17072        let nofollow = OFlag::O_PATH | OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW;
17073        assert_eq!(
17074            path_to_record_for_open(Path::new("/proc/self/fd/4"), nofollow, leader, table, None),
17075            Path::new("/proc/self/fd/4")
17076        );
17077        for spelling in ["/proc/self/fd/4/", "/proc/self/fd/4/.", "/dev/fd/4/"] {
17078            assert_eq!(
17079                path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), nofollow, leader, table, None),
17080                Path::new("/proc"),
17081                "{spelling}"
17082            );
17083        }
17084        // A thread with a table of its own: the process's links name the
17085        // leader's table, not the caller's, so they keep the spelling; its
17086        // own thread links still name its table.
17087        let split = DescriptorLinkOpener {
17088            own: Some((3, 5)),
17089            holds_process_table: false,
17090        };
17091        for spelling in ["/proc/self/fd/4", "/dev/fd/4", "/proc/3/fd/4"] {
17092            assert_eq!(
17093                path_to_record_for_open(
17094                    Path::new(spelling),
17095                    read,
17096                    split,
17097                    |_| { panic!("{spelling} names the leader's table, not the caller's") },
17098                    None
17099                ),
17100                Path::new(spelling)
17101            );
17102        }
17103        for spelling in ["/proc/thread-self/fd/4", "/proc/3/task/5/fd/4"] {
17104            assert_eq!(
17105                path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), read, split, table, None),
17106                Path::new("/proc"),
17107                "{spelling}"
17108            );
17109        }
17110        // A target without a recorded path, with a relative one, or with one
17111        // procfs resolves per caller, and another process's link, keep the
17112        // spelling. A numeric /proc/<pid> target is not per caller.
17113        for spelling in [
17114            "/proc/self/fd/5",
17115            "/proc/self/fd/6",
17116            "/proc/self/fd/8",
17117            "/proc/self/fd/9",
17118            "/dev/fd/10",
17119            "/proc/7/fd/4",
17120        ] {
17121            assert_eq!(
17122                path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), read, leader, table, None),
17123                Path::new(spelling)
17124            );
17125        }
17126        assert_eq!(
17127            path_to_record_for_open(Path::new("/dev/fd/11"), read, leader, table, None),
17128            Path::new("/proc/12")
17129        );
17130        // So does every open that names no descriptor link.
17131        for spelling in ["/proc/stat", "/proc/self/fd/4/stat", "/tmp/x"] {
17132            assert_eq!(
17133                path_to_record_for_open(
17134                    Path::new(spelling),
17135                    read,
17136                    leader,
17137                    |_| { panic!("{spelling} names no descriptor") },
17138                    None
17139                ),
17140                Path::new(spelling)
17141            );
17142        }
17143        // The path is N's as the open's lookup found it, and only while N
17144        // holds the same open file description: an open of N's link that
17145        // waited (a FIFO) while a thread sharing the table replaced N with a
17146        // /proc descriptor opened the FIFO, so it is not recorded as /proc.
17147        use super::LinkSource;
17148        let creator = crate::types::DetTid::from_raw(3);
17149        let fifo = LinkSource {
17150            fd: 5,
17151            path: Some(PathBuf::from("/tmp/dir/fifo")),
17152            open_file: crate::types::OpenFileId::new(creator, 7),
17153            reached: None,
17154        };
17155        let replaced = Some(crate::types::OpenFileId::new(creator, 8));
17156        let unchanged = Some(fifo.open_file);
17157        let spelling = Path::new("/proc/self/fd/5");
17158        assert_eq!(
17159            path_to_record_for_open(
17160                spelling,
17161                read,
17162                leader,
17163                |fd| fifo.path_if_unchanged(fd, unchanged),
17164                None
17165            ),
17166            Path::new("/tmp/dir/fifo")
17167        );
17168        assert_eq!(
17169            path_to_record_for_open(
17170                spelling,
17171                read,
17172                leader,
17173                |fd| fifo.path_if_unchanged(fd, replaced),
17174                None
17175            ),
17176            spelling
17177        );
17178        assert_eq!(
17179            path_to_record_for_open(
17180                spelling,
17181                read,
17182                leader,
17183                |fd| fifo.path_if_unchanged(fd, None),
17184                None
17185            ),
17186            spelling
17187        );
17188        assert_eq!(fifo.path_if_unchanged(4, unchanged), None);
17189    }

17191    /// Where the descriptor a link names has no recorded path (one received
17192    /// through `SCM_RIGHTS`, which has none), an open through
17193    /// the link records the procfs directory the kernel names for the opened
17194    /// descriptor (`Detcore::procfs_directory_named_for`): `/proc`, below
17195    /// which `stat` is `/proc/stat`. Without that name it keeps the
17196    /// spelling, as before. A recorded path of `N` still comes first, and the
17197    /// name is never taken for a link opened itself, a spelling that names no
17198    /// descriptor link, or a link to a table the caller does not hold. Only
17199    /// `/proc` and the pid-free paths below it are names the kernel's link
17200    /// may give (`procfs_directory_link`).
17201    #[test]
17202    fn an_open_through_an_unrecorded_descriptors_link_records_its_identity() {
17203        use std::path::Path;
17204        use std::path::PathBuf;
17205
17206        use super::DescriptorLinkOpener;
17207        use super::path_to_record_for_open;
17208
17209        let leader = DescriptorLinkOpener {
17210            own: Some((3, 3)),
17211            holds_process_table: true,
17212        };
17213        let read = OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_DIRECTORY;
17214        let proc = || Some(PathBuf::from("/proc"));
17215        for spelling in [
17216            "/proc/self/fd/10",
17217            "/dev/fd/10",
17218            "/proc/thread-self/fd/10",
17219            "/proc/3/fd/10",
17220            "/proc/3/task/3/fd/10",
17221        ] {
17222            let recorded =
17223                path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), read, leader, |_| None, proc());
17224            assert_eq!(recorded, Path::new("/proc"), "{spelling}");
17225            assert_eq!(recorded.join("stat"), Path::new("/proc/stat"));
17226            assert_eq!(
17227                path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), read, leader, |_| None, None),
17228                Path::new(spelling)
17229            );
17230        }
17231        assert_eq!(
17232            path_to_record_for_open(
17233                Path::new("/proc/self/fd/4"),
17234                read,
17235                leader,
17236                |fd| (fd == 4).then(|| PathBuf::from("/proc/12")),
17237                proc(),
17238            ),
17239            Path::new("/proc/12")
17240        );
17241        let nofollow = OFlag::O_PATH | OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW;
17242        assert_eq!(
17243            path_to_record_for_open(
17244                Path::new("/proc/self/fd/10"),
17245                nofollow,
17246                leader,
17247                |_| None,
17248                proc()
17249            ),
17250            Path::new("/proc/self/fd/10")
17251        );
17252        for spelling in ["/proc/self/fd/10/stat", "/tmp/x"] {
17253            assert_eq!(
17254                path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), read, leader, |_| None, proc()),
17255                Path::new(spelling)
17256            );
17257        }
17258        // A recorded path refused as per caller is not replaced by the name.
17259        assert_eq!(
17260            path_to_record_for_open(
17261                Path::new("/proc/self/fd/8"),
17262                read,
17263                leader,
17264                |_| Some(PathBuf::from("/proc/self")),
17265                proc(),
17266            ),
17267            Path::new("/proc/self/fd/8")
17268        );
17269        // A thread with a table of its own: the process's links name the
17270        // leader's table, whose N the caller's table does not describe, so
17271        // they keep the spelling; its own thread links take the name.
17272        let split = DescriptorLinkOpener {
17273            own: Some((3, 5)),
17274            holds_process_table: false,
17275        };
17276        for spelling in ["/proc/self/fd/10", "/dev/fd/10", "/proc/3/fd/10"] {
17277            assert_eq!(
17278                path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), read, split, |_| None, proc()),
17279                Path::new(spelling)
17280            );
17281        }
17282        for spelling in ["/proc/thread-self/fd/10", "/proc/3/task/5/fd/10"] {
17283            assert_eq!(
17284                path_to_record_for_open(Path::new(spelling), read, split, |_| None, proc()),
17285                Path::new("/proc"),
17286                "{spelling}"
17287            );
17288        }
17289        use super::procfs_directory_link;
17290        for accepted in ["/proc", "/proc/sys", "/proc/sys/kernel", "/proc/sys/net"] {
17291            assert!(procfs_directory_link(Path::new(accepted)), "{accepted}");
17292        }
17293        for refused in [
17294            "/tmp/dir",
17295            "/procfs",
17296            "/proc (deleted)",
17297            "/proc/sys (deleted)",
17298            "/proc/12",
17299            "/proc/12/task/12",
17300            "/proc/self",
17301            "/proc/thread-self",
17302            // A symbolic link to the caller's own /proc/self/net.
17303            "/proc/net",
17304            "/proc/sys/../12",
17305            "proc",
17306            "anon_inode:[eventfd]",
17307            "/memfd:x (deleted)",
17308        ] {
17309            assert!(!procfs_directory_link(Path::new(refused)), "{refused}");
17310        }
17311    }

17313    /// The kernel's name for a received procfs directory gives its components
17314    /// below `/proc` and the positions of the task numbers among them, which
17315    /// DBT translates to the guest's: a process's directory and a thread's
17316    /// below its `task`, nothing for the system directories, and no name
17317    /// procfs would not give.
17318    #[test]
17319    fn a_received_procfs_directory_names_its_task_positions() {
17320        use super::procfs_directory_task_positions;
17321        let parsed = |link: &str| procfs_directory_task_positions(link);
17322        let owned = |names: &[&str]| names.iter().map(|name| (*name).to_owned()).collect();
17323        assert_eq!(parsed("/proc"), Some((Vec::new(), Vec::new())));
17324        assert_eq!(
17325            parsed("/proc/sys/kernel"),
17326            Some((owned(&["sys", "kernel"]), Vec::new()))
17327        );
17328        assert_eq!(parsed("/proc/12"), Some((owned(&["12"]), vec![0])));
17329        assert_eq!(parsed("/proc/12/ns"), Some((owned(&["12", "ns"]), vec![0])));
17330        assert_eq!(parsed("/proc/12/fd"), Some((owned(&["12", "fd"]), vec![0])));
17331        assert_eq!(
17332            parsed("/proc/12/task/14"),
17333            Some((owned(&["12", "task", "14"]), vec![0, 2]))
17334        );
17335        assert_eq!(
17336            parsed("/proc/12/task/14/ns"),
17337            Some((owned(&["12", "task", "14", "ns"]), vec![0, 2]))
17338        );
17339        assert_eq!(
17340            parsed("/proc/irq/5"),
17341            Some((owned(&["irq", "5"]), Vec::new()))
17342        );
17343        for refused in [
17344            "/proc/012",
17345            "/proc/12/task/014",
17346            "/procfs",
17347            "/tmp/12",
17348            "proc/12",
17349            "/proc/12 (deleted)",
17350            "socket:[1]",
17351            "/proc/12/../13",
17352        ] {
17353            assert_eq!(parsed(refused), None, "{refused}");
17354        }
17355    }

17398    /// Every `fcntl` and `ioctl` that can make Linux signal a descriptor's
17399    /// owner at a moment set by host timing names SIGIO and SIGURG, plus the
17400    /// signal `F_SETSIG` chooses; every other command names nothing
17401    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
17402    #[test]
17403    fn async_io_arming_calls_name_their_host_timed_signals() {
17404        use reverie::syscalls::FcntlCmd;
17405        use reverie::syscalls::ioctl::Request;
17406        let bit = |signal: i32| 1_u64 << (signal - 1);
17407        let async_io = bit(libc::SIGIO) | bit(libc::SIGURG);
17408        for (cmd, expected) in [
17409            (
17410                FcntlCmd::F_SETFL(libc::O_ASYNC | libc::O_NONBLOCK),
17411                async_io,
17412            ),
17413            (FcntlCmd::F_SETFL(libc::O_NONBLOCK), 0),
17414            (FcntlCmd::F_SETOWN, async_io),
17415            (FcntlCmd::F_SETOWN_EX(None), async_io),
17416            (FcntlCmd::F_SETLEASE(libc::F_RDLCK), async_io),
17417            // DN_MODIFY, which the libc crate does not export.
17418            (FcntlCmd::F_NOTIFY(0x2), async_io),
17419            (
17420                FcntlCmd::F_SETSIG(libc::SIGUSR1),
17421                async_io | bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
17422            ),
17423            (FcntlCmd::F_SETSIG(0), async_io),
17424            (FcntlCmd::F_GETFL, 0),
17425            (FcntlCmd::F_SETFD(libc::FD_CLOEXEC), 0),
17426        ] {
17427            assert_eq!(fcntl_host_timed_signals(cmd), expected, "{cmd:?}");
17428        }
17429        for (request, expected) in [
17430            (Request::FIOASYNC(None), async_io),
17431            (Request::FIOSETOWN(None), async_io),
17432            (Request::SIOCSPGRP(None), async_io),
17433            (Request::FIOCLEX, 0),
17434        ] {
17435            assert_eq!(ioctl_host_timed_signals(request), expected, "{request:?}");
17436        }
17437    }

17439    /// The calls that give a session its controlling terminal (TIOCSCTTY, and
17440    /// TIOCGPTPEER without O_NOCTTY, which opens a pseudoterminal's other end
17441    /// as `open` does) or choose the terminal's foreground process group
17442    /// (TIOCSPGRP) name every signal Linux sends because of that terminal, at
17443    /// a moment set by host timing: SIGHUP and SIGCONT when it hangs up or the
17444    /// leader exits, SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGTSTP for its interrupt, quit and
17445    /// suspend characters, SIGWINCH when its size changes, and SIGTTIN and
17446    /// SIGTTOU when a background process group reads or writes it. Reading the
17447    /// foreground group (TIOCGPGRP), giving up the controlling terminal
17448    /// (TIOCNOTTY), opening the other end with O_NOCTTY, and setting the size
17449    /// (TIOCSWINSZ, whose SIGWINCH is sent inside the caller's call) name
17450    /// nothing (round-9 High 2 and the round-11 finding "Terminal resize
17451    /// remains an admitted host-timed interruption" of
17452    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
17453    #[test]
17454    fn terminal_control_calls_name_the_terminal_signals() {
17455        use reverie::syscalls::ioctl::Request;
17456        let bit = |signal: i32| 1_u64 << (signal - 1);
17457        let terminal = [
17458            libc::SIGHUP,
17459            libc::SIGCONT,
17460            libc::SIGINT,
17461            libc::SIGQUIT,
17462            libc::SIGTSTP,
17463            libc::SIGWINCH,
17464            libc::SIGTTIN,
17465            libc::SIGTTOU,
17466        ]
17467        .into_iter()
17468        .fold(0, |set, signal| set | bit(signal));
17469        for (request, expected) in [
17470            (Request::TIOCSCTTY(0), terminal),
17471            (Request::TIOCSCTTY(1), terminal),
17472            (Request::TIOCSPGRP(None), terminal),
17473            (Request::TIOCGPTPEER(libc::O_RDWR), terminal),
17474            (
17475                Request::TIOCGPTPEER(libc::O_RDWR | libc::O_CLOEXEC),
17476                terminal,
17477            ),
17478            (Request::TIOCGPTPEER(libc::O_RDWR | libc::O_NOCTTY), 0),
17479            (Request::TIOCGPGRP(None), 0),
17480            (Request::TIOCNOTTY, 0),
17481            (Request::TIOCSWINSZ(None), 0),
17482        ] {
17483            assert_eq!(ioctl_host_timed_signals(request), expected, "{request:?}");
17484        }
17485    }

17487    /// An `open` can give its caller a controlling terminal only without
17488    /// O_NOCTTY and O_PATH, only in a session leader, and only of a terminal
17489    /// Linux can make controlling. None of the inputs is the controlling
17490    /// terminal procfs lists, which a hangup clears
17491    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146,
17492    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
17493    #[test]
17494    fn an_open_acquires_a_controlling_terminal_only_as_a_session_leader() {
17495        assert!(open_can_acquire_controlling_terminal(OFlag::O_RDWR));
17496        assert!(!open_can_acquire_controlling_terminal(
17497            OFlag::O_RDWR | OFlag::O_NOCTTY
17498        ));
17499        assert!(!open_can_acquire_controlling_terminal(OFlag::O_PATH));
17500        // A host's /proc/tty/drivers, plus a driver whose name has a space.
17501        let table = Some(
17502            "/dev/tty             /dev/tty        5       0 system:/dev/tty\n\
17503             /dev/console         /dev/console    5       1 system:console\n\
17504             /dev/ptmx            /dev/ptmx       5       2 system\n\
17505             /dev/vc/0            /dev/vc/0       4       0 system:vtmaster\n\
17506             serial_8250          /dev/ttyS       4 64-95 serial\n\
17507             acm serial           /dev/ttyACM   166 0-255 serial\n\
17508             pty_slave            /dev/pts      136 0-1048575 pty:slave\n\
17509             pty_master           /dev/ptm      128 0-1048575 pty:master\n\
17510             unknown              /dev/tty        4 1-63 console\n",
17511        );
17512        // /dev/pts/3 is character device 136:3; minor 300 sets bits above 0xff.
17513        let pts3 = libc::makedev(136, 3);
17514        let pts300 = libc::makedev(136, 300);
17515        assert!(may_have_acquired_controlling_terminal(42, 42, pts3, table));
17516        assert!(may_have_acquired_controlling_terminal(
17517            42, 42, pts300, table
17518        ));
17519        assert!(!may_have_acquired_controlling_terminal(43, 42, pts3, table));
17520        // Serial lines, virtual consoles and /dev/tty can become controlling;
17521        // /dev/console, /dev/ptmx, /dev/vc/0, pseudoterminal masters, minors
17522        // outside every range and devices that are not terminals cannot.
17523        for (major, minor) in [(4, 64), (4, 95), (166, 7), (4, 1), (4, 63), (5, 0)] {
17524            let rdev = libc::makedev(major, minor);
17525            assert!(
17526                terminal_can_become_controlling(rdev, table),
17527                "{major}:{minor}"
17528            );
17529        }
17530        for (major, minor) in [(5, 1), (5, 2), (4, 0), (128, 3), (4, 96), (188, 0), (1, 3)] {
17531            let rdev = libc::makedev(major, minor);
17532            assert!(
17533                !terminal_can_become_controlling(rdev, table),
17534                "{major}:{minor}"
17535            );
17536        }
17537        // A table that cannot be read answers true, except for the devices
17538        // Linux never makes controlling. A line that does not parse answers
17539        // true, unless another line names the device.
17540        let null = libc::makedev(1, 3);
17541        assert!(terminal_can_become_controlling(pts3, None));
17542        assert!(terminal_can_become_controlling(null, None));
17543        assert!(!terminal_can_become_controlling(libc::makedev(5, 1), None));
17544        let garbled = Some("pty_slave /dev/pts 136 0-1048575 pty:slave\nnot a driver line\n");
17545        assert!(terminal_can_become_controlling(null, garbled));
17546        assert!(terminal_can_become_controlling(pts3, garbled));
17547        let master = Some("pty_master /dev/ptm 128 0-1048575 pty:master\nnot a driver line\n");
17548        assert!(!terminal_can_become_controlling(
17549            libc::makedev(128, 3),
17550            master
17551        ));
17552    }

17554    /// A session leader that opens a pseudoterminal's slave without O_NOCTTY
17555    /// gains it as its controlling terminal. Closing the master then hangs the
17556    /// slave up, which clears the controlling terminal procfs lists but changes
17557    /// neither the session nor the descriptor's device. A hangup that lands
17558    /// after the `open`, whether before or after the descriptor's stat, must
17559    /// not hide that the `open` may have acquired the terminal
17560    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
17561    #[test]
17562    fn a_hangup_after_the_open_does_not_hide_the_acquired_terminal() {
17563        use std::time::Duration;
17564        use std::time::Instant;
17565
17566        struct Child(libc::pid_t);
17567        impl Drop for Child {
17568            fn drop(&mut self) {
17569                // SAFETY: the pid is this test's own child, not yet reaped.
17570                unsafe {
17571                    libc::kill(self.0, libc::SIGKILL);
17572                    libc::waitpid(self.0, std::ptr::null_mut(), 0);
17573                }
17574            }
17575        }
17576
17577        // SAFETY (every block below): libc calls on descriptors, buffers and
17578        // a child process this test owns.
17579        let flags = libc::O_RDWR | libc::O_NOCTTY | libc::O_CLOEXEC;
17580        let master = unsafe { libc::posix_openpt(flags) };
17581        assert!(
17582            master >= 0,
17583            "posix_openpt: {}",
17584            std::io::Error::last_os_error()
17585        );
17586        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::grantpt(master) }, 0);
17587        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::unlockpt(master) }, 0);
17588        let mut slave_path = [0 as libc::c_char; 64];
17589        let path_len = slave_path.len();
17590        assert_eq!(
17591            unsafe { libc::ptsname_r(master, slave_path.as_mut_ptr(), path_len) },
17592            0
17593        );
17594        // `ready` carries the slave's descriptor number to this process;
17595        // nothing writes `release`, so this process's exit ends the child.
17596        let (mut ready, mut release) = ([0; 2], [0; 2]);
17597        assert_eq!(
17598            unsafe { libc::pipe2(ready.as_mut_ptr(), libc::O_CLOEXEC) },
17599            0
17600        );
17601        assert_eq!(
17602            unsafe { libc::pipe2(release.as_mut_ptr(), libc::O_CLOEXEC) },
17603            0
17604        );
17605        let pid = unsafe { libc::fork() };
17606        assert!(pid >= 0, "fork: {}", std::io::Error::last_os_error());
17607        if pid == 0 {
17608            // The child makes only async-signal-safe calls and allocates
17609            // nothing, so forking from a test harness thread is safe.
17610            unsafe {
17611                libc::alarm(60);
17612                libc::signal(libc::SIGHUP, libc::SIG_IGN);
17613                libc::close(master);
17614                libc::close(ready[0]);
17615                libc::close(release[1]);
17616                if libc::setsid() < 0 {
17617                    libc::_exit(2);
17618                }
17619                let slave = libc::open(slave_path.as_ptr(), libc::O_RDWR);
17620                if slave < 0 {
17621                    libc::_exit(3);
17622                }
17623                let bytes = slave.to_ne_bytes();
17624                if libc::write(ready[1], bytes.as_ptr().cast(), bytes.len()) != 4 {
17625                    libc::_exit(4);
17626                }
17627                let mut byte = [0_u8; 1];
17628                libc::read(release[0], byte.as_mut_ptr().cast(), 1);
17629                libc::_exit(0);
17630            }
17631        }
17632        let child = Child(pid);
17633        unsafe {
17634            libc::close(ready[1]);
17635            libc::close(release[0]);
17636        }
17637        let mut bytes = [0_u8; 4];
17638        let got = unsafe { libc::read(ready[0], bytes.as_mut_ptr().cast(), bytes.len()) };
17639        assert_eq!(got, 4, "the child did not open the slave");
17640        let slave = i32::from_ne_bytes(bytes);
17641        // The descriptor's stat, read before the hangup, as `handle_openat`
17642        // reads it before it classifies the open.
17643        let link = std::ffi::CString::new(format!("/proc/{pid}/fd/{slave}")).unwrap();
17644        let mut host_stat: libc::stat = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
17645        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::stat(link.as_ptr(), &mut host_stat) }, 0);
17646        let terminal = (
17647            libc::major(host_stat.st_rdev) as i32,
17648            libc::minor(host_stat.st_rdev) as i32,
17649        );
17650        let process = procfs::process::Process::new(pid).unwrap();
17651        let before = process.stat().unwrap();
17652        assert_eq!(
17653            (before.session, before.tty_nr()),
17654            (pid, terminal),
17655            "the child's open did not acquire the terminal"
17656        );
17657        assert!(opened_controlling_terminal(pid, slave, Some(&host_stat)));
17658        // Hang the slave up: Linux clears the session's controlling terminal.
17659        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::close(master) }, 0);
17660        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
17661        while process.stat().unwrap().tty_nr() != (0, 0) {
17662            assert!(
17663                Instant::now() < deadline,
17664                "the hangup did not clear the controlling terminal"
17665            );
17666            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
17667        }
17668        assert_eq!(process.stat().unwrap().session, pid);
17669        assert!(
17670            opened_controlling_terminal(pid, slave, Some(&host_stat)),
17671            "a hangup after the descriptor's stat hid the acquisition"
17672        );
17673        assert!(
17674            opened_controlling_terminal(pid, slave, None),
17675            "a hangup before the descriptor's stat hid the acquisition"
17676        );
17677        drop(child);
17678    }

17680    /// The ceiling is inclusive. A guest that reads the advertised
17681    /// `pipe-max-size` and asks for exactly that must be allowed to have it;
17682    /// refusing at the boundary would advertise a size that cannot be set.
17683    /// The pin is two of the host's pages, which Linux applies exactly at any
17684    /// page size; on x86-64 that is the 8 KiB it always was.
17685    #[test]
17686    fn the_pipe_capacity_is_two_host_pages() {
17687        // SAFETY: sysconf has no preconditions.
17688        let page = unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) };
17689        assert_eq!(i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()), 2 * page);
17690        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
17691        assert_eq!(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes(), 8192);
17692    }
17693
17694    #[test]
17695    fn the_pipe_ceiling_admits_exactly_the_pinned_capacity() {
17696        assert!(!pipe_capacity_request_exceeds_ceiling(
17697            deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()
17698        ));
17699        assert!(!pipe_capacity_request_exceeds_ceiling(
17700            deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes() - 1
17701        ));
17702        assert!(pipe_capacity_request_exceeds_ceiling(
17703            deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes() + 1
17704        ));
17705    }
17706
17707    /// A host pipe's capacity above the ceiling reads as the ceiling, so a
17708    /// default 16-page pipe and one the host shrank to two pages under
17709    /// `pipe-user-pages-soft` read the same. A capacity at or below the ceiling
17710    /// (Hermit's pin, or a guest's own shrink to one page) reads as it is.
17711    #[test]
17712    fn a_host_pipe_capacity_reads_no_larger_than_the_ceiling() {
17713        let ceiling = i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes());
17714        let page = ceiling / 2;
17715        assert_eq!(super::reported_pipe_capacity(16 * page), ceiling);
17716        assert_eq!(super::reported_pipe_capacity(1 << 30), ceiling);
17717        assert_eq!(super::reported_pipe_capacity(ceiling), ceiling);
17718        assert_eq!(super::reported_pipe_capacity(page), page);
17719    }
17720
17721    /// Two pages is load-independent only where `pipe-max-size` is at least
17722    /// two pages. On a host whose `pipe-max-size` is one page, a new pipe has
17723    /// one page below the quota and two above it, so the decision rests on the
17724    /// setting alone: both allocation states are refused alike. An unreadable
17725    /// setting is decided by the probe alone, which runs only then.
17726    #[test]
17727    fn two_pages_is_trusted_only_with_a_two_page_pipe_max_size() {
17728        let ceiling = i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes());
17729        let page = ceiling / 2;
17730        let unused = || panic!("the probe runs only for an unreadable setting");
17731        assert!(super::host_pipe_floor_is_two_pages(Some(ceiling), unused));
17732        assert!(super::host_pipe_floor_is_two_pages(Some(1 << 20), unused));
17733        assert!(!super::host_pipe_floor_is_two_pages(Some(page), unused));
17734        assert!(super::host_pipe_floor_is_two_pages(None, || true));
17735        assert!(!super::host_pipe_floor_is_two_pages(None, || false));
17736        // This host's probe runs; its answer depends on the host's quota and
17737        // capabilities, so it is not asserted.
17738        let _ = super::probe_two_page_pipe_max_size();
17739    }

17741    /// Shrinking stays legal. `tests/c/pipe_capacity.c`
17742    /// shrinks to one page and requires the value to round-trip, so a blanket
17743    /// clamp to the pinned capacity would break a guest-visible contract this
17744    /// repository already locked.
17745    #[test]
17746    fn shrinking_is_never_refused_by_the_ceiling() {
17747        for requested in [1, 4096, deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes() / 2] {
17748            assert!(
17749                !pipe_capacity_request_exceeds_ceiling(requested),
17750                "shrink to {requested} must remain permitted"
17751            );
17752        }
17753    }
17754
17755    /// The host's own ceiling is the value this change exists to stop
17756    /// consulting: 1048576 on a default host, 65536 on a hardened one. Both are
17757    /// refused now, so the guest-visible answer no longer depends on which host
17758    /// it is.
17759    #[test]
17760    fn host_ceilings_are_refused_identically_on_any_host() {
17761        let ceiling = deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes();
17762        // Above the two-page ceiling at any page size: twice it, eight times
17763        // it, and the default 1 MiB.
17764        for host_ceiling in [2 * ceiling, 8 * ceiling, 1 << 20] {
17765            assert!(
17766                pipe_capacity_request_exceeds_ceiling(host_ceiling),
17767                "{host_ceiling} must be refused regardless of the host sysctl"
17768            );
17769        }
17770    }

17797    #[test]
17798    fn pipe_capacity_failure_classifies_the_errno() {
17799        let created = [17, 18];
17800
17801        // The only success shape: Linux applied EXACTLY the capacity we asked for.
17802        assert_eq!(
17803            pipe_capacity_failure(created, Ok(i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()))),
17804            None
17805        );
17806
17807        // Successful-but-wrong capacity is a pipe whose size we did not choose. That is not a
17808        // kernel errno, so it is reported as EIO rather than dressed up as one.
17809        let mismatch = pipe_capacity_failure(
17810            created,
17811            Ok(i64::from(deterministic_pipe_capacity_bytes()) * 2),
17812        )
17813        .expect("a capacity Linux rounded away from the pin must not read as success");
17814        assert_eq!(mismatch.created_fds, created);
17815        assert_eq!(mismatch.error, Errno::EIO);
17816
17817        // A real kernel errno is preserved rather than rewritten.
17818        let denied = pipe_capacity_failure(created, Err(Errno::EPERM))
17819            .expect("a kernel refusal must not read as success");
17820        assert_eq!(denied.created_fds, created);
17821        assert_eq!(denied.error, Errno::EPERM);
17822
17823        // The descriptors are carried through every failure shape, because they are what the
17824        // caller has to close; losing them here is how they would leak.
17825        assert_eq!(denied.created_fds, created);
17826    }
17827
17828    #[test]
17829    fn pipe_capacity_failure_closes_both_created_descriptors() {
17830        if isolated_child(
17831            "syscalls::files::test::pipe_capacity_failure_closes_both_created_descriptors",
17832        ) {
17833            return;
17834        }
17835        let mut created = [-1; 2];
17836        assert_eq!(
17837            unsafe { libc::pipe2(created.as_mut_ptr(), libc::O_CLOEXEC) },
17838            0
17839        );
17840
17841        let pin_result = unsafe { libc::fcntl(created[0], libc::F_SETPIPE_SZ, -1) };
17842        assert_eq!(pin_result, -1);
17843        let pin_error = Errno::last();
17844        // Pin the errno, not just the failure. Without this the test asserts only that
17845        // `fcntl` returned -1, so it would still pass if the call failed for a reason we
17846        // did not engineer -- an invalid `created[0]` fails EBADF, every assertion below
17847        // still holds, and the capacity-pin path is never exercised at all.
17848        //
17849        // EINVAL is structural here, not a property of this host. `fcntl`'s argument is an
17850        // `unsigned long`, so -1 arrives as ULONG_MAX; `round_pipe_size` returns 0 for any
17851        // size above 2^31, and `pipe_set_size` maps that 0 to -EINVAL BEFORE it consults
17852        // `CAP_SYS_RESOURCE`. So the result does not depend on privilege or on
17853        // `/proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size`.
17854        assert_eq!(pin_error, Errno::EINVAL);
17855
17856        let failure = pipe_capacity_failure(created, Err(pin_error))
17857            .expect("the forced capacity-pin failure must enter the cleanup path");
17858        for close in failure.close_syscalls() {
17859            assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::close(close.fd()) }, 0);
17860        }
17861
17862        for fd in created {
17863            assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_GETFD) }, -1);
17864            assert_eq!(Errno::last(), Errno::EBADF);
17865        }
17866    }

17868    #[test]
17869    fn rendered_procfs_seek_follows_each_llseek() {
17870        use super::RenderedSeek::*;
17871        // generic_file_llseek (auxv, cmdline): SEEK_DATA and SEEK_HOLE at any
17872        // offset of a file of size 0, a negative one included, are ENXIO.
17873        for whence in [Whence::SEEK_DATA, Whence::SEEK_HOLE] {
17874            for offset in [i64::MIN, -1, 0, 1, i64::MAX] {
17875                assert_eq!(
17876                    super::rendered_procfs_seek(Generic, whence, offset, 0),
17877                    Err(Errno::ENXIO)
17878                );
17879            }
17880            assert_eq!(
17881                super::rendered_procfs_seek(Default, whence, 0, 0),
17882                Err(Errno::ENXIO)
17883            );
17884            assert_eq!(
17885                super::rendered_procfs_seek(SeqFile, whence, -1, 0),
17886                Err(Errno::EINVAL)
17887            );
17888        }
17889        // default_llseek compares signed: a negative SEEK_DATA offset stays
17890        // negative (EINVAL); a negative SEEK_HOLE offset becomes the size, 0.
17891        assert_eq!(
17892            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Default, Whence::SEEK_DATA, -1, 0),
17893            Err(Errno::EINVAL)
17894        );
17895        assert_eq!(
17896            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Default, Whence::SEEK_HOLE, -1, 5),
17897            Ok(0)
17898        );
17899        // vfs_setpos: s_maxbytes (MAX_NON_LFS) bounds generic_file_llseek only.
17900        let max = (1_i64 << 31) - 1;
17901        assert_eq!(
17902            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Generic, Whence::SEEK_SET, max, 0),
17903            Ok(max as usize)
17904        );
17905        assert_eq!(
17906            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Generic, Whence::SEEK_SET, max + 1, 0),
17907            Err(Errno::EINVAL)
17908        );
17909        assert_eq!(
17910            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Generic, Whence::SEEK_CUR, 1, max as usize),
17911            Err(Errno::EINVAL)
17912        );
17913        assert_eq!(
17914            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Default, Whence::SEEK_SET, max + 1, 0),
17915            Ok(max as usize + 1)
17916        );
17917        assert_eq!(
17918            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Generic, Whence::SEEK_SET, -1, 0),
17919            Err(Errno::EINVAL)
17920        );
17921        assert_eq!(
17922            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Generic, Whence::SEEK_END, 3, 0),
17923            Ok(3)
17924        );
17925        assert_eq!(
17926            super::rendered_procfs_seek(SeqFile, Whence::SEEK_END, 0, 0),
17927            Err(Errno::EINVAL)
17928        );
17929        assert_eq!(
17930            super::rendered_procfs_seek(Generic, Whence::from_raw(99), 0, 0),
17931            Err(Errno::EINVAL)
17932        );
17933    }

18032    #[test]
18033    fn host_network_notice_names_only_abstract_unix_addresses() {
18034        let path = std::mem::offset_of!(libc::sockaddr_un, sun_path);
18035        let family = (libc::AF_UNIX as u16).to_ne_bytes();
18036        let address = |sun_path: &[u8]| [&family[..], sun_path].concat();
18037        assert_eq!(
18038            abstract_unix_name(&address(b"\0myapp:3")),
18039            Some(&b"myapp:3"[..])
18040        );
18041        // A leading NUL alone is an abstract name of length zero.
18042        assert_eq!(abstract_unix_name(&address(b"\0")), Some(&b""[..]));
18043        // A path name, and a bare family (an autobind, which Hermit names
18044        // itself), are not.
18045        assert_eq!(abstract_unix_name(&address(b"/tmp/socket")), None);
18046        assert_eq!(abstract_unix_name(&family), None);
18047        assert_eq!(address(b"").len(), path);
18048
18049        let bound = host_network_abstract_bind_notice(b"x\0y\"z", false);
18050        assert!(
18051            bound.starts_with("hermit: NOTICE: the guest bound "),
18052            "{bound}"
18053        );
18054        assert!(
18055            bound.contains("\"@x\\x00y\\\"z\" under --network=host."),
18056            "{bound}"
18057        );
18058        assert!(bound.contains("--network=local"), "{bound}");
18059        let in_use = host_network_abstract_bind_notice(b"myapp:3", true);
18060        assert!(
18061            in_use.contains("\"@myapp:3\" under --network=host failed with EADDRINUSE"),
18062            "{in_use}"
18063        );
18064    }

18101    /// Records with the names `names`, as `serve_next_batch` encodes them
18102    /// from position 0, and the length of each name.
18103    fn directory_records(format: super::DirentFormat, names: &[&[u8]]) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<usize>) {
18104        let mut records = Vec::new();
18105        for (index, name) in names.iter().enumerate() {
18106            let entry = super::DirEntry {
18107                name: name.to_vec(),
18108                ino: 0x1111_1111_1111_1111,
18109                off: 0,
18110                ty: 4,
18111            };
18112            format.encode(&entry, entry.ino, index as i64 + 1, &mut records);
18113        }
18114        (records, names.iter().map(|name| name.len()).collect())
18115    }
18116
18117    /// `records` as Linux leaves them in a buffer that held `Pages::FILL`:
18118    /// the padding after each name is not written.
18119    fn as_linux_writes(format: super::DirentFormat, records: &[u8], names: &[usize]) -> Vec<u8> {
18120        let mut bytes = records.to_vec();
18121        let mut at = 0;
18122        for &name_len in names {
18123            let reclen = format.record_len(name_len);
18124            let padding = at + format.name_offset() + name_len + 1;
18125            let end = match format {
18126                super::DirentFormat::Dirent64 => at + reclen,
18127                super::DirentFormat::Legacy => at + reclen - 1,
18128            };
18129            bytes[padding..end].fill(Pages::FILL);
18130            at += reclen;
18131        }
18132        bytes
18133    }
18134
18135    const FORMATS: [super::DirentFormat; 2] =
18136        [super::DirentFormat::Dirent64, super::DirentFormat::Legacy];
18137
18138    const TEN: [&[u8]; 10] = [b"a", b"b", b"c", b"d", b"e", b"f", b"g", b"h", b"i", b"j"];
18139
18140    /// A buffer starting 16 bytes before a writable page, in a page the guest
18141    /// cannot write: Linux's first store, to the first record's `d_off`,
18142    /// fails, so the call fails and the writable page is left as it was.
18143    #[test]
18144    fn a_first_record_that_cannot_be_written_leaves_the_next_page_untouched() {
18145        for protection in [libc::PROT_NONE, libc::PROT_READ] {
18146            for format in FORMATS {
18147                let pages = Pages::new(&[protection, libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE]);
18148                let (records, names) = directory_records(format, &TEN);
18149                let copied = super::copy_records(
18150                    &mut LocalMemory::new(),
18151                    pages.address(PAGE - 16),
18152                    format,
18153                    &records,
18154                    &names,
18155                    0,
18156                );
18157                assert_eq!(copied, (0, Err(Errno::EFAULT)), "{format:?} {protection}");
18158                assert!(
18159                    pages.contents().iter().all(|&byte| byte == Pages::FILL),
18160                    "{format:?} after a page with protection {protection}: bytes changed"
18161                );
18162            }
18163        }
18164    }

18166    /// Guest memory whose every vectored copy fails with one error that is
18167    /// not a fault, as when the guest's thread is gone or the backend fails.
18168    struct FailingMemory(Errno);
18169
18170    impl reverie::syscalls::MemoryAccess for FailingMemory {
18171        fn read_vectored(
18172            &self,
18173            _: &[std::io::IoSlice],
18174            _: &mut [std::io::IoSliceMut],
18175        ) -> Result<usize, Errno> {
18176            Err(self.0)
18177        }
18178
18179        fn write_vectored(
18180            &mut self,
18181            _: &[std::io::IoSlice],
18182            _: &mut [std::io::IoSliceMut],
18183        ) -> Result<usize, Errno> {
18184            Err(self.0)
18185        }
18186    }
18187
18188    /// Only a fault ends a copy of directory records short. Any other error
18189    /// of the copy is the call's error, as it was before directory streams,
18190    /// and not `EFAULT`: reading the records back, copying them out (through
18191    /// a buffer whose first store crosses a page, and through one where none
18192    /// does), and reading the prefix the `getdents64` observer hashes.
18193    #[test]
18194    fn a_copy_error_other_than_a_fault_is_returned() {
18195        let buf = |offset| reverie::syscalls::AddrMut::<u8>::from_raw(16 * PAGE + offset).unwrap();
18196        for errno in [Errno::ESRCH, Errno::EIO] {
18197            let mut bytes = [0; 32];
18198            assert_eq!(
18199                super::read_guest_prefix(&FailingMemory(errno), buf(0), &mut bytes),
18200                Err(errno)
18201            );
18202            for format in FORMATS {
18203                let (records, names) = directory_records(format, &TEN);
18204                for offset in [0, PAGE - 4] {
18205                    let copied = super::copy_records(
18206                        &mut FailingMemory(errno),
18207                        buf(offset),
18208                        format,
18209                        &records,
18210                        &names,
18211                        0,
18212                    );
18213                    assert_eq!(copied, (0, Err(errno)), "{format:?} at {offset}");
18214                }
18215                let read =
18216                    super::read_records(&FailingMemory(errno), buf(0), records.len(), format);
18217                assert_eq!(read.err(), Some(errno), "{format:?}");
18218            }
18219        }
18220    }

18400    /// `kiocb_set_rw_flags` for a procfs file, in Linux 7.1's order.
18401    #[test]
18402    fn procfs_vector_flags_are_refused_in_linux_order() {
18403        use reverie::syscalls::Errno;
18404        const NOSIGNAL: i32 = 0x100;
18405        const UNKNOWN: i32 = 0x200;
18406        for accepted in [
18407            0,
18408            libc::RWF_HIPRI,
18409            libc::RWF_DSYNC,
18410            libc::RWF_SYNC,
18411            libc::RWF_APPEND,
18412            libc::RWF_NOAPPEND,
18413            NOSIGNAL,
18414        ] {
18415            assert_eq!(super::validate_procfs_vector_flags(accepted, true), Ok(()));
18416        }
18417        for (flags, errno) in [
18418            (libc::RWF_NOWAIT, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP),
18419            (libc::RWF_ATOMIC, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP),
18420            (libc::RWF_DONTCACHE, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP),
18421            (UNKNOWN, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP),
18422            (libc::RWF_APPEND | libc::RWF_NOAPPEND, Errno::EINVAL),
18423            (libc::RWF_NOWAIT | UNKNOWN, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP),
18424            (
18425                libc::RWF_APPEND | libc::RWF_NOAPPEND | UNKNOWN,
18426                Errno::EOPNOTSUPP,
18427            ),
18428            (
18429                libc::RWF_ATOMIC | libc::RWF_APPEND | libc::RWF_NOAPPEND,
18430                Errno::EINVAL,
18431            ),
18432            (
18433                libc::RWF_NOWAIT | libc::RWF_APPEND | libc::RWF_NOAPPEND,
18434                Errno::EINVAL,
18435            ),
18436        ] {
18437            assert_eq!(
18438                super::validate_procfs_vector_flags(flags, true),
18439                Err(errno),
18440                "{flags:#x}"
18441            );
18442        }
18443        // A file without `read_iter` (`/proc/modules`, `/proc/swaps`) takes
18444        // `RWF_HIPRI` alone, and refuses even the conflicting pair with
18445        // EOPNOTSUPP.
18446        assert_eq!(
18447            super::validate_procfs_vector_flags(libc::RWF_HIPRI, false),
18448            Ok(())
18449        );
18450        for flags in [
18451            libc::RWF_DSYNC,
18452            libc::RWF_APPEND,
18453            NOSIGNAL,
18454            libc::RWF_APPEND | libc::RWF_NOAPPEND,
18455        ] {
18456            assert_eq!(
18457                super::validate_procfs_vector_flags(flags, false),
18458                Err(Errno::EOPNOTSUPP),
18459                "{flags:#x}"
18460            );
18461        }
18462    }

18489    /// Records across two writable pages and into a third the guest cannot
18490    /// write, starting 40 bytes before the second page, so the third starts
18491    /// 4136 bytes in. Record 172 starts at 4128: Linux stores its position
18492    /// into record 171's `d_off` and its `d_ino`, which ends at the third
18493    /// page, and then fails at its `d_reclen`. The call returns 172 records
18494    /// and leaves that `d_ino` written.
18495    #[test]
18496    fn a_record_not_copied_is_left_as_linux_leaves_it() {
18497        let names: Vec<[u8; 1]> = (0..200u8).map(|i| [b'a' + i % 26]).collect();
18498        let names: Vec<&[u8]> = names.iter().map(|name| &name[..]).collect();
18499        for format in FORMATS {
18500            let rw = libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE;
18501            let pages = Pages::new(&[rw, rw, libc::PROT_NONE]);
18502            let start = PAGE - 40;
18503            let (records, lens) = directory_records(format, &names);
18504            let copied = super::copy_records(
18505                &mut LocalMemory::new(),
18506                pages.address(start),
18507                format,
18508                &records,
18509                &lens,
18510                0,
18511            );
18512            assert_eq!(copied, (172, Ok(172 * 24)), "{format:?}");
18513            let contents = pages.contents();
18514            let mut expected = as_linux_writes(format, &records[..4128], &lens[..172]);
18515            expected.extend_from_slice(&records[4128..4136]);
18516            assert_eq!(&contents[start..start + 4136], &expected[..], "{format:?}");
18517            assert!(
18518                contents[..start]
18519                    .iter()
18520                    .chain(&contents[start + 4136..])
18521                    .all(|&byte| byte == Pages::FILL),
18522                "{format:?}: bytes outside what Linux writes changed"
18523            );

18527    /// A second record with a 20-byte name, whose record ends past the end of
18528    /// what the guest can write. For `getdents64`, the NUL after the name is
18529    /// stored before the name and fails, so none of the name is written; for
18530    /// `getdents`, `d_type`, at the record's end, is stored before the name
18531    /// and fails. Either way the record's own `d_off` is not written: Linux
18532    /// stores it only with the next record or at the end of the call.
18533    #[test]
18534    fn a_name_is_stored_after_the_bytes_that_follow_it() {
18535        for format in FORMATS {
18536            let pages = Pages::new(&[libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE, libc::PROT_NONE]);
18537            let (records, names) = directory_records(format, &[b"a", b"abcdefghijklmnopqrst"]);
18538            let copied = super::copy_records(
18539                &mut LocalMemory::new(),
18540                pages.address(PAGE - 50),
18541                format,
18542                &records,
18543                &names,
18544                0,
18545            );
18546            assert_eq!(copied, (1, Ok(24)), "{format:?}");
18547            let contents = &pages.contents()[PAGE - 50..PAGE];
18548            let mut expected = as_linux_writes(format, &records[..24], &names[..1]);
18549            expected.extend_from_slice(&records[24..32]);
18550            expected.extend_from_slice(&[Pages::FILL; 8]);
18551            expected.extend_from_slice(&records[40..42]);
18552            match format {
18553                super::DirentFormat::Dirent64 => expected.push(records[42]),
18554                super::DirentFormat::Legacy => expected.push(Pages::FILL),
18555            }
18556            expected.resize(50, Pages::FILL);
18557            assert_eq!(contents, &expected[..], "{format:?}");
